subject: [move-stdlib] Introduce efficient OrderedMap implementation (#14872)
body:
## Description
Implement efficient OrderedMap implementation in move-stdlib, to replace/deprecate SimpleMap. It is an in-memory datastructure - i.e. doesn't store anything in separate resources.

Implementation is a SortedVectorMap, but given the efficiency improvements of vector operations with memcpy, it's performance characteristics are extremely good. 

Running different sizes tests (these are [full results](https://gist.github.com/igor-aptos/815f06754868db8ecedf1714e953af33)), we get milliseconds needed for 100 inserts and 100 removals on maps of different sizes:

```
num elements  SimpleMap       OrderedMap::SortedVectorMap
10            6.4             6.8
100           25.4            10.3
1000          673.9           12.8
10000         too long        19.5
```

Basically achieving log(n) performance, with very simple implementation.
rationale: The commit introduces a new OrderedMap implementation, documentation, and benchmark entries. It does not modify existing behavior to correct a defect, nor does it address any security-related issue.

subject: [move][stdlib] Add efficient BigOrderedMap implementation  (#14753)
body:
## Description
Having efficient and concurrent large-sized "Map" and "OrderedMap" implementations is useful across variety of needs.

Current SmartTable implementation has various limitations, from it being sequential, to it not having smart ways to deal with collisions. It cannot be improved - as the structs are unmodifiable, and so should be deprecated fully.

In this PR:
* provide efficient big "OrderedMap" implementation. BPlusTreeMap is chosen as it is best suited for the onchain storage layout - where majority of cost comes from loading and writing to storage items, and there is no partial read/write of them. It also rebalances in a way that reduces amount writes needed 
* writing to keys that are not close enough, to a BPlusTreeMap with multiple layers, is generally parallel. More elements in the BPlusTreeMap, the more operations will be parallel. 
* it is an enum, so can be evolved in the future as needed
* has an option to pre-pay and pre-allocate storage slots, and to reuse them, achieving predictable gas charges.
  * defined potentially generally useful StorageSlotsAllocator, to manage indexed storage slots for datastructures that need it. Easier to use and more flexible/configurable than directly using Table. (which is also an enum, and so can be evolved / new strategies can be added)
* keeps root note directly inside the resource, to reduce number of resources needed by 1, and optimizes operations when root is the leaf node.
* whenever key or value is inserted/modified, we check the size to make sure it is allowed (i.e. that it is smaller than max_node_size / max_degree). this requires bcs::serialized_size() call on every insert/upsert.
  * in case types have constant sizes, check is performed once, on construction, and then it’s skipped on insert/upsert
rationale: The commit introduces a new BigOrderedMap implementation and related documentation; it does not correct existing behavior, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: [move-vm][closures] Type and Value representation and serialization (#15670)
body:
* [move-vm][closures] Type and Value representation and serialization

[PR 3/n vm closures]

This implements types and values for functions and closures, as well as serialization. For a detailed discussion, see the design doc. It does not yet implement the interpreter and runtime verification.

Overview:

- `MoveValue` and `MoveTypeLayout` are extended to represent closures and functions. A closure carries the function name, the closure mask, the function layout, and the captured arguments. The function layout enables serialization of the captured arguments without any context.
- Runtime `Type` is extended by functions.
- `ValueImpl` is extended by a closure variant. This representation uses `trait AbstractFunction` to represent the function value and implement core functionality like comparison and printing. The existing trait `FunctionValueExtension` is used to create `AbstracFunction` from the serialized representation.
- Similar as with `MoveValue`, the serialized representation of `ValueImpl::Closure` contains the full function layout, enabling to deserialize the captured arguments context independently. This design has been chosen for robustness, avoiding a dependency of serialization from loaded functions, and to enable fully 'lazy' deserialization of closures. The later allows a contract to store hundreds of function values and on loading them from storage, avoiding loading the associated code until the moment the closure is actually executed.
- `AbstractFunction` is implemented in the loader such that it can be either in 'unresolved' or in `resolved' state.

subject: [vm] Signed Integer Basic VM Support
body:
Basic implementation of signed integer types in the VM:

- `i8` to `i256`
- New instructions `LdI<N>`, `CastI<N>`, and `Negate`. Those are gated by bytecode version v9.
- For the new types, extending `SignatureToken`, `TypeTag`, `MoveTypeLayout`, and `runtime_type::Type`. Perhihperhal types like Rest API not touched yet.
- Also extending `MoveValue` and `value_impl::Value`. Peripheral values like in Rest API not touched yet.
- (In general, we use https://github.com/aptos-labs/aptos-core/issues/17645 to track unimplemented features as above in the code via `TODO(#17645)`)
- Needed to introduce new core implementation of 256 bit integers. The existing one was not designed to support i256 and the conversions between both. It appears the most used crated for 256 bit ints is actually `ethnum`. Created a new module `int256` in core types based on `ethnum::{U256, I256}` which provides all needed functionality, specifically cross-casting between signed and unsigned ints. Notice that this change effects existing use of `u256` in Move and needs to be careful vetted.

There are no tests yet in this PR for signed integers, we first need to build tooling like assembler, compiler, etc. around signed ints for this. This can land anyway because its gated by bytecode version.
rationale: The commit introduces signed integer types and new VM instructions, which is a new feature addition rather than correcting existing incorrect behavior. No security-relevant bug is being fixed.

subject: [framework] Add support for reflection (#17892)
body:
* [framework] Add support for reflection

A new `std::reflect` module allows to create a function value from specified address and function name, as well as an expected function type. This feature is important for applications like bridges or tools. Example usage:

```
let fn : |address|u64 has store = reflect::resolve(@somewhere, utf8(b"mod"), utf8(b"fn")).unpack();
assert!(fn(my_addr) == some_value)
```

If reflection of a function value succeeds, its guaranteed that the referred function exists and has the specified type (including abilities). Thus, reflection does not add any new quality of risks to Move, since public functions can already be called from anywhere, and type consistency is guaranteed.

The PR also introduces a new `std::result::Result` type which mimics Rust's result type, and is used to report errors to the caller of `reflect::resolve`.

This is feature flag guarded and will need an accompanying AIP and auditing.

Unit tests have been added for all error situations.

* Add bulk order rejection event

This commit adds a BulkOrderRejectedEvent that is emitted when a bulk order
is rejected during placement. The event includes:
- market_id: The market where the rejection occurred
- account: The account whose bulk order was rejected
- rejection_reason: The reason code for the rejection
- description: A human-readable description of the rejection

This allows off-chain systems to track bulk order rejections separately
from individual order rejections.

Co-Authored-By: Warp <agent@warp.dev>

* Fix dead man's switch events to include market identification

This commit addresses security and usability issues with KeepAliveUpdateEvent
and KeepAliveDisabledEvent by adding market-specific information:

1. Added parent and market address fields to both events to distinguish
   between markets and prevent event confusion across different markets.

2. Added was_registered field to KeepAliveDisabledEvent to clearly indicate
   whether the user was actually registered in the tracker when disabling.

3. Updated function signatures:
   - keep_alive() now accepts parent and market addresses
   - disable_keep_alive() now accepts parent and market addresses

4. Added helper functions to market_types:
   - get_parent() to access the parent address
   - get_market() to access the market address

This prevents malicious actors from spamming events by creating markets
solely to exploit the keep_alive mechanism, and makes events properly
distinguishable across different market instances.

Co-Authored-By: Warp <agent@warp.dev>

* Fix parameter ordering in emit_event_for_bulk_order_modified

The function emit_event_for_bulk_order_modified had parameters in the order
cancelled_bid_sizes, cancelled_bid_prices, cancelled_ask_sizes, cancelled_ask_prices
(sizes first, then prices).

However, the call site in cancel_bulk_maker_order_internal was passing
arguments as cancelled_bid_prices, cancelled_bid_sizes, cancelled_ask_prices,
cancelled_ask_sizes (prices first, then sizes).

This commit reorders the function parameters to follow the prices-first
convention, which is consistent with the rest of the codebase and matches
the order returned by destroy_bulk_order_request().

Changed parameter order from:
- cancelled_bid_sizes, cancelled_bid_prices, cancelled_ask_sizes, cancelled_ask_prices

To:
- cancelled_bid_prices, cancelled_bid_sizes, cancelled_ask_prices, cancelled_ask_sizes

Added explicit documentation to dead_mans_switch_operations::keep_alive
stating that the function does not validate the account parameter, and
that it is the caller's responsibility to ensure proper signer validation
is performed before calling this function if needed.

This follows the same pattern as order_placement::place_order_with_order_id,

Co-Authored-By: Warp <agent@warp.dev>

* Fix documentation to match actual behavior of is_order_valid

Updated the documentation in dead_mans_switch_tracker::is_order_valid to
accurately reflect the actual implementation behavior regarding session
expiration.

Changed from:
- if current_time >= expiration_time: return false (inclusive)

To:
- if current_time > expiration_time: return false (exclusive)

The actual code (line 198) uses 'expiration_time_secs >= current_time',
which means the order is still valid when current_time equals
expiration_time_secs. The session expires only AFTER the expiration time,
not AT the expiration time.

Also updated the KeepAliveState struct documentation to clarify that
the session is expired when current time is strictly greater than
expiration_time_secs.

Co-Authored-By: Warp <agent@warp.dev>

* Remove unnecessary duplicate call in take_ready_price_based_orders

Refactored pending_order_book_index::take_ready_price_based_orders to
remove the second unnecessary call to take_ready_price_move_down_orders.

The function was calling take_ready_price_move_down_orders twice:
1. Line 153: with limit = order_limit (fills down orders up to the limit)
2. Line 156: with limit = order_limit (unnecessary duplicate)

Since the first call already attempts to fill up to order_limit, the
second call is redundant and has been removed.

The corrected logic is:
1. Fill up to ceil(order_limit/2) with price_move_up orders
2. Fill up to order_limit with price_move_down orders
3. Fill any remaining space (up to order_limit) with price_move_up orders

Added MinKeepAliveTimeUpdatedEvent to track changes to the minimum

2. Updated set_min_keep_alive_time_secs to:

3. Updated market_types::set_dead_mans_switch_min_keep_alive_time_secs

subject: [framework] Add hash-based caching for Move framework builds
body:
Previously, any change to Rust dependencies would trigger a full
rebuild of the Move framework (~3 minutes), even when Move source
files hadn't changed. This happened because aptos-framework is a
build-dependency of aptos-cached-packages, and Cargo re-runs
build.rs whenever build-deps are recompiled.

This change adds content-based caching:
- Compute SHA256 hash of all .move files and Move.toml files
- Store cached head.mrb in target/.framework_cache/
- Skip rebuild when hash matches, reducing build time to ~12s

This improves incremental build times by ~93% when only Rust code
changes (from ~2m45s to ~12s).

rationale: The change introduces hash‑based caching to speed up incremental builds; it does not correct incorrect behavior, only improves performance. No security‑related logic is altered, so it is neither a bug fix nor a security fix.

This is more reliable as it tracks actual recompilation rather than

subject: [vm] Use Arc<MoveStructLayout> for shared struct layout caching (#18640)
body:
* [vm] Use Arc<MoveStructLayout> for shared struct layout caching

Change MoveTypeLayout::Struct to hold Arc<MoveStructLayout> instead of
a plain MoveStructLayout. This enables the layout converter to cache
and share struct layouts within a single construction pass.

During layout construction in ty_layout_converter.rs, the same struct
type can be visited multiple times (e.g., enum variants sharing fields,
or the same generic instantiation in different positions). Previously,
each visit re-constructed the entire MoveStructLayout tree and
re-counted all its nodes toward the layout size limit, which was
wasteful and could cause spurious TOO_MANY_TYPE_NODES errors.

Now, a per-pass StructLayoutCache (HashMap keyed by StructNameIndex +
type args) stores Arc<MoveStructLayout> after first construction. On
cache hit, an Arc::clone() is returned with no re-construction or
re-counting. Depth is still checked on every visit to prevent stack
overflow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [vm] Restore invariant error for layouts

Keep decorated struct layout errors consistent with native handling and preserve the diagnostic message for debugging.

Co-authored-by: Wolfgang Grieskamp <wg@aptoslabs.com>

* [vm] Document layout cache invariant

Note cache must be scoped to a single traversal to preserve depth/cycle checking and avoid keeping cyclic layouts alive.

Co-authored-by: Wolfgang Grieskamp <wg@aptoslabs.com>

* Guarding use of cache by gas version

* [vm] Avoid cache key alloc when disabled

Only build the cache key when the local cache is enabled and
note the per-traversal cache scope at the entrypoint.

Co-authored-by: Wolfgang Grieskamp <wg@aptoslabs.com>

* [vm] Simplify runtime variant match

subject: [vm] Use Arc<MoveStructLayout> for shared struct layout caching (#18640) (#18694)
body:
* [vm] Use Arc<MoveStructLayout> for shared struct layout caching

Change MoveTypeLayout::Struct to hold Arc<MoveStructLayout> instead of
a plain MoveStructLayout. This enables the layout converter to cache
and share struct layouts within a single construction pass.

During layout construction in ty_layout_converter.rs, the same struct
type can be visited multiple times (e.g., enum variants sharing fields,
or the same generic instantiation in different positions). Previously,
each visit re-constructed the entire MoveStructLayout tree and
re-counted all its nodes toward the layout size limit, which was
wasteful and could cause spurious TOO_MANY_TYPE_NODES errors.

Now, a per-pass StructLayoutCache (HashMap keyed by StructNameIndex +
type args) stores Arc<MoveStructLayout> after first construction. On
cache hit, an Arc::clone() is returned with no re-construction or
re-counting. Depth is still checked on every visit to prevent stack
overflow.



* [vm] Restore invariant error for layouts

Keep decorated struct layout errors consistent with native handling and preserve the diagnostic message for debugging.



* [vm] Document layout cache invariant

Note cache must be scoped to a single traversal to preserve depth/cycle checking and avoid keeping cyclic layouts alive.



* Guarding use of cache by gas version

* [vm] Avoid cache key alloc when disabled

Only build the cache key when the local cache is enabled and
note the per-traversal cache scope at the entrypoint.



* [vm] Simplify runtime variant match

Handle runtime variant layouts via a direct match to avoid
an extra matches! guard and unreachable branch.

subject: [framework] Graceful reward tapering at APT supply cap
body:
Without this fix, when total APT supply reaches the 2.1B hard cap,
stake::distribute_rewards would abort on every epoch boundary, halting
consensus permanently.

This change makes rewards saturate to zero instead of aborting:

- optional_aggregator: add read_limit() to expose the overflow cap
- coin: add mint_headroom<CoinType>() view function returning
  (cap - current_supply), i.e. how many octas can still be minted
- stake::distribute_rewards: clamp the calculated reward to the
  available headroom before minting; if headroom is 0 the validator
  receives 0 rewards for that epoch and the epoch still advances

Behaviour at the cap:
  headroom > rewards  → full rewards paid (no change from today)
  headroom < rewards  → partial rewards paid (first validators in the
                         loop consume the remaining headroom; the rest
                         receive 0)
  headroom == 0       → all validators receive 0 rewards; chain runs
                         normally on fees only

https://claude.ai/code/session_01VbbLN9Qw1xXqjVQURvr2F4
rationale: The commit fixes a bug where reaching the hard supply cap caused stake::distribute_rewards to abort, halting consensus permanently. This denial‑of‑service condition is mitigated by clamping rewards to the remaining headroom, preventing the abort. The fix therefore addresses a security‑critical availability issue.

subject: [framework] Clamp storage refund mint at supply cap
body:
transaction_fee::mint_and_refund() calls coin::mint() in every
transaction epilogue when the storage refund exceeds the execution fee.
Without this fix, if total APT supply is at the hard cap (2.1B), the
coin::mint() call aborts, the epilogue fails, and the entire transaction
is rejected at the VM level -- which is far worse than the epoch-boundary
issue fixed for staking rewards.

Root cause: a storage refund is conceptually net-neutral (it returns
tokens that were burned when the storage fee was charged). However, if
staking rewards filled the supply headroom between the time the fee was
paid and the time the refund is claimed, no headroom remains and the
mint overflows.

Fix: apply the same headroom clamp as distribute_rewards. The refund
is capped at coin::mint_headroom<AptosCoin>(). In the rare case where
headroom < refund, the user receives a partial (or zero) refund rather
than the transaction aborting. The hard supply cap is never exceeded.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01VbbLN9Qw1xXqjVQURvr2F4
rationale: The commit clamps storage refund minting to the supply headroom, preventing an overflow abort when the total supply is at the hard cap. The pre‑fix behavior could be triggered by an attacker who fills the supply cap (e.g., via staking rewards) and then causes refunds, leading to transaction failures and a denial‑of‑service condition. This is a bug fix that addresses a security‑relevant availability issue.

subject: [framework] Replace aggregator cap with InflationBudget for APT supply cap
body:
Previous approach: hard limit in the supply aggregator blocked ALL minting
at 2.1B, including storage refunds and fee redistribution (restorative mints
that return previously-burned tokens). This forced defensive clamping in both
stake::distribute_rewards AND transaction_fee::mint_and_refund, and still
allowed edge cases where users could lose storage deposits.

New approach: enforce the cap only at the one true source of new APT --
stake::distribute_rewards -- via a dedicated InflationBudget resource.

Architecture:
  InflationBudget.remaining = MAX_APT_SUPPLY - genesis_supply  (set once at genesis end)
  Each epoch: remaining -= actual_rewards_minted

Mathematical invariant (holds unconditionally):
  supply = genesis_supply + total_rewards - net_burned
         ≤ genesis_supply + BUDGET          (rewards are capped at BUDGET)
         = MAX_APT_SUPPLY                   ✓
  where net_burned = total_burned - total_restored ≥ 0
  (you cannot refund/redistribute more than was burned first)

Consequences:
  - Storage refunds always succeed in full (no partial refund, no lost deposits)
  - Fee redistribution always succeeds (also net-neutral)
  - Only inflation tapers to zero as the cap is approached
  - No chain halt possible from any mint path
  - Aggregator reverts to parallelizable MAX_U128 limit (no hard aggregator abort)

Changes:
  aptos_coin: add InflationBudget resource + initialize_inflation_budget /
    consume_inflation_budget / inflation_budget_remaining API; switch back
    to initialize_with_parallelizable_supply (no aggregator cap)
  genesis: call initialize_inflation_budget after all genesis minting, before
    destroy_mint_cap
  stake::distribute_rewards: clamp rewards against inflation_budget_remaining()
    and call consume_inflation_budget(); remove coin::mint_headroom usage
  transaction_fee::mint_and_refund: remove clamp (provably unnecessary)

rationale: The commit replaces a hard supply cap that blocked all minting (including refunds) with an InflationBudget, fixing a bug where users could lose storage deposits and the chain could halt. This corrects incorrect behavior and prevents denial‑of‑service and fund loss, qualifying as a security fix.

subject: [vm] Charge randomness as a feature fee separate from gas
body:
Randomness transactions now pay a fixed APT fee (100,000 octas =
0.001 APT) that does not count toward the block gas limit, instead
of being charged as execution gas. This ensures randomness overhead
doesn't crowd out other transactions.

Introduces a "feature fee" category in the gas algebra — a separate
charging path (charge_feature_fee / feature_fee_used) extensible for
future feature fees (e.g., encrypted transactions). The fee is emitted
as a separate FeatureFee event gated on the EMIT_FEATURE_FEE feature
flag, keeping FeeStatement unchanged as a 5-field struct.

subject: [consensus][framework] Fix chunky DKG enable-feature: on_new_epoch + pipeline deadlock
body:
Two fixes for the enable-feature smoke test:

1. Framework: Add missing `chunky_dkg_config::on_new_epoch(framework)` call
   in `reconfiguration_with_dkg::finish()`. Without this, the chunky DKG
   config buffered via governance `set_for_next_epoch` was never applied.

2. Consensus pipeline: Break circular dependency in decryption pipeline when
   `decryption_enabled=true` but `secret_share_config=None` (bootstrapping
   epoch). The cycle was: has_rand_txns_fut -> prepare -> decrypt (waiting
   for secret_shared_key_rx from ordering) -> but ordering blocked on
   has_rand_txns_fut. Use `observer_enabled` flag to distinguish consensus
   nodes (return immediately) from observers (wait for key from leader).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change fixes a missing on_new_epoch call (behavioral bug) and, more importantly, breaks a circular dependency in the decryption pipeline that could deadlock consensus nodes during bootstrapping, leading to a denial‑of‑service condition.

subject: [framework] Fix division by zero in stake::update_stake_pool fee distribution
body:
Guard the fee apportionment division in `update_stake_pool` against a zero
denominator (`active + pending_inactive == 0`), matching the existing pattern in
`calculate_rewards_amount`.

The bug triggers when a validator with zero active and pending-inactive stake
has a pre-initialized `PendingTransactionFee` entry (aggregator value = 0).
Even though `fee_octa` is also 0, Move does not short-circuit `0 / 0` and
aborts.

In practice this surfaces as a flaky `test_large_total_stake` smoke test: the
local swarm defaults to `min_stake = 0`, so the newly-joined validator carries
zero stake. When the 4-second epoch expires naturally before the test's explicit
`reconfig()`, a second epoch transition calls `update_stake_pool` on the
now-active zero-stake validator and hits the division.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds a guard against division by zero in `update_stake_pool`, fixing a crash that occurs when a validator has zero active and pending-inactive stake. This crash can abort epoch transition logic, leading to a denial‑of‑service condition, thus constituting a security fix (availability impact).

subject: [framework] Fix division by zero in update_stake_pool
body:
`test_large_total_stake` is flaky because a natural epoch change can
activate a 0-stake validator before `force_end_epoch_test_only` runs.
When `update_stake_pool` then processes that validator, it divides by
`stake_active + stake_pending_inactive` which is 0, aborting a function
whose contract says it should never abort.

Guard the fee-split division against a zero denominator. When total
stake is 0 the split is irrelevant — `fee_pending_inactive` stays 0 and
the full `fee_octa` (itself 0 for a non-proposing validator) goes to
`fee_active`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds a guard against division by zero in update_stake_pool, fixing a crash that could be triggered when total stake is zero. An attacker who can cause a zero‑stake situation could force the function to abort, leading to a denial‑of‑service of epoch processing.

subject: [prover] Add proof blocks and lemmas to Move Specification Language (#18893)
body:
Extends MSL with `proof { ... }` blocks and `lemma` declarations that
guide the SMT solver through hard proofs.

Supported proof constructs:
- `assert expr` — assert an intermediate fact as a verification condition
- `assume [trusted] expr` — introduce a trusted assumption
- `let x = expr` — bind a name for use in subsequent statements
- `if (cond) { ... } else { ... }` — case split the proof
- `{ ... }` — scoped block (let bindings do not leak)
- `apply lemma(args)` — instantiate a lemma (assert requires, assume ensures)
- `forall x: T, ... {triggers} apply lemma(args)` — quantified lemma instantiation
- `calc(e1 == e2 <= e3 ...)` — calculational proof chain
- `post <stmt>` — defer statement to return point (where `result` is available)
- `split expr` — case-split on a bool or enum, generating separate
  verification variants for each possible value
- `spec lemma name(params) { requires ...; ensures ...; }` — standalone theorem

Proof tree flattening: the SpecTranslator now fully processes proof
blocks into flat `pre_proof`/`post_proof` vectors of `ProofAction`
(Assert/Assume/Split), handling path conditions, lemma expansion,
and pre/post routing. The Instrumenter simply iterates these vectors,
removing ~300 lines of tree-walking emission code.

`old()` is now allowed in post-context proof statements for `let`,
`apply`, and `forall...apply` (matching the existing `assert`/`if`
behavior), enabling `post apply lemma(old(x), x)` patterns.

`split expr` emits a Nop placeholder during instrumentation and records
the split expression. After instrumentation, the Nop is expanded into
multiple verification variants — one per case (2 for bool, N for an
enum with N variants). Each variant assumes the corresponding case.

Syntax: `spec lemma name(...)` at module level is a shorthand for
`spec module { lemma name(...) { ... } }`.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit introduces new proof language constructs and documentation for the Move Specification Language. It adds features and refactors spec handling but does not correct previously incorrect behavior nor address a security vulnerability.

* [prover] Reimplement state labels with mutation builtins and havoc+assume

Replaces the previous approach of tracking bytecode offsets and emitting
SaveMem instructions at specific program points to capture intermediate
memory snapshots, which was fragile and coupled spec interpretation to
bytecode layout.

The new approach introduces mutation builtins (publish, remove, update)
that explicitly model resource state transitions in spec expressions,
combined with a havoc+assume pattern in the Boogie backend. Instead of
saving memory at bytecode offsets, the backend havocs target memory and
constrains it via the mutation conditions.

  into pre/post/intermediate categories
- New spec mutation builtins (`publish`, `remove`, `update`) as
  first-class spec operations with Boogie translation
- Havoc+assume translation in Boogie replaces SaveMem-based intermediate
  state capture
- Simplified spec instrumentation by removing
  collect/emit_intermediate_saves
- Updated spec inference to emit mutation builtins
- Support across expression pipeline (simplifier, sourcifier, rewriter)
- Fixed variant field selection for enum types in spec context
- Added simplification rules for variant test expressions (negation

Add ConfigShadowV1 that runs chunky DKG alongside regular DKG but
forces epoch change after a configurable grace period if chunky DKG

safety net only fires when chunky DKG exceeds the grace period.

subject: [framework] chunky DKG stall recovery fixes
body:
Three related changes to the chunky DKG / randomness DKG stall
recovery flow:

1. Fix V2→V1 chunky-only-override recovery. When the chain wedges
   mid-reconfig (DKG done, chunky stuck) and operators apply
   chunky_dkg_override_seq_num to recover, V1's block prologue takes
   over. The lingering on-chain chunky session blocked the finalize
   check from ever calling finish(), so the epoch never advanced.
   Drop the stale chunky session from V1's try_start — V1 dispatch
   is the executor's signal that chunky is not running this attempt.

2. Enforce "at most one (Chunky)DKGStartEvent per epoch". Previously
   V1's try_start re-ran dkg::start(cur_epoch) after the override
   restart, emitting a second DKGStartEvent. It "worked" only because
   validator restart refreshed the DKG manager's in-memory state.
   Make dkg::start and chunky_dkg::start idempotent per epoch: skip
   overwrite + event emission if a session for dealer_epoch was
   already started (in_progress or last_completed). Move-Prover
   specs in dkg.spec.move / chunky_dkg.spec.move capture the
   idempotency postcondition.

3. Consolidate reconfig finalization. The decision "should we call
   finish()?" used to live in three places (chunky-off branch of
   finish_with_dkg_result, maybe_finish_reconfig_with_chunky_dkg, and
   try_complete_after_grace_period). Centralize into
   try_finalize_reconfig, and expose a mode-neutral
   try_advance_reconfig tick called from block_prologue_ext (V1) as
   well as block_prologue_ext_v2 (V2). Renamed from
   try_complete_after_grace_period. The V1 tick is what lets the
   V2→V1 recovery finalize without re-dealing DKG (dkg::start is
   now a no-op once DKG completed, so the tick is the only path to
   finish()).

Also document the two recovery paths in chunky_dkg_config_seqnum.move
and randomness_config_seqnum.move:
  - Governance force_end_epoch for "chain still alive, epoch stuck"
    (the common case).
  - Per-validator local seqnum override + sync_only halt for the
    rarer "consensus itself is broken" case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit fixes a stall in the DKG/chunky DKG recovery flow where a stale session prevented epoch finalization, causing the chain to wedge. This could be triggered by an attacker to halt progress, impacting availability, thus a security-relevant bug fix.

subject: [natives] Isolate rayon work on a dedicated pool
body:
Move natives that spawn rayon work (ark_ec MSM, pairing, multi-pairing)
currently run on the block-executor's par_exec pool. When the native
calls par_iter/collect, rayon pushes sub-tasks onto par_exec's deques
and wait_until work-steals other block-executor scope jobs onto the
same thread. Combined with writer-preferring RwLocks on per-txn
Scheduler state, this can close into a deadlock (observed in prod
thread dump).

Add a dedicated native-rayon pool sized from a new ExecutionConfig
field native_rayon_concurrency_level (default max(2, num_cpus/2)), and
a with_native_rayon helper that native callers use to hop onto it.
Wrap the rayon-calling sections of multi_scalar_mul_internal,
pairing_internal, and multi_pairing_internal. bulletproofs 4.0.0 has
no rayon dependency and is out of scope.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 56ff86ce1558cfff80f0e3dd11954567002cdcb4)
rationale: The commit isolates native rayon work onto a dedicated thread pool to prevent deadlocks observed in production when rayon tasks steal work from the block executor's pool. This fixes a bug that could cause the node to stall, constituting a denial‑of‑service vulnerability.

subject: chunky DKG stall recovery fixes (#19538)
body:
* [framework] chunky DKG stall recovery fixes

Three related changes to the chunky DKG / randomness DKG stall
recovery flow:

1. Fix V2→V1 chunky-only-override recovery. When the chain wedges
   mid-reconfig (DKG done, chunky stuck) and operators apply
   chunky_dkg_override_seq_num to recover, V1's block prologue takes
   over. The lingering on-chain chunky session blocked the finalize
   check from ever calling finish(), so the epoch never advanced.
   Drop the stale chunky session from V1's try_start — V1 dispatch
   is the executor's signal that chunky is not running this attempt.

2. Enforce "at most one (Chunky)DKGStartEvent per epoch". Previously
   V1's try_start re-ran dkg::start(cur_epoch) after the override
   restart, emitting a second DKGStartEvent. It "worked" only because
   validator restart refreshed the DKG manager's in-memory state.
   Make dkg::start and chunky_dkg::start idempotent per epoch: skip
   overwrite + event emission if a session for dealer_epoch was
   already started (in_progress or last_completed). Move-Prover
   specs in dkg.spec.move / chunky_dkg.spec.move capture the
   idempotency postcondition.

3. Consolidate reconfig finalization. The decision "should we call
   finish()?" used to live in three places (chunky-off branch of
   finish_with_dkg_result, maybe_finish_reconfig_with_chunky_dkg, and
   try_complete_after_grace_period). Centralize into
   try_finalize_reconfig, and expose a mode-neutral
   try_advance_reconfig tick called from block_prologue_ext (V1) as
   well as block_prologue_ext_v2 (V2). Renamed from
   try_complete_after_grace_period. The V1 tick is what lets the
   V2→V1 recovery finalize without re-dealing DKG (dkg::start is
   now a no-op once DKG completed, so the tick is the only path to
   finish()).

Also document the two recovery paths in chunky_dkg_config_seqnum.move
and randomness_config_seqnum.move:
  - Governance force_end_epoch for "chain still alive, epoch stuck"
    (the common case).
  - Per-validator local seqnum override + sync_only halt for the
    rarer "consensus itself is broken" case.

subject: [vm] Fix par_exec deadlock in with_native_rayon (#19615)
body:
`with_native_rayon` previously used `ThreadPool::install` to run MSM /
pairing work on the per-caller native pool. When the caller is a
`par_exec` rayon worker, `install`'s `wait_until` loop is cooperative:
while blocked on the native-pool latch, rayon keeps the caller busy by
stealing other jobs from its home pool onto it. Those stolen jobs can
then block on state the caller itself holds (e.g. a writer-preferring
per-txn RwLock that a sibling worker is waiting to upgrade), forming a
cycle through the caller and deadlocking block execution.

Switch the helper to `pool.spawn(op) + rx.recv()`. The `recv` is a real
OS park, so the caller leaves rayon's steal set entirely until `op`
finishes on the native pool. The 'static bounds are satisfied by
adding `move` at the three call sites; their inputs are owned locals.

Return `SafeNativeResult<R>` so the (unreachable) case of the native
worker disappearing surfaces as `InvariantViolation` instead of a
panic.

Includes a regression test that reproduces the old deadlock against a
sibling job waiting on a mutex the caller holds.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rationale: The commit fixes a deadlock in the VM's native rayon pool that could be triggered by crafted Move code, causing the VM to hang and making the node unavailable. This is a classic deadlock (CWE-833) leading to denial‑of‑service, thus a security‑relevant bug fix.

body:
Add a new bulk order placement API (v2) that supports repricing crossing orders
instead of discarding them. This feature helps market makers maintain liquidity
by collapsing crossing orders 1 tick away from the best price.

Key changes:
- Add BulkOrderRequest::V2 variant with reprice_crossing_orders flag
- Add BulkOrderPlaceResponse::Success_V2 to track repriced levels
- Implement repricing logic in bulk_order_utils that collapses crossing levels
- Add place_bulk_order_v2() API in market_bulk_order module
- Add comprehensive tests for repricing behavior
- Maintain backward compatibility with existing V1 API

Example: If best ask is 100 and MM sends bids at [101, 100, 95] with sizes [5, 10, 15],
the V2 API with reprice enabled will collapse the crossing bids (101, 100) into a single
bid at 99 (1 tick away) with size 15 (5+10), plus the original bid at 95 with size 15.

subject: [gas] Source BN254 Fr::one() cost from the correct param (#19686)
body:
Internal-wiring cleanup. No user-visible cost change.

Today, `crypto_algebra::one<Fr>()` on BN254 reads the BLS12-381
schedule param (`algebra.ark_bls12_381_fr_one`, ~7750 gas) instead
of the BN254 one. Users pay the right *amount* by accident — the
two ops have the same cost — but the bookkeeping crosses curves,
and `algebra.ark_bn254_fr_one` has correspondingly sat at 0 in the
schedule because no native ever read it.

This PR re-wires the native to the correct param and seeds the
new key with the same 7750. After activation, users see no cost
change; the schedule just stops lying about which param funds
which op.

Both edits are gas-version gated at RELEASE_V1_46 so pre-V46 nodes
remain bit-exact:

  - Schedule: rename to `algebra.ark_bn254_fr_one_v2` for >=V1_46,
    seeded at 7750. Pre-V46 keeps the original (zero-valued) key.
  - Native: charges `ALGEBRA_ARK_BN254_FR_ONE` for >=V1_46,
    `ALGEBRA_ARK_BLS12_381_FR_ONE` otherwise.

Activation requires governance to add the new key to the on-chain
gas schedule and bump the chain feature version to V1_46.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit corrects the gas schedule entry for BN254 Fr one from 0 to the proper cost and updates the native to use the correct param after V1_46. Previously the operation would have been free after the version bump, allowing an attacker to execute many such ops without paying gas, a potential DoS vector.

subject: [framework] Add epoch force-end watchdog config
body:
Introduce `EpochTimeoutConfig`, a governance-tunable on-chain resource
with `Option<u64> force_end_grace_period_secs`. When set, an in-progress
reconfiguration is force-finalized regardless of DKG / chunky DKG state

opts in.

subject: [smoke-test] Rewrite watchdog matrix per review feedback
body:
Drop the Class A/B/C internal taxonomy. Build one unified runner that
maps the matrix axes onto genesis configuration directly:

  - If prior randomness DKG = NotTriggered, genesis disables validator
    transactions AND randomness, so epoch 1 → 2 is a plain block_prologue
    sync reconfig with no DKG.
  - If prior chunky DKG = NotTriggered, genesis leaves chunky off and the
    ENCRYPTED_TRANSACTIONS feature off; chunky-on prior cases enable both.
  - Watchdog is *armed from genesis* via the new
    epoch_timeout_grace_period_secs_override field added to vm-genesis
    (plumbed through aptos-genesis config, lib, builder, mainnet, aptos
    CLI). Adds a corresponding initialize_with_grace_period helper in
    epoch_timeout_config.move.

Each test then publishes the on_chain_dice module while in epoch x-1,
arms failpoints for the prior outcomes, and runs ONE governance script
that buffers whichever features must flip on for epoch x (validator
transactions / randomness / chunky V1 / ENCRYPTED_TRANSACTIONS) and
calls aptos_governance::reconfigure. reconfigure auto-routes sync
(finish) vs async (try_start vs try_start_with_chunky_dkg) from the
*current* config — that gov-triggered reconfig IS the x-1 → x boundary.
No force_end_epoch.

Bumps epoch_duration_secs from 20 to 40 to give comfortable headroom
for the publish + governance work in epoch x-1.

rationale: The commit rewrites test watchdog matrix and adds a new configuration field for epoch timeout grace period. It is a refactor / test infrastructure change with no indication of correcting erroneous behavior, and no code changes suggesting a security vulnerability fix.

subject: [framework] Add epoch force-end watchdog config (#19813)
body:
* [framework] Add epoch force-end watchdog config

Introduce `EpochTimeoutConfig`, a governance-tunable on-chain resource
with `Option<u64> force_end_grace_period_secs`. When set, an in-progress
reconfiguration is force-finalized regardless of DKG / chunky DKG state
once `now >= reconfiguration_state::start_time_secs() + grace_period`
(equivalent to `epoch_start + epoch_interval + grace_period`).

This avoids the need for a framework upgrade to recover from a stuck
epoch — operators can react via governance instead. Disabled by default
at genesis; existing networks see no behavior change until governance
opts in.

The watchdog branch lives at the top of
`reconfiguration_with_dkg::try_finalize_reconfig` and emits a new
`ForceEndEpochEvent` for telemetry when it fires.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [smoke-test] Assert ForceEndEpochEvent in watchdog test

The previous test only asserted "epoch advanced" — which could mask a
regression where some other finalization path fires instead of the
watchdog. Scan transactions from before the governance change and
verify a `ForceEndEpochEvent` was emitted with `chunky_incomplete: true`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [framework] Make ForceEndEpochEvent an enum

Convert the event from a struct to a single-variant `V1` enum, matching
the modern pattern in `confidential_asset.move`. Move struct-layout
compatibility forbids adding fields to existing event structs in a
framework upgrade, so an enum gives us the option to add a V2 variant
later if we need additional fields (e.g., a `reason` discriminator if
other force-end triggers are added).

The on-chain event type tag is unchanged
(`0x1::reconfiguration_with_dkg::ForceEndEpochEvent`), so off-chain
subscribers don't need to change. The smoke test now also asserts
`__variant__ == "V1"` for completeness.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [framework] Reject zero grace period in epoch_timeout_config

A zero grace period would cause the watchdog to fire in the same block
prologue that triggers reconfig (since `now_us >= start_time_secs * 1e6`
holds immediately), bypassing DKG entirely on every epoch and breaking
randomness until corrected by governance. The natural mistake — using
`0` to mean "disabled" — would silently brick the chain's randomness.

Assert `grace_period_secs > 0` in `new_with_grace_period`; direct
governance scripts to use `new_disabled()` to turn the watchdog off.
Add a Move unit test asserting the zero case aborts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

  abort condition).

  in reconfiguration_with_dkg.spec.move so the prover sees the new

subject: [prover] Verifiable inline functions and inline higher-order functions (#20066)
body:
* [prover] Verifiable inline functions and inline higher-order functions

In verify mode, inline functions with explicitly given spec blocks are
compiled to bytecode and verified against their specs like regular functions;
`pragma verify = false` opts out. With `pragma opaque` they are additionally
retained (not expanded) at call sites, where the existing opaque machinery
applies their spec; without it, call sites expand the body as usual and the
function is verified standalone. The bytecode verifier is skipped in verify
mode, since generated code is only translated for the prover and may contain
constructs the VM rejects (e.g. closures capturing references).

Lambda arguments of retained calls are lifted; the lifted functions carry the
lambda's spec block and are verified against it, so behavioral predicates
(requires_of/aborts_of/ensures_of) assumed at call sites are proven rather
than trusted. Lambdas may capture immutable references and may modify
captured variables, directly or through field selections and index operations
(`x = e`, `s.x = e`, `v[i] = e`, `g(&mut s.x)`): the lifter converts the root
variable into a `&mut` capture, rewriting reads to dereferences and mutation
targets to go through the new parameter, and transfers the spec with
reference-typed parameter nodes.

At opaque call sites, spec instrumentation resolves the statically visible
closure construction, saves pre-state values of captured locations, havocs
the underlying locals on the success path, and rewrites behavioral predicates
to syntactic closures, merging captured post-state slots in parameter order
with those of non-captured `&mut` parameters; the Boogie backend translates
these via the per-function behavioral spec functions. The closure checker
restricts reference-capturing lambdas to direct arguments of retained calls,
and mutable aliasing between lambda captures and arguments of one call is
rejected. A converted capture is havoced as a whole; the lambda's spec frames
what is preserved.

Adds lambda spec inference via a new LambdaSpecInferenceProcessor
(--infer-lambda-specs, off by default, wired through the Aptos CLI),
running the existing WP-based analyzer on lifted lambdas with empty user
specs so behavioral predicates carry information at call sites instead of
degrading to trivial values; auto-enables SPEC_REWRITE_PURE_FUNS. Drops the
over-conservative closure-checker rule rejecting &mut-capturing closures
with copy -- Move's ability and borrow rules already keep them stack-
bounded. Adds an end-to-end test family modeled after vector::filter / map /
for_each / fold / for_each_mut (with opaque specs verifying standalone) and a
global-state variant, plus probes for the relaxed copy rule and each
inference shape.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [prover] Inline opaque HOFs: immutable captures, inference by default

A function type `|T|R` is opaque about whether its closure captured a
`&mut`, and the prover cannot soundly model writes through such an
implicit capture (`modifies_of<f> *` is intentionally unsupported), so
the construct is rejected: the lambda lifter rejects modifying a captured
variable, and the closure checker admits only immutable reference
captures as direct arguments of retained inline-opaque calls. The
`&mut`-capture machinery (lifter conversion, spec-instrumentation
captured-mut rewriting, Boogie backend pieces) is removed.

Lambda spec inference is now on by default (opt out with
`--no-infer-lambda-specs`): a lifted lambda with an empty user spec gets
`ensures`/`aborts_if` inferred so behavioral predicates carry information
at call sites instead of degrading to trivial values. Inference runs only
for lambdas selected for verification, so an unverified body cannot
contribute a trusted opaque spec.

At a retained inline-opaque call, a location must not be both mutated
through one argument and captured/referenced through another: the closure
model snapshots the captured location at call entry, while inline
expansion reads it at the callback after the sibling mutation. The
closure checker rejects this even when it is not a borrow conflict (the
`&mut` borrow may end before the read), keeping the prover model faithful
to the expanded program.

subject: [prover] Path-free prophecy reference model, now the default
body:
Represent mutable references in the Move Prover in the style of
RustHorn/Creusot prophecies instead of the WriteBack model. A mutable
reference is a (current, final) pair: the lender is eagerly set to a fresh
prophecy when the borrow is created, and the prophecy is resolved
(assume current == final) when the reference dies. This removes the need
for a statically known write-back path. The prophecy model is the default;
--path-refs (on the move-prover binary and the Aptos prove CLI) selects
the legacy WriteBack model.

Covers local-root, field-on-reference, vector-index, variant-field, table,
and global-root borrows; the inter-procedural boundary including opaque
calls; and closures with &mut parameters, including those produced by
lambda-lifting inline higher-order functions. Calls under a live global
borrow re-pin the borrowed resource slot after the call, since no
non-aborting callee can change an exclusively borrowed slot (the static
model gets this implicitly from its write-back ordering). The
instrumentation uses dedicated operations (ProphecyBorrow,
Resolve/ResolveReturn, ProphecyCommitGlobal, ProphecyRepin,
ProphecySyncCurrent/Final), each carrying its role in the type.

A reference binding ends -- and resolves -- at its live-range exit, at a
redefinition of its temp, or at the merged-exit move NormalizeExits
creates; that move is a final reborrow (a Creusot-style rename) which
inherits the prophecy, while every in-body &mut-to-&mut assignment
reborrows with a fresh one. In-code spec blocks and loop invariants
observe the current value of a borrowed lender through sync brackets
guarded by per-borrow-site path flags; a global lender syncs through the
borrow address saved at its site, immune to later reassignment of the
address local. Update invariants take their old() snapshots at the
BorrowGlobal sites of the committed reference -- the eager update makes
the borrow the mutation point -- with the relocated assertions guarded by
the same kind of path flags; ghost-variable updates relocate alike.

Data invariants over behavioral predicates must now be state-quantified
(forall S in *: S |~ ...); the free-state form is rejected with a compile
error. The lifted data-invariant axioms are completed so the quantified
form verifies: they are emitted for all output arities, and their body
translation supports pure spec functions and value-typed equality.
State-quantifier memory binders are derived from the same slot rule as
evaluator argument emission.

The move-prover unit suite runs under both models (default and the path
feature) sharing one baseline, owned by the default feature: the path
trial only verifies against it, also under baseline updating, so a model
divergence fails the trial instead of being masked. A per-test
// separate_baseline: path escapes the sharing where traces legitimately
differ. The framework (move-stdlib, aptos-stdlib, aptos-framework)
verifies under the default, with a side-by-side benchmark in
doc/dev/prophecies/. A &mut derived through a function value
(BorrowEdge::Invoke) is not yet supported and fails with a clear error.
See doc/dev/prophecies/prophecy_model.md for the design, its relation to
the literature, and the full list of limitations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit changes the Move prover's internal model for mutable references, a verification-time refactor with no functional change to runtime behavior. No bug fix or security impact is evident from the description, and the diff is unavailable to suggest otherwise.

subject: [consensus] Decouple encryption round from consensus round (#20065)
body:
* [consensus] Decouple encryption round from consensus round

Introduces a dense per-epoch encryption_round counter that increments
only on blocks producing a decryption key, so the trusted-setup capacity
no longer has to cover every consensus round (empty/timeout rounds no
longer waste capacity).

Move: new EncryptedBlockRound resource alongside PerBlockDecryptionKey,
bumped in decryption::on_new_block when a decryption key is present,
reset on epoch boundary in on_new_epoch.

Rust: OnchainEncryptedBlockRound mirror (OnChainConfig impl) read once
at epoch start / restart from the commit-root state view to seed the
in-memory counter. Within an epoch, encryption_round is propagated
purely via the parent decrypt-future chain — each block computes
parent.encryption_round + parent.produced_decryption_key().

DecryptionResult gains an encryption_round field; decrypt_encrypted_txns
takes parent_decrypt_fut and awaits it before computing the digest.
TrustedSetupExhausted check now compares the composed encryption_round
against num_rounds instead of block.round().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [consensus] Guard against execution windowing with decryption

Execution windowing and the dense decryption-round chain are not yet
verified to work together. With windowing, build_root seeds the chain
from the commit-root state but stamps the older window_root, and the
committed window blocks are re-pipelined on recovery; whether they
re-increment the round (overshoot) or pass through as no-key
(self-consistent) hinges on what feeds secret_shared_key_rx for
re-inserted committed blocks, which is untested. Until that path is
verified, fail fast at epoch start rather than risk a mid-epoch round
divergence across validators.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

subject: [consensus] Decouple encryption round from consensus round (#20065) (#20114)
body:
* [consensus] Decouple encryption round from consensus round

Introduces a dense per-epoch encryption_round counter that increments
only on blocks producing a decryption key, so the trusted-setup capacity
no longer has to cover every consensus round (empty/timeout rounds no
longer waste capacity).

Move: new EncryptedBlockRound resource alongside PerBlockDecryptionKey,
bumped in decryption::on_new_block when a decryption key is present,
reset on epoch boundary in on_new_epoch.

Rust: OnchainEncryptedBlockRound mirror (OnChainConfig impl) read once
at epoch start / restart from the commit-root state view to seed the
in-memory counter. Within an epoch, encryption_round is propagated
purely via the parent decrypt-future chain — each block computes
parent.encryption_round + parent.produced_decryption_key().

DecryptionResult gains an encryption_round field; decrypt_encrypted_txns
takes parent_decrypt_fut and awaits it before computing the digest.
TrustedSetupExhausted check now compares the composed encryption_round
against num_rounds instead of block.round().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [consensus] Guard against execution windowing with decryption

Execution windowing and the dense decryption-round chain are not yet
verified to work together. With windowing, build_root seeds the chain
from the commit-root state but stamps the older window_root, and the
committed window blocks are re-pipelined on recovery; whether they
re-increment the round (overshoot) or pass through as no-key
(self-consistent) hinges on what feeds secret_shared_key_rx for
re-inserted committed blocks, which is untested. Until that path is
verified, fail fast at epoch start rather than risk a mid-epoch round
divergence across validators.

subject: [prover] Per-granularity .bpl partitioning with parallel verification
body:
Adds an opt-in VerifyGranularity dimension (Shard / Module / Vc) orthogonal
to the existing --shards N control, plus a driver-managed worker pool that
runs up to proc_cores Boogie subprocesses concurrently for Module and Vc
modes. The Shard path is preserved bit-for-bit.

Motivation. With sharded mode the borderline-VC long tail is shared across
every procedure in the shard, and a single slow VC delays the rest of the
shard's procedures. Finer partitioning lets each .bpl be verified in
isolation and lets the prover run multiple .bpl files concurrently rather
than relying solely on Boogie's intra-process -vcsCores.

Architecture.
  * VerifyTargetSelector::{All, Shard{idx,total}, Module{module_id},
    Single{qid,variant}} replaces the older Option<usize> shard parameter
    on BoogieTranslator::new. is_verified dispatches in a four-arm match.
  * The driver in move-prover/src/lib.rs dispatches on
    BoogieOptions::granularity into drive_sharded / drive_per_module /
    drive_per_vc. Module / Vc modes generate .bpl files sequentially
    (codegen mutates the env extension and is not thread-safe) then verify
    in parallel via boogie_wrapper::run_boogies_parallel — a std::thread::
    scope worker pool sized by proc_cores. Results are returned in input
    order so diagnostics stay deterministic.
  * BoogieWrapper::analyze_subprocess_output is the env-touching half of
    the previous call_boogie_and_verify_output, called sequentially on the
    main thread for each captured raw output.
  * granularity != Shard with shards > 1 errors out before any verification
    starts.

Boogie thread management. In Module / Vc modes, -vcsCores is forced to 1.
Running proc_cores driver workers each with -vcsCores:proc_cores nests
parallelism to proc_cores^2 worker threads and empirically triggers Boogie/
.NET SIGSEGVs under contention. The driver pool is the single source of
parallelism in those modes.

Diagnostics. Every error message produced by analyze_subprocess_output and
call_boogie_and_verify_output is prefixed with the .bpl basename so module
/ VC mode failures map back without grepping logs. Inconclusive (timeout)
errors now include the Boogie procedure name and, when reverse-name lookup
succeeds, the Move-source-style 0xA::module::fun name. Boogie subprocess
crashes (non-zero exit, SIGSEGV) become non-fatal env diagnostics rather
than aborting the whole pool — the remaining .bpl files continue and all
failures are reported at the end.

Caveat. Per-VC mode pays prelude rendering N times where N is the verify-
target count; on small packages it is slower than sharded mode. Per-module
mode currently retains the package-wide MonoInfo (each .bpl carries axioms
for types it does not reference) and can be flaky on borderline VCs. The
follow-up per-.bpl axiom pruning addresses both — pruning narrows MonoInfo
to each .bpl's verify-target closure, predicted to give standalone-equiv-
alent fast deterministic behavior at framework scale. Composition with
this PR is the planned next step.

Framework. ProverOptions::granularity: Option<VerifyGranularity> with
OR-style merge from Prover.toml [backend]. Test harness supports
MVP_TEST_GRANULARITY={shard|module|vc}, MVP_TEST_CORES=N, MVP_TEST_DUMP=1.

Validated. move_framework_prover_tests (--granularity shard, default) at
172.94s — within historical baseline. move_stdlib_prover_tests under each
granularity: shard 17.58s, module 13.27s, vc 39.11s.
rationale: The commit introduces a new opt‑in verification granularity and parallel execution driver; it adds functionality rather than correcting previously incorrect behavior, and there is no indication of a security‑related defect being fixed.

subject: [prover] Per-module/VC pipeline rerun for content-equivalence with -f
body:
Module and VC granularity each emit one .bpl per partition, but without
intervention those .bpls are strictly weaker than what `move prove -f <module>`
produces: the single full-scope pipeline run computes a wider MonoInfo and
spec-instrumentation state than any one partition's verify targets need, and
the result is content drift that can flip verification outcomes (e.g. stake's
$1_stake_initialize_pending_transaction_fee$verify timed out under module mode
while passing under standalone -f).

Make per-module/VC mode rerun the bytecode pipeline per partition with the
primary-target set narrowed to that partition's source file. The model behaves
as if only that module were -f-targeted for the duration of the rerun, so the
emitted .bpl is byte-equivalent (modulo cosmetic auto-generated IDs) to what
standalone -f would produce.

Mechanism:
- `GlobalEnv::restrict_primary_targets_to(Some(file_ids))` (new) provides a
  non-destructive runtime override for `is_primary_target()`, mirroring the
  existing `treat_everything_as_target` pattern. `is_primary_target()` consults
  the override when set; the persistent `file_id_is_primary_target` is
  preserved.
- `drive_per_module` and `drive_per_vc` set the restriction per iteration,
  rerun `create_and_process_bytecode` to build a fresh `FunctionTargetsHolder`
  for that partition's .bpl, and clear the restriction after the loop. The
  per-module holders are threaded to phase-2 Boogie wrappers so output
  diagnostics are analyzed against the targets that actually produced each
  .bpl.
- `check_errors` is deferred to a single post-loop call so `report_diag`'s
  built-in Debug-fingerprint dedup collapses cross-rerun duplicate diagnostics
  (e.g. unused-invariant warnings emitted identically in every rerun).
- `VerifyTargetSelector` is lifted from `boogie-backend/bytecode_translator.rs`
  into a new `bytecode-pipeline/verify_target` module so the codegen filter and
  the broader pipeline can share one definition. `bytecode_translator.rs`
  re-exports it for existing callers.
- `mono_analysis::derive_for_selector` and the post-hoc env-extension swap in
  `generate_boogie_with_selector` are removed. They attempted to narrow
  MonoInfo after the full-scope pipeline ran, which was both unsound (it
  re-discovered cross-module references injected by spec instrumentation) and
  redundant once narrowing happens at pipeline level.

Cost: O(N_modules × pipeline) extra work. ~2s overhead on aptos-stdlib
(29 modules), ~40s on aptos-framework (~79 modules) — both dwarfed by
verification time.

Validated against aptos-stdlib and aptos-framework: per-module .bpl content
matches standalone `-f` modulo cosmetic IDs; verification outcomes are
deterministic where standalone is deterministic (math128/floor_log2's
pre-existing parallel-Boogie flakiness is unchanged and out of scope here).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit corrects the prover's per‑module/VC pipeline to eliminate content drift that caused inconsistent verification results. This is a tooling bug fix; the change does not address a vulnerability that could be exploited by an attacker.

subject: [execution] Decouple hot state root from TXN_INFO_V1
body:
`TRANSACTION_INFO_V1` previously controlled two things at once: whether
to assemble `TransactionInfoV1`, and whether that struct carried the hot
state root hash (committed to the ledger accumulator, i.e. consensus).

Introduce `HOT_STATE_ROOT_IN_TXN_INFO` (123) to separate them:

- `TRANSACTION_INFO_V1` alone now assembles `TransactionInfoV1` with
  `hot_state_checkpoint_hash` left `None`.
- `HOT_STATE_ROOT_IN_TXN_INFO` (requires `TRANSACTION_INFO_V1`)
  additionally populates the hot state root.

This allows enabling the V1 transaction info format without committing
the hot state root to consensus.

The V0/V1 decision in `do_ledger_update` is now keyed on
`ExecutionOutput::transaction_info_v1` directly rather than on the
presence of `hot_state_checkpoint_hashes`. Both the checkpoint-hash
computation and the chunk-replay re-derivation are gated on the new
flag so execution and replay stay consistent.

The `hot_state` smoke tests enable both flags, since their verification
oracle depends on the committed hot state root.

subject: [vm] Harden AIP-133 function reflection (#20147)
body:
* [vm] Harden AIP-133 function reflection

Address an audit of AIP-133 function reflection. reflect::resolve could
construct closures that bypass invariants the bytecode verifier enforces,
and some paths turned user input into VM invariant violations.

- event::emit: reflect::resolve refuses to resolve a list of forbidden
  functions (currently only 0x1::event::emit), returning FunctionNotAccessible.
  emit's call-site rules are enforced by the verifier (validate_emit_calls
  restricts it to the module defining the #[event] type) and cannot be upheld
  for a dynamically-resolved function value; modules emit their own events with
  a direct call.
- match_ty: reject binding a type parameter to a reference, so resolve
  returns FunctionIncompatibleType instead of an invariant violation.
- verify_function: reject expected function types whose abilities exceed
  PUBLIC_FUNCTIONS (e.g. key); a resolved public closure can never have them.
- object::exists_at: reject a non-struct type argument (e.g. a function type
  that declared the key ability) with a deterministic abort instead of
  letting it reach the data cache and trip a VM invariant violation.

Adds transactional PoC tests and e2e coverage that reflecting event::emit
is rejected.

contention on refund transactions.

subject: [vm] Function value storage format V2
body:
Function values were stored with a MoveTypeLayout written inline before
each captured argument (V1). This leaks a VM-internal representation
into storage and makes closure bytes non-canonical.

V2 stores captured arguments as a single opaque blob:

  [v2, module_id, fun_id, ty_args, mask, captured_blob]

Layouts are never stored; they are derived from the function signature
when the blob is decoded. In the VM, captured arguments are either
Serialized (bytes from storage) or Decoded (values). Reads of V1 and V2
both produce the serialized form when ENABLE_FUNCTION_DATA_FORMAT_V2
(127) is on, so V1 data upgrades to V2 on rewrite; with the flag off
behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. Reads of V2 are accepted
unconditionally except in from_bcs, where users could otherwise mint V2
data before the flag activates.

Captured arguments are decoded on demand: at closure calls, and during
equality/comparison/formatting via a ClosureMaterializer that loads the
function, derives layouts from its signature, decodes the blob and
charges gas (new closure_materialization gas params, gas version 55).
Equal function identity with equal blobs compares equal without
decoding.

The context-free MoveClosure keeps both formats (Decoded pairs for V1,
Blob for V2). The annotator decodes blobs using types resolved from the
function signature and falls back to raw bytes when the function is not
loadable; the API renders that fallback as __captured_blob__.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit fixes a bug where the Move VM stored type layout metadata inline with captured arguments, leaking internal VM representation into on‑chain storage. Exposing this internal layout can be considered an information disclosure vulnerability, and the change to an opaque blob removes that leakage. The message indicates the previous format was non‑canonical and could be abused, so the fix is both a bug fix and a security fix.

subject: [framework] Lazy module initialization support (#20235)
body:
Adds `aptos_framework::init` with `internal_maybe_initialize`, to be
invoked by compiler-injected code at module entry points. It marks the
calling module initialized and returns a signer for the module address,
which the caller passes to its initializer via a static local call;
returning the signer instead of dispatching a closure keeps the
initializer outside AIP-112's reentrancy resource lock.

The initialized module is determined by the VM from the caller's stack
frame via the new native `get_caller_address_and_module_id`, so a module
can only ever request initialization for itself; scripts abort. The
module id is an opaque hash of the module name, with the hashing charged
in gas like `std::hash::sha3_256`.

Initialization state is tracked per module id with an `only_once` flag:
`false` entries are reset on package upgrade so the initializer re-runs,
`true` entries survive upgrades and the flag is immutable once recorded.

A module published to an object lives at the object's address, and object
ownership is transferable and separable from the code, so object self-init
is gated on ownership: `code::publish_package` records the object's
transitive root owner per module at (re)publish, and self-init mints a
signer only while that owner is unchanged -- a transfer of the object or an
ancestor, or deletion, blocks it, and an object with no record is
fail-closed. Account addresses are not gated: publishing a module already
requires the account's signer. The feature is off by default, behind the
`LAZY_MODULE_INITIALIZATION` flag.

subject: [vm] Add charges for bcs value traversals
body:
bcs::to_bytes and bcs::serialized_size charged gas only per output byte,
but their real cost is proportional to the number of Value nodes in the
input: each call makes three O(node-count) passes (the read_ref deep copy,
the serialization, and the drop of the copy). BCS writes a Move struct as a
bare tuple, so a single-field wrapper struct is one node but zero output
bytes. A node-heavy, byte-light value could therefore be serialized in a
loop far more cheaply than the work it triggers, letting one compliant
transaction burn the whole execution-gas budget and stall block commit.

Charge CMP_COMPARE_BASE + CMP_COMPARE_PER_ABS_VAL_UNIT * value_size before
the deep copy, reusing the abstract-value-size dimension and constants that
cmp::compare already uses. Gated by a new timed feature MeterBcsByValueSize
so activation is a coordinated timestamp; replay is excluded so historical
gas is preserved.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit d3aab2582dff676eadda4ad07f83f50f59fe217b)
rationale: The commit adds gas charges proportional to the number of BCS value nodes, fixing a prior under‑charging that let an attacker craft a transaction with many nodes but few output bytes to exhaust the block's gas budget and stall block commitment, a classic resource‑exhaustion (DoS) issue.

subject: [move-prover] enumeration view for intrinsic maps (#20380)
body:
Map-traversal loops could not be proven functionally correct: the spec
vocabulary for intrinsic maps had no order-aware positions, so an aggregate
over a map was unstateable. This adds an enumeration view — key_at(m, i), the
i-th smallest key under cmp::compare, and rank(m, k), its inverse on contained
keys — so a loop invariant can index a traversal by position.

Model (native.bpl), per (impl, instance): uninterpreted $EnumKeyAt/$EnumRank
plus axioms for containment and rank inverting key_at, strict ascent under
cmp::compare where a cmp instantiation exists, rank-in-range, the removal and
insertion shifts, and rank preservation across a value write. All are guarded
by a well-formedness predicate $TableWf: Table admits cardinality-inconsistent
triples on which an in-range bijection cannot exist, so unguarded the axioms
are unsatisfiable for any finite key sort — containment would force $EncodeKey
surjective onto the integers. Emission is gated on the bindings and on non-bv
instances, so programs without the bindings get byte-identical Boogie.

Leaf walks get a third role, map_spec_leaf_offset(leaf, m): the number of keys
held by earlier leaves. That is what makes a leaf walk complete rather than
merely sound — each leaf holds the keys at offset .. offset + leaf size, and
the offsets tile 0 .. len — so the nested walk that for_each_ref expands into
can carry a position-indexed aggregate.

OrderedMap's iterator carries an index rather than a key, so iter_borrow_mut
could not be modeled at all; it produced "use of undeclared function:
$Update'...OrderedMap...'_entries". map_iter_borrow_mut now accepts an iterator
whose payload is a single integer field and resolves it through the
enumeration, which also required admitting an unparameterized iterator enum.
bv-flagged instances, where the enumeration is not rendered, fail loudly rather
than being modeled inconsistently: borrowing at an unconstrained key would let
the procedure abort where the map's abort predicate says it cannot.

Positions across mutation are stated positionally rather than through equality
with spec_set/spec_remove. $IsEqual on a ghost-bearing map is extensional, so
such an equality never yields the write term the axioms trigger on, and it is
in any case redundant with the containment and frame clauses already present.

Spec side: bindings and natives in both map files; rank clauses on
BigOrderedMap's iterator contracts; keys() bridged to the enumeration;
next_key/prev_key rank assumes; positional clauses on iter_modify and
iter_remove; and contracts for OrderedMap's iterator API, which had none — the
read path, all four mutation entry points, whose calls previously havocked the
map wholesale, and internal_lower_bound. mono_analysis validates the roles:
fixed signatures, spec native fun required, key_at and rank bound together, and
key_at required for a position-based borrow.

Tests: 43 #[verify_only] tests in big_ordered_map and 29 in ordered_map —
concrete ladders plus symbolic walks over while and for loops, including the
nested leaf walk — and 15 cells in the prover's own suite on self-declared
intrinsic maps. Every clause group was mutation-tested and carries an
ensures-false probe: a wrong positional clause on an opaque intrinsic-map
function makes callers' states inconsistent rather than merely weak, so
framework-wide vacuity detection (MVP_TEST_INCONSISTENCY=1) is part of the
gate. Validated with the framework prover batteries and the move-prover
functional and inference suites.

The for_each family remains unspecifiable at its call sites: those functions
are inline with function-typed parameters, so spec blocks on them are rejected,
and the inlined loop's header lives in framework text where a caller's
accumulator is out of scope. The hand-written equivalent is provable; closing
that gap needs a contracted non-inline fold rather than more axioms.

vec![1]) so the framework voting and governance tests, which assert
get_script_hash() matches their registered execution hash, behave
identically on both engines.

subject: [prover] Specification inference: diagnostics and soundness (#20470)
body:
* [prover] Specification inference: diagnostics and soundness

Weakest-precondition inference for Move specifications, separated from the Flow
and evaluation changes above it.

## Diagnostics

Inference reports per function instead of failing a whole run. A loop without an
invariant is named, along with what the bounded unrolling can see:

```
warning: WP inferred `vacuous` conditions after this loop without an invariant.
The loop havoc left part of the inferred condition unconstrained.
   ┌─ sources/spot.move:21:14
21 │         for (i in 0..ask_sizes.length()) {
   = source-visible loop-carried state: total, i
   = bounded loop-head facts (for paths reaching each head):
       head[1]: 0 < len(ask_sizes) ==> head[1].total == ask_sizes[0]
       head[2]: 1 < len(ask_sizes) ==> head[2].total == ask_sizes[0] + ask_sizes[1]
   = seek a predicate which includes the entry facts and is preserved by one
     back-edge; bounded observations are not an invariant or a proof
```

A timeout says why it timed out. The query is replayed under Z3 with
quantifier-instantiation profiling and the dominating definitions are named:

```
error: verification out of resources/timeout (timeout set to 40s)
  = timeout analysis replay: mixed quantifier and nonlinear arithmetic
    activity (117,101 observed quantifier instantiations)
  = top quantifier activity:
    InRangeVec<T>(v: Vec T, i: int): bool — 71,801+ instantiations
    $IsValid'u64'(v: int): bool — 31,861+ instantiations
```

Both are on by default. A timeout that reports only an exhausted budget is
nearly useless, and the replay costs one bounded solver run on a path that has
already failed; opt out with `--timeout-analysis=false`.

A partial abort result names which of its causes applied, and vacuous conditions
are dropped with a warning rather than written to source.

## Soundness

Ways an inferred contract could verify because its assumptions were
contradictory rather than because it held. All have regressions.

`aborts_of<f>` was translated as the literal `false` when `f` declared no
`aborts_if`, so a caller's `aborts_if aborts_of<f>(..)` became `assume false`.
A missing `aborts_if` means unspecified aborts, opaque or not, so the predicate
is now interpreted only from an exact source: the target's own `aborts_if`
clauses, or — for a concrete, non-opaque, non-native target — the abort
conditions the WP derives from its body, which never approximate. With neither
it stays uninterpreted, and everything else is still proven, modulo unknown
aborts. The derivation resolves a callee's aborts the way it already resolved a
callee's result values, and the memory those conditions read joins the
predicate's parameterization. Three framework helpers had to state what they
mean: `ristretto255`'s `point_clone_internal` and `point_decompress_internal`
do not abort, and `confidential_amount::compress_points` loops, which the
derivation does not describe.

The mutation predicates `publish`/`remove`/`update` had lost their whole-memory
frame, so a function with no `modifies` could mutate an unrelated address and
still verify. The frame is restated structurally, with the resource at the
target address pinned by `$IsEqual` so a mutable-borrow writeback still
verifies. This is also what makes a mutation predicate exact enough to define
an intermediate state label on its own.

An `aborts_if` naming the state between two opaque calls defines that label, and
the instrumenter established it by assuming the whole condition — which on the
success path asserts that the function aborted. Abort conditions are no longer
assumed there.

A behavioral predicate a loop invariant cannot resolve was replaced by `true` at
the occurrence, which under `!aborts_of<f>(..)` strengthens the invariant to
`false` instead of weakening it. The occurrence is marked instead, so the
conjunct-level weakening drops it — that is polarity-independent.

A struct field's data invariant was emitted for every function-typed parameter
of the same type as well, letting an invariant over a field establish
`!aborts_of<g>` for an unrelated parameter. It is emitted only for the field.

`object::spec_exists_at<T>` is declared without a body, so its declaration-level
`used_memory` could not carry the resource it reads and the pre-state label went
unsaved, producing Boogie which referenced an undeclared memory.

## Readability

Comparisons see through widening casts, abort clauses are read as the
disjunction they are and emitted simplest first, a scaled fraction is bounded by
its factor for `n <= d`, a guard tightens the range of what it compares, and
common-subexpression elimination can name a repeated guard. On the evaluation
corpus an inferred contract loses 15-41% of its characters.

## Also

Behavioral-predicate translation with Boogie declaration dedup; per-condition
diagnostic inspection; file names rendered relative to the working directory
when they lie beneath it; counterexamples that name the source entity of a
function value; variant selects dereferenced at the result type; `signer`'s
address accessors declared non-aborting, which WP needs to conclude anything
about a caller taking a signer.
