subject: MultiOffRamp - remove price update sequence number setter (#1073)
body:
## Motivation
Since merkle root and price updates are bundled together in one Commit
Report, they both share the same `sequenceNumber` that comes from the
`reportContext`. ~~Per OCR3, this `sequenceNumber` is monotonically
increasing, except in cases of config digest updates or issues with the
protocol.~~

~~The current OffRamp logic allows the same sequenceNumber to appear
more than once in a `Transmitted` event, which breaks the OCR3 spec.~~

## Solution
* ~~Enforce `sequenceNumber > latestSequenceNumber`~~ - this is by
design to allow out-of-order execution between a `t + 1` merkle root
report and a `t + 2` price update.
* Remove `setLatestSequenceNumber` function. Price updates can be done
manually in the worst case scenario. The sequence number reset can
already be done via the set OCR config flow.
rationale: The commit removes the sequenceNumber monotonicity check and the setLatestSequenceNumber function to align with OCR3 spec, fixing incorrect behavior. No evidence in the diff that the prior behavior posed a security vulnerability.

subject: [CCIP-2639] ccip capability launcher component (#1123)
body:
## Motivation

We need a component that consumes capability registry syncer updates and
launches CCIP oracles accordingly.

## Solution

Build a launcher component that implements the `registrysyncer.Launcher`
interface. The setup of the `launcher` package is as follows:

* bluegreen.go: defines structures that encapsulates ccip deployments,
i.e exec and commit oracles, and the blue/green deployment logic.
* diff.go: pure functions that diff registry states in order to
determine if there are any added, updated, or deleted dons that we
should care about.
* launcher.go: defines the `launcher` type which implements the
`registrysyncer.Launcher` interface. The `Launch` function is called by
the registry syncer whenever a new registry state is fetched. Note that
this registry state is not always different, we will most likely be
called with the same state more often than not, as the registry doesn't
change that often. It uses a handful of pure functions and applies state
updates only in a single function, `processDiff`.

On the contracts:
* Break out the types defined in `CCIPConfig.sol` into a separate
CCIPConfigTypes.sol which is then imported in CCIPConfig.sol and the OCR
config encoding interface, a helper used in tests.
* Use `Internal.OCRPluginType` instead of `PluginType` in order to be
consistent with the OCR3Base contracts that will be deployed on dests

subject: MultiOffRamp - family-agnostic messages (#1117)
body:
## Motivation
The Multi-OffRamp can be converted to be family agnostic by using more
generic `Any2EVM` structures and breaking the reliance on abi hashing

## Solution
* Remove `metadataHash` and use an implicit metadata hash composed of
`(prefix, srcChainSelector, destChainSelector, onRampAddress)`
* Convert `EVM2EVMMessage` to `Any2EVMRampMessage`, which uses a generic
`bytes sender`
* Decouple `messageId` from `hash(message)`
* Out-of-scope: EVM2Any OnRamp changes

Sample on why hashes between Any2X and X2Any are no longer equivalent:
```
Solana:
  - messageId: hash(Sol2AnyMessage msg)
  - (Sol2Any message could contain some extra fields that are SOL-specific)

Off-chain:
  - Sol2AnyMessage -> Any2AnyMessage -> Any2EVMMessage
  - Route SOL -> Ethereum

Ethereum:
  - messageId: hash(Any2EVMMessage msg)
  - (Any2EVMMessage will contain some EVM-specific fields, but not the SOL specific fields)

hash(Sol2AnyMessage) != hash(Any2EVMMessage)
```

---------

subject: MultiOnRamp - family-agnostic messages (#1140)
body:
## Motivation
* Converts the `EVM2EVMMultiOnRamp` to an `EVM2Any` family-agnostic ramp
to support non-EVM use-cases from a single multi-onramp.
* Collapses `sourceTokenData` + `tokenAmounts` into one
`RampTokenAmount` array (simplification to no longer require encoding /
decoding on-chain)

## Solution
* Message format changes: convert `EVM2EVMMessage` to
`EVM2AnyRampMessage`, which contains a more generic `receiver` target
and stores the family-specific args as bytes
* Note: `hash(Any2EVMRampMessage) != hash(EVM2AnyRampMessage)` - the
messages are now asymmetric
* Note: `EVM2AnyRampMessage.messageId = hash(EVM2AnyRampMessage)`, but
`messageId != hash(Any2EVMRampMessage)` due to the message asymmetry
* Add a `familyTag` to the dest chain config, to group multiple chains
under one family to perform validations
* Convert `extraArgs` to bytes, implement conditional flows to retrieve
EVM-specific fields
* Add `RampTokenAmount` which is constructed from
`Client.EVMTokenAmount` on the OnRamp. The struct unrolls
`SourceTokenData` and `EVMTokenAmount` into one struct, no longer
requiring additional decoding
* Out-of-scope: moving family-specific fee & validation logic to
`PriceRegistry` - to be done in next PR

## Motivation
In `CCIPConfig._validateConfig` we try to do an exhaustive amount of

1. Check whether a duplicate bootstrap P2P id, P2P id, signer, or
transmitter was passed in.

[CCIP-2595](https://smartcontract-it.atlassian.net/browse/CCIP-2595)

Created a library `SortedSetValidationUtil` in chainlink main-repo
https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink/pull/13774 to support

`CCIPConfigArraysValidation._ensureInRegistry`

index i both arrays can't be sorted at the same time.
Hence, we are going the enforce that p2pIds and bootstrapP2PIds are sent
sorted on function calls to in `CCIPConfig ` contract. This means that
these exhaustive checks for ` bytes[] signers` and ` bytes[]
transmitters` needs to be done in off-chain tooling.

subject: Family-agnostic ramps - refactor fee and family-specific logic to PriceRegistry (#1181)
body:
## Motivation
Lifts out family-specific fee & validation logic to the PriceRegistry -
isolating fees calculations to the PriceRegistry state. The refactor
converts the OnRamp to be fully dest-chain family agnostic - future
additions of chain families would typically require only changing the
PriceRegistry.

## Solution
* Move the `DestChainConfig` to the PriceRegistry, and completely remove
dest chain configs from the OnRamp. Since most of the dynamic config is
specific to fee & chain logic (with the exception of `maxDataBytes` /
`maxNumberOfTokens`), it is optimal to store the configs in a single
contract
* Moves all fee token configs to the PriceRegistry
* Removes duplicate `_validateMessage`. Since the Router always calls
`getFee` before `forwardFromRouter` - we can do the validations early in
`getFee`
* `PriceRegistry.getValidatedFee` - performs the previous `getFee` logic
* `PriceRegistry.getValidatedRampMessageParams` - performs the
chain-specific logic of `forwardFromRouter` - validating pool return
data, computing message fees and determining out-of-order exec

subject: Multi-Mechanism USDC Token Pools (#1280)
body:
## Motivation

Currently all USDC token transfers occur using Burn/Mint with calls to
Circle's CCTP system for cross-chain transfers. Certain chains in CCIP
have non-canonical USDC deployed and want to integrate the ability to
use CCIP as a canonical bridge whereby canonical-USDC is locked on the
source-chain and then minted on the destination chain. Then at a later
date, when circle decides to add that chain to CCTP, the non-canonical
USDC will be converted into canonical by burning the locked-tokens on
the source-chain. To accomplish this, the token pool needs to be capable
of identifying when tokens should be burned/minted with CCTP, or if they
should use regular lock-release, and act accordingly.

## Solution

`USDCTokenPool.sol` was been modified into a new file to allow for two
different mechanisms to be used simultaneously. The primary mechanism,
which is opt-out, and the secondary-mechanism which is opt in. These
mechanisms are configured on a per-chain-selector basis, and must be
manually enabled. In this implementation CCTP is the primary mechanism,
and Lock/Release is the alternative mechanism.

There are two new files
1. `HybridLockReleaseUSDCTokenPool.sol`, The actual implementation of
the hybrid pool structure.
3. `USDCBridgeMigrator.sol`, which contains the logic necessary to
conform to [Circle's migration policy
guide](https://github.com/circlefin/stablecoin-evm/blob/master/doc/bridged_USDC_standard.md#transferring-the-roles-to-circle)
rationale: The commit adds new contracts (HybridLockReleaseUSDCTokenPool, USDCBridgeMigrator) and associated tests, implementing a new hybrid mechanism for USDC token pools. It does not modify existing behavior to correct a defect, nor does it address any security vulnerability.

subject: Skip report execution on curse (#1408)
body:
## Motivation

The goal of this PR is to remove reverts on lane cursing for DON
execution transactions. If a lane is cursed, reverting will cause the
whole execution transaction to fail so any execution reports for other
lanes will be blocked.

## Solution

For DON execution transactions the behavior is now to skip the report
and emit a `SkippedReportExecution`. For manual execution we still
revert, otherwise the transaction will silently fail for the users.

---------

Co-authored-by: app-token-issuer-infra-releng[bot] <120227048+app-token-issuer-infra-releng[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>
rationale: The change stops a revert caused by a cursed lane from aborting the whole DON execution transaction, preventing a denial‑of‑service where an attacker could trigger a curse to block execution of other lanes. This fixes a bug and mitigates an availability issue.

body:
## Motivation

The goal of this PR is to implement a check to ensure that the OCR3
signature verification is enabled for the commit plugin on config. This
reduces misconfig risks and impact because previously an accidental
setting of `isSignatureVerificationEnabled=false` for the commit plugin
in the `OffRamp` would have required a redeploy to be fixed.

## Solution

Add a check enforcing `isSignatureVerificationEnabled=false` for the
commit plugin in `_afterOC3Config`.
rationale: The commit adds a runtime check in OffRamp's _afterOC3Config to enforce that the commit plugin's isSignatureVerificationEnabled flag cannot be false. Previously the contract could be mis‑configured with signature verification disabled, allowing unauthenticated commit messages to be processed, which could be exploited to steal or misdirect funds. Enforcing the check corrects this faulty behavior and mitigates the authentication bypass.

subject: GasLimitOverride for manuallyExecute (#1375)
body:
## Motivation
1. OffRamp should now use destExecData to extract the gas used for 
2. Manual execution should enable user to override the gas amount for
releaseOrMint per token.

## Solution
1. Removed int32 `maxTokenTransferGas` & `maxPoolReleaseOrMintGas` and
used the gas encoded in `RampTokenAmount.destExecData`
2. add a new Struct which holds the receiverExecutionGasLimit and
transferGasAmounts
```
struct GasLimitOverride {
    uint256 receiverExecutionGasLimit;
    uint256[] tokenGasOverrides;
}
```
tokenGasOverrides is an array of GasLimits to be used during the
relaseOrMint call for the specific tokenPool associated with token

Note: 
The gas limit can not be lowered as that could cause the message to
fail. If manual execution is done from an UNTOUCHED state and we would
allow lower gas limit, anyone could grief by executing the message with
lower gas limit than the DON would have used. This results in the
message being marked FAILURE and the DON would not attempt it with the
correct gas limit.

for the above we have kept a check that `tokenGasOverrides` < gas
encoded in `RampTokenAmount.destExecData`

---------

Signed-off-by: 0xsuryansh <suryansh.shrivastava@smartcontract.com>
Co-authored-by: app-token-issuer-infra-releng[bot] <120227048+app-token-issuer-infra-releng[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>
rationale: The change adds a GasLimitOverride struct and enforces that token gas overrides cannot be lower than the gas encoded in destExecData, preventing an attacker from manually executing with a reduced gas limit that would cause message failure and a denial‑of‑service. This corrects previous behavior where lower gas limits were allowed, constituting a bug fix with security impact.

subject: Hybrid Token Pools: Remove problematic liquidity functions and add incoming supply lock (#1396)
body:
## Motivation

Minor Changes to the HybridLockReleaseTokenPool to better meet Circle's
bridge requirements

1. Add additional supply lock on incoming messages when a proposal has
been created. I.E When a proposal for a chain selector is active, new
tokens cannot be released or locked to ensure better security control on
the destination-chain's token supply.
2. `withdrawLiquidity()` and `transferLiqudity()` have been removed to
avoid issues with the supply lock. Allowing for withdrawing liquidity
that has been provided would allow for the supply on the destination
chain to be greater than the locked amount on the source chain,
preventing a successful migration from occuring.

3. Comment fixes for invariants
rationale: [MEV] The commit removes withdrawLiquidity() and transferLiquidity() and adds a supply lock when a migration proposal is active, fixing a logic flaw where liquidity could be moved after a proposal, causing destination‑chain token supply to exceed the locked amount on the source chain. This defect could be exploited to tamper with token supply and disrupt migrations, so it is a security‑relevant bug fix.

subject: Make forwardFromRouter non reentrant (#1437)
body:
## Motivation
Currently the `OnRamp` performs 3 separate calls to the `FeeQuoter` on
the hot path, including 2 in the `forwardFromRouter` function:

1. `getValidatedFee`
2. `processMessageArgs`
3. `processPoolReturnData`

This is done to follow the CEI pattern and guard against reentrancy due
to the untrusted calls to the pools. This is not optimal for gas but it
also makes contract interactions more complex.

## Solution

Implement a non reentrant flag and reorder the `forwardFromRouter`
function layout. The calls to the pools are now performed first, relying
on the reentrancy protection. We reduce the `FeeQuoter` calls in
`forwardFromRouter` to a single `processMessageArgs` call.

## Notes

Optimizer runs had to be decreased due to contract size which is why gas
diffs are showing a gas increase. At equivalent runs diffs are:
```
test_ForwardFromRouterExtraArgsV2_Success() (gas: -65 (-0.045%))
test_ForwardFromRouterSuccessLegacyExtraArgs() (gas: -65 (-0.045%))
test_ForwardFromRouterSuccessCustomExtraArgs() (gas: -65 (-0.045%))
test_ForwardFromRouter_Success() (gas: -65 (-0.045%))
test_ForwardFromRouterSuccessEmptyExtraArgs() (gas: -66 (-0.046%))
test_ForwardFromRouterExtraArgsV2AllowOutOfOrderTrue_Success() (gas: -65 (-0.057%))
test_forwardFromRouter_WithValidation_Success() (gas: 318 (0.113%))
test_E2E_3MessagesMMultiOffRampSuccess_gas() (gas: -1139 (-0.074%))
```
rationale: The change adds a non‑reentrant guard to `forwardFromRouter` and reorders calls to pools before FeeQuoter interactions, fixing a reentrancy vulnerability that could have been exploited to manipulate token transfers and steal funds.

subject: Validate transmitter lengths against F values (#1432)
body:
## Motivation
Improves validations for OCR3 and CCIPConfig contracts

## Solution
Covers validations:
* `fChain <= F`, since `F` represents the full role DON
* Allows setting empty transmitters in CCIPConfig to allow
`len(transmitters) <= len(signers)`, while still enforcing
`len(transmitters) >= 3 * fChain + 1`
* Validates non-zero transmitters length in MultiOCR3
* Validates `len(signers) >= len(transmitters)` in MultiOCR3

### Tooling implications
* When setting OCR configs on OffRamp contracts, the list from
CCIPConfig must be filtered to exclude 0-bytes addresses. The reason for
this is that the MultiOCR3Base disallows zero addresses and duplicates
* Signer and transmitter duplication must be checked in tooling scripts
off-chain prior to setting CCIPConfig (otherwise it will result in
OffRamp breakage)
* `chainConfigs` must be set before OCR3 configs due to the added
`fChain == F` validation
* If `fChain` becomes higher than `F` after updates, existing OCR3
configs get invalidated without an on-chain check (since it is difficult
to do). There should be an off-chain validation script that prevents
this (first, F should be increased for all configs, only after which
fChain can be increased)
* `OffRamp` transmitters.length should be validated such that it meets
the `3 * fChain + 1` criteria off-chain, since `fChain` is not tracked
in the `OffRamp`


### Gas
| Function Name | min | avg | median | max | # calls |

|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------|--------|--------|---------|---------|
| validateConfig (without loop check) | 7040 | 20701 | 8436 | 122591 |
11 |
| validateConfig (with loop check) | 7040 | 21006 | 9132 | 123442 | 11 |
rationale: The diff adds strict validation of transmitter and signer lengths (e.g., enforcing fChain <= F, len(transmitters) >= 3*fChain+1, and signers >= transmitters). Previously these checks were missing, allowing misconfiguration that could reduce fault tolerance and enable a small set of malicious actors to control OCR3 consensus, a classic input validation security issue.

## Motivation
The goal of this PR is to standardize the message hashing functions.
Currently we have equivalent but inconsistent message hashing functions:
```solidity
function _hash(Any2EVMRampMessage memory original, bytes memory onRamp) internal pure returns (bytes32)
```
and 
```solidity
function _hash(EVM2AnyRampMessage memory original, bytes32 metadataHash) internal pure returns (bytes32)
```

## Solution
Standardize to `function _hash(message, metadataHash)` and consistently
encode dynamic fields.

subject: feat: add getter to return all source chain config (#1477)
body:
## Motivation
The current offchain initialization process involves calling
getSourceChainConfig(sourceChainSelector), which retrieves
configurations for a specific source chain selector. However, there's no
mechanism to fetch a complete list of supported source chains during the
initialization phase. This limitation complicates the process, as the
full list of source chain selectors is not readily available.

## Solution
To address this, the proposed solution introduces an enumerable set of
all source chain selectors. By implementing a getAllSourceChainConfig()
function, we can easily retrieve the complete list of source chains
on-chain. This eliminates the need for additional rounds of OCR gossip
to share known source chains, simplifying initialization and improving
efficiency.

---------

subject: ArbitrumValidator.sol - use .call to transfer value
rationale: The change replaces .transfer with Address.sendValue (call) to avoid transfer failures caused by gas stipend limits, fixing a situation where the contract could become unable to withdraw its balance, which is a denial‑of‑service availability issue.

subject: Updated Buffer library to v0.8 version
rationale: The change wraps arithmetic in `unchecked` to prevent overflow reverts in mask calculations. Previously, large `len` values could cause a Solidity 0.8 checked overflow, reverting the transaction and allowing an attacker to trigger a denial‑of‑service. Adding unchecked fixes the bug and mitigates the DoS risk.

subject: ArbitrumValidator.sol - add explicit config access modifier
rationale: The update adds non‑zero checks for gasPriceBid and maxGas, preventing an attacker with config access from setting them to zero and causing underpayment for L2 gas, which could lead to loss of funds. This is a bug fix that also mitigates a security issue.

subject: Add CBOR with bignum support for uint

This prevents malformed request data that could be supplied by an attacker to corrupt oracle payloads, a data‑integrity issue.

subject: [Functions] Separate event for invalid IDs (#8652)
body:
Emitting UserCallbackRawError when request ID was invalid had several issues:
1. It's not a user error - our contracts set the IDs.
2. OCR can sometimes send the same report twice (expected behavior). If we emit UserCallbackRawError on the second attempt, we cause observability issues (e.g. latency is calculated based on the last one instead of the first one).
3. Similarly - emitting this event causes seom problems in core node state transitions (unwanted and confusing error logs).

Apart from new event, I also cloned old interfaces into the testing dir, to avoid migrating changes in the future.
rationale: The change corrects the previous behavior where an invalid request ID caused a revert and emitted a generic UserCallbackRawError event. It now returns a specific enum and emits an InvalidRequestID event, fixing incorrect error handling and observability. The diff does not introduce or mitigate a security vulnerability.

subject: Split plugin service into multiple instances
body:
The primary focus of splitting into multiple instances is taking slices of the
total number of upkeep ids per instance such that there is no overlap. This
involves a change to the registry implementation to take the mod of an upkeep
id and determine if the remainder equals the instance id.

Each instance of the plugin requires a different registry instance. Futher
cleanup can be done to reduce resource usage, but the general idea should
function correctly.
rationale: The change fixes a bug where a single latestEpoch value was shared across multiple plugin instances, allowing a report from one instance to overwrite the epoch for others. This could be exploited to cause denial‑of‑service of upkeep execution, so the fix mitigates that security risk.

* Parallelize getUpkeepInfo (#9600)

Parallelize how we fetch upkeep information:

Extract a getUpkeepInfo function
Update getUpkeepInfo to accept a channel of uint16
Run 5 separate instances of getUpkeepInfo that each read from the same channel
Feed the channel with all the upkeep IDs we want to fetch info for
When getUpkeepInfo completes, send the info result into a results channel
When all the ids have been sent, close the id channel
This will cause each instance of getUpkeepInfo to terminate their loops and return
This unblocks the wait group
Read from the results channel and use the upkeep info as needed

subject: fix(contracts): inline isContract() call in EVM2EVMOffRamp (#471)
body:
## Motivation
Compiling the `EVM2EVMOffRamp` token implementation for
[TVM](https://developers.tron.network/v3.7/docs/virtual-machine-introduction)
fails with the following error:

```
TypeError: Member "isContract" not unique after argument-dependent lookup in address.
--> github/smartcontractkit/ccip/contracts/src/v0.8/ccip/offRamp/EVM2EVMOffRamp.sol:438:8:
    |
438 | !message.receiver.isContract() || !message.receiver.supportsInterface(type(IAny2EVMMessageReceiver).interfaceId)
    | ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

See https://github.com/tronprotocol/tronbox/issues/136 for more details.

## Solution

This change inlines the isContract() call to avoid ambiguity. Open
Zeppelin solves this issue similarly (see
https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/pull/3945/files).
rationale: The change only inlines an isContract() check to resolve a compilation ambiguity on TVM; it does not alter runtime logic or fix a security-relevant defect.

subject: [lock/unlock] feat: arb L1<->L2 bridge plugin support (#490)
body:
This PR implements off-chain bridging support for Arbitrum and for the
Mock Bridge being used in the integration tests. In order to properly
test this logic in the integration tests a lot of changes unfortunately
had to be made and this PR is quite big. This description aims to
summarize the changes on each part of the rebalancer codebase so far.

## Bridges
"Bridging support" in the context of the rebalancer plugin involves
mainly two things as of time of writing (and may potentially involve
more things in the future as we develop this plugin):

1. Determining transfer state: The plugin needs to know the state of
each pending transfer that was initiated using a bridge. Certain states
allow the plugin to perform certain actions. For example, a pending
transfer in the state "finalized" means that the plugin can instruct the
Rebalancer contract onchain to inject liquidity into the attached
liquidity container.
2. Determining bridge-specific arguments: Each "side" of the bridge
involves using different sets of arguments for many bridges, and
therefore bridges are directional - e.g L1 -> L2 and L2 -> L1 are
different bridge implementations. For example, for the L2 -> L1
direction, the bridge-specific arguments determined for finalizing
withdrawals on L1 are fundamentally different than finalizing transfers
in the L1 -> L2 direction.

The `Bridge` interface in
`core/services/ocr2/plugins/rebalancer/bridge/bridge.go` is the
interface that will be implemented for all bridge directions and chains
supported. See the interface for the exact methods, which have
descriptive comments.

### Arbitrum L1 <-> L2 Bridge Implementations

In this PR, the `Bridge` interface referenced above is implemented for
both directions of the Arbitrum One bridge, L1 -> L2 and L2 -> L1. Their
contents are mostly based off of the scripts merged in #480, so in
essence there is not much new here other than rejigging some things in
order to be able to properly implement the logic housed in those
scripts.

## Graphs and Discovery

Discovery of the graph of liquidities was tightly coupled to the EVM
implementation of the `Rebalancer` interface in the `liquiditymanager`
package, and this was causing issues for initializing the bridges, since
they also need to know a lot of information about the graph as well,
mainly the rebalancer and bridge adapter contract addresses.

As such, this PR factors out the discovery from `liquiditymanager` into
a new `discoverer` package. This package provides the `Discoverer`
interface which is able to discover rebalancers starting from a
master/root/main rebalancer contract and network.

Right now only an EVM implementation is provided, which will be
sufficient for our needs, but can be expanded in the future if there are
non-EVM rebalancers.

The `liquiditygraph` package was renamed to `graph` since it is now
housing much more than just liquidity data:

```golang
type XChainRebalancerData struct {
	RemoteRebalancerAddress   models.Address
	LocalBridgeAdapterAddress models.Address
	RemoteTokenAddress        models.Address
}

type Data struct {
	Liquidity         *big.Int
	TokenAddress      models.Address
	RebalancerAddress models.Address
	XChainRebalancers map[models.NetworkSelector]XChainRebalancerData
}
```

The data housed now closely mirrors what is on-chain, since pretty much
all of. this is needed in the off-chain components (e.g bridge
implementations).

## Rebalancing Algorithms

The `random` and `dummy` algorithms have been deleted to ease
maintenance burdens and only `pingpong` is now available and used within
tests.

## Plugin Logic

Plugin logic has been changed in order to account for fetching
bridge-specific data. The phases now operate as follows:

1. `Observation`: the plugin syncs the rebalancer graph, by doing a
discovery and updating the liquidities on each rebalancer. This behavior
was there before and is unchanged. *Additional behavior*: we check the
previous outcome and check if there are any _proposed transfers_ from
the committed outcome. These outcomes are then _resolved_ by using the
bridge implementations. See `resolveProposedTransfers` in
`core/services/ocr2/plugins/rebalancer/plugin.go` for more details.
2. `Outcome`: the plugin constructs an outcome by: (a) computing median
liquidity per-chain (b) computing the consensus graph of connections
between chains (c) consensus on pending transfers. This behavior was
there before and is unchanged. *Additional behavior*: we compute a
quorum on the _resolved transfers_ that have been sent as part of the
observation. This is similar to the pending transfers consensus but
involves a little more details. See `computeResolvedTransfersQuorum` in
`core/services/ocr2/plugins/rebalancer/plugin.go` for details.
3. `Reports`: the previous plugin logic here was actually buggy. In
order to make it clearer what this function is supposed to do the code
now determines _incoming_ and _outgoing_ transfers for each network.
_Incoming_ transfers are transfers that are meant to generate `Receive`
instructions in the report, and _outgoing_ transfers are transfers that
are meant to generate `Send` instructions in the report. See `Reports`
in `core/services/ocr2/plugins/rebalancer/plugin.go` for more details on
this.
4. `ShouldTransmitAcceptedReport`: check the sequence number that has
been transmitted onchain and compare it to the provided `seqNr`. If
`onchainSeqNr < seqNrArg` then we return `true`, otherwise we return
`false`.

subject: [lock/unlock] OP L1 finalization in bridge adapter (#606)
body:
## Motivation

The Optimism L1 bridge adapter needs to be able to both prove
withdrawals and finalize them on L1.

## Solution

* Add Optimism withdrawal proving and finalization on L1 functionality
to the bridge adapter. Tweak the scripts to prove and finalize
withdrawals through the adapters rather than on the Optimism contracts
directly to prove that they work.
* Fix a bug with ETH cross-chain transfers, on both L1 and L2 adapters:
since Optimism transfers ETH rather than WETH cross-chain through their
native bridge, stuff ends up reverting when we call `withdraw` on the
WETH contract prior to bridging.
* Fix a bug where we were using `withdrawTo` without actually sending
the ETH along with the call. The Optimism contracts dependency we're
using isn't bedrock so the `withdrawTo` function signature did not have
`payable`. Instead we copy/paste the `withdrawTo` function signature
directly from
[`L2StandardBridge.sol`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/f707883038d527cbf1e9f8ea513fe33255deadbc/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L2/L2StandardBridge.sol#L114-L122),
since we can't import it directly due to the exact 0.8.15 version
specified in the contract's pragma.

## Follow ups

* Direct follow up: support multiple-stage finalization in
Rebalancer.sol. Right now Rebalancer.sol assumes that a single
successful call to `finalizeWithdrawERC20` will give it access to funds,
however this is not the case for Optimism. This will be implemented in
an upcoming PR to keep diffs small and manageable.
* Future work: Explore the differences between `bridgeETHTo` and
`bridgeERC20To`, which are on `StandardBridge.sol`, vs. `depositERC20To`
and `withdrawTo` which are on L1StandardBridge.sol and
L2StandardBridge.sol respectively.
* Future work: Use contracts-bedrock imports instead of plain contracts.
rationale: The commit adds missing functionality (prove/finalize withdrawals) and corrects two bugs: ETH cross‑chain transfer handling and an incorrect non‑payable `withdrawTo` signature. These changes restore intended behavior but do not introduce or mitigate any security‑relevant checks, access controls, or value‑transfer safeguards.

subject: Permissionless token pools (#652)
body:
This PR is mainly focussed on the CCIP side of self serve token pools.
Some additional contracts had to be written/changed, but in review,
please focus on the CCIP & token pool side of self serve, not on the
TokenAdminRegistry.

Considerations

- Token pools are now considered hostile
  - This goes for both in- and output
  - Source side
    - Call to `sourcePool.lockOrBurn` from the onRamp
- Does not strictly have to be through a callWithExactGas call, as CCIP
is not paying for gas used here
      - Same for return data bomb
      - It returns the destPool and optional extraData
- DestPool has to be checked for length to mitigate the risk of return
data bombs through this field
- Since the onRamp is EVM2EVM, we can assume the address is an
abi.encoded(address) and therefore 32 bytes
        - ExtraData is checked like it was before
  - Dest side
    - We used to make a call to `getToken`
- Since this would be a hostile call, and require the full
callWithExactGas protection, we opted to fold this getter into the
`releaseOrMint` call. This saves a significant amount of gas, and makes
sure we only have to do a single call to the hostile contract.
    - We call `releaseOrMint` on the `pool` provided on the source side
- The pool data is considered hostile, as it came from an untrusted
source
- We need to ensure the address is valid and it contains a contract
      - The releaseOrMint call was already done through callWithExactGas

This brings the number of onchain calls to token pools to 2 per
transferred token: one on the source chain and one on the destination.
This is the absolute minimum possible.


Reviews for this PR should focus on

- Hostile token pool interactions
  - DoS
  - Unusual reverts
  - Gas bombs
  - Return data bombs
- The changes to CCIP and their impact on the security and availability
of the protocol

Please do not focus on

- The TokenAdminRegistry, except for things that would impact the
changed CCIP design

subject: Return dest denomimination token amount from pool (#762)
body:
This PR enables the destination chain pools to specify the amount that
was minted or released from the pool. Using this functionality, it is
possible to create token pools that support tokens with different
decimals on different chains. There are various ways to implement this,
for instance, using the token pool return data to encode the source
chain decimals or some shared decimal schema. A pool could also maintain
a full decimal mapping of all remote chains and do the calculations on
the remote chain.

We have also removed the duplicated check for the contract size of a
pool. Since `_callWithExactGasSafeReturnData` already does this check,
we only have to catch it in `_trialExecute` to safely remove the
duplicated check.


Due to the optimization in the check, the PR reduces gas usage while
adding the token pool functionality
rationale: The commit introduces a new feature to return destination-denominated token amounts and removes a duplicated contract size check; it does not correct previously incorrect behavior nor address a security vulnerability.

subject: Implement PriceRegistry price data feed fallback (#718)
body:
## Motivation
Currently, the Price Registry relies on periodic price updates on-chain,
which is expensive and grows significantly as the number of supported
tokens grow. Instead, we can utilise price data feeds when they are
available on chain to significantly save on gas costs.

## Solution
Add ability to set data feeds per-token for the owner, which are then
used if available instead of the price mapping.

* Assumption: once a feed is set - we no longer need the fixed price -
so it is removed for gas cost savings
* Assumption: the same staleness threshold can be used for both data
feeds + manual token mappings
* Assumption: the `_getTokenPriceFromDataFeed` values will not underflow
on division if excessDecimals exceeds 36
rationale: The commit introduces a new feature (price feed fallback) to reduce gas costs and does not correct previously incorrect behavior. No security vulnerability is being patched; the change is not presented as a fix to a security issue.

subject: pass token into lockOrBurn (#913)
body:
## Motivation
To add defence in depth, we pass the token to be locked/burned into the
pool so it is able to validate the token is supported by the pool.

## Solution
Passing in the token also enables creating a token pool which supports
multiple tokens. To ensure the correct destination token is minted, the
pool should return the source/dest token in the extraData. This can then
be read by the dest pool.

We check for `isSupportedToken` during the setting of a pool for a
token. This reduces the odds of a misconfiguration and closes some
potential exploit pathways.

The PR also makes all pool IO checks consistent by adding helpers for
lockOrBurn and ReleaseOrMint.

Optimizations for the onRamp had to be lowered a bit due to the extra
arguments used.
rationale: The change adds the token parameter to lockOrBurn/releaseOrMint and validates it with isSupportedToken, fixing a missing input validation that could allow misconfiguration and unauthorized token locking/burning, which is a security-relevant defect.

subject: MultiAggregateRateLimiter - validation based contract with OffRamp implementation (#916)
body:
## Motivation
Re-designs the usage of the aggregate rate limiter, with a focus on the
OffRamp. The main motivations are:

* reduction of contract size in the OffRamp (and in next PR - for the
OnRamp) - from 24.79KB to 20.32KB
* increased flexibility & decoupling for message validations, allowing
to perform more than just rate limit checks
* ability to more easily control opt-in validations, with an easy way to
globally disable them

## Solution
The solution consists of multiple parts:
* `IMessageValidator`: an interface for hook contracts that can be
plugged into OffRamps/OnRamps to validate messages. The validation
functions revert if the validation criteria are not met
* `MultiAggregateRateLimiter`: the `AggregateRateLimiter` contract, but
converted to support multiple chains, with rate-limit specific logic
pulled in from the OffRamp. The contract now implements the
`IMessageValidator` interface
* `MultiOffRamp`: allows configuring an optional `IMessageValidator`,
which can perform any validation (in this case, we could set it to a
`MultiAggregateRateLimiter` contract)
* (removed) ~~`RateLimiterNoEvents`: the `RateLimiter` library converted
to exclude events (since they should now be per-chain). It was not
converted to a `RateLimiterMultiChain` to maintain the simplicity of the
library (since it should only act as a token bucket)~~

### Design choices
* `validateIncomingMessage` does not batch messages. The reason for this
is:
* To preserve generic chain inputs `Any2EVM`. Passing a batch of
`Any2EVM` messages requires more complex refactoring since we only have
`EVM2EVM` messages, which only get converted in `executeSingleMessage`
* Batching multiple messages would mean that rate limiting could fail
all messages, as opposed to treating them as isolated messages and
succeeding a large batch (e.g. in the current approach, the rate limit
could fail 1 out of 3 messages, but the other 2 would succeed. In
batching, this would not be the case)
* The logic is more in line with the previous `releaseOrMint` logic,
which treats each message as a single isolated unit
* Note that the main drawback is the gas cost - we are making multiple
external calls in this case
* A single `MultiAggregateRateLimiter` / `IMessageValidator` contract
should be used by both the OnRamp and the OffRamp, ~~which means that
the rate limiting state is shared~~
* (this is now separated per-lane) ~~We do not make a distinction of
lane `src -> dest` and `dest -> src`~~
* **All** `IMessageValidator` get caught by the validations in the
ramps. The reason is simplicity - unexpected failures should not trigger
unexpected bubbling reverts, and with this approach we do not need to
handle each specific validation error
* The message validator is expected to be shared by all lanes in a
single multi-ramp contract

### Out of scope for this PR
* OnRamp handling and on-ramp specific configurations in
`MultiAggregateRateLimiter`
* Message batching `MultiARL` / `IMessageValidator` (passing an array
instead of a single message)
* Considerations on whether the `MultiARL` should be per-lane or global
* (the expected behaviour is to not reset the ARL state on lane
re-deployments) ~~Multi-ARL state resets on re-deployment for a lane~~

rationale: The commit introduces a new MultiAggregateRateLimiter contract and refactors OffRamp to use a pluggable IMessageValidator. It is a feature/architectural change, not a correction of previously incorrect behavior, and the diff shows no security‑related bug being fixed.

subject: Let tokens hop through the offRamp (#962)
body:
## Solution
To ensure the end user gets the exact tokens they expect, we add an
extra hop through a trusted contract. Since token pools will be
considered hostile in the self-serve world, they cannot be trusted to
release the correct number of tokens, or even the correct token.

The offRamp functions as the trusted "hop" for all token releases, which
means that unless the token itself is malicious and simply doesn't
transfer when the offRamp calls the function, it should either revert or
deliver the exact number of tokens.


Other changes

- The mock usdc messenger now properly sends USDC to the receiver
  - This validates the correct mint privileges are supplies
- The offchain test doesn't appear to pass in the correct receiver of
this USDC, so we had to supply the USDC pool with funds manually. This
is not a downgrade of the test: previously no tokens were emitted or
ever sent to the receiver. In the new scenario the receiver gets the
correct number of tokens.
rationale: The commit changes token release flow to route through a trusted offRamp, fixing a defect where hostile token pools could release incorrect amounts or wrong tokens, which could lead to fund loss. This is a behavior change addressing a security issue.

defining a custom error for each error

`setOCR3Configs`

Since merkle root and price updates are bundled together in one Commit
Report, they both share the same `sequenceNumber` that comes from the
`reportContext`. ~~Per OCR3, this `sequenceNumber` is monotonically
increasing, except in cases of config digest updates or issues with the
protocol.~~

more than once in a `Transmitted` event, which breaks the OCR3 spec.~~

## Solution
* ~~Enforce `sequenceNumber > latestSequenceNumber`~~ - this is by
design to allow out-of-order execution between a `t + 1` merkle root
report and a `t + 2` price update.
* Remove `setLatestSequenceNumber` function. Price updates can be done
manually in the worst case scenario. The sequence number reset can
already be done via the set OCR config flow.
rationale: [MEV] The commit removes the setLatestSequenceNumber function and related enforcement, eliminating the ability for an actor to reset the sequence number nonce. subject: MultiOffRamp - family-agnostic messages (#1117)
body:
## Motivation
The Multi-OffRamp can be converted to be family agnostic by using more
generic `Any2EVM` structures and breaking the reliance on abi hashing

## Solution
* Remove `metadataHash` and use an implicit metadata hash composed of
`(prefix, srcChainSelector, destChainSelector, onRampAddress)`
* Convert `EVM2EVMMessage` to `Any2EVMRampMessage`, which uses a generic
`bytes sender`
* Decouple `messageId` from `hash(message)`
* Out-of-scope: EVM2Any OnRamp changes

Sample on why hashes between Any2X and X2Any are no longer equivalent:
```
Solana:
  - messageId: hash(Sol2AnyMessage msg)
  - (Sol2Any message could contain some extra fields that are SOL-specific)

Off-chain:
  - Sol2AnyMessage -> Any2AnyMessage -> Any2EVMMessage
  - Route SOL -> Ethereum

Ethereum:
  - messageId: hash(Any2EVMMessage msg)
  - (Any2EVMMessage will contain some EVM-specific fields, but not the SOL specific fields)

hash(Sol2AnyMessage) != hash(Any2EVMMessage)
```

---------

rationale: The change refactors MultiOffRamp to use generic Any2EVM structures and removes metadataHash, but does not correct erroneous behavior; it adds new functionality without fixing a defect, and no security-relevant issue is evident in the diff.

## Motivation

to support non-EVM use-cases from a single multi-onramp.

decoding on-chain)

`EVM2AnyRampMessage`, which contains a more generic `receiver` target

under one family to perform validations
* Convert `extraArgs` to bytes, implement conditional flows to retrieve
EVM-specific fields
* Add `RampTokenAmount` which is constructed from
`Client.EVMTokenAmount` on the OnRamp. The struct unrolls
`SourceTokenData` and `EVMTokenAmount` into one struct, no longer
requiring additional decoding

subject: feat: CCIPConfig, adding exhaustive checks for p2pIds and bootstrapP2PIds  (#1178)
body:
## Motivation
In `CCIPConfig._validateConfig` we try to do an exhaustive amount of
validations,
the following validations remained
1. Check whether a duplicate bootstrap P2P id, P2P id, signer, or
transmitter was passed in.
2. Check that p2p ids in cfg.bootstrapP2PIds are included in cfg.p2pIds

Ticket
[CCIP-2595](https://smartcontract-it.atlassian.net/browse/CCIP-2595)
## Solution
Created a library `SortedSetValidationUtil` in chainlink main-repo
https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink/pull/13774 to support
these sort, duplicate and subset check in `CCIPConfig`.
These changes are cherry-picked
This library can also be used in the optimisation of
`CCIPConfigArraysValidation._ensureInRegistry`

Regarding 1 : Since each p2pId at index i corresponds to the signer at
index i both arrays can't be sorted at the same time.
Hence, we are going the enforce that p2pIds and bootstrapP2PIds are sent
sorted on function calls to in `CCIPConfig ` contract. This means that
these exhaustive checks for ` bytes[] signers` and ` bytes[]
transmitters` needs to be done in off-chain tooling.


[CCIP-2595]:
https://smartcontract-it.atlassian.net/browse/CCIP-2595?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

subject: Family-agnostic ramps - refactor fee and family-specific logic to PriceRegistry (#1181)
body:
## Motivation
Lifts out family-specific fee & validation logic to the PriceRegistry -
isolating fees calculations to the PriceRegistry state. The refactor
converts the OnRamp to be fully dest-chain family agnostic - future
additions of chain families would typically require only changing the
PriceRegistry.

## Solution
* Move the `DestChainConfig` to the PriceRegistry, and completely remove
dest chain configs from the OnRamp. Since most of the dynamic config is
specific to fee & chain logic (with the exception of `maxDataBytes` /
`maxNumberOfTokens`), it is optimal to store the configs in a single
contract
* Moves all fee token configs to the PriceRegistry
* Removes duplicate `_validateMessage`. Since the Router always calls
`getFee` before `forwardFromRouter` - we can do the validations early in
`getFee`
* `PriceRegistry.getValidatedFee` - performs the previous `getFee` logic
* `PriceRegistry.getValidatedRampMessageParams` - performs the
chain-specific logic of `forwardFromRouter` - validating pool return
data, computing message fees and determining out-of-order exec

subject: Manual-execute-gas-overrides (#1256)
body:
currently, gas amounts are placed in the SourceTokenData. However, for
the multi-ramps, the token data should be chain-family agnostic, which
will likely require the destGasAmount lift to another field

- add a new Struct which holds the receiverExecutionGasLimit and
transferGasAmounts

```js
struct GasLimitOverride {
    uint256 receiverExecutionGasLimit;
    uint256[] tokenGasOverrides;
}
```

- `tokenGasOverrides` is an array of GasLimits to be used during the

    s_rateLimitedTokensLocalToRemote;

library cherrypicked from chainlink repo `EnumerableMapBytes32`

subject: Multi-Mechanism USDC Token Pools (#1280)
body:
## Motivation

Currently all USDC token transfers occur using Burn/Mint with calls to
Circle's CCTP system for cross-chain transfers. Certain chains in CCIP
have non-canonical USDC deployed and want to integrate the ability to
use CCIP as a canonical bridge whereby canonical-USDC is locked on the
source-chain and then minted on the destination chain. Then at a later
date, when circle decides to add that chain to CCTP, the non-canonical
USDC will be converted into canonical by burning the locked-tokens on
the source-chain. To accomplish this, the token pool needs to be capable
of identifying when tokens should be burned/minted with CCTP, or if they
should use regular lock-release, and act accordingly.

## Solution

`USDCTokenPool.sol` was been modified into a new file to allow for two
different mechanisms to be used simultaneously. The primary mechanism,
which is opt-out, and the secondary-mechanism which is opt in. These
mechanisms are configured on a per-chain-selector basis, and must be
manually enabled. In this implementation CCTP is the primary mechanism,
and Lock/Release is the alternative mechanism.

There are two new files
1. `HybridLockReleaseUSDCTokenPool.sol`, The actual implementation of
the hybrid pool structure.
3. `USDCBridgeMigrator.sol`, which contains the logic necessary to
conform to [Circle's migration policy
guide](https://github.com/circlefin/stablecoin-evm/blob/master/doc/bridged_USDC_standard.md#transferring-the-roles-to-circle)
rationale: The commit adds new hybrid USDC token pool contracts and related tests, implementing a new feature rather than correcting existing faulty behavior. No bug fix or security vulnerability mitigation is evident in the diff.

## Motivation

The goal of this PR is to remove reverts on lane cursing for DON
execution transactions. If a lane is cursed, reverting will cause the
whole execution transaction to fail so any execution reports for other
lanes will be blocked.

## Solution

For DON execution transactions the behavior is now to skip the report
and emit a `SkippedReportExecution`. For manual execution we still
revert, otherwise the transaction will silently fail for the users.

## Motivation
The current offchain initialization process involves calling
getSourceChainConfig(sourceChainSelector), which retrieves
configurations for a specific source chain selector. However, there's no
mechanism to fetch a complete list of supported source chains during the
initialization phase. This limitation complicates the process, as the
full list of source chain selectors is not readily available.

## Solution
To address this, the proposed solution introduces an enumerable set of
all source chain selectors. By implementing a getAllSourceChainConfig()
function, we can easily retrieve the complete list of source chains
on-chain. This eliminates the need for additional rounds of OCR gossip
to share known source chains, simplifying initialization and improving
efficiency.

subject: Support aliases for contracts in `relations.json` (#53)
body:
This PR adds an optional rule to relations.json called alias. This rule is used to derive the key that is assigned to a contract in pointers.json. If this rule is not provided, the contract name will be used as the alias instead. This rule has two special characters: @ and +.

@ followed by a function name is used to read a value from that contract's function. + is used as a delimiter.

Example: @symbol+Delegator will equate to cDaiDelegator for cDai's delegator contract.

Other changes in this PR:

* Move alias logic from standalone Spider script to DeploymentManager
* Add a new type to DeploymentManager called AliasesMap to keep track of all the aliases for an address
* Delete standalone Spider script
* Support writeToDisk option for Spider that writes a pointers.json file to cache

WIP: Run Spider on Development (#88)

* WIP: Run Spider on Development

This patch adds support for effectively running spider on development. We increase support for running Deployment Manager without hitting disk (cache is just stored in memory), and for development, we make sure that all deploys write the information that would have been spidered. Thus, when we run "spider" on development, it should have all of the necessarily build artifacts already loaded. This should hopefully help unify how we look at deployment management, such that development is not full of one-off deviations. We're currently fighting getting the hardhat build artifacts to align with traditional solc artifacts, but overall, this patch should be close to working. The idea in a nutshell is:

* If you deploy from `npx hardhat node && yarn deploy --network development`
* Or: `yarn deploy --network goerli`
* Or: `yarn sceanrio --bases development`
* Or: `yarn sceanrio --bases goerli`

In each of those cases, we should always be getting and pulling configuration from the spider metadata. In the cases of development, it will be put there after running `scripts/deploy-comet.ts` (to disk for a hardhat node and just in memory for a development scenario). In the cases of goerli, it should come from remote. There's some middle ground that will need to be decided (e.g. deployments in a scenario to goerli should also pull from memory).

So, all-in-all, this patch is attempting to unify the many ways to get deployment data, via spider, in cases where things might truly come from Etherscan or otherwise in cases where we push to that cache ourselves on deploy.

 c. We inconsistently used ES6 Maps. We often did a = new Map(); a[key] = value, which is pretty wrong, and then later did JSON.serialize(a). subject: Refactor of Deployment Manager
body:
Deployment Manager was born out of the idea that spider was crucial to the scenarios system. That is, after you spider, you should have access to then read those contracts. When you deploy contracts, they should be stored similar to how spider might crawl them. But this led to a concern that DeploymentManager was picking up a large amount of state that it handled inconsistently.

This patch reworks Deployment Manager such that it uses a single clean state object "cache" that is a read-through, write-though cache. That is, basically, it stores things in memory as it reads and writes from disk to make it fast, but if it didn't, it would work the same, just slower. This makes a convenient-use module that is used for scenarios and other tasks.

We refactored Deployment Manager sub-areas as modules with clean exported functions, which now have unit tests. This allows us to cleanly understand the behavior of say "spider" through a variety of configurations.

We refactor Relations.json to now be part of the TypeScript Hardhat config. This is 1) to gain the benefit of type-checking on the file, which was becoming more complex, and 2) to allow us to use small amounts of JavaScript for things like "how do I read the asset list from a Comet contract?."

We refactored Spider's use of aliases. Specifically, when looking for more contracts (the branch out "discovery" part of spider), we now mark those discovered contracts with the alias from the parent (e.g. Comet might say that its assets should be aliased by their ERC-20 symbol). We then allow the user to specify the configuration for those contracts via the alias or the contract name. So we could say that "DAI" has a special spider configuration and/or that "FiatTokenProxy" (USDC) does. This should allow us better diversity in handling different real-world situations, and is particularly well-suited for the current spidering of Comet.

We refactor Proxies to be `alias -> proxy address` from `address -> proxy address` since aliases.json already contains the link `alias -> address` and it should be eaiser for a human to read what this means.

Overall, this code should be significantly better and easier to use than the previous code.

Note: this is a WIP still as we need to finish fixing the interface of DeploymentManager and make sure that scenarios will now pass with these changes. These final changes should be very light compared to the overhaul already in this PR.

Finally, we deploy a new version of Comet to Fuji.
rationale: The commit primarily refactors the Deployment Manager, introduces new cache and alias handling, updates tests and CI configuration, and adds a new test contract. No behavior change fixing a defect is evident, nor any security-relevant change.

subject: Restructure scenario runner and get it working for scenarios with multiple solutions (#123)
body:
List of changes to different components of the scenario framework:

Workers/Runners:
1. Instead of each worker having a single runner that runs all bases for a scenario, a worker now creates a separate runner per base. Each runner holds a `World` for a different base. A single scenario will be run on all runners.
2. The runner takes a single scenario now instead of a list of scenarios.
3. The runner now returns the `Result` directly back to the worker instead of directly posting this to the parent. The worker then aggregates all the `Result`s from each runner and posts them to the parent. This is to prevent the first runner's `Result` from prematurely exiting the worker.

Snapshots: 
We had discussed only snapshotting after context initialization, but this is problematic because the context initialization is dependent on the scenario (e.g. await scenario.initializer(world)). Instead, I maintain two types of snapshots: a global one for the World and a local one for the context. The World snapshot is for resetting the runner back to a clean state of the world. The local context snapshot is for re-using the same context between multiple solutions of the same scenario.
rationale: The commit changes the runner to return a Result instead of invoking a callback per base, fixing a premature exit bug when handling multiple solutions. This is a functional bug fix, not related to security, funds, or attacker exploitation.

subject: Kovan Migration
body:
> Are you suggesting coconuts migrate?

This patch improves migrations, with the intent of building out a proper Kovan test-net.

First: we improve migrations by storing and retreiving the artifacts returned from `prepare` (and provide them to `enact`). This allows us to, say, deploy a bunch of contracts in the preparation step, store them, and later create a governance proposal that references those deployed artifacts. We aim to create a system that allows review prior to creating a governance proposal.

Second: we create a `gen:migration` task that will create a shell migration script for you. The primary purpose is we previously had migrations numbered sequentially, but that doesn't work if multiple PRs are creating migrations. So we use a timestamp-name combination now to prevent conflicts. This does not guarantee run-order, but nothing does, and that feels okay for now. E.g. some migrations might be merged into master but never run or accepted by governance. Note: there is currently no "run all migrations" command- each is run one-off, so skipping some is fine.

Third: We add `clone` to deployment manager (which is a light wrapper around import and deploy), which alleiviates a lot of the complexity in our previous migration script. We opt to use contract map overrides instead of "writing aliases," and overall, our migrations have become a lot simpler. We move Fuji's migration to our new style.

Fourth: We add `simulation` to the migrate task. This allows a user to see the effects of running a migration before running it actually. This should alleiviate a lot of concerns of "I wasted 50 ETH trying to test if my task worked." This will also allow others to test the effects of someone else's migration before it runs. This is not part of the scenario-framework (which will separate test migration scripts), but just a convenience for users of the CLI.

Fifth: we improve the `hardhat migrate` CLI commands to be easier and more intuitive, and we add a `MIGRATION.md` to explain the process for new users.

Sixth: we add a Kovan `configration.json` and migration. This will allow us to have a test-net on both Fuji and Kovan. Note: we opt into Kovan instead of Goerli as ChainLink doesn't have Goerli contracts, and we'd prefer to not have to simulate prices ourselves, even on test-net. We choose high-quality assets for the test-net, namely: USDC (base), WETH, WBTC, COMP, LINK and UNI.

Seventh: Brave Brave Sir Robin, Sir Robin Ran Away.

Eighth: We begin to attach to GitHub Actions as our runner. Specifically, the goal is that a user will run migration scripts in GitHub Actions (as opposed to "I ran this locally, here's my output"). This is to make it easier for auditors to understand the code that was run that created a given set of contracts and takes a risk out of the equation (e.g. a user says they deployed one thing, but actually deployed another). This isn't an end-all-be-all, but it should be helpful in general.

Ninth: We remove Goerli and Kovan from Bases, since they are temporarily non-functional until we get a proper Kovan deploy up, via the GitHub Actions above.
rationale: The commit introduces new CI workflows, documentation, and migration tooling without altering existing logic or fixing incorrect behavior. No changes address a previously exploitable vulnerability, so it is neither a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: Fuzzing, Context Props and Recursive Proxies (#208)
body:
* Fuzz requirement instead of comet config

Fix Issues with Forking and Snapshotting

This patch fixes issues with forking context and snapshotting. We ensure that forks actually do not conflict with one another by deep-cloning any necessary functions. Secondly, we improve snapshots so they are used between solutions of a solution-set. We probably need to work on what destructuring from CometContext looks like, which will be added to this branch before it's merged.

Context Properties

This patch creates "ContextProperties", which is a transformed version of context that is passed into scenarios. This allows us to not have to attach every possible value to the context object for destructuring, which becomes an issue when an object like `comet` changes (and thus should be received by an async getter), which either makes the scenario code more complicated (`let comet = await context.getComet()`), or we say `context.comet = comet` and then later if that value changes, we need to effectively observe those changes and reset this mirror-object. Instead, now, we create a function that is effectively: `getContextProperties(context) -> { comet: ..., ... }`. This function then can pull the data from the canonical source, but now the scenario can just destructure `{comet}` from this and not have to deal with guessing if this value is up to date (or awaiting it).

Additionally, we change `cache` to use `Map`s instead of objects for tracking its data and perform a smarter version of `deepClone`, which previously had a mistake that is was transforming `Map`s and other non-JSON data structures into flat objects, which then was failing further code. The new code deep clones Maps correctly and otherwise takes values as-is.

* Add recursive proxy support

* Add config for out-moded networks

* Fix issue with spidering after upgrade

* get scenarios working with chainid in forkspec

Co-authored-by: kevincheng96 <kevincheng96@hotmail.com>
rationale: The change replaces a JSON‑based deepClone with a proper Map‑aware recursive clone and updates the Cache class to use Map instead of plain objects, fixing functional bugs. No code paths introduce or mitigate security‑relevant checks, so it is not a security fix.

subject: Configurator (#160)
body:
This is an implementation of the advanced architecture described in RFC 021, but with some changes to enhance upgradeability, namely a separate Configurator contract that is upgradeable. The overall system looks something like:

Timelock -> ProxyAdmin -> Proxy -> Configurator
                       \
                        > Proxy -> Comet

Timelock is an admin of ProxyAdmin, which is an admin of the two proxies. Timelock is also an admin of Configurator, meaning only the Timelock can set parameters in Configurator.
rationale: The commit introduces new contracts (Configurator, ProxyAdmin extension) and refactors the factory signature, but does not correct previously incorrect behavior; it is a feature addition rather than a bug fix, and no security-relevant bug is addressed.

subject: GovernorSimple and updated SimpleTimelock (#280)
body:
This PR enhances our testnet governance setup to include an updated version of Timelock (has admin now) and a GovernorSimple that allows a group of admins to propose, cancel, queue, and execute proposals.

This PR also modifies some scenarios and unit tests to work with the new governance flow. I've also added new migration scripts to transition our testnets to this new governance flow. These migrations have been run using Github Actions.

Also, I've included a script (scripts/verify-comet.ts) that verifies the new Comet that gets deployed by CometFactory. For some reason, Etherscan is unable to verify contracts deployed by another contract (e.g. CometFactory), so a hacky way to get around this is to deploy another contract with the same bytecode via an EOA and verify that one instead. Since the two contracts share the same bytecode, both get verified. Obviously, this is not desirable so I also sent a message to Etherscan's support team to see if we can get this fixed.
rationale: The commit introduces new GovernorSimple and SimpleTimelock contracts and related test and deployment changes. It adds functionality rather than correcting existing incorrect behavior, so it is not a bug fix and does not address a security issue.

subject: Add Migration Constraint (#274)
body:
* Add Migration Constraint

This patch adds Migration Constraint, which runs each pending migration for each scenario to make it easy to automatically verify that each property tested by a scenario will continue to hold if that migration were to be prepared and enacted. A few notes:

 1. We currently are doing subsets, but we should considered ordered subsets, i.e. if migrations are run in different orders, do the properties still hold.
 2. Migrations currently are very bad at knowing if they were enacted. The hope is that this will be significantly easier when they start using Governance (e.g. they can just check to see if a Proposal with the same name/description/actions has been enacted. We could add the ability to check on-chain if a migration has been run, but that's costly and more complex than leaving it up to the migration itself to decide with the `enacted` function each migration must implement.
 3. Currently this is opt-in via `{ migrate: true }` flag. We should consider what requirements we want (e.g. is this just automatically enabled for all scenarios? Can scenarios specify they _should break_ if certain migrations are run?).

All-in-all, this should be a powerful tool to test that properties hold even after changes to the protocol are made, and has been a cornerstone of the intention of scenarios from inception.

* update timelock migrations

* migrate: true

* make signer a governor of SimpleGovernor

* return Migration loader if already exists

* update unit tests

Co-authored-by: Scott Silver <silversh@gmail.com>
rationale: The change introduces a new Migration Constraint testing feature, updates deployment scripts, and refactors imports. It does not correct previously incorrect behavior nor address any vulnerability; therefore it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: Derive store front discount from liquidationFactor (#327)
body:
The store front discount is now derived from a collateral asset's liquidationFactor. The formula is:

DiscountFactor = StoreFrontPriceFactor * (FACTOR_SCALE - Asset.LiquidationFactor), where FACTOR_SCALE=1e18

The storeFrontPriceFactor has now been repurposed to be the fraction of the liquidation penalty (1 - liquidationFactor) that goes to the buyer of collateral instead of the protocol.

e.g. A storeFrontPriceFactor of 1e18=100% means the buyer's discount is equals to the entire liquidation penalty. A value of 0 means the buyer will have to buy the collateral at market price (without a discount).
rationale: [MEV] The commit changes the discount calculation for collateral liquidation from a static storeFrontPriceFactor to a formula that incorporates the asset's liquidationFactor, removing a previous check that prevented storeFrontPriceFactor from exceeding liquidationFactor. The old logic could allow an excessively high discount, enabling attackers to buy liquidated collateral at too low a price and drain protocol funds, a clear economic vulnerability. The new logic fixes this miscalculation, making it a security-relevant bug fix.

subject: Fix CometActor/NonceManager forking (#435)
body:
This PR fixes a bug where the wrong nonces were being used in a new scenario I was trying to write (the one created in this PR).

The root issue is that when a scenario context is forked, the CometActors in the forked context use the signers from the old deployment manager instead of the new deployment manager. This is a problem because we recently started using NonceManager to represent signers in deployment manager. NonceManagers are stateful and therefore can have their nonces get out-of-sync if different NonceManagers are used for the same signer. In the new scenario introduced in this PR, we use deployment manager to deploy a new contract directly in the scenario, which uses the signer from the new deployment manager. Then, when we try to fast execute a proposal, the old signer from the CometContext's CometActor is used, causing a nonce mismatch.

The fix in this PR constructs CometActor using the new deployment manager's signers when forking CometContext.
rationale: The commit fixes a bug where forked scenario contexts used signers from the old deployment manager, causing nonce mismatches. This is a functional correctness issue in the testing framework, not a vulnerability that could be exploited to compromise security.

subject: Support multiple Comets using one Configurator (#437)
body:
This PR modifies the Configurator implementation to support multiple deployments of Comet so only a single Configurator instance needs to be deployed per chain. Instead of storing a single Configuration and factory address, the Configurator now stores a mapping from Comet proxy addresses to their respective Configuration and factory addresses. Because Configurator.deploy() now takes a Comet proxy address as an argument, a small change is also made to the CometProxyAdmin.deployAndUpgradeTo(...) function to use this new interface. I also removed the logic of setting an initial factory and configuration from the initializer and, instead, added new setters to set these after initialization.

This PR also updates our unit tests, scenarios, deployment logic, and migration scripts to work with the new Configurator implementation.

For scenarios specifically, I added a new flag called upgradeAll to the ModernConstraint that upgrades all contracts. This is needed in scenarios that need to upgrade more than just Comet. For example, we need to upgrade the CometProxyAdmin in a small number of our scenarios that use the Configurator.

TLDR: Contract changes are:

Change Configurator storage for factory and configuration to be mappings
Move the setting of the initial factory and configuration out of the initializer
Modify the CometProxyAdmin to use the new interface for Configurator.deploy(address)
rationale: The change introduces support for multiple Comet deployments by converting single storage variables to mappings and adjusting the Configurator interface; it is a feature/architectural refactor rather than a correction of erroneous behavior.

subject: Fix overflow bug that occasionally occurs when supplying 0 base (#455)
body:
This PR fixes a math overflow bug that occasionally occurs when supplying 0 base. I also added a unit test to verify the fix, as well as another unit test to show a weird quirk that can occur when withdrawing 0 base. 

**Bug details:**
In `supplyBase`, we calculate `dstPrincipalNew` using `dstPrincipal` (old principal value before amount is supplied). The formula is:

`int104 dstPrincipalNew = principalValue(presentValue(dstPrincipal) + signed104(amount))`

When `amount=0`, the formula condenses to:

`dstPrincipalNew = principalValue(presentValue(dstPrincipal))`

Due to the fact that both `principalValue` and `presentValue` round down in favor of the protocol, we can actually end up with a value of `dstPrincipalNew < dstPrincipal`. 

This breaks our assumption in `repayAndSupplyAmount` that `newPrincipal >= oldPrincipal` MUST be true. In the old code, this would cause `supplyAmount` returned from `repayAndSupplyAmount` to be an extremely large number (`uint104(-1)` to be precise), which would later cause an overflow during an addition operation. The new code now explicitly checks this assumption and sets both `repayAmount` and `supplyAmount` to 0 if the assumption is violated. We apply a similar check in `withdrawAndBorrowAmount` as well.
rationale: The commit adds guards to prevent a scenario where supplying 0 base could cause newPrincipal < oldPrincipal, leading to an underflow that produced a max uint104 value and later overflow during addition. This could be exploited to cause incorrect token accounting or transaction reverts (DoS). The fix corrects the faulty arithmetic, addressing a security-relevant overflow bug.

subject: Support deploying specific contracts instead of all at once (#476)
body:
This PR improves our deployment scripts in a few ways:

- Consolidate all deployment options into DeployCometOptionalParams so only a single object for optional params needs to be passed into deployComet
-Introduce a new ContractsToDeploy optional param that allows for more specificity in which contracts to deploy. This should put us in the right direction for mainnet and L2 migrations that don't need certain contracts (e.g. SimpleTimelock and GovernorSimple)

ContractsToDeploy usage:
If ContractsToDeploy is not provided as an optional param, all contracts will be deployed. The interface also has an all property that explicitly states to deploy all contracts. The all property can be combined with other properties to deploy "all but some" contracts. e.g.

`{ all: true, timelock: false }`

will deploy all contracts except for the Timelock.
rationale: The commit adds a new deployment option (ContractsToDeploy) and refactors deployment scripts to use it, without correcting any previously incorrect behavior or addressing a security vulnerability.

subject: Fault tolerant deploys (#489)
body:
This PR makes our deploys more consistent by handling network failures using retries and timeouts (to handle hanging txns). A new function `asyncCallWithRetry` is added to the `DeploymentManager` for this purpose.

I opted to implement the retry/timeout logic at the function level. The other approach would be to wrap an entire deployment script around one retry/timeout handler, but this requires us to cache which txns were already executed, which is difficult to generically do. The trade-off with my approach is that we have to explicitly wrap ad hoc (non-deploy) txns such as `usdc.initialize()` with an `asyncCallWithRetry` function in the deployment script.
rationale: The commit adds retry/timeout logic to deployment scripts to improve fault tolerance. This is a reliability enhancement (new feature) rather than correcting incorrect behavior, and it does not address a security vulnerability.

body:
We are working towards a simplified/standard workflow which we still need to document:

 1. Open a PR with a migration script
 2. Run 'prepare' workflow in GitHub CI
  - this should deploy any necessary contracts
  - maybe go post in the forum about it for review

  - this should make any necessary gov proposals

  - deploys any necessary contracts

subject: Fix scenario admin issue for chains without GovernorSimple (#495)
body:
Right now, scenarios set the admin signer to be the address returned by `governor.admins(0)`. This works on testnets where the governor contract is `GovernorSimple`. However, this wouldn't for mainnet because `GovernorBravo` doesn't have an `admins` list to read from. 

This PR fixes the issue by setting the admin signer to be `comet.governor()`, which could either be an EOA or a contract address (`Timelock`), and using it to directly sign txns for contract upgrades. Since the admin could be a contract address, we have to set the next block's base fee to 0 and set the gas price to 0 whenever sending a txn with it.
rationale: The commit only modifies test scenario files to use the admin signer directly and adjust gas settings; it does not change any production contract logic, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: Standardize deploy scripts, and deploy once per base (#497)
body:
* Standardize deploy scripts, and deploy once per base

Cleans up and refactors a bunch of the deploy code.
We no longer have a separate code path for development deploys, and we make them more efficient by only deploying once per base instead of once per scenario.
As a result, we also avoid redeploying all tokens during 'upgrades' in development.

Of note: we store the world in the context to avoid passing it around everywhere, and to prevent incorrect usage.
In addition, the deploy logic now lives in the deployment manager, and is performed by scenario plugin (Worker), which gives the scenario plugin a stronger dependency on the deployment manager dependency.
However these plugins were already coupled for other reasons, and there are likely other benefits that can come of this.

* Make network retry logic a little more robust

* Fix default arg for deployMissing and hanging in sourceTokens

Also adds a bit better debugging and some other modest fixes to sourcing.
Now we are actually not re-deploying all the time, and things are also relatively much faster, as they should be.

Also, reduce the number of workers by default since 6 probably isn't helping on most machines.

* Remove the signers reset which is causing some nonce issues

Not really sure about how this works, but looked hacky anyway, so better to remove if causing an issue.
But could use a second opinion, especially since I'm not sure about what it was supposed to be fixing.
rationale: The commit mainly refactors deployment scripts and includes fixes such as correcting a default argument for deployMissing, addressing a hanging issue in sourceTokens, and removing a signers reset that caused nonce problems. These are functional bug fixes rather than changes that mitigate exploitable security vulnerabilities.

subject: Add option to lazily verify contracts (#484)
body:
One contributing factor to the flakiness of our deployment scripts is that each contract is verified right as it is deployed, rather than after all of the contracts have been deployed. Since contract verification happens over network requests to etherscan, they can sometimes fail (e.g. API throttling, normal network request failures) and require the entire deployment script to be re-ran from the start, wasting a lot of gas and time.

In an attempt to reduce the overall flakiness of our deployment scripts, this PR introduces an option to lazily verify contracts. Instead of verifying each contract the moment they are deployed, the deployment manager will cache the verification arguments and allow all contracts to be verified at the end of the deployment using the `verifyContracts` function.
rationale: The commit introduces a new lazy verification option for contract deployment, which is a feature addition and does not correct previously incorrect behavior. No security vulnerability is being fixed.
