subject: Improvements to CometProxyAdmin and Configurator (#516)
body:
This PR pulls out and isolates the contract changes introduced in Jared's refactoring PR #515. I've added unit tests and scenarios to test the new code paths.

Summary of two changes: 
The first adds an deployUpgradeToAndCall so that we can atomically perform the first Comet impl deploy + initialize, and so that governance proposals only need a single action to upgrade and initialize a new Comet impl.

The second is a change to Configurator which re-allows re-setting the Configuration for a Comet, but only if the invariants on baseToken and tokenIndexScale are not violated. This means we can always call setConfiguration(newConfig) e.g. in scenarios to upgrade, instead of having to diff and call each of the setters for any changed fields (which is also error prone), and may one day be useful for an otherwise-too-large governance proposal.
rationale: The commit changes Configurator.setConfiguration to allow re‑setting a configuration only when baseToken and trackingIndexScale remain unchanged, adding a validation check that previously was missing. subject: Fix deployment manager contract cache and spidering issues
body:
Adds interfaces for contracts we use in scens and deployments.
These artifacts are now used by spider, since we've had some trouble verifying the cloned contracts, and are afraid we may lose the ability to verify very old contracts, if we haven't already.
This also doesn't cache the artifacts spider reads locally in the contract cache, since that creates an extra step of having to purge the cache after changes are made to the artifacts, as well as creates a broken condition where if we first read the contract as an artifact, we won't be able to deploy it.
In all, this means we are guaranteed that everything in the contract cache is pulled from etherscan and deployable.

Finally, this gets rid of the invalidate/rebuild the contract cache for the deployment manager, since we can just directly use the results of spidering.
This is significantly faster, and avoids the problem that we would have rebuilding the contracts from disk without spidering now that the artifacts aren't kept in the cache.
rationale: The change corrects broken behavior in the deployment manager where cached artifacts could become stale or unverified, leading to deployment failures. It is a bug fix to tooling, with no indication that the prior behavior could be exploited to compromise funds, keys, or contract integrity.

subject: Separate whales for testnet

For prior testnets, we completely controlled the COMP allocation, so we were able to delegate to the top mainnet whale when cloning gov.
For new goerli, we are leveraging an existing gov installation, so we need to know about some external COMP whales.

subject: Add back `enacted` step and programmatically set it after running migrations (#567)
body:
This PR adds back an optional `enacted` step in our migrations and programmatically sets it whenever a migration is run with `enact` on. We are bringing `enacted` back so we have a way to prevent scenarios from running the same migration again once it has already been enacted on-chain.

Example commits of GHA adding `enacted` after running a migration:
https://github.com/compound-finance/comet/pull/566/commits/04aab559697102d09d580fb688bfa6012cc13555
https://github.com/compound-finance/comet/pull/566/commits/16b3daf885609aae3ff48c604941408315500153
rationale: The change reintroduces an optional `enacted` step and writes it after a migration runs, preventing the same migration from being executed again. Previously, migrations could be replayed, potentially causing duplicate on‑chain actions (e.g., token transfers or upgrades). Adding this guard fixes a functional bug and mitigates a replay/re‑execution security issue.

* Price feeds for WETH deployment + Bulker changes for OZ audit (#625)
 This PR implements and modifies price feeds to support the upcoming WETH deployment. The favored plan so far is to use ETH-denominated price feeds as opposed to USD price feeds, but stick with using 8 decimals for prices to avoid having to change the `Comet` and `Configurator` implementations.
 This would require:
  - A new wrapper price feed (`ScalingPriceFeed.sol`) that scales prices up or down to 8 decimals
  - A new `ConstantPriceFeed` that always returns 1e8 for the `WETH` base asset, since should always hold a 1:1 value with ETH
  - Modifications to the `WstETHPriceFeed` to return prices in terms of ETH instead of USD

 This is an alternative approach to #626, which is a more complex change but could be a better long-term solution.
 *Note: This PR also now contains the changes from #634 and #635, which address some suggestions made by OZ for their audit of `WstETHPriceFeed` and `Bulker`.*
rationale: The commit introduces new contracts and configuration for mainnet ETH deployment (price feeds, bulker changes, supply cap constraint) without modifying existing logic to correct a defect; it is a feature addition rather than a bug fix, so no security fix is implied.

subject: Bulker contract updates for audit (#635)
body:
This PR contains the following contract changes to `BaseBulker` and `MainnetBulker` based on OZ's recent audit:

- **L-05 Lack of return validation** - We added transfer success checks to these transfer calls.
- **L-09 Partial implementation of Ownable library** - We added a `transferAdmin` function to the `BaseBulker` contract. We will stick with a self-implementation of the Ownable logic to stay consistent with the rest of the contracts in the repo (like `Configurator`).
rationale: The commit adds explicit success checks for ERC20 transfer and transferFrom calls (doTransferIn/doTransferOut) and reverts on failure, fixing the previously unchecked return values (L-05). The prior behavior could be exploited to make token transfers silently fail while the contract proceeds, leading to loss or misallocation of funds, a security issue.

subject: wstETHPriceFeed and BaseBulker stylistic changes (#634)
body:
This PR contains changes to the following (mostly stylistic) issues highlighted in OZ's audit:

- **L-04 Missing docstrings** - We added a comprehensive set of docstrings to the various constants and functions in the `BaseBulker` and `MainnetBulker` contracts.
- **L-06 Possible mismatch between native and wrapped tokens in different chains** - It is true that the `BaseBulker` is only intended to work for EVM chains with a native token and wrapped native token that implements the IWETH interface. We have documented this requirement more clearly.
- **L-07 sweepToken can potentially call a malicious token** - We expect the admin of the `Bulker` (the `Timelock`) to never sweep malicious tokens, but we added a cautionary note just in case. That being said, we think that a malicious token is unable to attack the contract and steal user’s funds since the `Bulker` never delegatecalls to any external contracts.
- **L-08 Unsafe explicit casting of integers** - We purposely avoided the safe conversion of `wstETHScale` because it is always going to be less than `type(int256).max`. We added a note to explain this.
- **N-01 Coding style could be improved** - We updated the `wstETHPriceScale` immutable variable to be an int256.
- **N-02 Confusing documentation** - We fixed the documentations mentioned in this issue.
rationale: The commit primarily adds documentation, stylistic changes, and minor type adjustments. No functional bug is corrected, and no security-relevant behavior is altered; changes like admin mutability and new errors appear to be preparatory rather than fixing an exploitable defect.

subject: Price feeds for WETH deployment + Bulker changes for OZ audit (#625)
body:
This PR implements and modifies price feeds to support the upcoming WETH deployment. The favored plan so far is to use ETH-denominated price feeds as opposed to USD price feeds, but stick with using 8 decimals for prices to avoid having to change the `Comet` and `Configurator` implementations. 

This would require: 
- A new wrapper price feed (`ScalingPriceFeed.sol`) that scales prices up or down to 8 decimals
- A new `ConstantPriceFeed` that always returns 1e8 for the `WETH` base asset, since should always hold a 1:1 value with ETH
- Modifications to the `WstETHPriceFeed` to return prices in terms of ETH instead of USD

This is an alternative approach to #626, which is a more complex change but could be a better long-term solution.

*Note: This PR also now contains the changes from #634 and #635, which address some suggestions made by OZ for their audit of `WstETHPriceFeed` and `Bulker`.*
rationale: The commit primarily introduces new price feed contracts and refactors existing code to use a generic IPriceFeed interface, which is a feature addition and refactor. While it mentions audit suggestions, the provided diff does not show concrete security-related bug fixes, so there is insufficient evidence to label it as a bug or security fix.

subject: WETH deployment audit changes (#641)
body:
These are changes in response to the WETH deployment [audit](https://gist.github.com/andresbach/a01686b1ef8bdf51d46046f2cfc93307) conducted by OZ:

- **L01 - Lack of input validation** - We originally avoided zero address checks because there are a vast amount of accidental addresses that can be set here and checking for a specific one seems unnecessary. However, we have reconsidered that position after seeing the reasons for including a zero address check listed in this [post](https://forum.openzeppelin.com/t/removing-address-0x0-checks-from-openzeppelin-contracts/2222/13).
- **L02 - Improper implementation of Chainlink AggregatorV3Interface** - We updated the hard-coded return values for `roundId` and `answeredInRound` to be 1 to comply with the Chainlink specification.
- **L04 - Incomplete/confusing documentation** - We updated the documentation based on the provided suggestions.

Our full audit responses are [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A8TrUdTtD7DXr1U5HOqSS1Xl81rjBZdlDC7LS4No4Bw).
rationale: The commit adds input validation to prevent setting admin to the zero address (preventing loss of admin control) and corrects ConstantPriceFeed to return non‑zero roundId/answeredInRound per Chainlink spec, fixing incorrect oracle data that could be misused.

subject: WETH deployment audit changes (#641)
body:
These are changes in response to the WETH deployment [audit](https://gist.github.com/andresbach/a01686b1ef8bdf51d46046f2cfc93307) conducted by OZ:

- **L01 - Lack of input validation** - We originally avoided zero address checks because there are a vast amount of accidental addresses that can be set here and checking for a specific one seems unnecessary. However, we have reconsidered that position after seeing the reasons for including a zero address check listed in this [post](https://forum.openzeppelin.com/t/removing-address-0x0-checks-from-openzeppelin-contracts/2222/13).
- **L02 - Improper implementation of Chainlink AggregatorV3Interface** - We updated the hard-coded return values for `roundId` and `answeredInRound` to be 1 to comply with the Chainlink specification.
- **L04 - Incomplete/confusing documentation** - We updated the documentation based on the provided suggestions.

Our full audit responses are [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1A8TrUdTtD7DXr1U5HOqSS1Xl81rjBZdlDC7LS4No4Bw).
rationale: The commit adds a zero‑address check to BaseBulker.transferAdmin, preventing the admin from being set to address(0) which could lock admin functions (availability impact). This is a bug fix and a security fix (improper input validation).

subject: Spider USDC deployment before calling `fromDep` (#644)
body:
We need to spider the `USDC` deployment before calling `fromDep` on it so all the aliases are populated in the cache. Otherwise, `fromDep` may try to import an `undefined` contract. 

There are many approaches to this and this PR takes the simplest approach of spidering in the deploy script. Another approach could be to handle the spidering directly in `fromDep`.
rationale: The change adds spidering of the USDC deployment before calling fromDep, fixing a bug where fromDep could import an undefined contract, but the issue does not expose security consequences such as fund loss or unauthorized actions.

subject: Support multiple connections to Seacrest in Enact (#692)
body:
Currently, running `Enact` in CI using Seacrest will fail when multiple networks are used (e.g. for cross-chain governance proposals that read from Polygon and write to mainnet). This is because Seacrest's connection with WalletConnect is for a specific chain, so trying to access a different chain will result in a `could not detect network` error.

This change supports making multiple connections to Seacrest/WalletConnect, all from a single phone. We introduce optional `GOV_NETWORK` and `GOV_NETWORK_PROVIDER` env variables to override the provider for a specific chain when creating the HREs. The `Enact` CI job determines the `GOV_NETWORK` based on what the original selected network is.
rationale: The commit fixes a CI failure when using multiple networks by adding support for multiple Seacrest connections and new env variables. This corrects incorrect behavior but does not address a security vulnerability.

subject: Implement setRewardsClaimed (#703)
body:
This PR introduces a `setRewardsClaimed` function that gives the admin the ability to set rewards claimed for any user. This gives us the ability to initialize a new reward distribution that doesn't necessarily have to retroactively reward all past usage of Comet. 

We would have to compute off-chain the amount that each user would be able to claim at a specific block number `x` and write it on-chain via the `setRewardsClaimed` function. This allows us to essentially set the start time of the rewards accrual to be after that specific block number `x`.
rationale: The commit introduces a new admin function (setRewardsClaimed) and related tests; it does not correct previously incorrect behavior, nor does it address a security vulnerability.

subject: Diff checker for state changes after running a migration (#729)
body:
This adds a diff checker to check for state changes after a migration is run. This allows us to more comprehensively check for state changes because, right now, our migration verification logic will not catch any unintentional state changes. For example, in a proposal that only touches collateral factors, we'll check that `collateralFactor == some new amount`, but not that `liquidationFactor == old amount`. We could also potentially generate a report of all the state changes for easier viewing.

In order to isolate the state changes of each migration, we get rid of the `VerifyMigrationConstraint` and move the verify checks directly into the `ProposalConstraint` so that verification is called right after a proposal is executed. This way, we can verify the state changes of a specific migration without having the diffs be affected by other migrations or pending proposals.
rationale: The commit adds a new diff‑checking utility and adjusts verification flow for migrations, which is a testing/verification enhancement rather than correcting faulty production behaviour. No security‑relevant logic is altered, so it is neither a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: Make updateBasePrincipal virtual so that it can be overridden (#749)
body:
My team received a grant from CGP 2.0 to add Flexible Voting support to Compound V3.

In order to implement our extension we need to be able to determine, for any given block:

how much principal a given account has supplied up to that time, and
how much total principal has been supplied to Comet up to that time
Our belief is that the easiest way to do this involves overriding the Comet.updateBasePrincipal function to store a couple checkpoints. You can see the PR for this work in ScopeLift/flexible-voting#46, and the specific overrides we need to make here. Since updateBasePrincipal is the single way that principal balances are updated by the system, being able to add checkpointing to it greatly simplifies our task.

Thanks in advance!

subject: Multiplicative Price Feed (#757)
body:
This generalizes the logic used in the recently audited [`WBTCPriceFeed`](https://github.com/compound-finance/comet/pull/737) to create a `MultiplicativePriceFeed` that derives its price from multiplying the prices from two other price feeds together. 

This is a flexible wrapper price feed that can be used to generate prices for any asset that does not have a price feed that fits Comet's expected price denomination. e.g. if we wanted to add `cbETH` to `cUSDCv3`, there is no Chainlink price feed for `cbETH / USD`, so we would need to multiply the `cbETH / ETH` and `ETH / USD` price feeds together to get `cbETH / USD`
rationale: The commit only introduces a new MultiplicativePriceFeed contract and associated tests; it does not modify existing functionality, so it is a feature addition rather than a bug fix, and no security-relevant behavior is altered.

subject: update lexi order
rationale: [MEV] The change fixes an incorrect lexicographic comparison that returned true whenever the first string was shorter, regardless of content. In a DEX order book this can misorder orders, enabling an attacker to manipulate execution order (MEV). The fix adds proper min-length iteration and correct length tie‑break, addressing the ordering bug.

rationale: The commit introduces a new governance module and updates pool metadata to include it, which is a feature addition/refactor. No bug behavior is corrected, and no security-relevant issue is addressed.

subject: create pool through state
rationale: The commit changes pool creation to return a proper pool_key and updates state to use that key for uniqueness checks. Previously a placeholder empty string was used, causing all pools to share the same identifier, which prevented creation of additional pools (availability issue). The fix corrects this logic bug, restoring proper pool tracking and preventing a denial‑of‑service condition.

subject: syntax
rationale: The change only replaces borrow_mut calls with the newer &mut indexing syntax, which does not alter program logic or security properties; it is a syntactic refactor, not a bug fix.

rationale: The commit only deletes a source file and likely moves code to a new module (refactor/separation) without changing logic or fixing a defect; no security-relevant changes are evident.

rationale: The commit removes an unused UID field from the DeepPrice struct and drops the need for a TxContext when initializing it. This changes the struct's layout and initialization semantics, fixing a bug where an unnecessary object ID was being created. No evidence in the diff indicates that the previous behavior was exploitable or posed a security risk.

rationale: The commit introduces new staking functionality, adds fields and helper functions, and modifies existing APIs. It does not appear to correct previously incorrect behavior, but rather adds a feature. No security-relevant bug is being fixed.

subject: warnings
rationale: The commit removes public functions that directly modify voting power and changes several APIs to take immutable pool references instead of mutable ones, preventing unintended or malicious updates to pool state and voting power. This corrects a behavior that could be exploited to tamper with governance parameters.

subject: test send_treasury
rationale: The diff only adds a new public function send_to_treasury that transfers a fee to the pool's treasury; it does not modify existing behavior, so it is a feature addition rather than a bug fix, and there is no indication of fixing a security-related defect.

rationale: The commit only renames a struct field and refactors deposit and treasury transfer functions into a combined implementation without changing observable behavior; it appears to be a code cleanup rather than a correction of faulty logic or a security vulnerability.

subject: fun def
rationale: The change removes the `public` qualifier from the `send` function, restricting it from being called by external modules. Previously any module could invoke `send` to transfer a Coin<T>, which is an access‑control flaw that could be exploited to move funds. Removing the visibility fixes this security issue.

subject: update functions
rationale: The change only removes a helper function and reorders parameters in internal functions without altering logic or fixing a previously incorrect behavior; it appears to be a refactor rather than a bug or security fix.

subject: user
rationale: The commit adds proper per‑user stake tracking (User struct, increase_user_stake/remove_user_stake) and replaces placeholder zero values in stake/unstake. Previously stake/unstake ignored individual balances, allowing incorrect accounting that could be exploited to claim rewards or withdraw funds improperly, a security‑relevant defect.

subject: burn
rationale: The change adds missing burn logic in get_user_mut and updates the burn function to actually transfer DEEP tokens to the burn address, fixing a bug where stale balances were not burned. This could have allowed users to retain tokens they should not have, leading to fund loss, thus a security-relevant business‑logic fix.

subject: burn
rationale: The changes introduce a new claim_rebates function, modify reset_rebates to return a value, and refactor the burn function signature. These are feature additions and refactoring, not corrections of incorrect behavior, and no security-relevant issue is evident in the diff.

Stale state can be exploited for profit by submitting orders before the pool is refreshed, a classic MEV/ordering attack, thus a security‑relevant fix.

subject: deep fees
rationale: The change adds a missing DEEP fee deposit before maker order placement and passes the fee amount into the order functions, fixing a bug where maker fees were not collected, which could be exploited to avoid paying fees and profit from the pool.

subject: feat: Create new sandbox command
body:
*Summary*
When we are running the indexer in a
sandbox environment we need to point
it to custom package ids for core and
margin during runtime.
This was not currently possible
since we used hard coded package ids for
mainnet and testnet.

We also needed a way to support localnet,
therefore using a local_ingestion_path
instead of remote_store_url.

These changes enable us to specify a new
`sandbox` command that expects the
package ids and the sandbox environment
as CLI arguments.

The package ids are overwritten during
runtime only when the sandbox command
is specified.

*Changes*
- Introduce new sandbox.rs module that
contains the core logic.
- Define different ingestion configs
at main.rs
- Modify lib.rs to use the sandbox package_ids
- Define separate Dockerfile for sandbox indexer

*Testing*
1. Use `cargo run -- sandbox --help` to learn more.
2. All existing tests should still pass.
3. Try running the indexer on localnet (the sandbox repo
can help you on this).
rationale: The commit introduces a new sandbox command and related configuration to allow custom package IDs and local ingestion paths. This is a feature addition rather than a correction of incorrect behavior, and the diff does not address any security-relevant flaw.

body:
Implement the Slush DeFi Quickstart Provider API (OpenAPI v1.1.0) as a
new /slush/v1/ route module in the deepbook-server, exposing DeepBook
margin lending pools as LENDING strategies.

Key design decisions:
- Reuses existing margin_metrics infrastructure (margin_pool_snapshots)
  for pool state data (TVL, utilization, depositor counts) rather than
  making duplicate RPC calls
- Fetches APY from Abyss Protocol vault indexer with 5-minute caching
- Correctly constructs deposit and withdraw PTBs with proper arguments
  and TransferObjects commands for SupplierCap and returned Coin objects
- Returns 501 Not Implemented for withdraw/cancel since DeepBook margin
  withdrawals are instant (no hold period)

New files:
- slush/types.rs: Request/response types matching OpenAPI spec exactly
- slush/config.rs: Pool configuration and vault mapping (env-driven)
- slush/apy.rs: Abyss Protocol APY client with TTL cache
- slush/ptb.rs: PTB construction for deposit and withdraw transactions
- slush/handlers.rs: Axum handlers for all 9 endpoints
- slush/routes.rs: Route definitions nested under /slush/v1/

Configuration via env vars:
- MARGIN_REGISTRY_ID: Object ID of the MarginRegistry shared object
- SLUSH_VAULT_MAPPING: JSON mapping of pool IDs to Abyss vault addresses

subject: fix: remove serial id from margin_manager_state, use margin_manager_id as primary key
body:
The SERIAL id column exhausted its 32-bit max (2,147,483,647) because
INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE consumes a sequence value on every

subject: deepbook: add cancel_live_order(s) graceful cancel APIs (DBU-349)
body:
Adds `cancel_live_order` and `cancel_live_orders` on `Pool`. Both no-op
when an order id is not in the balance manager's `account_open_orders`
(already filled, cancelled, expired-and-swept, or not owned by this BM),
instead of aborting with `big_vector::ENotFound` like `cancel_order` /
`cancel_orders` do today.

Existing entrypoints are unchanged (no ABI break). Authorization stays
strict: orders in `account.open_orders()` belong to that BM by
construction, so the live path still routes through `cancel_order` and
its `EInvalidOrderBalanceManager` assert.

The batch variant snapshots `account_open_orders` once and removes ids
from the local copy as it cancels them, so duplicate ids in the input
vector miss the second `contains` check instead of aborting.

Tests cover: live cancel, already-filled skip (single + batch),
unknown id no-op, and duplicate ids in the input vector.

subject: predict: inventory-aware mid shift
body:

UP mid toward the side the book is bleeding, widening asymmetric spreads with
a zero-edge floor at the fair price.

  (`Σ (q_up − q_dn) · √(p · (1 − p))`), updated incrementally on every
  insert/remove so MTM and aggregate walks share the same cost.
- vault: plumb the per-leg Bernoulli weight into insert/remove and expose
  `oracle_directional_aggregate`.
- pricing_config: add `depth_multiplier` (global tuning knob, defaults to 1x)
  plus `compute_up_quote`, which scales the raw ratio by
  `√(reference_tte / max(tte, min_tte))`, caps it at ±1, maps it to a
  per-strike mid shift using the distance to the nearest binary bound, and
  clamps both quotes at the fair price.
- predict: compute the post-insert fair-price Bernoulli weight inside the
  mint/redeem (and range) paths so quotes see the new inventory before
  executing; thread the aggregate + TTE into `compute_up_quote` from
  `get_trade_amounts` and `get_range_trade_amounts`.
- math: small `bernoulli_weight(p)` helper; constants gain
  `default_depth_multiplier`, `ms_per_day`, `reference_tte_ms`, `min_tte_ms`.
- registry: admin entry point `set_depth_multiplier`.

subject: predict: use n(d₂) as inventory risk weight
body:
Replace `√(p·(1−p))` with the true binary delta proxy `n(d₂)` (standard
normal PDF at d₂) for the per-strike weight that feeds
`directional_aggregate`. `n(d₂)` is the strike-dependent part of the
textbook binary delta `Δ = e^(−rτ)·n(d₂)/(S·σ·√τ)`; the constant
factors are absorbed into `depth_multiplier` and `tte_factor`.

Oracle factors out a private `compute_d2` helper so `compute_price`
(CDF) and the new `compute_risk_weight` (PDF) share one SVI walk.
`math::normal_pdf` wraps the existing `exp` primitive. Spread formula
is unchanged — `√(p·(1−p))` is still correct there as a variance-based
width.

Python sim mirrors the change: `svi_d2` feeds both the UP price
(`norm.cdf`) and the new `risk_weight_at` (`norm.pdf`).
rationale: The commit replaces the previous sqrt(p·(1−p)) weight with a normal PDF based risk weight, correcting the inventory risk calculation. This changes behavior, indicating a bug fix, but the change is limited to simulation/oracle logic and does not address a security vulnerability such as oracle checks, slippage bounds, or ordering exploits.

verified `pyth_lazer::update::Update` and rederives `forward = spot * basis`
against the cached operator basis. Renames the existing cap-gated
`update_prices` to `update_basis` to reflect that its primary intent is
refreshing the carry ratio at a low ~10s cadence. Both endpoints bump
`oracle.timestamp` so Lazer is the authoritative freshness signal for
user-facing 30s staleness; `basis_timestamp` gates a separate 60s window
on operator cadence.

Initial production scope is BTC/USD only (Pyth Lazer feed id 1); the feed
id is stored on `OracleSVI` at creation.

`simulations/stubs/` exposing only the `i64`/`i16`/`feed`/`update` symbols
the oracle module references. `run.sh` publishes the stub first on
localnet and pins predict to the resulting address via
`[dep-replacements.sim]`, avoiding the real pyth_lazer → wormhole

subject: predict: make oracle staleness thresholds admin-configurable
body:

from compile-time macros to `OracleConfig` fields with admin setters,
capped at 60s via `max_staleness_threshold_ms!()` so the liveness gate
can't be loosened into irrelevance.

`assert_live_oracle` and `assert_quoteable_oracle` now take
`&OracleConfig` as receiver; all six call sites in `predict.move` use
`predict.oracle_config.assert_*(...)` method syntax. The basis threshold
is threaded into `oracle::update_spot_from_lazer` / `apply_lazer_spot`
as a `u64` parameter — since `oracle.move` can't import `oracle_config`
(the import direction is reversed). The Lazer entry is demoted to
`public(package)` and a public wrapper `predict::update_spot_from_lazer`
reads the threshold from `OracleConfig` before delegating, so the
stale-basis check can't be bypassed from a PTB.

Also converts the remaining `assert_authorized_cap(oracle, …)`,
`apply_lazer_spot(oracle, …)`, and `compute_price(oracle, …)` call sites
in `oracle.move` to method-call syntax.

rationale: The change moves staleness thresholds from compile‑time macros to admin‑configurable fields and caps them, and modifies `update_spot_from_lazer` to require the threshold from `OracleConfig` via a wrapper, preventing callers from bypassing the stale‑basis check. Previously an attacker could call the internal function directly and skip the freshness validation, allowing use of stale oracle data for pricing, which is a security vulnerability.

subject: predict: Lazer-primary spot with BS fallback and update_basis circuit breaker
body:
Lazer is now explicitly authoritative for the master spot. While the last
Pyth Lazer push is within `lazer_authoritative_threshold_ms` (default 2s),
operator `update_basis` calls refresh basis and re-derive forward against
the cached Lazer spot but leave `prices.spot` alone. Once Lazer has been
silent longer than that, the operator spot flows through as a fallback,
bumps `spot_timestamp`, and emits `OracleSpotFallbackEngaged`.

- Rename `OracleSVI.timestamp` → `spot_timestamp` and add
  `lazer_spot_timestamp_ms`. Two independent timers: `spot_timestamp`
  gates the halt check (whichever feed owns spot), `lazer_spot_timestamp_ms`
  answers "is Lazer currently authoritative?".
- Drop default spot halt gate from 30s → 3s. With the 1s operator cadence,
  the fallback path keeps the oracle live through arbitrary-length Lazer
  outages; when both feeds go silent the gate trips within 3s.
- Add basis circuit breaker on `update_basis`: per-push spot deviation
  (10%), per-push basis deviation (5%), absolute basis range [0.9, 1.1].
  First push after activation skips the deviation guards (no baseline);
  the absolute bounds always apply. All four are admin-configurable via
  `registry::set_basis_bounds`.
- Demote `oracle::update_basis` to `public(package)`, move the PTB entry
  to `predict::update_basis`, which threads bounds + lazer-authoritative
  window from `OracleConfig` into the primitive. Same pattern as
  `update_spot_from_lazer`: PTB callers cannot bypass admin thresholds.
- Admin entrypoints: `registry::set_basis_bounds` and
  `registry::set_lazer_authoritative_threshold_ms`.
- Simulation runtime: retarget `updateBasisTx` to `predict::update_basis`
  and thread the Predict object through.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds a circuit‑breaker and deviation checks to `update_basis` and introduces a fallback when the Lazer feed is stale, fixing a defect where stale or out‑of‑range oracle data could be accepted. This validation prevents malicious price manipulation, a classic oracle tampering issue.

subject: predict: gate expiry settlement on Lazer and tighten circuit-breaker ceilings
body:
Closes two reviewer gaps on the Lazer-integration branch:

1. Settlement race: both `update_basis` (operator) and
   `update_spot_from_lazer` (permissionless, trust-root) could freeze
   `OracleSVI.settlement_price` at expiry on a first-writer-wins basis.
   That contradicts the "Lazer is the authoritative master spot" model.

   Introduce `lazer_settlement_authoritative_threshold_ms` (default 60s,
   longer than the 2s live-update window since settlement is
   irreversible). `update_basis`'s terminal branch now aborts with
   `ELazerAuthoritativeAtExpiry` while Lazer has pushed within the
   settlement window; once Lazer goes stale or has never pushed, the
   operator remains the settlement fallback so the oracle can't get
   permanently stuck. Plumbed through `OracleBounds` (per-oracle) and
   `OracleConfig` (admin seed) with cap-authorized + admin setters and
   event widening on `OracleBoundsUpdated` /
   `OracleStalenessConfigUpdated`.

2. Open circuit-breaker setters: `validate_basis_bounds_inputs` in both
   `oracle` and `oracle_config` admitted trivially-disabling values —
   `max_*_deviation <= 100%` and `min_basis < max_basis` with no
   absolute envelope. Tighten to `max_basis_deviation_ceiling!()` (10%),
   `min_basis_floor!()` (0.5), `max_basis_ceiling!()` (2.0), and
   `> 0` on the deviation caps to close the zero-deviation no-op.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The commit fixes a race condition where both the operator (update_basis) and the permissionless Lazer feed could set the oracle's settlement_price at expiry, potentially allowing a malicious operator to freeze the price and cause downstream financial loss. Adding the ELazerAuthoritativeAtExpiry check and new authoritative threshold prevents unauthorized state changes, addressing a security-relevant oracle manipulation issue.

verified `pyth_lazer::update::Update` and rederives `forward = spot * basis`
against the cached operator basis. Renames the existing cap-gated
`update_prices` to `update_basis` to reflect that its primary intent is
refreshing the carry ratio at a low ~10s cadence. Both endpoints bump
`oracle.timestamp` so Lazer is the authoritative freshness signal for
user-facing 30s staleness; `basis_timestamp` gates a separate 60s window
on operator cadence.

Initial production scope is BTC/USD only (Pyth Lazer feed id 1); the feed
id is stored on `OracleSVI` at creation.

Simulation wiring: adds a minimal local stub `pyth_lazer` package under
`simulations/stubs/` exposing only the `i64`/`i16`/`feed`/`update` symbols
the oracle module references. `run.sh` publishes the stub first on
localnet and pins predict to the resulting address via
`[dep-replacements.sim]`, avoiding the real pyth_lazer → wormhole
dependency (wormhole source is designed to be linked as pre-published
bytecode and cannot be compiled fresh against 2024.beta).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict sim: snapshot Move.lock around predict publish

test-publish regenerates `[pinned.sim.*]` entries in Move.lock with
instance-specific local paths (e.g. `runs/apr14-1637/deps/pyth_lazer`),
leaving the file dirty in git after every sim run. Back it up before
publish and restore from the same .bak mechanism used for Move.toml.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: make oracle staleness thresholds admin-configurable

Promotes `staleness_threshold_ms` and `basis_staleness_threshold_ms`
from compile-time macros to `OracleConfig` fields with admin setters,
capped at 60s via `max_staleness_threshold_ms!()` so the liveness gate
can't be loosened into irrelevance.

`assert_live_oracle` and `assert_quoteable_oracle` now take
`&OracleConfig` as receiver; all six call sites in `predict.move` use
`predict.oracle_config.assert_*(...)` method syntax. The basis threshold
is threaded into `oracle::update_spot_from_lazer` / `apply_lazer_spot`
as a `u64` parameter — since `oracle.move` can't import `oracle_config`
(the import direction is reversed). The Lazer entry is demoted to
`public(package)` and a public wrapper `predict::update_spot_from_lazer`
reads the threshold from `OracleConfig` before delegating, so the
stale-basis check can't be bypassed from a PTB.

`apply_lazer_spot(oracle, …)`, and `compute_price(oracle, …)` call sites

* predict: Lazer-primary spot with BS fallback and update_basis circuit breaker

Lazer is now explicitly authoritative for the master spot. While the last
Pyth Lazer push is within `lazer_authoritative_threshold_ms` (default 2s),
operator `update_basis` calls refresh basis and re-derive forward against
the cached Lazer spot but leave `prices.spot` alone. Once Lazer has been
silent longer than that, the operator spot flows through as a fallback,
bumps `spot_timestamp`, and emits `OracleSpotFallbackEngaged`.

- Rename `OracleSVI.timestamp` → `spot_timestamp` and add
  `lazer_spot_timestamp_ms`. Two independent timers: `spot_timestamp`
  gates the halt check (whichever feed owns spot), `lazer_spot_timestamp_ms`
  answers "is Lazer currently authoritative?".
- Drop default spot halt gate from 30s → 3s. With the 1s operator cadence,
  the fallback path keeps the oracle live through arbitrary-length Lazer
  outages; when both feeds go silent the gate trips within 3s.
- Add basis circuit breaker on `update_basis`: per-push spot deviation
  (10%), per-push basis deviation (5%), absolute basis range [0.9, 1.1].
  First push after activation skips the deviation guards (no baseline);
  the absolute bounds always apply. All four are admin-configurable via
  `registry::set_basis_bounds`.
- Demote `oracle::update_basis` to `public(package)`, move the PTB entry
  to `predict::update_basis`, which threads bounds + lazer-authoritative
  window from `OracleConfig` into the primitive. Same pattern as
  `update_spot_from_lazer`: PTB callers cannot bypass admin thresholds.
- Admin entrypoints: `registry::set_basis_bounds` and
  `registry::set_lazer_authoritative_threshold_ms`.
- Simulation runtime: retarget `updateBasisTx` to `predict::update_basis`
  and thread the Predict object through.

* predict: per-asset basis circuit-breaker bounds

Replace the single `OracleConfig.basis_bounds` field with a
`Table<String, BasisBounds>` keyed by `underlying_asset`, so BTC, ETH,
and other assets can be tuned independently without per-oracle state.
`validate_basis_push` reads bounds for the oracle's asset and falls back
to `constants`-module defaults when no explicit entry is set, so new
assets don't block oracle creation. A single admin call now propagates
to every expiry of the same asset.

* predict: guard u64 overflow in Lazer price normalization

`magnitude * pow10(shift)` could silently overflow when scaling Lazer
prices into the 1e9-scaled u64 representation, even with `shift <= 18`
already asserted. Route both multiply branches through a
`checked_scale_up` helper that aborts with a named `ELazerPriceOverflow`
instead of letting the VM raise an unnamed arithmetic abort.

Spot 10% → 2%: comfortably catches scale errors and fat fingers without

subject: [predict] gate Lazer settlement on update freshness (DBU-389) (#983)
body:
The permissionless `update_spot_from_lazer` → `apply_lazer_spot` path
settled the oracle whenever `status == PENDING_SETTLEMENT`, with no
check that the incoming Lazer update was actually fresh. If Lazer
stalls, anyone could replay the last still-signed Lazer update past
expiry and lock in an outdated settlement price before the operator
fallback engages.

Gate the Lazer settlement branch on
`now - lazer_published_at_ms <= lazer_settlement_authoritative_threshold_ms`
(new `ELazerStaleAtExpiry`). Mirror-image of the existing
`ELazerAuthoritativeAtExpiry` check on the operator path: together they
ensure exactly one source drives settlement — Lazer when fresh, the
operator fallback once Lazer has been silent past the window.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The diff adds a freshness check (assert now <= published_at + threshold) before applying a Lazer settlement, fixing a missing validation that allowed replay of stale oracle data. This prevented an attacker from replaying an outdated signed Lazer update to lock in an outdated settlement price, a classic oracle manipulation leading to financial loss.

subject: predict: inventory-aware mid shift
body:
Skew the per-strike UP mid by the vault's signed directional inventory so
LP quotes asymmetrically: when the vault is net short UP across strikes,
push the mid up (mint widens, redeem pinned at fair); symmetric on the
other side. Defends against toxic flow by raising the cost of one-sided
accumulation while keeping non-toxic flow at near-fair pricing.

Math
- Per-strike weight: n(d₂(K)) — strike-dependent part of the textbook
  binary delta Δ = e^(−rτ)·n(d₂)/(S·σ·√τ); constants absorbed into
  depth_multiplier and tte_factor.
- Aggregate: Σ (q_long_leg − q_short_leg) · n(d₂_K), accumulated on every
  range insert/remove at trade-time fair price.
- Raw ratio: aggregate · √(ref_tte / max(tte, min_tte)) / (balance · depth_multiplier).
- Clamped to ±1, scaled by the room to the binary boundary ((1−p) or p),
  added to fair price. Symmetric spread sits on the shifted mid; clamps
  enforce mint ≥ fair and redeem ≤ fair (zero-edge floor).

Pricing is post-trade — apply_*_delta runs before quote_*_amounts, so a
buyer sees the inventory their own order created. Larger orders pay more.

Public API change
- quote_unit_price now returns (mint_price, redeem_price) instead of
  (fair_price, fee_rate); the symmetric tuple can't represent the
  inventory-shifted asymmetry. No external callers depended on the old
  shape (verified across scripts/, crates/, sim runtime).

Admin knobs
- depth_multiplier (default 1×): controls skew amplitude independently
  of spread. Smaller → stronger response to a given imbalance.
- reference_tte_ms (default 7d), min_tte_ms (default 1d): tte_factor
  amplification curve. Setters enforce min_tte_ms ∈ (0, ref_tte_ms].

Tests
- 47 new tests across 4 files covering: aggregate accounting, sentinel
  boundaries, round-trip cancellation, surface-drift residual, order-size
  monotonicity, per-matrix isolation, normal_pdf ground truth, and
  admin-setter abort guards.

Known limitations
- Aggregate drifts when the SVI surface moves between mint and redeem.
  The residual is bounded by qty · |w_open − w_close|; no per-position
  weight storage by design.
- tte_factor amplification can overflow i64::mul_scaled under aggressive
  admin configs. set_min_tte_ms only requires value > 0; tightening to
  e.g. 1 hour is a follow-up.
- compute_up_quote serves both binaries and ranges. Math works (range
  fair ∈ [0, 1] like a binary); rename deferred.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit introduces new inventory‑aware pricing logic, new config fields, and API changes. It adds functionality rather than correcting previously incorrect behavior, so it is not a bug fix and therefore not a security fix.

body:
Add 24 tests across two paths:

Math precision and edge cases (13 tests in inventory_skew_tests):
- tte_factor at exact ratios (1× at ref_tte, 2× at ref_tte/4, 0.5× at 4·ref_tte)
- Ratio clamp at exactly 1.0 vs 0.999 just below saturation

subject: predict: symmetric per-strike mid shift, drop zero-edge floor
body:
Range pricing now shifts each boundary's UP probability independently
and takes m(L) - m(H) as the range mid, so DN's mid is FS - m(K) when
UP's is m(K). This preserves the 1 UP + 1 DN = $1 invariant under any
aggregate sign: paired mint cost stays at FS + 2·spread instead of
rising under imbalance, and the discounted side now attracts the
rebalancing flow.

The zero-edge floor is removed. Under heavy imbalance mint can sit
below fair on the side the vault wants to grow and redeem can sit
above fair on the side it wants to shrink — the LP intentionally
takes a worse-than-fair fill on rebalancing trades.

subject: predict: inventory-aware mid shift (#995)
body:
* predict: inventory-aware mid shift

Skew the per-strike UP mid by the vault's signed directional inventory so
LP quotes asymmetrically: when the vault is net short UP across strikes,
push the mid up (mint widens, redeem pinned at fair); symmetric on the
other side. Defends against toxic flow by raising the cost of one-sided
accumulation while keeping non-toxic flow at near-fair pricing.

Math
- Per-strike weight: n(d₂(K)) — strike-dependent part of the textbook
  binary delta Δ = e^(−rτ)·n(d₂)/(S·σ·√τ); constants absorbed into
  depth_multiplier and tte_factor.
- Aggregate: Σ (q_long_leg − q_short_leg) · n(d₂_K), accumulated on every
  range insert/remove at trade-time fair price.
- Raw ratio: aggregate · √(ref_tte / max(tte, min_tte)) / (balance · depth_multiplier).
- Clamped to ±1, scaled by the room to the binary boundary ((1−p) or p),
  added to fair price. Symmetric spread sits on the shifted mid; clamps
  enforce mint ≥ fair and redeem ≤ fair (zero-edge floor).

Pricing is post-trade — apply_*_delta runs before quote_*_amounts, so a
buyer sees the inventory their own order created. Larger orders pay more.

Public API change
- quote_unit_price now returns (mint_price, redeem_price) instead of
  (fair_price, fee_rate); the symmetric tuple can't represent the
  inventory-shifted asymmetry. No external callers depended on the old
  shape (verified across scripts/, crates/, sim runtime).

Admin knobs
- depth_multiplier (default 1×): controls skew amplitude independently
  of spread. Smaller → stronger response to a given imbalance.
- reference_tte_ms (default 7d), min_tte_ms (default 1d): tte_factor
  amplification curve. Setters enforce min_tte_ms ∈ (0, ref_tte_ms].

Tests
- 47 new tests across 4 files covering: aggregate accounting, sentinel
  boundaries, round-trip cancellation, surface-drift residual, order-size
  monotonicity, per-matrix isolation, normal_pdf ground truth, and
  admin-setter abort guards.

Known limitations
- Aggregate drifts when the SVI surface moves between mint and redeem.
  The residual is bounded by qty · |w_open − w_close|; no per-position
  weight storage by design.
- tte_factor amplification can overflow i64::mul_scaled under aggressive
  admin configs. set_min_tte_ms only requires value > 0; tightening to
  e.g. 1 hour is a follow-up.
- compute_up_quote serves both binaries and ranges. Math works (range
  fair ∈ [0, 1] like a binary); rename deferred.

subject: margin v5: post-trade risk_ratio invariant on order placement (#1006)
body:
* margin v2: post-trade risk_ratio invariant on order placement

Adds `_v2` variants of every margin-routed order placement entry that
recompute the manager's `risk_ratio` against Pyth after the trade
settles and abort if the post-trade ratio breaches the borrow floor.
This closes the wash-trade drain vector exploited in the v3/v4
incident where attackers iterated proxy-side fills at oracle-band-edge
prices to walk a manager from `min_borrow_risk_ratio` (1.2499) down
toward zero.

V2 entries:
- pool_proxy::place_limit_order_v2 / place_market_order_v2 — assert
  post-trade `risk_ratio >= min_borrow_risk_ratio` (skip when no debt).
- pool_proxy::place_reduce_only_limit_order_v2 / market_v2 — assert
  monotonic improvement: `risk_ratio_after >= risk_ratio_before`.
  Defense-in-depth against edge-of-band fills that the existing
  reduce-only quantity predicate doesn't catch.
- margin_manager::execute_conditional_orders_v2 + private helpers
  process_collected_orders_v2 / place_pending_order_v2 / etc — same
  borrow-floor invariant after each per-fill placement; one bad fill
  reverts the whole txn.

V1 deprecation:
- pool_proxy::place_{limit,market,reduce_only_limit,reduce_only_market}_order
  and margin_manager::execute_conditional_orders preserve their on-chain
  signatures (required for upgrade compatibility) but bodies are replaced
  with `abort EDeprecatedUseV2`.
- margin_manager::add_conditional_order is left as v1: registration only,
  no fund movement, no risk surface to gate.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin v2: migrate existing tests + add regression coverage

Migrates every callsite of the deprecated v1 trading entries to the
new `_v2_for_test` wrappers in `test_helpers`. Adds:

- 4 v1 deprecation tests asserting each aborted v1 entry fires
  `EDeprecatedUseV2` (pool_proxy place/market/reduce-only x2).
- The two existing `test_place_reduce_only_market_order_ok*` tests are
  flipped to `expected_failure(EReduceOnlyMustImproveRiskRatio)` —
  with the standard test orderbook (bids at 0.99 / asks at 1.01),
  reduce-only market fills hit the band edge and the v2 monotonic
  invariant correctly aborts. The matching limit-price-at-oracle
  variants still pass `_ok`.
- `place_limit_order_v2_no_debt_at_oracle_price_ok` sanity test that
  the post-trade invariant short-circuits when manager has no debt.

Test wrappers in `test_helpers` (`place_*_v2_for_test`,
`execute_conditional_orders_v2_for_test`) take the original v1 args plus
margin pool refs and build oracle objects internally so callers don't
pay the take_shared/build/destroy cost per call.

311 tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin v5: bump MARGIN_VERSION + soften deprecation comment

- Bump `MARGIN_VERSION` from 4 to 5. The new package needs to be enabled
  via `enable_version(5)` after deployment; v3 and v4 should be kept
  enabled in parallel so existing manager objects can still complete
  wind-down paths (repay, withdraw, reduce-only).
- Reword the v1-deprecation header comment in `pool_proxy.move` to a
  neutral description of the v2 invariant rather than referencing past
  on-chain events. Source comments stay public-facing and timeless.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin v5: hoist conditional-order risk check out of the inner loop

`process_collected_orders_v2` previously recomputed `risk_ratio` after
every successful `place_pending_order_v2` fill. Move PTBs are atomic —
any abort inside the loop reverts every earlier fill in the same call —
so a single check after the loop is functionally equivalent: a breach of
the invariant aborts the whole txn either way.

Hoisting the check saves up to `N - 1` Pyth reads on the happy path,
where `N` is the number of fills (capped at `MAX_CONDITIONAL_ORDERS = 10`).
The only behavioral difference is in the abort case: the loop now runs
all fills before discovering the breach instead of stopping at the first
bad iteration. The happy path is the common case, so this is a net win.

Skipped entirely when no fills landed (`executed_ids` empty) or the
manager has no debt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin v5: reduce-only uses monotonic check; Option<u64> for risk_ratio_before

Reduce-only entries now require `risk_ratio_after >= risk_ratio_before`
(monotonic improvement) instead of the borrow-floor check. The borrow-floor
check would trap users in the 1.1–1.25 danger zone (between liquidation
and borrow thresholds) — exactly the people who most need to wind down
via reduce-only. Monotonic doesn't trap and additionally catches within-
band value leak that the floor check would allow.

Replaces the prior `0` sentinel for "manager has no debt" with
`Option<u64>` in `read_risk_ratio_if_indebted` and
`assert_reduce_only_monotonic`. A `0` sentinel could be misread as a
real `risk_ratio` of zero (a bankrupt manager); `option::none()` makes
the absence explicit and uses the type system to enforce caller handling.

Non-reduce-only entries (`place_limit_order_v2`, `place_market_order_v2`)
still use the borrow-floor `assert_post_trade_solvent`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin v5: explicit ENoDebtToReduce on reduce-only entries

Reduce-only on a no-debt manager previously collapsed into the generic
`ENotReduceOnlyOrder` via the quantity predicate (which fails because
both `base_debt > base_asset` and `quote_debt > quote_asset` evaluate
false when both debts are zero). Surface this distinct case explicitly:

- Add `ENoDebtToReduce` error constant.
- In each `place_reduce_only_*_v2` entry, after computing
  `risk_ratio_before_opt = read_risk_ratio_if_indebted(...)`, assert
  `risk_ratio_before_opt.is_some()` (raising `ENoDebtToReduce` if not)
  before the quantity predicate. The predicate keeps `ENotReduceOnlyOrder`
  for "wrong-side debt" or "quantity exceeds gap" cases.
- Simplify `assert_reduce_only_monotonic` to take `risk_ratio_before: u64`
  rather than `Option<u64>`. The caller has already destructured `Some`
  by the time this helper runs, so the helper's contract is straightforward.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin v5: drop ENoDebtToReduce + read_risk_ratio_if_indebted helper

The reduce-only quantity predicate (`base_debt > base_asset` or
`quote_debt > quote_asset`) already aborts for no-debt managers — both
arms evaluate `0 > x` (where x >= 0), which is always false. So by the
time we'd call `risk_ratio` to compute `risk_ratio_before`, debt is
guaranteed and the function is safe to invoke directly (no
divide-by-zero in `risk_ratio_int`).

This makes the `read_risk_ratio_if_indebted` helper unnecessary — its
only purpose was to gate the no-debt case that the predicate already
catches. The corresponding `ENoDebtToReduce` error code is unreachable
and is also removed.

Reduce-only entries now call `margin_manager.risk_ratio(...)` directly
after the predicate passes. Same observable behavior, less code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin v5: cover the three remaining new error codes with tests

Adds tests for every error code introduced by the v5 changes that wasn't
already covered:

1. `pool_proxy::EInsufficientRiskRatioAfterTrade` —
   `place_limit_order_v2_borrow_at_floor_then_adverse_fill_aborts`.
   Borrow exactly to the borrow floor (1.25), sell the borrowed asset
   against the standard test orderbook bid (0.99). The 1% adverse fill
   drops risk_ratio to ~1.2475, breaching the floor.

2. `margin_manager::EDeprecatedUseV2` for `execute_conditional_orders` —
   `execute_conditional_orders_v1_aborts`. Calls the v1 entry directly
   and asserts the abort fires.

3. `margin_manager::EInsufficientRiskRatioAfterTrade` —
   `execute_conditional_orders_v2_post_loop_check_aborts`. Sets up a
   manager at the borrow floor, registers a `trigger_above` conditional
   order whose pending limit ASK fills at the orderbook bid (0.99).
rationale: [MEV] The commit adds post‑trade risk_ratio checks (EInsufficientRiskRatioAfterTrade) and aborts when the invariant is violated, fixing a previously missing validation that allowed wash‑trade attacks to drive a manager's risk ratio to zero and drain funds. This corrects a bug and mitigates an exploitable security flaw.

subject: margin v5: clear all shares when liquidation withdraws all collateral (#1007)
body:
* margin v5: clear all shares when liquidation drains collateral

Fix residual borrow shares left on an empty manager when a position is
liquidatable but still slightly solvent (risk_ratio in [1.0, 1.05] with
the default 5% reward). The old `risk_ratio < float_scaling()` gate only
fired on insolvent positions; when assets sat between debt and
debt*1.05, the liquidator drained all collateral at `max_repay` but the
proportional branch left a sliver of borrow shares behind as silent bad
debt (no `pool_default` was recorded). Switch to
`assets_in_debt_unit <= debt_with_reward`, which fires for the whole
exhausted-collateral range and clears every share.

Adds tests:
- test_liquidate_slightly_solvent_clears_all_shares: drives the bug
  scenario and asserts shares + assets are zero post-liquidation
- test_liquidate_partial_keeps_proportional_shares: scenario (c)
  regression guard so the fix doesn't over-clear shares on healthy
  partial liquidations
- test_liquidate_one_sided_base_collateral_base_debt: regression for
  the audit-reported `withdraw_with_proof` abort on a missing key
  (already fixed in #756 via auto-creating a zero balance; this test
  locks in same-asset-borrow liquidation behavior)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin v5: add edge-case tests for liquidation share-clearing

Adds five tests targeting boundary conditions around the
`assets_exhausted && repay_amount == max_repay` gate that could leave
the manager in a bad state if the gate fires when it shouldn't, or
fails to fire when it should:

- test_liquidate_partial_in_slightly_solvent_range_keeps_residual:
  in the [1.0, 1.05] range with a small repay coin (repay_amount <
  max_repay), the IF guard's second predicate must fail so the
  proportional ELSE branch runs and residual debt + collateral remain.

- test_liquidate_records_pool_default_when_repay_below_debt:
  at risk_ratio ~ 1.01, the fix must record an honest pool_default
  via decrease_supply_absolute. Asserts pool.total_supply() strictly
  drops (pre-fix would have silently grown it via the phantom reward).

- test_liquidate_near_risk_ratio_one_records_large_default:
  deep into the slightly-solvent range (risk_ratio ~ 1.00125), the
  default magnitude approaches the ~1.9% theoretical maximum. Asserts
  supply_drop in [500, 800] USDC for a 40k USDC debt.

- test_liquidate_just_outside_assets_exhausted_runs_proportional:
  assets_in_debt_unit is one unit above debt_with_reward (scenario c
  by the slimmest margin). The IF guard's first predicate must fail
  — proportional must run, residual shares remain.

mint_cutoff_ms`, the mint aborts with `EMintCutoffReached`. Zero

* predict: per-asset linear time-to-expiry fee ramp (DBU-412)

compensate LPs for rising pin/gamma risk. The fee ramps from 1x at the
start of a window to a max multiplier at expiry:

assets can use a larger ramp, and all of an asset's expiry markets
inherit it automatically. Applied at the single fee site (quote_fee_rate),

subject: predict: gate version sync through Registry; drop manager mirror (#1041)
body:
The five permissionless `update_allowed_versions` entries accepted a raw
`VecSet<u64>` from the caller, allowing anyone to overwrite a shared
object's mirrored allowed-versions set with an arbitrary value — e.g.
`vec_set::empty()` would DoS every version-gated operation on that
object until the next sync.

Replace with `sync_*_allowed_versions(&Registry, &mut Target)` entries
on `registry.move`, which read the canonical set from the Registry and
copy it into the target. Each target module exposes a
`public(package) set_allowed_versions` setter only callable from within
the package; the public API never accepts a user-supplied set.

Also drop `allowed_versions` from `PredictManager` entirely. The
manager wraps a `BalanceManager` and tracks per-user positions added
through market flows; it owns no protocol-critical state independent
of the market/oracle/pool flows that already gate themselves. Per-user
mirrors don't scale (N users vs. small number of markets) and the only
operations they gated — `deposit`, `withdraw`, `set_builder_code` —
move user-owned cash, not protocol state.

Test plan:
- sui move test --gas-limit 100000000000 → 18 pass (was 17; +1 positive
  test for sync_market_oracle_allowed_versions).
- bunx prettier-move -c sources/**/*.move tests/**/*.move clean.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit removes public `update_allowed_versions` functions that let any caller overwrite a shared object's allowed‑versions set, which could be set to empty and cause a denial‑of‑service for all version‑gated operations. The fix restricts the setter to internal package use and syncs from a canonical Registry, correcting an access‑control bug.

subject: DBU-420: Predict DEEP staking (epoch active/inactive) for fee discounts and loss rebates (#1049)
body:
* DBU-420: Predict DEEP staking for tiered fee discounts and loss rebates

Add DEEP staking to the Predict package. DEEP is locked in the Registry
(Balance<DEEP> custody); each PredictManager mirrors its locked amount and
lock-end timestamp. Staking power is computed live as
staked_DEEP * min(remaining_lock / 365d, 1)^2 — it decays as the lock runs
down, the period weight saturates at 1 beyond a year, and power is uncapped.

Power grants two tiered benefits (10k-DEEP power per tier):
- Trading-fee discount: +5% per tier, capped at 50%, applied to the protocol
  fee at mint and live redeem (margin only, never payout backing).
- Loss rebate: +10% of the eligible rebate per tier, capped at 100%; the
  un-granted remainder compounds entirely into PLP idle balance.

Leverage is not gated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: express stake_tier_step via deep_decimals constant

Make the 10k-DEEP tier step explicit as 10_000 * deep_decimals!() instead of a
raw 10_000_000_000 literal, and add deep_decimals (1e6 raw units per DEEP).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: linear staking benefits, 2-year horizon, emit fee discount

- Replace the stepped 10k-DEEP tiers with a linear ramp: fee discount and loss
  rebate scale with power and reach their max (50% / 100%) at max_benefit_power
  (100k DEEP), capped above it.
- Move the staking-power lock horizon from 1 year to 2 years: full weight needs
  a 2-year lock; longer locks still saturate at 1.
- Emit the applied fee-discount fraction on the FeeAccrued trade event.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: hard-reject DEEP stake locks longer than 2 years

Add max_lock_days (derived from the 2-year horizon) and assert lock_days is
within 1..=max_lock_days in stake_deep, so locks past the cap abort with
EInvalidLockDays instead of silently saturating.

claim_trading_loss_rebate is intentionally permissionless — it credits the
manager via its deposit cap and compounds the leftover into PLP cash, so PLP
value accrues without the owner acting. Clarify this in the doc comment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Move the staking benefit threshold out of a compile-time constant into a new
StakeConfig (nested in ProtocolConfig), with a registry AdminCap setter
(set_max_benefit_power) bounded within 1k..10M DEEP. Staking benefit functions

Full weight is reached at a 1-year remaining lock (squared), so 100k DEEP for
1 year = max, 0.5 year = 25% of max. The lock can still run up to 2 years, which
keeps power at the cap for longer as it decays rather than adding weight.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: burn 50% of DEEP on early unstake

Add registry::early_unstake_deep — unstaking before the lock ends burns

ProtectedTreasury path deepbook core uses) and returns the rest to the owner.
Calling it after expiry aborts (EStakeNotLocked); use unstake_deep then.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Record the token::deep::burn(ProtectedTreasury, Coin<DEEP>) pattern (mirrored
from deepbook::pool::burn_deep) and the test setup, learned while adding the
predict early-unstake burn.

don't revert when an account is owed nothing.

Capture the design principle surfaced while scoping multi-asset PLP yield:
distributing reward assets to a freely-transferable share Coin requires either
locking it (acc-per-share + reward_debt) or folding rewards into redemption

* predict: remodel DEEP staking to epoch active/inactive (no lock, no burn)

Replace the time-lock/live-power model with DeepBook-core-style epoch staking:
- PredictManager tracks active_stake/inactive_stake/stake_epoch; update_stake
  rolls inactive -> active on the first interaction in a new epoch (run by
  mint/redeem/claim).
- stake_deep adds to inactive (activates next epoch); unstake_deep returns all
  active+inactive at any time, no penalty, no burn. Removed early_unstake_deep,
  the 50% burn, ProtectedTreasury, and the lock/horizon constants.
- Benefits are linear in active_stake: ratio = min(active_stake / max_benefit_power, 1);
  fee discount up to 50%, rebate up to 100%; stake above the max earns no extra.
  max_benefit_power stays admin-configurable (default 100k DEEP).

(bounded 0-100%, default 100%) out of compile-time constants into StakeConfig,

* rules: lazily-rolled epoch state is stale until its update runs

Capture the gotcha from the predict epoch-staking remodel: active_stake only
reflects the current epoch right after update_stake(ctx); call it before reading,
treat the bare getter as possibly stale, and note the == epoch guard is safe
because epochs are monotonic (skipped epochs still roll on the next interaction).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: two-tier benefit curve (lower/upper stake thresholds)

Replace the single max_benefit_power with a two-segment benefit curve: the
benefit ratio rises 0->50% of max over 0..lower_benefit_power, then 50%->100%
over lower..upper_benefit_power, capped above. Both thresholds are admin-tunable

default 1.1M; invariant upper > 2*lower so the upper segment is shallower).

10% up to 100% at 1.1M.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: hold staked DEEP custody in PoolVault instead of Registry

Move the pooled staked_deep Balance<DEEP> (grouped with the other vault
balances, after insurance_fee_balance) and the stake_deep/unstake_deep
entrypoints into plp::PoolVault. Per-manager active/inactive accounting stays on

subject: predict: admin SUI/DEEP incentive assets for the PLP pool
body:
Admin can donate SUI or DEEP into the PLP pool as LP-owned incentives that vest
linearly over a window. No PLP is minted: the vested value accrues to existing
holders pro-rata and the asset accrues to them in-kind.

- Two fixed incentive assets (SUI, DEEP) held as named IncentiveState fields on
  PoolVault. Pinning the set (vs an open generic set) lets withdraw return
  (Coin<DUSDC>, Coin<SUI>, Coin<DEEP>) directly and drops the WithdrawalReceipt
  hot potato, dynamic-field + TypeName machinery, and per-type claim calls.
  DEEP incentive is a separate balance from staked_deep (manager custody).
- Linear streaming (slush-style): each IncentiveState holds a locked balance
  vesting into a released balance over [last_compound_ms, end_ms]. compound()
  moves locked * elapsed / remaining on wall-clock time, run lazily on supply,
  withdraw, and receive_*_incentive (a new deposit vests the prior schedule,
  then rolls the remainder into a fresh window). Duration in (0, max] (365 days).
- Only the released balance enters NAV, so the share price itself is the
  accumulator: a new supplier pays for already-vested value and can't dilute
  holders, and an instant supply+withdraw cannot capture the still-locked
  remainder (compounding advances on wall-clock time only).
- Incentives are fully decoupled from PoolSync: PoolSync is expiry-only and
  finish_pool_sync returns just the DUSDC value. supply values both incentives
  inline (value_incentives: vest + price each non-empty asset from its bound,
  fresh feed, skipping empty) and prices shares against DUSDC + incentive value.
  No sync_incentives step, no per-asset sync bookkeeping. supply takes the two
  feed sources + Clock; withdraw pays incentives in-kind (no oracle, no sources)
  so a stale feed can't block exits.
- Valuation reuses the option-pricing oracle structure (no incentive_oracle
  module): pyth_source::value_in_dusdc converts the released balance from the
  source's 1e9 spot into DUSDC units; the binding (feed + decimals) is asserted
  via EIncentiveFeedMismatch and freshness via pricing::assert_pyth_spot_fresh.
- Registry: deposit_sui_incentive / deposit_deep_incentive cache the binding
  into the vault.
- simulations: supply/withdraw pass the (ignored, incentive-free) sources + Clock.

rationale: The change adds new admin incentive functionality and updates transaction helper signatures; it does not correct previously incorrect behavior nor address a security vulnerability.

subject: predict: PredictManager cap system + self-owned constructor (DBU-413) (#1042)
body:
Mirror BalanceManager's cap pattern on PredictManager so contracts can
hold and trade through a manager without owning the sender key.

- Add PredictTradeCap / PredictDepositCap / PredictWithdrawCap (owner-
  minted, tracked in a per-manager allow_listed VecSet), plus a per-tx
  PredictTradeProof generated by the owner or any PredictTradeCap holder.
  Cap mints emit Predict{Trade,Deposit,Withdraw}CapMinted events; revoke
  is uniform across cap types.
- Stash the inner BalanceManager WithdrawCap on PredictManager alongside
  the existing DepositCap. All custody routes through these inner caps so
  the inner BM owner check never trips from a cap holder's call.
- expiry_market::mint now requires &PredictTradeProof. Redeem is split
  into `redeem` (requires a PredictTradeProof; works on live or already-
  resolved orders, dropping the proof when no payout authority is needed)
  and a permissionless `redeem_settled` (settled / liquidated cleanup,
  no proof; aborts EProofRequiredForLiveRedeem on a still-live order). A
  private redeem_internal holds the shared lifecycle dispatch. Settle-mint
  / settle-live-redeem internals route the fee withdraw / payout deposit
  through the proof.
- predict_manager::new_self_owned (via registry::create_self_owned_manager)
  sets the inner BalanceManager owner to the manager's own ID-as-address
  using balance_manager::new_with_custom_owner_caps_v2. ctx.sender() can
  never match, so owner-direct paths are permanently unreachable and the
  caps returned at construction are the only authority on this manager.
  Intended for vaults / custodial products that don't want a deployer-key
  trust anchor.
- Reserve PredictManagerKey slot 0 for sender-owned managers, slot 1 for
  self-owned, named in constants::{sender,self}_owned_manager_slot!() so
  the reservation is documented in one place.
- 8 new predict_manager unit tests covering cap mint / revoke, proof
  generation by owner and by trade-cap holder, and cross-manager proof
  rejection, plus a flow test asserting redeem_settled rejects a live order.

Requires deepbook admin to authorize PredictApp on the deepbook Registry
via authorize_app<PredictApp> before new_self_owned can run on chain.

subject: Block same-timestamp Predict mint and redeem (DBU-472) (#1085)
body:
* Block same-timestamp Predict mint and redeem

Record each position's open time (clock.timestamp_ms()) at mint and reject
a live redeem whose timestamp equals it. A single transaction reads one
Clock, so this closes the atomic mint -> oracle-update -> redeem arbitrage
that would round-trip a freshly minted order against a price the same tx
pushed. The open time is carried forward across partial-close replacements,
so seasoned positions stay closable in multiple steps.

DPU-472

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Unit-test the same-timestamp redeem guard

Move the open-time comparison into a factual predict_account assertion
(assert_not_opened_at, owning the open-time state) so the abort path is
covered by running unit tests instead of only the disabled flow test:
the same-timestamp abort (ESameTimestampRedeem), the missing-position
abort, and the pass case that reads back the stored open time.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Keep redeem-timestamp policy in expiry_market

predict_account is position state only: expose a position_opened_at_ms
getter and move the same-timestamp redeem assertion back into
expiry_market::redeem_live_internal (EMintRedeemSameTimestamp), where the
redeem flow owns the policy. The getter keeps its missing-position unit
coverage; the abort path is covered by the disabled flow test.
