subject: harness: C-1 flush ceiling is the object-cache limit, not compute (#1105)
body:
* Stress-run harness changes: allocation-cap raise + nav-stress-nodes strategy

Capacity-stress sizing so the gas wall binds before the capital wall
(the pool-total run previously OOG'd entangled with EInsufficientCash),
plus the payout-tree probe strategy (wide strike spread toward the
1,000-node cap, distinct-strike tracing). Used by the 2026-07-06 C-1
campaign; findings PR follows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* harness: decouple keeper settlement from the flush (fixes retention brick)

The keeper did flush+settle in one PTB, so a BS live-pricing outage that
aborted the flush also reverted the settlement inserts; expired markets
piled up unsettled until their exact-expiry prices aged out of Pyth-history
retention and every flush bricked on a missing dynamic field (2026-07-06
campaign, nav-stress-nodes / batch-max-markets). Split into two PTBs:
keeperSettleTx (per market: insert exact spot + rebalance_expiry_cash ->
ensure_settled -> sweep; needs only the Pyth spot, no BS pricing) runs
first, then the flush values the post-settle active set. A BS outage now
defers only the flush; settlement keeps clearing every tick. Mirrors the
production keeper's decoupled lanes (deepbook-services decision 0010).

Also folds in: honest stall diagnostics (consecutiveSettleDefers tracks
real settlement stalls, not flush OOGs; the stall log reports the actual
error tag, not the hardcoded "Pyth-history outage" guess; failures tagged
by lane). And FLUSH_GAS_BUDGET 50e9 -> 15e9: signExecThreaded pins one
gas coin per sender, and a 50e9 floor starved the keeper's shrinking coin
(219 gas-starved flushes); 15e9 stays above the 5e9 computation cap so the
nav-stress breakpoint is preserved while ~tripling the coin's runway
(runway mitigation, not a full gas-coin fix).

Validated: nav-stress campaign, bug oracle clean, settle/flush distinct
(4/4), 0 stalls, nav-stress gas curve intact, NAV stable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* harness: fix keeper gas starvation (refill floor above budget)

Root cause of the 219 gas-starved flush submits (batch run 2026-07-06):
signExecThreaded pins one gas coin per sender, so the keeper's flush coin
can't self-top-up; meanwhile the refill loop's floor was 2e9 — far below
the 50e9 flush budget — so the coin dropped under budget but stayed way
above the refill trigger, and with no other coin to gas-smash against it
starved permanently. Fix: raise GAS_REFILL_FLOOR to 30e9 (above the
keeper's budget, so the coin is topped up before it drops under), and give
the keeper process a modest SIM_GAS_BUDGET (15e9) so its cheap
settle/liquidate/rebalance/roll txs don't each demand a 50e9 coin under a
large trader batch budget. Completes the FLUSH_GAS_BUDGET change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* harness: settle in a bounded loop so mid-tick expiries don't defer the flush

The decoupled flush reads the active set after the settle pass, so a market
expiring DURING that pass was still active-but-unsettled at flush time and
tripped ensure_settled (dynamic_field borrow) -> the flush deferred one tick
(boundary race). Widened vs the old coupled code because the flush read is
later in the tick. Fix: factor settleExpired(feeds) (fresh clock + active
read each call) and loop it (bounded 3 passes) until nothing is past-expiry,
then flush — so stragglers are swept before the flush values them. Cuts the
boundary-race deferrals to near-zero, tightening the wall's uncertainty band.
Self-recovering behavior unchanged; a real settlement stall still surfaces.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* harness: flush re-inserts straggler observations (replace the settle loop)

The 3-pass settle loop (prior commit) backfired: each pass adds latency, so
in high-churn batch-max-markets far more markets expired DURING the loop —
58 flush deferrals. Root cause was deeper: decoupling REMOVED the flush's
observation inserts, so any past-expiry market in the flush's active set
aborts value_expiry (dynamic_field). Fix: single durable settle pass (lane,
brick fix) + the flush re-inserts exact-expiry observations for boundary-race
stragglers (past-expiry active at flush time) so value_expiry settles them
inline. Verified 7-min: deferrals 58->4, dynamic_field brick gone, gas clean,
book growing. Residual: a market expiring during the flush's own execution
window (grows with book size) — the inherent race the original harness also
had; not fully eliminable without flush-retry or an oracle-classification change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* harness: surface the real VM error on PTB abort + object-cache repro strategies

A framework-level MovePrimitiveRuntimeError in 0x2::dynamic_field::borrow_child_object
names only the framework fn, and errorTag truncated it to 120 chars, so the trace,
console, and bug oracle all showed a meaningless string. The true cause sat in the saved
failed-tx artifact's dry-run executionErrorSource the whole time ("Object runtime cached
objects limit (1000 entries) reached") — the C-1 flush ceiling was chased for days off the
truncated framework string. Now runtime.ts prints the VM error live on every failed tx, and
the analyze bug oracle prints the distinct executionErrorSource behind flagged framework
aborts.

Adds two repro strategies for the object-cache ceiling: tree-node-sweep (single 1x market,
distinct strikes -> isolates payout-tree node count with zero leverage pages) and
tree-node-cumulative (two markets ~600 nodes each -> proves the cache is cumulative across
the flush PTB, not per-command). predict-harness rule updated: read executionErrorSource on
a PTB abort, and sui move test does not enforce execution-layer limits (object cache / gas /
object size) — reproduce those on localnet.

* predict-predeploy: correct C-1 binding wall to the object-cache limit

The 2026-07-01 model called the pool flush computation-bound (the 5M compute cap). It is
not: the pool-total wall is the Sui object-runtime cached-objects limit (1000 dynamic-field
children per tx), which binds at 16-50% of the compute cap. Earlier pool-total runs hit
expiry_cash::EInsufficientCash (capital) before reaching it; raising the allocation cap
exposed the object wall. Driver = distinct payout-tree nodes (one Table child per strike
tick, walk_linear loads every node), cumulative across the flush PTB.

Corrects the C-1 capacity model and fix options, marks the payout-tree probe done, and adds
evidence/c1-object-cache-flush-2026-07-07.md (batch-max-markets repro + tree-node-sweep
causation + tree-node-cumulative scoping). No Move change; the fix stays open on C-1.

* harness: address review nits — scope gas-budget comment, fix _vm_errors abort filter

Two LOW findings from the PR review:
- keeperService FLUSH_GAS_BUDGET comment claimed the pool flush OOGs at the 5e9 compute
  cap; that holds only for the single dense nav-stress market. The pool total binds earlier
  on the object-cache limit (C-1) at ~16-50% of the cap. Scoped the comment accordingly.
- analyze._vm_errors filtered MoveAborts by "MoveAbort" not in executionErrorSource, but a
  guard MoveAbort's executionErrorSource reads "status ABORTED" (no MoveAbort token) while
  status.error carries MoveAbort(...); guard aborts would have leaked into the VM-error
  summary. Now filters on "status ABORTED" in src OR "MoveAbort" in status.error. Verified
  on the batch-max-markets artifacts: 3 MEMORY_LIMIT errors surfaced, 14 guard aborts excluded.

* harness: strategies declare their probed wall; oracle whitelists it (expected-outcome B)

A stress strategy that deliberately probes a capacity ceiling (e.g. the object-cache flush
limit) was flagged as a bug by the oracle — the tree-node-sweep run's own expected aborts made
its verdict FAIL. Fix: Strategy.expect declares the terminal wall(s) it probes; the runner emits
them as a trace record; analyze whitelists a declared abort for THAT run only (never globall
rationale: The commit fixes a bug where a combined keeper flush+settle could be aborted by a pricing outage, causing settlement inserts to be reverted and the system to brick on a missing dynamic field, leading to a denial‑of‑service condition. Decoupling settlement from flush prevents the buildup of unsettled markets and restores availability, addressing a resource‑exhaustion DoS issue.

subject: predict: drift becomes a measured fact; acceptance moves to the pool level
body:
Restructure per the PLP-price framing: the guarantee we actually want is
'flush PLP price within a bound of the fresh-walk price', whose only
correct denominator is pool NAV — so per-market acceptance is the wrong
altitude.

- valuation_mark is now a dumb tracker: liability walk + trade deltas +
  drift(pricer) measuring potential dollar NAV drift since the walk. It
  owns no acceptance policy and no config.
- expiry_market exposes three dumb facts via individual getters:
  free_cash, marked_liability, mark_drift(pricer), plus mark_computed_at_ms.
- plp aggregates all three per market, asserts the freshness ceiling per
  mark (the one guard a stalled feed cannot fool), and judges drift ONLY
  in aggregate at finish_flush: total_drift vs pool NAV.
- Probe machinery removed from this head; it returns as the internal
  implementation of drift() when the model lands.

INTERIM: drift() returns 0 and the aggregate check is a documented no-op
— this head has freshness-only protection. Draft-only state; the drift
model and threshold land next.

rationale: The change restructures valuation and drift handling, removes a flushable check, and adds new getters without altering any validation logic or fixing a previously exploitable condition. It appears to be a refactor rather than a bug fix, and no security-relevant behavior is introduced or corrected.

subject: predict: fill in drift(pricer) — closed-form oracle-drift envelope
body:
The mark snapshots raw anchors at the walk (forward + SVI params; raw so
the formula can evolve without stored state aging, and both sides derive
through the same code at read time). drift(pricer) returns
pricing::drift_envelope between anchor and live: an upper bound on any
single contract's price move, in fractions of full payout, built from the
normal curve's max slope (0.4) times a term-by-term bound on the worst d2
move — forward shift over the variance floor, plus one Lipschitz charge
per SVI parameter delta over the strike band where prices are not pinned.
Every term is zero when nothing moved; degenerate surfaces (zero floor,
wing slope near 1, absurd band) return full face, fail-closed. Bound by
construction: the surface IS these six numbers, so there is no strike
between samples to hide a reshape in.

Not yet charged (documented): the skew-correction term's own drift and
the ulp tail beyond the pad — both to be priced by the envelope
validation measurements. plp aggregation/enforcement unchanged (stub).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds new macros and functions to compute a drift envelope and related utilities, but does not modify existing logic to correct a previously incorrect behavior. It appears to be a new feature/extension rather than a bug fix, and no security-relevant vulnerability is addressed.

subject: predict: charge the skew correction in the drift envelope; complete the bound
body:
The implemented price subtracts phi(d2) * w'(k) / (2 sqrt(w)); the clamp
is 1-Lipschitz, so |dP| <= |dN(d2)| + |d correction|. Three new legs
charge the correction's drift: phi_max times the w' change (per-parameter
Lipschitz, sigma-floored), phi_max times the sqrt(w) change scaled by the
correction's max height, and that height times the density's own move
(phi's slope <= 0.25 times the already-bounded d2 move).

Structural fix found during derivation: 'prices pinned outside |d2| = 4'
is false for the skew-adjusted price — deep-wing corrections can pull
prices off their pins (the P-11 mechanism) — so the band threshold now
widens dynamically until phi(D) decays past the correction's max height.

Hardening: the term assembly moves to u128 with a single fail-closed cap
at full face, so envelope-corner surfaces saturate the drift instead of
aborting mid-flush; sub-1e-4 variance floors (sub-seconds to expiry or
degenerate surfaces) fail closed early.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The diff adds explicit floors, caps, and u128 arithmetic to the drift envelope calculation, preventing overflow/abort conditions that could produce incorrect pricing or transaction failures. Such mispricing can be exploited for profit or cause denial‑of‑service, making it a security‑relevant bug fix.

finish_flush enforces the budget for real: total accepted worst-case

fill at is within the configured fraction of the fresh-recalculation

subject: predict: price drift into the flush mark as a bid/ask spread; kill the threshold
body:
The flush mark becomes two-sided: supplies price the pool at mid NAV plus
the counted marks' combined worst-case drift, withdrawals at mid minus it.
The true pool value provably sits inside the interval, so the transacting
party bears the marks' staleness, incumbents can be neither diluted nor
drained, and a same-flush round trip strictly loses the spread — stale-NAV
arbitrage dies by construction. Fully fresh marks collapse the spread to
the exact single mark.

Deleted: the aggregate drift threshold, its error code, and the
nav_mark_drift_epsilon knob with its constants and setter — the spread is
fully determined by the measured bound, so there is no tolerance left to
configure. ValuationConfig shrinks to the freshness ceiling (the stalled-
feed backstop no spread can replace). The pool_nav == 0 open edge
dissolves: nothing asserts against a zero budget; a degenerate bid just
refunds through the existing non-executable path. Wide spreads self-
resolve through each request's own min-out limit (miss, carry, refund).
Flush availability becomes unconditional.

subject: predict: fix review Criticals — anchor-priced write-through, band under-coverage; add vault revision guard
body:
Review findings on the drift machinery (2 Critical understatements, 1 High
isolation defect, 1 Medium abort path, comment drift):

- CRITICAL anchor consistency: write-through deltas were valued at each
  op's own oracle, which endpoint drift cannot bound (an oracle round trip
  between refresh and flush leaves near-zero endpoint drift while a
  peak-priced mint stays in the sum). Deltas are now valued at the mark's
  STORED anchors: hooks pass the added/removed orders themselves and
  valuation_mark prices their ranges at anchor_svi/anchor_forward, so the
  marked liability is a single-anchor valuation of the current book and
  quantity x endpoint-envelope provably bounds it. Liquidation paths
  return the knocked-out Orders; redeems remove the original and re-add
  any partial-close remainder, both anchor-priced.
- CRITICAL band under-coverage: unpinned_band's round-down chain could
  collapse the quadratic to W <= A and return K = 0 at low variance
  (review counterexample: drift understated ~13.6x). The band now takes
  max(quadratic + 10% + pad, analytic slope-free floor D*sqrt(A) + A/2 +
  10% + pad) — over-covering is conservative-safe.
- HIGH same-PTB isolation: with the valuation lock gone, a vault-cash op
  (rebalance/sweep/claim) composed between collection and finish could
  desynchronize collected atoms from live idle (double-count or omit
  moved cash). The ledger now carries a revision counter bumped on every
  cash movement; the potato snapshots it at start and finish_flush
  asserts it unchanged. Trade flows (account<->market cash) remain
  outside the guard: their collected-atom miss nets to fee dust.
- MEDIUM: extreme forward ratios guard-return full face before math::div
  can overflow-abort (increase direction now fails closed like decrease).
- Identical snapshots return exactly 0 drift (no tail pad), so an atomic
  refresh-and-flush PTB reproduces the old exact-single-mark behavior.
- Stale comments: budget/threshold language updated to spread semantics;
  FlushExecuted doc re-attached to the right struct.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The commit replaces value‑based liability removal with order‑based anchor‑priced removal, fixing a critical under‑estimation of liability that could be exploited to cause under‑collateralized liquidations and fund loss. This logical error is a security defect (financial tampering) and the change is a bug fix.

subject: predict: fail closed when band rounding swallows the strike band
body:
With a real wing slope the true band W strictly exceeds A, so a computed
w_minus_a of zero is always a round-down artifact (the low-variance
ill-conditioned corner; reviewed counterexample understated drift 13.6x
through an empty band). Detect it and return none — drift_envelope
charges full face, the market prices at its worst case, and a refresh
re-anchors it. No abort: the flush lands, the degenerate market's
uncertainty is priced into the spread, and other markets are unaffected.
Partial rounding shrinkage (band reduced but nonzero) is deliberately
left to the envelope-validation measurement before any further hardening.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The diff adds a guard that returns none when w_minus_a == 0, fixing a bug where rounding could produce a degenerate band and allow mispricing. The previous unchecked case could be exploited to obtain favorable pricing, leading to financial loss, thus a security-relevant fix (improper input validation, CWE-20) with high severity.

subject: predict: guard the flush potato against interleaved cash moves
body:
The flush potato reads each market's free cash at its collect and pool
idle at finish. An internal cash move composed between those commands in
the flush PTB itself (rebalance_expiry_cash is permissionless; PTB
atomicity blocks everyone else) lands the moved amount in both reads or
neither, double- or under-counting it in the priced NAV and letting a
pre-queued LP request fill at the corrupted mark.

Add a cash_revision counter on the vault Ledger, bumped inside the
internal-transfer primitives (send_expiry_cash, receive_expiry_cash,
realize_pending_protocol_profit) so an untracked move is unrepresentable.
start_pool_valuation snapshots it into the potato; finish_flush asserts
it unchanged (ECashMovedDuringValuation), aborting the malformed PTB.
Mint/redeem stay exempt: they move external cash and its liability
write-through in one bucket at one instant, coherent whenever read.

Review finding 3 (flush cash isolation), approved disposition.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The change adds a cash_revision counter and asserts it unchanged between start_pool_valuation and finish_flush, preventing internal cash moves from interleaving and corrupting NAV calculations. Previously, an attacker could reorder internal cash transfers to double‑ or under‑count cash, enabling profitable front‑running of LP requests, a clear security issue.

Six verified reductions from the algebraic-simplicity sweep, all
behavior-identical or <=1-ulp pool-side: expiry_fee_multiplier and
benefit_ratio fused to single mul_div_down; is_executable_mark reduced
to a u128 cross-multiplied band test; compute_nd2 strike-ratio widening

subject: predict: anchor-price the valuation-mark write-through, move the mark into strike_exposure
body:
The mark's write-through deltas were the op's own priced amounts
(net_premium, redeem_amount, swept liquidation values). Endpoint drift
between the stored anchors and the flush oracle cannot bound values
priced at a third, intermediate oracle state: a round trip that spikes at
trade time and returns by flush leaves near-zero endpoint drift while the
peak-priced delta stays in the sum (review Critical 1).

Re-express every delta in the anchor basis instead. An order's terms
(boundary ticks, quantity, floor) fully determine its value at any oracle
state, so hooks now value the affected orders at the mark's stored
anchors: the marked liability stays exactly the current book valued at
one snapshot, and quantity x endpoint-envelope provably bounds its
revaluation. The op's execution price touches only cash, which the flush
reads live and exact. pricing::from_anchors rebuilds a Pricer from the
stored anchors, so the existing pricing surface (range_price,
gross_order_value) is the single evaluator — no parallel anchor-pricing
formula. The delta uses walk semantics (gross - floor, floored at zero),
not order_value's holder-close zeroing of liquidatable orders: the walk
carries a liquidatable-yet-unliquidated order's value until an actual
knock-out removes it, and the write-through must round-trip the walk.

The mark also moves from ExpiryMarket into StrikeExposure, next to the
only state it tracks: every book mutation (mint insert, live-redeem
close/replace, liquidation knock-out) now writes through inside one
module, deleting expiry_market's six scattered hook sites and the u64
plumbing that threaded liquidation values out solely to feed the mark.
ExpiryMarket keeps thin forwarders and the pricer-to-market binding
check; the plp flush surface is unchanged.

Review finding 1 (write-through anchoring), approved disposition.

rationale: [MEV] The commit removes incorrect write‑through of valuation marks and moves the liability accounting into StrikeExposure, fixing a misvaluation bug that could let an attacker exploit price spikes between oracle reads, leading to financial loss. This is a behavior‑changing fix with security impact (incorrect accounting), thus a security fix of high severity.

subject: predict: restate the pricing basis envelope as a factor; single-read builder code on redeem (DBU-566)

This corrects a correctness defect that could be exploited to cause transaction failures or financial loss.

subject: predict: delete implied and duplicate asserts; implied-assert rule (DBU-566 Tier B group 1)

Four provably-redundant asserts removed with the implication stated at

duplicates of assert_valid_order_shape, same error code), cadence
admission >= tick (forced by positivity + divisibility), the trailing

in-diff implication comments; no response-policy entry because no
response changes.

New Validation And Ownership rule: implied asserts are deletable only
when their premises are same-scope asserts or upgrade-required bounds,
never admin-tunable values. B7's quantity-lots bound deliberately kept:
it is the packing leaf's own domain guard (leaf self-consistency), and
assert_valid_order_shape's lower-tick bound kept (deleting shifts an
abort code on one input slice).

subject: predict: pin the 15 measured drift-envelope violations in the parity vectors
body:
The DBU-557 sweep over 11 days of captured BTC oracle history found 15
exact-confirmed pairs where the chain's own fixed-point up_price moves MORE
than drift_envelope allows — all in one regime: near-expiry 5m surfaces at
ultra-low total variance (w ~ 1e-7, sigma at the pricing-safe minimum),
identical SVI between snapshots, forward moves of ~2e-8 relative. Mechanism:
one ulp of fixed-point total variance moves the price by
~phi(d2)*|k|/(2*w^1.5)*1e-9, which exceeds the envelope's 1.5e-4 tail pad
below w ~ 5e-6; observed exceedances reach 4.3e-4 of face. These vectors
embed the violating pairs (real forwards, violating strike), so this test
now certifies the violating numbers through the production oracle ingest:
|up0 - up1| > envelope on chain. The envelope needs a quantization-aware
term or a higher variance floor — tracked with the measurement report.

set covered only the quantity intent — the budget intent had to convert
budget->quantity before the gate, which required leaking the priced
entry probability out through quote_mint_entry_probability (sole
consumer: the sizing helper) and re-pricing the identical range inside
the gate: up to 4 compute_nd2 evaluations per mint_exact_amount where 2
suffice, on the gas-amplified batched-mint path.

quote_mint_terms_for_amount is the second full constructor — price
once, invert the budget, lot-clamp, full admission — one constructor
per user intent. The peephole API and the expiry_market sizing helper
are deleted: nothing exports a raw priced fact, so the single-entry
invariant is now structural. The shared funnel tail is extracted as
mint_prepared_terms (demonstrated duplication).

gate before the caller's min_quantity floor, so a dust budget aborts
ENetPremiumBelowMinimum instead of EMintQuantityBelowMin; the guard
test moves to a real budget + high floor, keeping EMintQuantityBelowMin
coverage. Rule added to predict-contracts.md (intent-complete terms
gates, no priced-fact exports); H-5's double-pricing bullet resolved.

subject: predict: close gate covers its outcome space — LiveCloseTerms (DBU-566, C2+C4a)
body:
The close side had C1's disease in the outcome-space direction: the
intent "close this order at the current price" has two priced outcomes
(live close, knock-out), but close_and_quote_live_order covered only the
first — the flow classified knock-outs in a separate pre-gate pricing
call (liquidate_live_order on the target) whose result it then ignored,
re-pricing the identical range inside the gate and round-tripping a
tombstone through the table on knock-out.

(LiveCloseTerms::KnockedOut | LiveClose — the package's first enum),
pure so flow policy runs pre-mutation; close_live_order consumes it by
value and applies the priced transition, mirroring the mint side's
quote/allocate split. An immediate knock-out removes the full (Q,F),
emits OrderLiquidated, and records no tombstone (the holder is redeeming
in the same transaction); the shared zero-payout account tail is
extracted. The under-floor predicate is single-homed (it was expressed
at three sites). C4a: emit_order_liquidated reads quantity/floor_shares
from the Order it already receives; event schema unchanged.

Behavior parity: slippage floors and the same-timestamp guard still gate
only the live-priced path (knock-out bypass preserved); both events
emitted on knock-out; the same-timestamp/close-quantity abort order is
unchanged (quantity validation stays in the consuming close).
liquidation.md documents the no-tombstone immediate case; outcome-space
gate rule added to predict-contracts.md.

subject: margin: add place_reduce_only_market_order_and_repay_loan (#1035)
body:
* margin: add place_reduce_only_market_order_and_repay_loan

Bundles a reduce-only market order with a loan repayment so a leveraged
position can be wound down atomically. The standalone reduce-only entry
checks risk_ratio on the swap-only state, before any repay — a market
close pays the spread, which strictly lowers the oracle-valued ratio and
aborts. Repaying first deleverages the manager, lifting the ratio and
absorbing the slippage; the monotonic check then passes on the net state.
Slippage stays bounded by the price-tolerance band, so deferring the
solvency check past the repay does not weaken security.

This is also the only wind-down path for a manager whose ratio has
drifted into the liquidation..min_borrow danger zone: it cannot reach the
borrow floor in a single swap, but it can climb out by deleveraging.

Exposes margin_manager::risk_ratio_int and ::repay as public(package) so
pool_proxy can compute the single-debt-pool risk ratio and repay; both
were already the internal impls (no new wrappers).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin: address review - keep repay in place, drop redundant settle

- Keep `repay` at its original location, only widening it to public(package)
  (minimal in-place visibility change rather than a relocation).
- Drop the post-trade `withdraw_settled_amounts` call: `place_market_order`
  already settles the taker fill into the manager's balance via
  `vault.settle_balance_manager`, so the proceeds are drawable by `repay`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin: take both pools in close-and-repay; no margin_manager changes

Rework the entry to take both margin pools (distinct objects, so no &mut
aliasing) and use the existing public `risk_ratio` (two-pool) and
`repay_base`/`repay_quote`, mirroring `place_reduce_only_market_order_v2`.

This reverts margin_manager.move entirely: `risk_ratio_int` and `repay`
stay private — no public(package) widening was needed. Also tightens the
entry's doc comment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin: gross-holdings cap for reduce-only exit (asymmetric ask/bid)

Move the reduce-only quantity cap from net debt to gross holdings so a
position can be fully unwound: the ask (closing a long) may sell up to the
full base the manager holds, while the bid (covering a short) stays capped
at the net short (base_debt - base_asset) so it cannot flip into a fresh
long. Applied to place_reduce_only_limit_order_v2 and the close-and-repay
entry. Document place_reduce_only_market_order_v2 as superseded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Capture the flip-into-fresh-long bug and why the unwind cap must be gross
on the selling side but net on the buying side.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin: min_open_risk_ratio — separate opening floor from borrow floor (#2)

Opening near-max leverage aborted because the post-trade solvency check
reused min_borrow (1.25), leaving no room for the opening trade's spread.
Add a per-pool min_open_risk_ratio floor between liquidation and min_borrow:
assert_post_trade_solvent now checks against it instead. Default is the
midpoint of liquidation and min_borrow, stored as an optional dynamic-field
override (mirrors MaxOrderTtlKey) that self-heals if a later risk-param
change strands it. Admin-set via set_min_open_risk_ratio.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(move rules): open floor (min_open_risk_ratio) distinct from borrow floor

Capture why the post-trade open floor must differ from the borrow gate and
the self-healing derived-default override pattern.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin: v3 conditional execution — deleverage so stops fire in danger band (#8, #10)

Add execute_conditional_orders_v3: takes the margin pools as &mut and, after
each market-type conditional fill, repays the loan with the proceeds, then gates
on net (post-repay) risk_ratio >= the pre-fill ratio. This lets a stop-loss fire
in the liquidation..min_borrow band — a swap alone only lowers the oracle-valued
ratio, which the v2 borrow-floor gate rejects — and the order executes and is
removed instead of looping the bot (#10). v2 is left unchanged for upgrade
compatibility; integrators migrate to v3.

Move the repay owner check from the internal repay into the public repay_base/
repay_quote wrappers so the permissionless executor can deleverage (safe: repay
only moves the manager's own funds against its own debt). Share the
collect/place/finalize helpers between the v2 and v3 executors.

* docs(move rules): v3 conditional deleverage + upgrade-compat _vN rule

Capture why danger-band stops must deleverage (not just swap), the

Clarify on add_conditional_order that the conditional itself never expires;

* margin: tests for free-borrowed-funds order (#3) and limit-type SL via v3 (#8)

Close the two coverage gaps from the audit: a normal order placed with free
borrowed funds in the [min_open, min_borrow) band succeeds (#3), and a

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin: add place_market_order_and_repay_loan + reduce-only min_size floor

Add a non-reduce-only place_market_order_and_repay_loan: place a market order,

close/deleverage tool — a full close drives debt to 0 (risk_ratio MAX) so it

min_size) — so a sub-lot net debt isn't stuck in reduce-only (margin-disabled)

* margin: reduce-only bid cap rounds net short up to the next lot

Change the reduce-only bid cap from net.max(min_size) to reduce_only_bid_cap =

Limit sibling of place_reduce_only_market_order_and_repay_loan: places a limit

subject: ci: make the Move format check actually check the Move files (#1126)
body:
* ci: make the Move format check actually check the Move files

The check passed on 45 of the repo's 182 Move files. Three defects, each of
which silently narrowed it:

- The glob `packages/predict/**/*.move` ran unquoted in bash, where globstar is
  off by default, so `**` collapsed to `*` and matched exactly one directory
  level. sources/config/, sources/events/, sources/strike_exposure/ and every
  nested test directory were never checked. Quoting it hands expansion to
  prettier, which recurses.
- Only four packages were enumerated. account, propbook, block_scholes_oracle,
  fixed_math, token, dusdc, dbtc and deepbook_core_account were checked by
  nothing, and a new package would have been added unchecked. One glob over
  packages/ covers them and cannot go stale.
- `npm i @mysten/prettier-plugin-move` ignored the lockfile and installed
  whatever was latest, so CI enforced 0.4.0 while package.json declared ^0.3.5 —
  a version that range excludes. A plugin release could turn unrelated PRs red.
  Installing via the lockfile makes the version a deliberate, reviewable bump.

Bumps the plugin to 0.4.0 to match what CI was already enforcing, rather than
downgrading CI to the stale declaration. Adds .prettierignore for Move build
output so a local run sees the same file set as CI's fresh checkout.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: format the Move files the check had never reached

Mechanical `prettier-move --write` under the now-pinned 0.4.0. Trailing commas
in import lists, blank lines between adjacent macros, and one rewrapped call —
no semantic change.

These drifted precisely because the check could not see them. With the glob
fixed they would otherwise fail CI on whatever unrelated PR touched them next,
which is also how they leaked into #1125 as collateral reformatting.

Verified per package: deepbook 381/381, deepbook_margin 372/372, predict
393/393; all three build clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci: point contributors at the pinned formatter, not bunx

Pinning CI was only half the fix. CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and .claude/rules/move.md
all still said `bunx prettier-move`, which resolves whatever plugin version is
latest and so bypasses the lockfile pin from the other side: the next release
would format locally in a way CI rejects, reintroducing exactly the drift this
PR removes.

Adds `format:move` / `format:move:check` scripts and has CI run the check script
itself, so the file set and the plugin version have one definition that CI and
contributors share and cannot diverge from. Docs now say run it before opening a
PR, and say plainly not to use bunx/npx/global prettier/sui move format.

move.md also records why a whole-repo format is safe (the tree is formatted at
HEAD, so it is a no-op outside your own edits) and what it means if it is not:
upstream drift belongs in its own PR, not silently in yours.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

rationale: The commit fixes a CI formatting check that previously missed many Move files due to glob and version issues, correcting the tooling behavior. This is a bug fix in the CI pipeline, but it does not alter runtime logic or introduce security mitigations.

subject: docs(predict): document unreachable abort codes and sentinel field semantics
body:
Third tranche of the DBU-575 sweep. Comment-only; no code changes.

Unreachable abort codes (.claude/rules/unit-tests.md Rule 4 — "for a code that is
genuinely structurally-unreachable in production, document why instead of
contriving a bypass test"). Each was flagged as missing an `expected_failure`
test; each is unreachable at a single package version, so the doc is the correct
remedy rather than a contrived bypass:

- protocol_config::assert_version / `EPackageVersionDisabled` —
  `bump_version_watermark` only ever stores the running `current_version!()`, so
  `version_watermark` can never exceed the version of the package that wrote it,
  and `current_version!() >= version_watermark` always holds. The gate fires only
  after a live upgrade, against a superseded package.
- propbook `EWrongVersion` × 4 (pyth, BS spot/SVI/forward feeds) —
  `create_and_share` stamps the feed with `current_version!()` and `migrate` only
  advances forward to that same compiled constant.

Sentinel and unit semantics (.claude/rules/move.md — comment struct fields with
non-obvious mapping semantics, sentinel values, or units):

- account::Auth — `owner` is meaningful only under `AUTH_OWNER`; under `AUTH_APP`
  it is the `@0x0` sentinel and never read (app authority comes from the
  registry's authorization, not an address here). Previously a bare
  `owner: address` gave no hint that half its states are meaningless.
- order_events::OrderMinted.leverage — 1e9-scaled, 1e9 = 1x, the floor enforced
  at mint (`strike_exposure_config.move:127`). Its neighbour `entry_probability`
  already documented its 1e9 scale; leverage did not.

subject: docs(account): document EInvalidAuth as unreachable; drop a false claim
body:
Independent review caught this stack introducing exactly the defect it exists to
remove: the new `Auth.kind` comment read "anything else is rejected by
`EInvalidAuth`", advertising a rejection path that cannot execute.

`Auth`'s fields are module-private and it has exactly three constructors — two
set `AUTH_OWNER` (:123, :128) and one sets `AUTH_APP` (:288). `load_account_mut`
reaches `assert!(kind == AUTH_APP, EInvalidAuth)` only in the `kind != AUTH_OWNER`
branch, which already implies `AUTH_APP`, so the assert can never fire. No third
kind is constructible, so nothing is ever "rejected" there.

That makes EInvalidAuth unreachable by the same argument this stack applies to
EPackageVersionDisabled and the four propbook EWrongVersion codes — and it was
the one Rule 4 gap left open in a file this stack already edits. Documented as
unreachable (unit-tests.md Rule 4: document why rather than contrive a bypass)
and the field comment corrected to state what is actually true.

Verified: `sui move build --lint` clean (account); account tests pass.

* test(predict): cover the lp_book tail/middle-page unlink relink

`lp_book`'s request queue is a linked list of 64-entry pages. `unlink_empty_page`
relinks neighbors when a page empties, but only the `next = some` branch was
covered: a FIFO drain always empties the head page, so `prev = some` (unlinking a
page while an earlier one still exists) was never exercised. That branch is
reachable via `cancel_supply_request`, which removes by index from any page.

Two tests, both driving real public flows and asserting queue integrity through a
follow-up drain (not the private pointers):
- `cancel_tail_page_request_unlinks_page_and_keeps_queue_drainable` — 65 requests
  (2 pages); cancel the lone tail-page entry, so unlink runs with `prev = some`,
  `next = none`. Then drain must still fill all 64 page-0 requests.
- `cancel_entire_middle_page_relinks_both_neighbors` — 129 requests (3 pages);
  cancel the whole middle page, so unlink runs with BOTH `prev` and `next` some,
  the full double relink. Then drain must reach page 2 only through page 0's
  rewired `next`, filling all 65 survivors.

Negative control: the tail-page test was verified to FAIL against a deliberately
broken relink (`prev.next` pointed at the removed page), so it catches list
corruption rather than passing vacuously.

Verified: predict 423/423 (421 + 2 new); `sui move build --lint` clean;
prettier-move 0.4.0 clean. Test-only; no source change.

Surfaced by the DBU-575 sweep.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(predict): verify the middle-page backward relink (Codex review)

Codex advisory review on 22c34217 flagged that the middle-page test verified only
the forward relink (`page 0.next -> page 2`, observed by the drain reaching page
2). The backward relink (`page 2.prev -> page 0`) was written and then overwritten
by page 0's own later unlink before any read, so a wrong `page 2.prev` passed
silently — a forward drain never reads `.prev`.

Split the single test into one per direction:
- `cancel_middle_page_forward_relinks_predecessor_to_successor` — the original
  drain, unchanged, covering `page 0.next -> page 2`.
- `cancel_middle_page_backward_relinks_successor_to_predecessor` — after emptying
  the middle page, empties page 2 too (its lone index 128). Page 2's unlink reads
  `page 2.prev` while page 0 is still full and untouched, so nothing can overwrite
  it first; if the middle unlink left it pointing at the removed page 1, the
  `borrow_mut` hits a missing page and aborts.

The two directions cannot share one setup: the forward drain and the backward
unlink consume `.next` and `.prev` at mutually exclusive points.

Negative control: the backward test was verified to FAIL against a broken
`next.prev = prev` relink.

Verified: predict 424/424; `sui move build --lint` clean; prettier-move 0.4.0
clean. Test-only.

body:
* feat(deepbook): add place_post_only_limit_order graceful wrapper

Adds a non-aborting wrapper around place_limit_order with POST_ONLY:
- Reads only the opposite side (best_ask for bids, best_bid for asks)
- Returns None instead of aborting when the order would cross
- Empty opposite side always allows placement

Also exposes best_bid_price / best_ask_price as public Option<u64>
getters on Pool, and refactors mid_price to reuse them.

DBU-366

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(deepbook): fix post-only wrapper self-matching to SELF_MATCHING_ALLOWED

The graceful post-only wrapper took a self_matching_option parameter and
forwarded it to place_limit_order. Because the wrapper only ever forwards a
*non-crossing* order, self-matching (which governs how a crossing fill treats
the taker's own maker orders) had no effect on the forwarded placement — the
parameter was dead and misleading. Worse, CANCEL_TAKER would abort
ESelfMatchingCancelTaker against the caller's own expired order at a crossing
price, which the pre-check skips as non-live, re-introducing the very abort the
wrapper exists to avoid.

Drop the parameter and hardcode SELF_MATCHING_ALLOWED (symmetric with the
hardcoded POST_ONLY). A caller that wants to cross and cancel its own resting
orders should call place_limit_order directly. Adds a regression test placing
past the caller's own expired crossing order.

Addresses the cancel-maker/cancel-taker self-match finding from the Codex review.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(deepbook): bound the expired-order scan in mid_price / best-price getters (DBU-594) (#1140)

* fix(deepbook): bound the expired-order scan in mid_price / best-price getters

consistent with what a trade sees (a live order past the cap is unreachable by a

subject: fix(predict): add a backwardation floor to the pricing-safe envelope
body:
The pricing-safe envelope had a basis CEILING (`forward <= factor * spot`, the
contango cap) but no basis FLOOR. `load_live_pricer` re-anchors the live forward
as `mul_div_down(pyth_spot, bs_forward, bs_spot)`, so a tiny `bs_forward` (or large
`bs_spot`) collapses the re-anchored forward toward 0:

- forward small-but-positive (basis ~1e-14): every real strike deep-OTM, so
  compute_nd2 returns 0 for all — every range price 0, mint premium 0. A trader can
  mint real positions for free during the degenerate window (value leak), with NO
  abort. This is the genuinely new hole.
- forward exactly 0: `EZeroForward` deep in compute_up_price.

Fix: add the symmetric basis floor `assert!(spot.div_ceil(factor) <= forward)`
(basis >= 1/factor), so the re-anchored forward stays >= pyth_spot / factor > 0.

NOTE — this CHANGES a deliberate, documented behavior. The prior code left the
lower basis bound out on purpose (the removed test's own comment: "there is no
LOWER basis bound"), premised on the :368-374 claim that "compute_nd2's deep-tail
saturations keep pricing live." That premise is false for a realistic strike grid:
a 0.6 forward puts every BTC strike deep-OTM, so prices collapse to 0 rather than
saturating live. The floor corrects the envelope to match that reality. The audit's
own recommended fix (an absolute `spot <= max_pricing_spot` ceiling) was verified
INCOMPLETE — it blocks the one stated scenario but not the class (a tiny bs_forward
collapses the forward at any spot magnitude); the basis floor closes the class.

Test: `re_anchored_zero_forward_aborts` is retargeted to
`re_anchor_collapsing_surface_rejected_at_envelope` (its degenerate input is now
rejected at the input gate, EBlockScholesInputsInvalid, before re-anchoring). New
`surface_with_basis_below_min_aborts` pins the floor; verified by negative control
(fails without the assert). `EZeroForward` is kept as a backstop for the residual
sub-100 normalized pyth spot — its now-marginal reachability is a Rule-4 follow-up.

Found by the 2026-07-17 predict-audit (verify panel codex-degraded; verified
against source in the main loop).

Verified: `sui move build --warnings-are-errors` clean; predict 428/428;
prettier-move 0.4.0 clean.

Closes DBU-596.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds a missing lower‑bound check on the forward price (spot/div_ceil(factor) <= forward). Previously a tiny forward could collapse pricing to zero, letting attackers mint positions for free (value leak). Adding the assert fixes the bug and prevents the exploitable economic loss, qualifying as a security‑relevant fix.

subject: fix(propbook): bounded-carry Pyth settlement (accept most-recent within window) (DBU-598)
body:
Reshape the settlement gate from strict feedUpdateTimestamp==envelope to
bounded-carry: accept a price carried within constants::max_settlement_carry_ms
(2s) at-or-before the whole-millisecond envelope/expiry, keyed at the envelope,
retaining the true feed timestamp. A price carried from beyond the window is
rejected (ESettlementCarryExceedsWindow) so a stale value cannot lock the
insert-only settlement key. Strict equality would have stalled settlement
whenever Pyth carried a price forward at the boundary; the bounded window keeps
settlement live as a most-recent-as-of-expiry mark while barring an unbounded
stale lock-in.

Settlement stays permissionless; the window is compiled, not caller-supplied
(a passed window on a permissionless insert could be set arbitrarily large).
Live-pricing freshness (age carried prices by feedUpdateTimestamp), the
feed<=envelope guard, and the v1->v2 version/rotation machinery are unchanged.

Docs reversed from strict to bounded-carry (RP-4, decisions, invariants, risks,
pricing-and-oracles, propbook README); residual disclosed: permissionless +
window lets a caller pick the most favorable real print within the window near a
strike boundary. Harness snapshot filter relaxed to within-window to match.

Verified: propbook 68/68 (within-window settles, beyond-window aborts), predict
427/427, builds --warnings-are-errors, format:move, predeploy check.py, harness
tsc --noEmit all green.

subject: predict: skew quotes by the pool's directional inventory (DBU-627)
body:
Predict quotes every trade at the oracle's fair mark, so the pool takes on
directional inventory at no price. This skews the quoted probability by the
pool's own net position: risk-adding flow prices worse, rebalancing flow
prices better.

The mechanism was built once before against the pre-rework contracts (#995,
merged then reverted; #999, closed) and is recorded as a rejected direction
in docs/design/decisions.md, conditioned on solving the aggregate's drift and
overflow. Both are solved here structurally rather than bounded:

- Drift. The stored aggregate is exact signed position lots, derived by one
  owned evaluator from atoms that round-trip losslessly through the packed
  order id, with no oracle input. A removal subtracts bit-equal what the
  insert added, so no surface movement between open and close can leave a
  residual. The earlier build weighted the stored aggregate by a live-surface
  n(d2), which is precisely what drifted. Moneyness weighting moved to read
  time, where it is recomputed from the current mark and cannot go stale.
- Overflow. There is no time-to-expiry amplification term — that was the
  named overflow source. Every intermediate is a bounded fixed-point value,
  and max_max_skew_shift keeps the shift strictly inside (0, 1) at both tails,
  so skewed_up_price needs no saturating clamp. The same bound is what keeps
  the budget-sizing search's cost function monotone in quantity.

Quotes are post-trade: a trade is priced against the inventory it creates, so
it cannot be dodged by splitting or resequencing, and a complete partition of
the line always costs more than its payout. The skew is confined to the trade
path. NAV, the LP flush mark, and liquidation candidate selection all continue
to read the exact fair mark, so inventory can never push an order across its
knockout or move the mark that prices LP supply and withdraw.

Ships disabled (max_skew_shift = 0). Whether the skew improves LP outcomes
under the fee-only model is unproven and out of scope here, so markets quote
fair until an admin snapshots a nonzero shift into a new expiry.

subject: test(predict): enroll P-15 — pricing error decides the knock-out, forfeiting real equity
body:
The knock-out predicate compares a computed gross against an integer
threshold, treating the fixed-point range probability as the position's
value. That probability carries certified approximation error (up to 3,610
units at 1e9 in this package's own reference data), which at production
quantities spans many whole units, so a threshold can sit strictly between
the computed gross and the true gross. The decision is then made by the sign
of the approximation error rather than by solvency — and the consequence is
discrete, not proportional: a knocked-out holder forfeits all equity above
the floor.

The enrolled flow holds a 1e9 contract on (90, 110] with floor 581,663,191
(threshold 684,309,636). The contract computes gross 684,309,632, knocks the
order out, and pays zero; the independent true gross is 684,309,642, leaving
the holder solvent and owed 102,646,451 — about ten percent of the position.
The test grants the payout its full certified pricing error plus the close
fee before asserting, so it can only fail on the classification.

Also adds two composition regressions that survive today: the book's
aggregated liability covers the sum of per-order payables, and a set of
positions with a certain combined settlement is reserved in full.

checkers green.

subject: test(predict): pin computed-price monotonicity where true gaps are sub-unit
body:
The price memo's `price <= previous` assert is a point comparison over active
boundary ticks, and RP-15 blocks LP fills pool-wide when it fires. A truly
monotone surface that merely computed as inverted would therefore brick the
flush with nothing for the publisher to correct.

Attacked across total variances 1 to 50, ticks 60 to 16,600, at both the
admissible grid and adjacent ticks, including a band where consecutive true
prices differ by a fraction of one raw unit while remaining resolvable. No
spurious inversion exists: the evaluation error is a smooth function of
strike, so adjacent strikes carry nearly identical error and it cancels in
the comparison rather than deciding it. The guard is safe because of the
comparison's shape, not because the error is small.

Pins that property as a regression, and records the contrast with P-15, where
the comparison is against a fixed integer derived by a different route and the
error therefore decides the outcome.

body:
Compute total variance, sqrt(w), and d2 at u128/1e18 in compute_nd2_terms:
flooring the b*inner product to 1e9 discarded the whole low-variance signal
(a 5-minute surface has w ~ 1e-8, about ten raw units at 1e9), inflating
pricing error to ~0.4% at short expiry. Replace the three fixed error tiers
(8/48/1e6) with evaluation_error_for_variance, an e(w) table keyed on the
evaluation's total variance, and add a beta^2 <= 9*min_tv admission gate
(beta = b*(1+|rho|)) that holds the skew correction clear of the [0,1] clamp
so every admitted evaluation lands in an e(w) band. Expose math::isqrt for the
u128 variance square root. Real Block Scholes surfaces clear the gate ~2x
(100% of observed surfaces); 1-minute pricing error drops from ~0.4% to ~5e-5.

subject: predict: certify PLP-price error and abort the flush above the 1% bound
body:
The second deviation chain: carry the certified up_price error up through the NAV
computation to the pool mark, and abort the flush if the PLP price could deviate
from true NAV by more than 1%.

The price memo stores each boundary's error alongside its price; walk_linear sums
the liability error (one node's price shifts both its start and end terms, so its
contribution rides |start - end|); correction_value sums the knock-out credit's
error; exact_live_liability and current_nav_with_error carry it (free cash is
exact); value_expiry accumulates total_nav_error across markets; and finish_flush
asserts total_nav_error <= 1% * pool_nav before the mark fills any queue
(EPlpPriceTooImprecise). Public current_nav stays u64 for quotes/devInspect.

Same pattern as the contract-price side, threaded through the longer NAV chain.
The flush abort is pool-wide by design (one mark prices both queues), and 1% is
loose enough to clear healthy books — it fires when a degenerate low-variance
surface makes the aggregate priced terms imprecise.

subject: fixed_math: collapse the certified product to an exact multiplier
body:
Every production certified product has one exact operand — a payout-tree net
quantity, a leveraged order quantity, a stored SVI rho or b — so the general
product rule `d(ab) = |a| db + |b| da + da db` had two terms that were
identically zero at every call site, each still paying a full u128
multiply/divide through `try_mul_div_up`. Replace `mul_scaled` with
`mul_exact`, which keeps only the surviving `|k| da` term.

The two removed terms are exactly zero, not bounded: `try_mul_div_up(x, 0, 1e9)`
returns `Some(0)` and `saturating_add(0)` is the identity, so every center and
every certificate radius is bit-identical. The two pricing call sites swap
operand order, which is safe because `i64::mul_scaled` is commutative in both
magnitude (u128 product) and sign (XOR), and `from_parts` canonicalizes zero.

This removes two u128 mul/div/Option round-trips per payout-tree boundary and
per active leveraged order — the per-order `Approx` work the dense-NAV flush
regression was traced to.

subject: predict: store payout-tree net payout instead of static floor
body:
The tree's consumers read two disjoint projections: the NAV walk reads
`quantity` alone, and the reserve/settlement reads read `quantity -
floor_shares`. Nothing reads `floor_shares` alone — every liquidation site takes
it from the packed order id, never from the tree. The stored basis was therefore
the one basis neither consumer wanted, and `net_payout()` re-derived it on every
aggregate read.

Store `net_payout` directly. The invariant flips the right way round: a negative
aggregate net payout becomes unrepresentable, where before it was merely implied
by the per-order `F <= Q` invariant surviving summation and re-evaluated as an
unguarded subtraction at each read. The quantity that becomes derived (implied
floor) is one no consumer reads.

`PayoutSummary` drops both quantity components with it — no consumer reads a
subtree's aggregate quantity — taking the node payload from 9 fields to 7 and
halving `combine_summaries`' additions. `net_payout()` and `add_terms()` are
deleted; `positive_net_delta` loses two subtractions per call. Per resummarize
that is 6 subtractions and 4 additions removed.

The conversion now happens once at the write boundary, where `order::assert_valid`
is the `F <= Q` authority. That makes `quantity - floor_shares` a real subtraction
on the partial-close slice, which underflow-aborts if a closed slice ever violated
the invariant — a property that was previously unchecked at the tree. Five
production-flow tests cover that path, including the tightest case
(`partial_close_to_last_lot_keeps_survivor_floor_within_quantity`).

Contained to one module: `PayoutTerms` and `PayoutSummary` are named nowhere
else, `insert_range`/`remove_range` keep their signatures, and `walk_linear` is
untouched.

Verification: Predict warning-strict build and 477/477 with no expected value
changed; the round-trip oracle `gc_mutated_tree_matches_rebuilt_survivor_tree`,
both `EInsufficientPayoutTerms` guards, and the backing/settled-solvency reserve
oracles all green; pinned Move formatting unchanged; predeploy check clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change fixes a previously unchecked subtraction (quantity - floor_shares) that could underflow and abort, leading to potential denial‑of‑service or incorrect payout calculations. Storing net_payout directly and enforcing the F <= Q invariant at write time removes the vulnerability.

subject: predict: fuse the certified pricing kernel into one flow
body:
The UP digital price and the error bound on that same price were computed by two
different bodies of code in two different packages. `pricing.move` held the
formula; `fixed_math::approx` held a general interval-arithmetic type whose ten
nonlinear propagation rules — ln, sqrt, square, quotient, fused mul-div, normal
CDF and PDF, negation, doubling, unit clamp — existed to certify it. Every one of
those rules had exactly one caller, and that caller was the pricing kernel. You
could not read a price step and the bound on its error without opening two files.

Fold the certified kernel into one function. `up_price_certified` computes the
value and the radius side by side: each fixed-point step is followed by the
propagation that bounds its distance from the true real-valued quantity. Four
private helpers stay behind it because they are genuinely re-entered or genuinely
separable — `certified_ln_ratio`/`certified_ln` (two call paths), `certified_div`
(d2 and the variance slope), and `certified_smile_correction` (the three-ball
outward corner evaluation). `compute_up_price_approx` and its five helpers are
gone.

`approx` keeps only what a certified value needs *after* its producer certifies
it: sums, differences, exact-multiplier scaling, and the two 1-Lipschitz clamps.
That is exactly the algebra NAV composes — the payout-tree walk, the leveraged
correction, marked liability, market NAV, and pool NAV contain no product of two
uncertain values, no division, and no transcendental. Thirteen functions, four
leaf macros, and the module's only error constant are deleted; the type goes from
321 lines to 129.

`ENegativeSqrtInput` is deleted rather than relocated because it is unreachable in
the kernel: the sqrt input is a sum of two squares, both nonnegative by
construction. Its abort was reachable only through the general type's contract.

Behavior is unchanged. Verification is bit-identity in both coordinates, not just
the center: the full Predict suite passes with no test edited and no expected
value changed (477/477), which pins every center; and a temporary probe over all
40 reference-corpus points captured each range price's error radius before and
after — identical at every point. fixed_math is 150/150 after dropping the tests
whose subject was deleted.

Known coverage delta: the per-primitive enclosure and saturation tests in
`approx_tests` lose their subject, since the propagation they exercised is now
private to the kernel. End-to-end enclosure against the independent Python
reference (`pricing_exact_tests`) still covers the composed radius, but the
fail-closed saturation branches are no longer directly pinned. Restoring that as
production-flow scenarios is follow-up work, not covered here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit only refactors the pricing kernel by merging functions and removing unused code; the author explicitly states behavior is unchanged and the diff shows no functional changes, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: predict: move the contract-price precision gate to pricing
body:
Mint refuses to admit a contract price whose numerical error exceeds 0.1%,
because an uncertain entry price transfers real value between the trader and the
pool. That policy lived in `strike_exposure` — a module about exposure indexing —
which had to receive a certificate from `pricing` and re-check it. The producer
of the error and the enforcer of the bound were different modules, so the bound
travelled as data and `pricing` exported a certificate type solely to carry it.

`pricing::admitted_range_price` now produces the price and enforces the bound in
one place, returning a plain `u64`. Callers get a price they may act on or no
price at all. `range_price_approx` is deleted, `EPriceTooImprecise` and
`max_contract_price_deviation` move to `pricing` (code 18), and `strike_exposure`
drops its highest code with no renumbering. Mint's whole interface to pricing is
now u64 in, u64 out.

The tests that used `range_price_approx` are converted to the production paths,
not to a test-only replacement:

- Dual-kernel center parity (`pricing_tests`) now compares `range_price` against
  `admitted_range_price` — same claim, production surface on both sides.
- The exact-value corpus and the NAV enclosure test read the certified price
  through `price_and_cache` + `cached_range_price`, which is how NAV actually
  reads it: price each finite boundary into the memo ascending, then read the
  range back out. Radius-soundness coverage against the independent Python
  reference is unchanged, and it now exercises the path the protocol uses rather
  than a mint-only helper.
- Assertions on the certificate are restated as the production promise where the
  gate applies: an admitted price is within 0.1% of the independent reference.
- `finite_ratio_underflow_does_not_false_certify_range` becomes an
  `expected_failure`. Its subject is unchanged and is the sharpest case in the
  file: two boundaries that each price accurately, whose difference collapses to
  zero. Admission must refuse that rather than sell a contract at zero on a
  surface where neither boundary is near zero.
- `extreme_surface_is_admissible_but_not_numerically_certifiable` splits in two,
  because its two halves are now separate observations: the economic band still
  admits the surface (`range_price`), and the numerical gate still rejects it
  (`expected_failure` on `admitted_range_price`).

fixed_math 150/150, predeploy check clean. Both new `expected_failure` tests were
checked for non-vacuity — deleting the final call in the finite-tail test makes it
fail, so the abort comes from the call under test and the two preceding admissions
genuinely succeed. RP-20's pinned test name follows the rename; the policy, the
threshold, and the response are unchanged.

rationale: The commit moves the 0.1% price‑precision check from a downstream module (strike_exposure) to the producer (pricing) and removes a certificate that could be forged, fixing a bug where imprecise contract prices could be accepted. Accepting such prices could be exploited to cause financial loss, so the fix mitigates a security issue.

subject: predict: bound how far the NAV oracle may differ from the contract
body:
Every NAV test in this module asserts `current_nav` exactly equals an independent
per-order reference. That works only because every fixture is engineered to make
the two agree bit-for-bit: one boundary tick, a price of exactly 0.5, even
quantities. The engineering is invisible in the assertions and is the reason no
fixture prices a real multi-tick smile — on any realistic book the contract's
boundary-aggregated walk and the reference's per-order sum round at different
points, exact equality fails, and there was nothing to assert instead.

Derive the bound so realistic fixtures become possible. The two sides compute the
same function and differ only in where integer truncation lands, and three of the
four candidate divergence sites contribute exactly zero:

- The knock-out predicates are equivalent, not just similar. The contract tests
  `ceil(rv*ltv/S) <= F`, the reference `rv <= floor(F*S/ltv)`; both reduce to
  `rv * ltv <= F * S` because F and rv are integers.
- The floor cap agrees exactly — `clamp_upper` is `min(rv, F)`, so the contract's
  per-order net is the reference's contribution verbatim.
- The range price feeding the correction agrees bit-for-bit: `cached_range_price`
  then `mul_exact` floors the same product once that `mul_down` does.

All divergence is therefore in the linear term, where the reference floors once
per order and the boundary walk floors once per node. The pre-truncation identity
is exact, each floor errs within one raw unit, and zero-net nodes contribute
nothing, giving `|current_nav - reference_nav| <= N + M` raw units for N distinct
finite boundary ticks and M open orders — structural counts, independent of
prices, quantities, floors, and leverage. A `(-inf, h]` order biases the
difference upward by construction, since the contract computes `q - floor(P(h)q/S)`
where the reference computes `q - ceil(P(h)q/S)`.

Two oracle fixes fall out of the derivation:

- `index_now` is deleted. It scaled the floor by a floor index that the static-floor
  model does not have; every call site passed 1.0, where `mul_down(F, 1e9) == F`. A
  knob whose only non-default value silently breaks the contract/reference
  equivalence is worse than no knob.
- The knock-out threshold moves to u128. `math::div_down(F, ltv)` casts `F*S/ltv`
  to u64 unchecked, which overflows for `F > 2^63` at the 0.5 LTV floor. Unreachable
  at realistic sizes, but it was a live sharp edge in the oracle.

No assertion is weakened. The existing fixtures stay dust-free and keep exact
equality, which is strictly stronger than the bound; the bound is documented for
the fixtures that will price a real smile. 478/478 with no expected value changed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit only modifies test code (removing a float argument from check_nav calls) and does not change production logic. No bug in functional code is corrected, nor is any security-relevant behavior altered.

subject: predict: add a NAV fixture that actually rounds
body:
Every existing NAV fixture is built so the contract and the reference agree
bit-for-bit — one boundary tick, a price of exactly 0.5, even quantities. That
makes exact equality possible but leaves the boundary-aggregated walk untested
in the only regime production runs in: a real smile, where each node and each
order truncate at different points.

Add a book that rounds. Seven orders over five distinct boundary ticks (80..120)
on a smooth high-variance surface, with quantities that are lot multiples but not
round in 1e9 terms, so `price * quantity / 1e9` is non-integral throughout. It
reaches what the ATM fixtures structurally cannot:

- five payout-tree nodes rather than one, so the walk has real shape;
- shared boundaries carrying BOTH signs of net quantity (ticks 90 and 120 net
  negative), exercising `mul_scaled`'s toward-zero truncation in the direction
  that rounds a signed total UP rather than down;
- a `(-inf, h]` order, whose `tree.base` anchor makes the contract floor where the
  reference ceils;
- 1x and leveraged orders sharing ticks, so the correction walk subtracts over a
  boundary set it does not define;
- both `is_liquidatable` branches, by repricing the surface beneath the book after
  minting — with a precondition assert that somebody really is knocked out, so a
  reprice that stopped knocking anyone out fails instead of silently going vacuous.

The fixture measures 4 raw units of aggregation dust before the reprice and 2
after, against a bound of 12 (5 ticks + 7 orders). That is the derivation from
ff770a13 confirmed against a live book rather than only on paper: had the
divergence-site enumeration missed a term, the observed delta could have exceeded
the bound. The deltas are reported here rather than asserted — pinning contract
output would make the test a change-detector instead of a check against the
independent oracle.

479/479, predeploy check clean.

subject: predict: cover the certified kernel's exact-zero slope branch
body:
The two pricing kernels take their zero-slope shortcut on different conditions:
the scalar one returns `N(d2)` whenever `w'` is zero, while the certified one also
requires a zero radius, because a slope that merely rounded to zero still carries a
possible correction. Instrumenting both regimes across the suite showed the split
is not academic, and not where it was expected.

The rounded-zero regime (`w' == 0` with a radius) is reached by 93 of 479 tests —
the default fixture SVI has `|rho| == 1` and `b == 10_000`, so `rho + x/root`
collapses toward zero below the forward and `slope * b` truncates away. That path
is thoroughly exercised.

The exact-zero regime had ZERO coverage. It needs `b == 0`, and the two fixtures
that supply a flat-variance surface both read only the scalar `range_price`, so
nothing ever drove `b == 0` through the certified kernel. `b == 0` is admissible in
production — `assert_inputs_pricing_safe` bounds `b` from above only, and a flat
surface with `a >= 1.0` satisfies the positive-variance guard — so this was a
live, untested branch on the mint path.

Pin it where the flat surface already exists: `at_the_forward_is_exactly_one_half`
now asserts the certified kernel agrees with the scalar one on that surface.
Re-instrumenting confirms the new assertion is what reaches the branch, so the
coverage is real rather than incidental.

No source change. The branch was correct — it returns `N(d2)` with the CDF's own
radius and no correction term, which is what the arithmetic requires — but correct
and untested is how the next edit breaks it.

479/479.

rationale: The commit only adds or modifies test code to increase coverage; no production code behavior is changed, so it does not fix a bug nor address a security issue.

subject: predict: require a positive SVI wing slope, deleting two branches
body:
`b` is SVI's wing slope. Every real Block Scholes surface in the committed corpus
has it between 6.3e-6 and 7.4e-3; it is never zero, because a zero slope is a flat
total variance with no smile at all. Nothing enforced that, so the pricing math
carried structure for a shape no publisher produces.

Require `b > 0` at load and two branches stop being representable:

- `up_price_certified`'s zero-slope early return. It needed a slope that is exactly
  zero with a zero radius, and `certified_div` always returns a radius of at least
  one raw unit, so with `b > 0` the condition can no longer hold.
- The zero-absorbing branch of the slope product itself, for the same reason on
  both operands.

The scalar kernel keeps its own `w'.is_zero()` shortcut, which fires on a slope
that merely ROUNDS to zero and is still reachable. The kernels therefore still
reach that price by different routes, and still agree: a zero slope center makes
`mul_div_down`'s product zero, so the certified subtraction is a no-op. That is
the non-trivial case of the centers-agree theorem, and it is now pinned directly
in `at_the_forward_is_exactly_one_half` — verified by instrumentation to reach the
correction path rather than the shortcut.

This supersedes c8809b36's framing. That commit added coverage for the exact-zero
branch after instrumentation found it unreached; the better answer was to make it
unreachable by construction, so the test now covers the rounded-zero case instead.
Its message and the matching ledger entry also state that `b == 0` needed
`a >= 1.0` to pass the positive-variance guard. That is wrong: the guard is total
variance at or above 1e-9, which one raw unit of `a` satisfies. `b == 0` was more
reachable than described, not less.

`FLAT_SVI_B` moves from 0 to the smallest admissible slope, and the zero-total-
variance guard test now gets its zero from `|rho| == 1` zeroing the wing increment
rather than from a zero slope. Both keep their original subjects.

480/480, predeploy check clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds a validation that the SVI wing slope `b` must be > 0 and removes special zero‑slope handling, preventing previously reachable code paths that could return an incorrect price. An attacker could have supplied `b == 0` to trigger the shortcut and obtain a manipulated price, leading to potential financial loss. The fix closes this by rejecting such inputs.

subject: predict: replace the certificate algebra with an accumulator
body:
`Approx` was a numeric type: a value, a radius, and five arithmetic operations
that threaded both through five modules. But nothing downstream of a price is
nonlinear. The payout walk, the leveraged correction, marked liability, market NAV
and pool NAV contain no product of two uncertain values, no division and no
transcendental, so a composed radius is only `Σ term_error(quantity, price_radius)`
over the terms a traversal visits. The radius never needed to travel WITH the
value.

So it no longer does. `walk_linear` and `correction_value` take a `&mut u64` and
accumulate as they go, returning plain `I64` and `u64`. Their value arithmetic
becomes the operations that already existed: `i64::mul_scaled` and `i64::add` for
the signed boundary sum, `math::mul_down` for a scaled quantity, `.min()` for the
floor cap, `saturating_sub` for the two projections to nonnegative. `Approx`'s
`add`/`sub`/`mul_exact`/`clamp_nonnegative`/`clamp_upper` were re-exporting those
with a radius rider; the rider is now one counter.

What remains is `certified::Certified`, a two-field label with accessors, a
constructor, the shared `term_error` derivation, and the relative-deviation
predicate the two gates read. It carries a value across a module boundary where
two bare `u64`s would silently swap, and it has no arithmetic at all.
`fixed_math::approx` is deleted — 129 lines and twelve functions for roughly forty.

`term_error` is the one derivation every traversal calls, including the
zero-absorbing case that `mul_exact` owned: an exact zero quantity or a
certified-exact zero price contributes no radius, where the naive formula would
add a rounding leaf. Two accumulations of the same aggregate cannot disagree
because there is only one expression of it.

`fixed_math` now holds exactly what propbook imports plus predict's scalar
primitives, which is a real boundary rather than a historical one.

Verification is bit-identity in both coordinates. The suite passes with no
expected value changed (480/480, fixed_math 142/142), which pins the values; and
the multi-tick NAV fixture — which exercises the payout walk, both correction
branches, and the market-level subtraction — reports the same NAV value AND the
same radius before and after, at both surfaces: 300018675721/451 and
300673039880/421. Saturating addition on u64 is associative and commutative, so

subject: predict: require a positive SVI baseline, deleting the variance backstops
body:
SVI's raw parameterization permits a negative baseline `a` offset by the wing
term, and the envelope accommodated that: it bounded `|a|`, then approximated the
analytical minimum variance `a + b·sigma·sqrt(1 - rho²)` at load to catch
baselines that over-offset the wing, and kept a per-strike positive-variance abort
because that approximation's directed rounding was never a proof.

Predict does not read those surfaces. Requiring `a > 0` at `Pricer` construction,
beside the existing `b > 0`, makes total variance positive at every strike by
construction, and all of that machinery becomes unreachable:

- `assert_min_total_variance_positive` and `min_svi_variance_increment` are
  deleted. The latter ran a square root and three multiplications on EVERY priced
  transaction to bound something a positive baseline settles for free.
- Both kernels lose the `a.is_negative()` branch and both positive-variance
  aborts. `wide_total_var = wide_increment + wide_a`, and `a >= 1` raw unit puts
  it at or above the one-unit floor the assert was checking.
- `EBlockScholesMinVarianceInvalid` and `ENonPositiveVariance` have no live sites
  and are removed; the surviving codes renumber to close the gaps (pre-deploy).

Guard duty inventory, since two aborts are being removed rather than moved. Their
incidental job was arithmetic headroom for the `d2` quotient: total variance had
to stay positive so `sqrt(w)` was a nonzero divisor. `a > 0` preserves that with
more margin than before — `wide_total_var >= 1e9` gives `sqrt_var >= 31_622`,
where the old guard permitted exactly the same floor by a longer route.

Envelope shape comes from 12,827 real on-chain observations (24h, one oracle, one
underlying): `a` runs 3.9e-7 to 2.5e-4 and `b` runs 6.0e-6 to 9.3e-3, both far
inside the bounds. The dataset carries no sign column for `a`, so it cannot say
whether negative baselines occur upstream — this is a policy decision that they
are not read, not an observation that they do not exist.

Four tests collapse to two. The three that drove negative or zero `a` were probing
math those surfaces can no longer reach, so they become one rejection each for a
negative and a zero baseline; eight constants that existed only to construct
degenerate variance surfaces go with them.

478/478, predeploy check clean. The concepts doc described the old
bound-`|a|`-and-approximate design as shipped and is updated in the same change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit removes per‑strike aborts for non‑positive variance and instead enforces a>0 at construction, fixing crashes that could occur when total variance became zero or negative. The previous behavior could be triggered by malicious SVI parameters, leading to division‑by‑zero panics and transaction failures (DoS).

subject: predict: drop the unreachable zero-absorbing disjunct on the slope product
body:
The slope product absorbed either operand being a certified exact zero. One of
those cases cannot occur: `x` is `k - m`, its radius is `k`'s radius, and
`certified_ln` always adds a leaf of at least three raw units on both of its
paths, so `x_error` is never zero. Instrumenting the disjunct across the suite
confirms it: zero hits in 478 tests.

The `rho.is_zero()` case stays. It is reachable — a symmetric smile is a real
surface — and it is not merely a shortcut: an exact zero multiplier contributes no
radius, where the general form would add a rounding leaf. Removing it would
inflate the radius by one raw unit rather than preserve it.

Bit-identical: the removed branch never fired. 478/478 with no expected value
changed.
