subject: sessions: bind session grants to the venues they name
body:
A session grant stored only an expiry, so an active session could mint app
auth for any Pool or ExpiryMarket the caller chose to pass. App auth carries
no owner or operation restriction, and the spot wrapper funds each order by
withdrawing the account's entire base, quote and DEEP balance, so a session
intended for trading on one venue could route the account into a
caller-created pool and take the other side of the trade.

Grants now carry the Pool and ExpiryMarket ids they cover. Each wrapper
passes the id of the object it is about to act on, and auth minting refuses
an id the grant does not name. Grants must name between one and twenty
distinct venues; reauthorizing replaces the terms rather than extending them,
so a grant is narrowed the same way it is widened.
rationale: The change adds venue restrictions to SessionGrant, fixing a prior bug where a session could be used to mint app auth for any venue, allowing unauthorized trades and potential fund loss. This is an improper access control vulnerability.

subject: sessions: gate spot grants on traded assets, not on venue ids
body:
Naming venues in the grant stranded the Predict entrypoints. Cadences run as
short as one minute over a rolling deployment horizon, so the markets a session
needs next do not exist when the owner authorizes it, and up to sixty can be
live against a twenty-entry grant. Those entrypoints did not need the gate
either: they take no type parameters, settle only in DUSDC, withdraw the quoted
cost rather than the balance, and bind the pricer to the market, so there is no
caller-chosen venue to constrain. They now check only that the session is live.

The spot entrypoints are generic and fund an order from the account's whole
balance, so they keep a gate, on coin types rather than pool ids. DeepBook
registers at most one pool per asset pair, so naming the assets pins a session
to the canonical pools for them and admits pools created after the grant, while
still refusing a pair that routes a held asset into a caller-minted coin.
rationale: [MEV] The change replaces venue‑ID gating with coin‑type gating for session grants, fixing a bug where a session could be authorized for any venue ID, allowing attackers to create malicious pools after the grant and route assets improperly, leading to potential fund loss.

subject: predict: resumable full-pool flush without pausing trading (DBU-754) (#1265)
body:
* predict: resumable full-pool flush without pausing trading (DBU-754)

Splits the flush into an atomic pricer snapshot (SnapshotStage hot potato),
resumable one-market-per-transaction valuation, and a finish that drains the
LP queues below eligibility cutoffs recorded at the snapshot instant. Trading
is never gated: a snapshotted market's trades record range and measured
cash-row deltas on its ValuationStamp, and value_expiry reconstructs the
snapshot-instant NAV exactly (walk_linear_adjusted rolls per-boundary
quantities back with identical rounding; deleted boundaries price from the
log). try_settle gates per market; LP cancels stay gated (frozen-mark free
look); keeper cash flows, market creation, and config stay gated. Aborts are
O(1): stamps go stale by flush ordinal and clear lazily. max_payout_tree_nodes
is derived from the transaction object budget; max_valuation_window_ms and
max_valuation_log_ops are admin-tunable. Registers: RP-29 (resolves C-1),
RP-30, RP-31; new C-2/C-5/P-32.

* predict: let rebalance_expiry_cash run mid-flush with full maintenance compensation

The measurement-only flush closed the clamp distortion but left cash
maintenance unavailable for the window: a market that exhausted its
buffer mid-flush had mints and closes abort on backing until the flush
landed, with exits paying the price. Maintenance is now recorded the
same way trades are: an in-window live top-up or surplus sweep folds
into the pending market's stamp (so snapshot_nav keeps excluding it —

the branch genuinely moved cash. Settled sweeps stay uncompensated:
a swept market contributes zero and idle is its counted location.

subject: predict: never block settlement during a flush (#1281)
body:
* predict: never block settlement during a flush

A market that reached expiry mid-flush could not settle until its own value_expiry
ran: try_settle aborted EMarketPendingValuation while the market carried an
in-flight flush's stamp. That gate was conservative, not load-bearing — the frozen
mark is settlement-invariant. value_expiry/snapshot_nav read only the stamp's
frozen cash rows, the frozen pricer, and the payout tree's frozen shadow, and
settlement mutates none of them (record_settlement sets scalars, the settled sweep
moves live cash and deactivates, a settled redeem decrements a scalar).

Remove the gate: a market settles the instant it reaches expiry, even mid-flush and
even before its own value_expiry, and the flush still folds its frozen pre-expiry
mark. Keep the first-entry stale-stamp reconcile; drop the now-unused
EMarketPendingValuation constant. The snapshot stage still refuses to stamp an
already expired-unsettled market (EExpiredMarketNotSettled), now purely a
settle-first requirement that settlement being unblocked always satisfies.

Flip the two gate tests to positive and add settle-before-value_expiry coverage for
the sweep and settled-redeem paths (mark == control in every case). Docs:
decisions.md, RP-29(b), RP-4, and the RP-29 pinning list.

run") — an integrator gating its settle lane on that would defer settlement that

architecture.md, and two spots in liquidity-and-nav.md. Softened the decisions.md
claim that settle-first is "always satisfiable": settlement is never blocked BY THE
FLUSH, but both-exact-sources-absent still blocks it and still blocks starting the

RP-29 now records the duty inventory the guard removal requires: the newly
reachable settled-and-stamped state, every consumer verified against it, the

Tests: all three new tests settled ON the strike, where settlement_in_range is
false — so every payout was zero, the redeem never reached its cash leg, and the
sweep never exercised a nonzero retained liability. They now settle in the money,
and each first trades mid-window so the payout tree carries copy-on-write shadows

subject: margin: retire the legacy Pyth entrypoints (DBU-756) (#1267)
body:
* margin: retire the legacy Pyth entrypoints (DBU-756)

Every entrypoint that priced a position off legacy Pyth Core now aborts
`EDeprecatedUseUpgradedPyth`, and the package-private readers behind them are
deleted, so no code path in `deepbook_margin` can read a legacy feed. The
signatures stay frozen — Sui's `compatible` policy forbids removing them — and
each retired entry names its `_upgraded` twin.

Retired: 12 entries in `margin_manager`, 8 in `pool_proxy`, and the two
permissionless vault entries in `margin_liquidation`. `MARGIN_VERSION` goes to 8;
`disable_version(7)` is what actually takes the old bodies off chain, since a
dependent published against v7 keeps calling them through its own linkage table.

Both families were live and authoritative until now, each enforcing its own
staleness window with no cross-feed comparison, and `PythReading` erased which
feed produced a price — so a caller chose per call between two marks that could
sit a full window apart. This was expected to self-close when Pyth stopped
publishing legacy Core; it did not, because third parties keep those objects
fresh.

The behavioural suites move to the upgraded entrypoints, keeping their coverage.
`dual_feed_window_tests` now pins the window closed rather than describing what

subject: predict: block live flows inside a window before expiry (DBU-789) (#1295)
body:
* predict: block live flows inside a window before expiry (DBU-789)

A binary's probability moves further per unit of spot as expiry nears, so a
fixed oracle staleness is worth progressively more to whoever sees the move
first: the edge scales as sqrt(staleness / time_to_expiry) and grows without
bound as the remaining time goes to zero. No finite fee prices that region and
no achievable oracle cadence removes it, so bound the region instead.

Live quotes, mints, and live redeems now abort inside no_trade_window_ms of
expiry. Default 2s, tunable 0..15s, 0 disables. The check sits in
assert_live_flow_allowed -- the one gate all three flows already share -- so a
new trade entrypoint routed through it cannot miss the block.

Settlement, settled redemption, and liquidation are untouched: the window
closes new and closing risk, never an exit from a settled market. The setter
is not gated on valuation-in-progress, matching set_trading_paused, so a
stalled flush cannot trap a safety control.

subject: predict: size a mint inside an all-in budget (DBU-834) (#1310)
body:
* predict: size a mint inside an all-in budget (DBU-834)

Add `expiry_market::mint_exact_cost` and its account quote twin
`quote_mint_exact_cost_for_account`, plus the matching Sessions wrapper.

`mint_exact_amount` sizes on the pre-fee premium and only asserts `max_cost`
after sizing, so the trading fee, congestion surcharge and inventory-impact
charge land on top of the budget. Callers wanting to spend a fixed total had to
quote first, subtract an estimated fee load off-chain, and pad it against fee
state moving before execution — spending under budget and leaving dust.

The new entrypoint makes the total the sizing input: a lot search whose probe is
the same all-in sum the mint charges, evaluated against execution-time fee,
subsidy, congestion and book state. The fill is the largest lot-rounded quantity
whose all-in cost fits, so the unspent remainder is below one more lot's all-in
cost and no fee estimate is needed. Every term is nondecreasing in quantity
while pre-trade state is fixed, which is what makes the search exact.

To keep one home for the sum, `compute_mint_quote` and the search probe both go
through `mint_quote_at`. `StrikeExposure` gains a `MintRange` token that prices
the range and samples the payout-tree reads once, so the search evaluates
candidates without re-pricing or re-walking the tree; `quote_mint_terms` now
composes it, and the close path keeps its own reads in
`live_close_inventory_impact`.

Existing entrypoints are unchanged, and the new surface is additive.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: cover all-in budget mint sizing (DBU-834)

Sizing is pinned from both sides at every fee term: one raw unit below the next
lot's all-in cost mints the lot below it, and a budget equal to a fill's all-in
cost spends the budget exactly. Each cost term is exercised inside the budget —
builder fee, sponsor subsidy (at the rate and at the sponsored-balance cap), the
congestion surcharge, and the inventory-impact charge below its curve's kink,
across it, and over a disjoint book where the prospective liability switches from
gap-driven to max-driven.

Budget edges: dust and zero budgets reject on the minimum premium, an unfunded
account sizes to zero instead of underflowing the withdrawal, an oversized budget
saturates at the lot cap, and a fill whose cost would exceed its own maximum
payout still aborts. Gates carry the mint and its quote through market pause,
global trading pause, and the pre-expiry no-trade window.

Two tests contrast the entrypoints on one spend figure: premium sizing quotes a
debit above it, and, when a congestion surcharge lands between quote and
execution, aborts `EMintCostAboveMax` where cost sizing resizes and fits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: pin the budget search's inventory-impact charges independently (DBU-834)

The impact assertions read the charge back from a quote, so they agreed with
whatever the contract computed. Derive each one by hand from the curve instead —
the quadratic arm below the scale, the capped arm above it, and the max-driven
branch where a prior position on the same range carries the point max — and add
the missing case where the candidate range already holds payout, which is the
only shape whose charge depends on that range's own peak.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: record the all-in budget mint decision and its surface (DBU-834)

RP-36 records what the sizing search decides and what it deliberately does not:
the fill is exact to one lot because every charge is nondecreasing in quantity
and the probe is the charge, while the maximum-payout bound and the minimum
premium still abort the sized fill rather than moving it. `mint_exact_amount`
is unchanged, so RP-13 and RP-19 continue to describe it.

The concept docs gain the third mint shape and its quote twin, the Sessions
README lists the new wrapper, and the Predict contract rules carry the bound
vocabulary for three entrypoints plus the standing requirement that a budget
search probe the function that charges.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: bound the cost search by the fill's own maximum payout (DBU-834)

The marginal inventory-impact rate rises with liability, so the largest fill a
budget can pay for is sometimes one whose all-in cost exceeds the most it could
ever pay out. Sizing bounded only by the budget therefore handed
`compute_mint_quote` a fill it had to reject: on a high-impact market, a budget
the account could afford aborted `EMintCostAboveMaxPayout` while a smaller
budget on the same market minted cleanly — and the read-only quote aborted the
same way, leaving no way to discover a workable budget.

The probe now bounds each candidate by `max_cost.min(quantity)`, so sizing steps
down to the largest fill that clears both bounds; the charge still enforces the
payout bound on whatever is admitted. A market where no size is admissible buys
nothing and rejects on the minimum premium, as a dust budget does.

Also: `mint_terms` asserts the range it consumes belongs to this exposure, since
the range now carries the book reads its impact charge is priced against and the
quote path has no allocation to catch a mismatch; and the monotonicity comment
records why the impact charge cannot fall — the two arms of the prospective
liability meet exactly at the branch switch, so it holds for any
`backing_buffer_lambda`, not only one below 1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: keep the non-monotone payout bound out of the budget search (DBU-834)

Folding `all_in_cost <= quantity` into the budget search's predicate assumed it
was monotone in quantity. It is not: cost and quantity both rise, and the
independent floors in each cost term let the comparison flip from false back to
true at a larger lot wherever unit cost sits within rounding of one. At the
above-payout fee rate `quote_mint_tests` already uses, it flips 21 times across
the first 400 lots — 2_970_000 costs 2_970_001 and fails while 3_990_000 costs
exactly 3_990_000 and passes — so a binary search over it discarded everything
above the first failure and returned 2_960_000 for a 4_000_000 budget. A caller
whose `min_quantity` sat in between got `EMintQuantityBelowMin` on a mint an
exact-quantity request of the same size performs.

Sizing now searches the budget alone, which is monotone, and consults the payout
bound only on the resulting fill. If that fill breaches it, a second search runs
strictly below it, where every candidate already fits the budget. When no smaller
fill clears the bound the budget fill is admitted, so a market where every size
is loss-making reports `EMintCostAboveMaxPayout` rather than an empty fill's
admission error.

Regressions pin that flip from both sides at hand-derived quantities, the
step-down, and the loss-making market. Coverage also grows where the entrypoint
was thin: `min_quantity` as the slippage guard for this shape — a price move, a
surcharge and a payout-limited step-down each abort against a floor taken from
the quote, and the repriced fill mints at its own floor — plus the wrong-pricer
and wrong-owner gates on the mint and its quote, a cost-sized position closing
live and redeeming a settled win, the referral split and `OrderMinted` carrying
the sized fill, and the cross-book guard on admitting a quoted range.

The entrypoint docs also qualify the one-lot remainder: it holds when the budget
is what limits the fill, and a fill limited by the payout bound, the lot cap or
expiry cash backing leaves more.

subject: predict: add USDC to the PLP pool without minting shares (add_usdc_to_plp) (#1315)
body:
* predict: add USDC to the PLP pool without minting shares

`plp::add_usdc_without_shares` is a permissionless entrypoint that joins a
USDC payment straight to pool idle liquidity and mints no PLP. Because
`total_supply` does not move, the whole payment falls inside the value the
next flush's mark divides by an unchanged share count, so NAV per PLP rises
for every current holder. This is the path for incentives and operator
top-ups: `request_supply` mints offsetting shares and leaves the mark where
it was, `lock_capital` is one-time and admin-only, and
`sponsor_fee_incentives` funds a reserve deliberately excluded from NAV.

The addition does not touch the profit basis. That basis tracks cash the
pool sent to and got back from expiries, so an outside payment is neither a
debit nor a credit, `lp_pool_value` leaves `exclusion` unchanged, and the
protocol reserve takes no share of it.

Gates: the pool must be bootstrapped (`ENotBootstrapped`) because at zero
supply there is no share base to credit; the amount must clear
`min_usdc_addition` (10 USDC, `EBelowMinUsdcAddition`); and the whole flush
is refused via `assert_not_valuation_in_progress`, so an addition can never
land between the seal's idle capture and `finish_flush` and decide by
transaction timing whether that flush's queued withdrawals were paid from
it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: bound no-shares contributions by the executable price ceiling

Self-review of the previous commit found a permanent, permissionless brick.
`add_usdc_without_shares` moves pool value up by an arbitrary amount while
`total_supply` stays put, so it can drive the implied PLP price above the
executable band's 100x ceiling. Past that ceiling `lp_book::drain` refunds
every supply and withdraw head (RP-2), and `total_supply` grows only through
a supply fill, so nothing brings the price back down — the LP layer is over
for good. Against the 10 PLP genesis-lock share base that costs about
1,000 USDC, for anyone.

This invalidated RP-2's stated risk profile, which rests on the degenerate
ratio being unforceable ("attacker must win oracle-priced bets"). The
entrypoint is now admission-gated at the source: the idle the contribution
would create must satisfy `lp_book::within_price_ceiling`, the same band
formula the mark itself uses, factored out of `is_executable_mark` so the
guard and the mark cannot drift. The test reads idle rather than pool NAV
(NAV needs a flush) because idle is exactly the protocol-controlled share —
the guard stops this entrypoint from manufacturing the degenerate ratio and
leaves market-driven NAV moves to RP-1/RP-2, which own them. It is one-sided
because a contribution can only move the price up, and it aborts rather than
clamping because this is a single-user, user-recoverable action.

Also unifies the vocabulary on "contribution": `min_usdc_contribution`,
`EBelowMinUsdcContribution`, and the new `EContributionExceedsPriceCeiling`
now agree with the event's `contributor` field. The entrypoint name is
unchanged.

RP-2 records the re-checked upper-band reachability and its new pinning
tests; `predeploy/check.py` is clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: correct how the adjacent USDC-in paths are described

Two claims in the previous commits were looser than the code.

`request_supply` was described as leaving the mark where it was. It mints
shares against the deposit NET of the supply fee and joins the whole escrow
to idle, so the fee leg is unshared value that does move the mark. True only
at the shipped 0% supply rate, and the docs said it unconditionally.

`sponsor_fee_incentives` was described as funding a reserve excluded from
NAV. It is excluded while parked — in the pool reserve and in each market's
`fee_incentive_balance`, which `current_nav` does not read because it sums
`market.cash` — but a consumed subsidy joins the mint payment into
`market.cash` and so does reach pool value, capped at
`fee_incentive_subsidy_rate` of each trade's fee.

The decision record now states both precisely, notes that losing trades on
purpose was the only pre-existing route for an arbitrary third party, and
names the supply and withdraw fee legs as the two shipped mechanisms that
already move value to holders without minting shares. No behavior change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: keep the ceiling guard out of lp_book

Reverts lp_book.move to main. The previous commit factored the band's upper
test out of `is_executable_mark` into a package-visible
`within_price_ceiling` so `plp` could share it. That was a pure refactor with
no behavior change, and putting one in front of reviewers of a behavior
change costs more attention than it saves.

`plp::add_usdc_without_shares` now restates the comparison inline
(`ceil(idle/band) <= supply`) against the same
`constants::executable_price_band_factor`, so the band width stays
single-homed even though the comparison is written twice.

The two definitions are held together behaviourally instead of by a shared
symbol: `a_contribution_to_the_price_ceiling_is_accepted_and_the_pool_still_fills`
contributes to the exact ceiling the guard admits and then requires a flush
to fill there, so a band that moved on either side fails it. Verified by
mutating `is_executable_mark`'s ceiling to exclusive with lp_book otherwise
untouched and watching that test go red — the same drift signal the shared
symbol gave, with no diff in lp_book.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: rename the entrypoint to add_usdc_to_plp

Renames `plp::add_usdc_without_shares` to `plp::add_usdc_to_plp`, and the
names that mirror it so the entrypoint, its event, and the test helpers stay
greppable from one another:

  add_usdc_without_shares        -> add_usdc_to_plp
  UsdcAddedWithoutShares         -> UsdcAddedToPlp
  emit_usdc_added_without_shares -> emit_usdc_added_to_plp
  usdc_added_without_shares_*    -> usdc_added_to_plp_*
  add_usdc_without_shares_direct -> add_usdc_to_plp_direct

The no-shares property now lives in the doc comment and the event doc rather
than the identifier, so the first line of each states it. The "contribution"
vocabulary is unchanged (`min_usdc_contribution`,
`EBelowMinUsdcContribution`, `EContributionExceedsPriceCeiling`, and the
event's `contributor` field) — it names the thing the call creates, which the
rename does not affect.

Name only; no behavior change. The concept page's "Adding USDC without
shares" heading and its in-page anchor are prose and stay as they are.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: record the ceiling guard's accepted residual

The admission gate bounds idle, not the mark. `gross_pool_value` is
`idle + active_expiry_value`, so a pool whose ACTIVE NAV has already carried
it near the band ceiling can still be pushed over by a contribution the
idle-side test admits: 10 PLP against 990 USDC of active NAV prices at 99
USDC/PLP, and a 100 USDC contribution passes the guard while taking the mark
to 109.

Recorded rather than fixed. The crossing was already reachable by losing
trades to the pool on purpose (the fee component lands immediately, the
premium in full at settlement), it needs ~100x appreciation over the share
base before a contribution of any size matters, and it burns the whole
contribution for nothing in return. Closing it exactly needs the mark, which
needs a flush, and RP-1 already rejected mark-level guards for bricking
legitimate appreciation and recapitalization states; a stored last-flush NAV
would only relocate the approximation at the cost of new state on the flush
path.

What the gate does remove is the cheap universal case: an unaged pool at its
genesis share base, no appreciation required, ~1,000 USDC.

Marked UNPINNED in RP-2 — reaching the near-ceiling state needs a funded
market with oracle-priced NAV, which the no-market LP fixture cannot build.

Docs only; no behavior chan

subject: predict: bound add_usdc_to_plp contributions by pool cash at a tenth of the band (#1319)
body:
* predict: count deployed market cash in the add_usdc_to_plp ceiling guard

The price-ceiling guard on `plp::add_usdc_to_plp` tested idle alone, but the
flush mark counts every dollar `rebalance_expiry_cash` moved from idle into a
market. Rebalancing is permissionless, so a contributor could fill the idle
ceiling, park it in a market, and contribute again, or simply contribute to
the idle ceiling of any pool with a funded market. Either way the next flush
marks above the executable band, every LP request refunds (RP-2), and
`total_supply` can never grow to bring the price back down.

The guard now tests pool cash: idle, plus the net cash deployed into active
expiries (`pool_accounting::deployed_expiry_cash`, sent minus received per
active expiry, floored at zero), plus the contribution. Moving idle into a
market leaves that sum unchanged, so parking no longer reopens headroom.
Cash is an upper bound on the pool's own share of the mark, since marked
liabilities only lower a market's NAV below its cash; trader inflows above
net funding stay the market-driven residual RP-2 owns.

RP-2 and the public docs now describe the guard that ships and the revised
residual.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: cap add_usdc_to_plp contributions at a tenth of the executable band

The contribution guard admitted pool cash up to the flush's own executable
ceiling of 100 USDC/PLP. LP fills after a contribution only push the price
up: `quote_supply_shares` floors minted shares and the supply and withdraw
fees are retained in the pool. A pool contributed to exactly the ceiling
therefore left the band on the next uneven fill. From 10 USDC / 10 PLP, a
990 USDC contribution and a 10.000001 USDC supply left 1,010.000001 USDC over
10.1 PLP, and every later supply and withdraw refunded (RP-2), with zero fees
and no markets.

Contributions are now capped at 10 USDC/PLP of pool cash
(`constants::contribution_price_ceiling_factor`), a tenth of the band. The
margin absorbs fill rounding and a supply fee at the 5% cap (at most ~1.05x
per flush); a retained withdraw fee only carries the price out when one flush
burns at least 9/(9 + rate) of shares, 99.98% at the shipped 0.2%, the same
near-total exit that already crosses the band from parity. The inline
comment no longer restates `lp_book`'s band, since the guard now uses its
own ceiling.

Tests replay the uneven-deposit sequence and a maximum-supply-fee deposit
from the ceiling and require the following flush to fill. RP-2, risks.md,
decisions.md and the liquidity concept page describe the new ceiling and the
revised residual.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: correct the contribution-ceiling residual and derive it from the band

An independent review of the previous commit found the residual overstated.
Retained withdraw fees accumulate across flushes: supply-and-withdraw round
trips of any size carry a pool out of the band once their fees add up to
(band - p) * supply USDC, about 990 USDC from parity on the 10 PLP genesis
share base. That route needs no contribution and predates add_usdc_to_plp,
but RP-2 never recorded it, and the docs claimed only a near-total single
flush exit could cross. RP-2 now records it with its cost, drops the claim
that the upper band cannot be cheaply forced while the guard stands, and
states the gate's narrower job: a contribution never itself leaves the band,
and ordinary LP activity after one has nine times the pool's cash of room.

Also corrected: the attacker's cost is the full value added to the pool, not
everything they put in; the trader-loss route needs 9/(1 - share) times the
pool's cash (ten at the default 10% share); only unrealized marks reverse;
and pool cash can refuse a contribution at or below parity while a losing
market is still active.

`contribution_price_ceiling_factor` is now `executable_price_band_factor / 10`
so the relation lives in code. Test and source comments are tightened, and
the deployed-cash acceptance test is renamed to what it checks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: record the trading-fee route, pin it, and bump current_version to 4

Follow-ups from the security review of 1841a563.

Trading fees are one-way pool income the contribution guard cannot see. A
hedged UP and DOWN pair of equal quantity pays quantity + fees and takes
quantity back whichever side wins, so the pool keeps exactly the fees at the
trader's cost of the fees alone. With the contribution ceiling at the band
itself, one 50-contract ATM mint carried a ceiling-parked genesis pool to
1,000.225 USDC over 10 PLP and refunded the next supply. At a tenth of the
band the same trade leaves 100.225 USDC and the supply fills.
`fee_income_at_the_contribution_ceiling_stays_inside_the_band` pins that. It
sizes its contribution from the ceiling constant, so restoring the ceiling to
the band fails it. RP-2, risks.md and decisions.md now name the fee route
alongside trader losses and withdraw-fee round trips.

`current_version` goes to 4. Testnet already runs a v3 package with the
idle-only guard against the same shared PoolVault, and the watermark can
only retire it from a package that claims a higher version.

The liquidity concept page now lists all four admission gates, including
the bootstrapped-pool gate, and names the genesis lock as the other way
USDC enters the pool.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: keep current_version at 3, the next Mainnet package version

`current_version` tracks the Mainnet package version. Mainnet runs v2 and is
not upgraded until after this PR, so the upgrade that ships this code
publishes v3. Testnet running ahead does not drive the number. This reverts
the bump to 4 from the previous commit.

Accepted consequence: Testnet's older v3 package, carrying the idle-only
guard, cannot be retired by the version watermark and stays callable on
Testnet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: record the parking residual and pin the ceiling tests to the constant

Follow-ups from the sui-pr-security-review run on this PR.

Parking idle in a market is neutral for the contribution guard only while
that market has received back no more than it was sent: net funding floors
at zero per market, so idle sent into a market that has already returned
profit is not counted until it makes up that profit. A contribution can land
above the ceiling by up to the active markets' returned profit, and leaving
the band that way still needs about nine times the pool's cash of it on top
of a full contribution. Accepted rather than fixed with new per-market state.
RP-2, decisions.md, the liquidity page and the deployed_expiry_cash doc now
say so, and `parking_into_a_market_that_returned_profit_lowers_guard_cash`
pins the behaviour.

The uneven-deposit and maximum-supply-fee ceiling tests contributed a fixed
90 USDC, so they stayed green with the ceiling restored to the band. They now
size the contribution from `contribution_price_ceiling_factor` through a
shared `contribute_to_ceiling` helper, and both fail under that mutant.

subject: predict: limit redeem_settled_permissionless to an admin allowlist of keepers (#1323)
body:
`expiry_market::redeem_settled_permissionless` let any sender redeem any
account's settled order without the owner's signature. It now aborts with
`ENotSettledRedeemKeeper` unless the sender is on an allowlist that `AdminCap`
manages through `protocol_config::add_settled_redeem_keeper` and
`remove_settled_redeem_keeper`. The allowlist starts empty, so the keeper path
is closed until admin adds an address. The payout still goes to the order's
account, and the owner-auth `redeem_settled` path never consults the list.

The change keeps the upgrade compatible with the deployed package. The
entrypoint's signature is unchanged, and the set is a `VecSet<address>` in a
dynamic field on `ProtocolConfig` (the struct layout is frozen), created on the
first add. The rest is additive: two admin entrypoints, one event
(`SettledRedeemKeeperUpdated`), and new error codes appended after the highest
existing ones. Adding is version-gated. Removing is not, so admin can drop a
compromised keeper during an emergency freeze.

`current_version` becomes 4 (Mainnet v3 + 1). Older packages keep the open
entrypoint until admin runs `bump_version_watermark` from the upgraded package.

The flow-test fixture allowlists alice so existing keeper-path tests keep
running in her transaction. New tests cover the empty default, add/remove,
both new admin aborts, the freeze asymmetry, the event bytes, an unlisted
sender, a listed third party redeeming into the owner's account, revocation,
and the owner path ignoring the list. The localnet simulation and harness
allowlist their redeeming signers during fresh setup. Docs, the decision
record, and the retired RP-11 banner describe the new rule.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit restricts the previously unrestricted `redeem_settled_permissionless` entrypoint by adding an admin‑controlled allowlist, fixing an access‑control flaw that let any sender redeem another account's settled order. This corrects improper authorization and thus is a security fix.

subject: margin: stop the bad-debt supply write-off at zero (DBU-371) (#1322)
body:
* margin: stop the bad-debt supply write-off at zero (DBU-371)

`margin_state::decrease_supply_absolute` subtracted a liquidation default
from `total_supply` unchecked. Borrowers accrue the protocol spread that
suppliers never receive, so once unwithdrawn protocol fees exceed the
vault's cash a full liquidation can book a default larger than
`total_supply`, and the liquidation aborted with an arithmetic error
instead of writing off the bad debt. Saturate the write-off at zero.

Adds a unit test for the clamp and an end-to-end regression that ports
the external report's PoC (20 BTC collateral, 800k USDC borrowed, ten
years of accrual, $80k -> $5k crash) to the upgraded-Pyth entrypoints.

Adds a pool-level test that `repay_liquidation` still returns the full
shortfall as the default while the supply write-off stops at zero, and
extends the end-to-end regression to show a wiped pool can be
recapitalized with `admin_inject_capital` and accept new supply at a fair
share price.

Previously the transaction would abort, leaving bad debt unwritten and allowing an attacker to trigger a denial‑of‑service or financial loss by forcing such a liquidation.

subject: claude: default pull requests to a code-then-docs stack (#1326)
body:
Pull requests that mix Move source with prose make code reviewers page
through documentation diffs to find the behavior change, and make docs
review wait on code review.

The new `stacked-prs` skill splits one change into two stacked pull
requests: code first (source, tests, manifests, scripts), then docs and
setup (Markdown, package docs, predeploy registers, .claude/, CLAUDE.md,
.github/) based on the code branch. `stack.py` classifies the changed
paths, stages one layer at a time from the source branch (renames split
into delete + add, binary-safe), and verifies the stack's top tree equals
the source tree. The skill also covers opening both pull requests, keeping
them in sync, and restacking after a squash merge.

CLAUDE.md makes the stack the default pull-request shape, asks for one
branch name per stack (the docs layer appends `-docs`), routes the skill
from the manual-trigger table, and lets documentation land in the docs
pull request stacked directly on the code instead of the same one.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit only introduces a new Claude skill and supporting script for splitting pull requests into code and docs layers. It adds documentation and tooling without modifying existing application logic, fixing a bug, or addressing any security-relevant behavior.

subject: predict: admin-set fee-incentive subsidy rate and reserve withdrawal (DBU-856) (#1325)
body:
* predict: admin-set fee-incentive subsidy rate and reserve withdrawal

The share of each mint's trading fee paid from sponsor-funded incentives was a
fixed 20% constant, and sponsored USDC could only leave the pool reserve by being
spent on subsidies.

`protocol_config::set_fee_incentive_subsidy_rate` (AdminCap) now sets the rate
within [0, 50%], stored in a dynamic field on ProtocolConfig because Mainnet is
live and the struct layout is frozen. An unset field reads the old 20%, so no
migration is needed. Quotes and mints read it live, so a change reaches markets
already trading; the exact-cost budget search samples it once. The 50% ceiling
means a trader always pays at least half of every trading fee, so no promotion
makes volume free; any ceiling at or below 100% also keeps the subsidy from
exceeding the fee and keeps that search exact (RP-36).

`plp::withdraw_fee_incentives` (AdminCap) withdraws any amount of the pool-level
fee-incentive reserve. It does not reach live markets' allocated balances, which
return to the reserve at the settled-market sweep. Neither call is gated on the
valuation flag: no flush figure reads the rate or the reserve.

Ships in the v4 upgrade alongside #1323, which already set current_version to 4.
Older packages keep charging 20% until the watermark retires them. Documentation
is in the docs pull request stacked on this one.

subject: predict: emit ExpiryPnl from the settled-expiry sweep (DBU-857) (#1324)
body:
* predict: emit ExpiryPnl from the settled-expiry sweep (DBU-857)

A settled expiry's own result was not observable on-chain. `MarketSettled`
carries only the settlement price, and `ExpiryProfitMaterialized` reports
recognized profit: netted against other expiries' carried losses, split
into protocol and LP cuts, and never emitted for a loss.

The settled sweep now also emits `vault_events::ExpiryPnl`, on every
expiry's first settled sweep (even one that returns no cash) and again on
any later sweep that returns more. It reports the pool's lifetime net cash
result on the expiry, received minus sent, as an `in_profit` flag and an
absolute `amount`, with the pool vault and market ids, the underlying, the
cadence-period start, the expiry, the settlement price, and both lifetime
totals. The figure is gross of the protocol/LP split and of cross-expiry
loss netting, and it counts the sponsor fee subsidies mints moved into
expiry cash; the struct doc says to subtract `OrderMinted.fee_incentive_subsidy`
to isolate the trading result.

`period_start_ms` is the market's stored reference-tick time (expiry minus
the cadence period): markets do not record their creation time, and a new
`ExpiryMarket` field would not be upgrade-compatible. A comment where
`registry.move` derives that time names the event as a consumer.

Tests compare each emitted event with a BCS mirror struct: a winning order
(loss), a losing order (profit) whose repeat sweep emits nothing, a
sponsored mint whose subsidy counts as received, an unfunded market whose
first sweep returns no cash, and the flush path.

numeric utilities applies. No behavior change: the loss and profit tests

subject: predict: admin-set fee-incentive live target and lifetime cap rates (#1332)
body:
* predict: admin-set fee-incentive live target and lifetime cap rates

Each live rebalance topped a market's sponsor-funded incentive balance up to a
fixed 2% of its cadence allocation cap, and a market could receive at most a
fixed 10% over its life. With the subsidy rate now admin-set, those fixed slices
decided whether the configured rate held: at a 10,000 USDC allocation cap a

subject: predict: relax the SVI input bounds for SSVI short-tenor slices (DBU-849) (#1335)
body:
Block Scholes SSVI surfaces narrow sigma toward expiry: in their backfill
83% of one-minute slices sit below the 1e-3 floor, which aborted every
pricer load over them, including the flush's atomic snapshot. Lower the
floor to the provider's recommended 1e-5, and remove the |a| <= 100 cap so
a is constrained only by positive minimum total variance, which the
provider recommends; that check now compares instead of summing, so it
cannot overflow at a = u64::MAX. Every slice of the current-style feed
still loads.

The floor also kept sigma^2 representable in the 1e9 smile root. Take
sqrt((k - m)^2 + sigma^2) from exact u128 squares at 1e18 instead; the 1e9
root misprices real one-minute slices by up to 49% relative once the floor
is lowered. simulations/python_replay.py mirrors the new root.

Tests: a generated reference (generate_ssvi_reference.py) pins real SSVI
slices and synthetic surfaces at the floor, past the former a cap, at
rho = -1, at one and under one raw unit of variance, each at its real
forward and at a unit forward, with budgets derived from math.move's
documented primitive bounds; guard tests pin the envelope boundaries and
the provider-width corners; a flush-liveness pair pins the floor on the
mandatory valuation path.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change removes an unsafe magnitude cap and replaces a sum‑based variance check with a comparison to avoid integer overflow at a = u64::MAX, which previously caused crashes (abort) during pricing. This fixes a bug and mitigates a potential denial‑of‑service where an attacker could supply extreme SSVI parameters to trigger the overflow.

subject: server: bound the work an intervalized volume request can cost (#1275)
body:
* server: bound the work an intervalized volume request can cost

/historical_volume_by_balance_manager_id_with_interval walked one database
query per bucket over a caller-supplied window, with only "interval > 0"
between the request and the loop. A wide window with a small interval turned
one unauthenticated request into millions of serial reads, and the seconds to
milliseconds conversions wrapped on extreme values.

The window is now bounded before the first query runs: timestamps must be
non-negative and ordered, the window may not exceed 90 days, and it may not
need more than 500 buckets. The interval must parse as a positive number of
seconds and its millisecond form must fit in an i64. Time conversions
saturate instead of wrapping, and repeated pool names no longer widen every
per-bucket IN list.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* server: widen the volume window cap to a year of daily buckets

A 90-day ceiling refused the endpoint's most natural request — a year of
daily volume — while the bucket budget already bounds the query count at
500, comfortably above the 365 buckets that window needs. The window cap is
there to bound how much of order_fills one request may scan, and the
non-intervalized volume endpoints accept an unbounded window for the same
scan today, so the tighter ceiling bought little.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* server: drive the bucket walk from the budget, not from a comparison

The saturating loop condition could not terminate when end_time clamped to
i64::MAX: saturating_add returns i64::MAX forever, the condition stays true,
and current_start never advances, so the handler issued database queries
without end. Making end_time's conversion saturating is what put i64::MAX in
reach — the previous wrapping multiply could never land on it — so the guard
added to bound this loop is what opened the hole.

The walk now runs over the bucket count the budget already computed, so the
number a request is admitted on is the number of queries it can cost, and
there is no second derivation of where the walk ends. Every bucket lands
inside [start_time, end_time], so the arithmetic cannot overflow.

end_time is also floored at the epoch: about two dozen other handlers
subtract a lookback from it with plain arithmetic, and a clamp to i64::MIN
would underflow them. A pre-epoch end_time selects nothing either way.

Also: cover the termination case, the pool-name dedupe's result-neutrality
and the default interval; name the multi-decade test for the bound it
actually asserts; and correct the OpenAPI entry, which declared interval both
required and defaulted, and stated a minimum interval stricter than the code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change adds strict validation and caps on the intervalized volume request (non‑negative timestamps, ordered window, max 365‑day range, max 500 buckets, interval size checks) preventing an unauthenticated request from spawning millions of DB reads, which previously could be exploited to cause a denial‑of‑service.

subject: predict: mints and live redeems abort on a stale Pyth spot instead of pricing on the fallback (DBU-869) (#1342)
body:
* predict: mints abort on a stale Pyth spot instead of pricing on the fallback

While use_pyth_spot_for_forward is set, a live pricer falls back to the Block
Scholes forward when the Pyth spot is missing, unusable, or older than
pyth_spot_freshness_ms, and until now a mint executed on that fallback like any
other flow.

Every mint and mint-quote entrypoint now aborts pricing::EPythSpotStale in that
state. The shared mint gate (expiry_market::assert_live_mint_allowed) calls the
new pricing::assert_pyth_spot_fresh, which re-evaluates the load's own selection
predicate from the pricer's snapshotted Pyth timestamp, so it fails exactly when
the load fell back. load_live_pricer is unchanged: live redeems, current_nav and
the flush snapshot still price on the fallback, so exits and valuation stay live
through a gap in Pyth updates. With the setting clear the check is skipped.

No stored config or struct layout changes; the rule reuses the existing window.

Tests: mint_pyth_freshness_tests covers all six gated entrypoints, the window
boundary from both sides, a feed with no observation, the configured window, the
redeem exemption, and both recovery paths. The RP-24 stale-Pyth same-transaction
test now pins its exemption on a live redeem, since a mint refuses that state.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: split the mint Pyth abort into unavailable and stale, tighten comments and tests

Review follow-ups to the mint-only Pyth freshness gate:

- The gate fired EPythSpotStale for a feed with no usable spot as well as for an
  old one. It now aborts EPythSpotUnavailable (17) when the pricer recorded no
  usable Pyth spot, and EPythSpotStale (18) when it recorded one older than the
  window, matching the Block Scholes Unavailable/Stale pair.
- Pricer's doc said trade paths gate a pricer on market id alone; mints now also
  gate on its recorded Pyth timestamp, whose zero sentinel is load-bearing. The
  struct, field, and snapshot-site comments say so.
- The gate's doc no longer claims exact equivalence with the load when an admin
  changes PricingConfig between the load and the mint in one transaction.
- Setter and constant docs state that the freshness window is locked during
  valuation and that a window shorter than Pyth landing latency stops minting.
- Tests: a non-positive Pyth print, a widened window admitting an older spot, an
  assertion that the literal window is the configured default, and named
  constants for the budget-mint arguments.

* predict: live redeems also abort on a stale Pyth spot instead of pricing on the fallback

Move the `pricing::assert_pyth_spot_fresh` call from `assert_live_mint_allowed`
to the end of `assert_live_flow_allowed`, the gate every mint, mint quote, and
`redeem_live` shares. While `use_pyth_spot_for_forward` is set, a live close now
aborts `EPythSpotUnavailable` or `EPythSpotStale` instead of executing on the
Block Scholes-forward fallback, like a mint. Valuation (`load_live_pricer`,
`current_nav`, `live_order_value`, the flush snapshot) keeps the fallback;
settlement and settled redemption read no live price and are unaffected. On a
mint the Pyth check now runs before the trading and mint pauses.

Tests: rename `mint_pyth_freshness_tests` to `live_trade_pyth_freshness_tests`;
the stale live redeem now aborts, with the window boundary pinned on a redeem
from both sides and the unavailable case on a rebound unseeded feed; recovery by
deselecting Pyth or a new push covers mints and redeems; new pins for an
unseeded feed with Pyth deselected, the Pyth check running before the trading
pause, and `current_nav` and a full flush pricing an open order on the fallback
forward while the Pyth spot is stale. `expiry_market_gate_tests` gains
`redeem_live_while_trading_paused_closes` for the exit side of the trading
pause. `pyth_write_same_tx_succeeds_when_pyth_read_is_stale` is re-pinned on
live valuation, since no live trade accepts a stale Pyth read now.

The fresh-deployment plan publishes predict_math before Predict and
predict_orders after it, ahead of Sessions. The journal records the
OrderDesk from the companion's publish receipt. enable_order_flow
allowlists the companion's OrderFlow witness through
protocol_config::set_order_flow, replacing the removed policy init, and a
create_queue step creates each initial market's MarketQueue at the ID

policy and floor and checks every active market's queue, and the

subject: deepbook: cap the gas price the EWMA reads at 100k MIST (#1360)
body:
* deepbook: cap the gas price the EWMA reads at 100k MIST

The EWMA gas-price state used the transaction's gas price as is, up to
the protocol maximum. Treat any gas price above 100_000 MIST as 100_000
when seeding the state, updating it, and computing the z-score and the
taker penalty. Updates also read a stored mean above the cap as the cap.

This bounds the stored mean and keeps the update's squared distance and
the scaled gas price inside u64 for every admissible gas price.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* deepbook: read the stored EWMA mean through the cap in z_score and the penalty

update already read a stored mean above the cap as the cap. z_score and
apply_taker_penalty still used the raw stored mean, so a mean recorded
before the cap existed could still overflow z_score's division when
called directly. All three now read the mean through one capped_mean
helper.

Adds tests for an update over a mean above the cap with variance at
u64::MAX, and for z_score and the penalty over a mean above the cap with
variance 1_000_000 MIST^2 and 1.

* propbook: admin-set the Block Scholes SVI model per store (DBU-906)

A Block Scholes SVI series id hashes the provider model name, and Propbook
hardcoded "SVI", so a store could only ever accept and serve that one
surface. Block Scholes now also publishes its SSVI-adjusted short-tenor
surface under a separate model (SVI_REGIME), and moving a network onto it
would otherwise take a source change that also rides into every other
network's next upgrade.

subject: predict: admit sub-precision price inversions in the NAV walk (DBU-790) (#1296)
body:
* predict: admit sub-precision price inversions in the NAV walk (DBU-790)

The payout-tree NAV walk aborted ENonMonotonePrice on any rise in UP price
between ascending active boundaries. The pricer floors N(d2) and the skew
correction separately, so a valid, butterfly-free surface can rise by one raw
unit in the tails (P-35), and two active boundaries straddling that ripple
stalled the market's valuation and the pool-wide flush.

The walk now keeps a running minimum and aborts only on a rise above
`pricing::price_monotonicity_tolerance` (2 raw units). Each boundary still
walks at its quoted price, and a tolerated rise is charged, rounded up, on the
quantity ending at that boundary, so liability never reads below the per-order
sum beyond boundary rounding. Where the old walk returned a value, the new walk
returns the same value; it aborts only where the old walk aborted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* predict: pin the rise charge at a mixed boundary and through the flush (DBU-790)

Two tests for the NAV walk's rise charge:

- a_risen_boundary_charges_only_the_quantity_ending_there: the risen
  boundary closes a self-inverted order and opens a larger one, so the
  charge must fall on the ending quantity alone for the walk to equal the
  per-order sum.
- a_tolerated_rise_is_charged_through_the_flush: an order minted in band
  that ends at the risen boundary after the surface ages. Live NAV and the
  flush mark both read the market at the per-order sum plus exactly the
  charge. No flow test failed before this when the charge was removed.

The flush assertion the dust-flush regression used moves into a helper
both flow tests share.

subject: margin: cap pool utilization at 100% (DBU-1070) (#1382)
body:
* margin: cap pool utilization at 100% (DBU-1070)

Borrow can exceed supply once a liquidation default writes supply down,
possibly to zero while other borrows are outstanding. `utilization_rate`
read zero supply as idle and otherwise returned the uncapped
`borrow / supply`, so interest in that state did not follow the curve
and the ratio could exceed what fits in u64.

`utilization_rate` now reads 100% whenever borrow is at or above supply,
including zero supply with borrow outstanding. The borrow gate also
checks borrow against supply directly, because a capped utilization can
no longer exceed a `max_utilization_rate` of 100%.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* margin: keep the supplier rate on borrow above supply

`true_interest_rate` multiplied the borrow rate by utilization, which is
now capped at 100%. Suppliers still receive the net interest on all of
the borrow, so once borrow reaches supply the rate is computed from
`borrow / supply` directly. Below that it is unchanged, and zero supply
reads 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change caps utilization_rate at 100% and adds checks to prevent borrow > supply, fixing an integer overflow and incorrect interest calculation that could be triggered after a liquidation default, potentially allowing an attacker to manipulate interest rates or cause aborts leading to fund loss or denial of service.

charged it interest for time before it existed.

placed market order was removed as executed even when it filled only in

* predict: admin-managed cadence table (DBU-1106)

Market lengths were six compiled-in cadences (1m, 5m, 1h, 1d, 1w, 30d), so
any new length needed a package upgrade. The registry now keeps a cadence
table, a vector of periods indexed by cadence ID stored as a dynamic field
on the Registry, seeded with the six built-ins on the first add.

- registry::add_cadence (AdminCap, version-gated) appends a period: a whole
  number of minutes, at most one year, unique, at most 16 cadences. Emits
  CadenceAdded.
- registry::cadence_periods returns the table; cadence_configs now returns
  one row per entry. Rows stored before a cadence was added read as
  disabled and pad when written.
- The slot rule ranks by period: a cadence skips an expiry that an enabled
  cadence with a longer period divides. Identical to the former ID order
  for the six built-ins.
- set_template_cadence_config rejects terms that push one underlying's
  enabled windows past max_live_expiry_markets.

subject: propbook, predict: price Block Scholes SVI at 1e18 behind an admin-set store decimals (DBU-1152)
body:
Block Scholes signs SVI parameters at 1e9 fixed point. On an SSVI slice
`a` is about theta/2, a raw unit or two at 1e9 10-20 s before a one-minute
expiry, so rounding the inputs alone moves short-dated prices by percent-scale
amounts (P-33), and a slice whose `a` rounds to zero with an increment under
one raw unit fails the load gate (EBlockScholesMinVarianceInvalid) and aborts
pricer loads and the flush snapshot. The provider's websocket can sign at
more decimals, but the decimals are part of the signed series id.

Propbook: each BlockScholesSVIStore carries admin-set SVI decimals in a
dynamic field (SviDecimalsKey), 9 until registry::set_block_scholes_svi_decimals
sets 18. svi_sid, svi reads and apply_svi_batch derive from the stored model
and decimals together; svi_decimals returns the scale so readers interpret
rows correctly. The setter is version-gated like the model setter, accepts
only 9 or 18, and emits BlockScholesSVIDecimalsSet. current_version stays 2:
old-decimal rows are the same surface at lower precision, so the upgrade does
not need to retire the version-2 writers.

Predict: read_inputs takes the store's decimals. At 9 nothing changes. At 18
every parameter rounds half up to 1e9 for the snapshot and the envelope, and
a and b are priced at the 1e18 they arrive at. The minimum-variance gate runs
at 1e18, without the 1e9 floor on the increment, on both the stored tuple
every live price uses and the snapshot's rounded one, so every admitted
snapshot can also price on its own. VolSnapshot keeps a and b at 1e9 because
its layout is fixed, so an 18-decimal admission records the full-precision
tuple in the market's SVI cache, a VecMap from SVI source time to PricingSVI
that pricing keeps on the market's UID (SviKey, 64 entries, first tuple per
source time kept). A fill prices from the entry for its snapshot's source
time when it is the snapshot's whole calibration (a and b round to the
snapshot's, and rho, m and sigma equal it); otherwise it prices from the
snapshot, so a miss costs precision, never the fill. The roll-down takes a and b at 1e18 for both
scales, which on a 9-decimal tuple is pmath::roll_down exactly. The live read
now narrows straight into the snapshot (RawSVI is no longer built) to fit the
package budget. predict_math is unchanged.

Package size (module bytes and names, type origins, a 9-package linkage
table): main 101,228 -> 102,355 of Sui's 102,400.

Tests: Propbook SID pins at 18 decimals, store switch, set-back, model plus
decimals together, unsupported values and the version gate, and the registry
entry. Predict: an exactly scaled 18-decimal slice prices bit for bit as at 9;
a sub-unit slice aborts at 9 and prices to true math at 18; a slice that only
prices at 1e18 and one whose true minimum is negative are refused; the cache's
hit, miss, rounding check, another surface's tuple, first-wins, eviction and
absent-cache cases; and three order-flow fills: one admitted at 18 pricing from
the cached tuple, one admitted at 9 pricing from its snapshot, and one admitted
at 9 that picks up full precision once a later admission caches its
publication.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit fixes rounding and decimal handling for BlockScholes SVI pricing that previously caused price miscalculations and load gate aborts, leading to potential financial loss or service crashes. Correcting the decimal scaling prevents exploitable pricing errors, which is a security-relevant defect.

subject: predict: match a cached SVI tuple's zero sign and hold an ambiguous publication by neither (DBU-1152)
body:
A slightly negative `a` that rounds to zero at 1e9 becomes a nonnegative
zero in the snapshot (i64::from_parts), but the cache comparison kept the
cached tuple's negative sign, so such a fill never matched its own entry and
priced at a = 0. The rounded `a` now takes its sign through from_parts as the
snapshot's did.

An SVI model switch can bring two calibrations published at one source time
that round to the same snapshot, which source time and 1e9 values cannot
tell apart. When an admission brings a different tuple for a source time the
cache already holds, the entry is poisoned (sigma 0, below the envelope's
floor) so it matches no snapshot, and every order on that time prices from
its own 1e9 values instead of one surface's order filling at the other's
precision.

narrow_input takes a precision flag instead of a u128 scale, which keeps the
package inside the limit: 102,395 of Sui's 102,400 bytes.

Tests: a negative `a` that rounds to zero matches its snapshot; a second
calibration under one publication is held by neither; recording the same
tuple again keeps one entry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The commit fixes a logic bug where a slightly negative 'a' rounded to zero kept a negative sign in the cache, causing fills to be priced at a=0 and allowing ambiguous publications to poison the cache. This mispricing can be exploited for financial gain, constituting a security-relevant defect. The changes correct sign handling, cache updates, and scaling logic, addressing the vulnerability.

subject: fix flaky test
body:
A test failed in our CI, run is here https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/actions/runs/6040647861/job/16391896616

the test was breaking when a fuzzed array input had duplicate entries in it (specifically address 0x55FaaD6F3E1C2B8829eAbAf7aA01d91d5491732b)

This is an issue with the test itself, where it’s just not written to handle this case.

if the same address (Strategy) is in the array 2x then this will fail
https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/blob/bde39f5fcb6ec9947dd43318fc463e7ca17a84d6/src/test/unit/DelegationUnit.t.sol#L1066
because it is checking that the difference is equal to the share amount, rather than (share amount * number of times the address is in the array).
it’s an implicit assumption in the test logic that there’s no repeat.

This PR is a simple fix to this failure.
rationale: The commit only modifies test code to handle duplicate addresses in a fuzzed array, fixing a flaky test. It does not change production contract logic, so it is not a bug fix of functional behavior nor a security fix.

subject: Remove Slashing Functionality (and related tests)
body:
Description copied from ticket:
We do not plan to have slashing as part of M2. Leaving this in production code confuses auditors & security researchers, requires undue maintenance, and just generally "muddies the waters".
Slashing functionality has remained in our codebase despite these plans, partly for historical reasons and partly to ensure that we are not "painting ourselves into a corner" to too great a degree.
Removing this functionality means clear acceptance of a decision that has already been made explicitly, as well as being made implicitly many times over -- slashing will not be "unpaused" without an upgrade.
Given that the functionality is very likely to change without upgrading and changing it, by removing the functionality from our main codebase, we are simplifying what we actually plan on shipping, with no decrease in "real" / usable functions.
If we wish to reintroduce the same functionality, we can simply revert the changes that remove it, or similar.
Development of slashing features can still of course also be done at any time, on a branch.
rationale: The commit removes slashing functionality and related tests; it does not correct incorrect behavior but merely deletes unused code, so it is not a bug fix and not a security fix per the given criteria.

shares, whether through undelegation, redelegation, or a simple
withdrawal
- Changes in `StrategyManager.sol`, `IShareManager.sol`,
`SlashingLib.sol`, and `EigenPodManager.sol` to accommodate new
accounting
- New test files and changes to others to reflect new accounting and
invariants
- Updated `docs/SharesAccounting.md`

**Result:**

System is now robust to stakers with arbitrary EigenPod states

subject: refactor: registrar interfaces (#1102)
body:
**Motivation:**

Currently there is no way for an AVS implementing these callback
functions of the IAVSRegistrar.sol to verify that the operatorSetIds
belong to their operatorSets. The register/deregister callback functions
are updated to include the address field.
This PR is combining
https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/pull/1092 and
https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/pull/1085

Additionally, the try/catch design for deregistering from operatorSets
was impacting state between AVS and core contracts due to not having
proper gas estimates when submitting transactions. Solutions exploring
passing some suitable gas paramter were explored but eventually removing
it entirely was deemed the best solution.

**Modifications:**

- Added `avs()` view function that is checked upon `setAVSRegistrar`
- added `address avsIdentifier` field in the callbacks, this should
match the `avs()` view function on the AVSRegistrar
- Removed try catch on `deregisterForOperatorSets`

**Result:**

AVSRegistrars cannot be used for multiple operatorSets and AVSRegistrars
can doublecheck to verify that a register/deregister callback is
correctly called for their contracts.
Registration state between AVS and Eigenlayer core contracts for
OperatorSets are now done in atomic transactions (if entrypoint is
always through the AllocationManager)
rationale: The change adds an avsIdentifier address to registrar callbacks and enforces that the registrar supports the specific AVS, fixing a missing access control check that previously allowed an AVSRegistrar to be used for multiple operator sets, potentially leading to unauthorized registration/deregistration and fund loss.

subject: feat: pectra compatibility (#1053)
body:
Updates checkpoint proof system to be Pectra compatible. The breaking
change to EigenPods is the `BeaconState` container increasing to have 37
fields, which results in the tree height to be > 5.

We need to solve for the following cases:

- Prevent deneb proofs from being submitted to pectra blocks
- Ensure that the PECTRA_FORK_TIMESTAMP is the first timestamp at or
after the pectra hard fork for which there is a non missed slot

To do this, here is the upgrade process:

1. Pause checkpoint starting & credential proofs
2. Upgrade after fork is hit
3. Run script to detect the first timestamp at or after the pectra hard
fork for which there is a non missed slot
4. Set pectra fork timestamp to the first timestamp at which there is a
pectra block header
5. Unpause

- Updated balance container and validator container proofs to pass in a
proof timestamp & pectra fork timestamp to check against which tree
height to use for the beacon state
- Modify storing variables in memory to handle stack too deep errors
- Note that since the 4788 oracle returns the PARENT beacon block root,
our check against the pectra fork timestamp returns the previous tree
length for proofs that are <= `pectraForkTimestamp`

- Post pectra, we can upgrade the EigenPod to deprecate the fork
timestamp case handling once all in progress pre-Pectra checkpoints have
been completed

- [x] Unit Tests
- [x] Integration Tests simulating upgrade
- [x] Mekong Deployment
- [x] Update Integration Test User to use validators >32 ETH
rationale: The commit introduces Pectra compatibility, new errors, events, and setter functions to handle a new fork. It is a feature addition and refactor, not a correction of previously incorrect behavior, and the diff shows no security-related bug being fixed.

subject: fix: DSF increase on checkpointed nonzero shares (#1176)
body:
**Motivation:**

There exists an edge case where:

1. Alice queues a withdrawal for all her shares
2. Alice's operator is slashed
3. Alice checkpoints (no rewards or slashes). This actually increases
her DSF, even though there wasn't a balance increase on the beacon chain
4. Alice completes withdrawal as tokens
5. Alice redeposits

After step 5, Alice's withdrawable shares are overcounted due to
increasing the DSF. Note that in step 4 if Alice completes her
withdrawal as shares she can still inflate her withdrawable shares.

**Modifications:**


The fix is to prevent any state updates if `addedShares` is 0. In
addition, we also update `recordBeaconChainETHBalanceUpdate` to only
call the DM if there is a nonzero `balanceDeltaWei`, which is symmetric
to the behavior in the `StrategyManager`.

Regression tests:

- [x] testFuzz_noCall_zeroBalanceUpdate
- [x] testFuzz_deposit_delegate_allocate_slash_checkpointZeroBalance
- [x]
testFuzz_deposit_delegate_allocate_slashAndQueue_checkpoint_redeposit
- [x]
testFuzz_deposit_delegate_allocate_slashAndQueue_completeAsTokens_redeposit
- [x]
testFuzz_deposit_delegate_allocate_slashAndQueue_checkPoint_completeAsShares

**Result:**

Inflating withdrawable shares edge case fixed.
rationale: The commit fixes an edge‑case where a zero‑share update incorrectly increased the beacon‑chain slashing factor, allowing a user to inflate withdrawable shares and withdraw excess tokens. This is a logic bug that could be exploited for financial gain, so it is a security‑relevant bug fix.

subject: test: checkpoint with no added shares (#1191)
body:
<!-- 
    🚨 ATTENTION! 🚨

closed without review.

- Label your PR with the correct type (e.g., 🐛 Bug, ✨ Enhancement, 🧪
Test, etc.)
    - Provide clear and specific details in each section
-->

**Motivation:**

`EigenPodManager.recordBeaconChainETHBalanceUpdate` currently has a bug
where shares increases of 0 addedShares will forward a call to the
DelegationManager and updates the DSF. This can be manipulated to
increase your DSF and inflate a staker's inflatable shares. The test in
this PR demonstrates a possible exploit scenario.

**Modifications:**

Added test file `Integration_CompleteCP_WithNoAddedShares` and
integration test `test_completeCP_withNoAddedShares`

Setup is as follows:
1. Setup a Staker EigenPod where they are initially slashed and have a
non-WAD BCSF
2. Queue withdraw all deposit shares setting it to 0
3. Start/Complete checkpoints with 0 addedShares
- This triggers the following code block in `SlashingLib.sol` when
updating the DSF and increases the staker's DSF
```
if (prevDepositShares == 0) {
    // If this is the staker's first deposit or they are delegating to an operator,
    // the slashing factor is inverted and applied to the existing DSF. This has the
    // effect of "forgiving" prior slashing for any subsequent deposits.
    dsf._scalingFactor = dsf.scalingFactor().divWad(slashingFactor);
    return;
}
```
4. Deposit again (in this case complete withdrawals as shares from step
3)
5. Delegate to an Operator

Staker ends up having inflated withdrawable shares and as a result is
able to delegate way more share than they should be able to for an
operator.


**Result:**

After this issue is fixed, this integration test should pass
rationale: The commit only adds/updates integration test files and adjusts test tolerances; no production contract code is changed. Therefore it does not fix any existing bug, nor does it mitigate a security issue.

subject: fix: zero duration (#1216)
body:
**Motivation:**

The `RewardsCoordinator` currently allows `0` duration reward
submissions which leads to a divide-by-zero bug in the rewards
calculation in the sidecar.

This has already been patched in testnet and mainnet in the sidecar by
ignoring any such reward submissions:
1. https://github.com/Layr-Labs/sidecar/pull/266
2. https://github.com/Layr-Labs/sidecar/pull/275

**Modifications:**

* Added validation to ensure `duration > 0` 
* Relevant tests
* Updated docs and interface natspec

**Result:**

Fixed `EL21-01: Division By Zero In Rewards Calculation Due To Zero
Duration` issue by SigmaPrime.
rationale: The commit adds a require(duration > 0) check, fixing a zero‑duration path that caused a divide‑by‑zero in rewards calculation. An attacker could submit a zero‑duration reward to trigger the bug and halt reward processing, constituting a denial‑of‑service vulnerability.

subject: fix(cantina): deposit share cast bug (#1265)
body: **Motivation:** *Explain here the context, and why you're making that change. What is the problem you're trying to solve.* Fix for high sev bug found in Cantina competition. **Modifications:** Contract Changes (EPM): - Safecasting uint256 `depositSharesToRemove` to int256 since this input is provided by the user through `DelegationManager.queueWithdrawals` Tests: - Unit test `testFuzz_removeDepositShares_revert_depositSharesOverflow` which does not bound fuzzed values of `depositSharesToRemove` and checks for casting overflow, negative shares, or a valid input - Removed all `uint224` usage in the EPM unit tests - Regression test POC showing the inflation of staker shares based on original finding `testFuzz_deposit_revertOverflow_queueWithdrawal` Screenshot below is test with the expectedRevert message commented out and with original unsafe casting implementation in the EPM. We can clearly see the depositSharesAfter is much larger than originally... Updated Certora Spec: - Fixed certora parametric rule `integrityOfRemoveDepositShares` to not constrain input values and assert invalid input does not affect depositShares. Updated rule passes here https://prover.certora.com/output/748112/55c59f0cc8144022afe5c22dd1818b77/?anonymousKey=850e5552efec6219cdf5c386b6dc1d62629138e9 **Result:** Fix for bug --------- Co-authored-by: Yash Patil <40046473+ypatil12@users.noreply.github.com>
rationale: The change replaces an unsafe cast of a user‑controlled uint256 to int256 with SafeCast, preventing overflow that previously allowed depositShares to be inflated via a large depositSharesToRemove value. This corrects a bug and mitigates a vulnerability where an attacker could gain excessive shares, a classic integer overflow issue.

subject: test: zeus queued deployments + arbitrary envs (#1287)
body:
**Motivation:**

We want to support Zeus config parsing to enable testing of queued
deployments. Our original deployment parser lacked the flexibility
needed to support Zeus without requiring changes to Zeus itself.
Additionally, the `User` and `AVS` contracts deployed by the
`IntegrationDeployer` aren't able to properly read config from
`IntegrationDeployer` leading to bandaid solutions.

**Modifications:**

- Removed `InitialDeploymentParser`: About 1k lines -> 100 for parsing.
- Added `ConfigParser`: A parser that supports both fast TOML parsing
and Zeus-style parsing.
- Added `ConfigGetters`: A abstraction that allows contracts deployed by
the `IntegrationDeployer` to easily access the current configuration.

**Result:**

Contracts deployed through the `IntegrationDeployer` can now reliably
access their configuration, and Zeus integration is possible without
needing to modify Zeus.
rationale: The commit introduces new configuration parsing utilities and test changes to support Zeus integration. It adds features and refactors parsing logic without correcting previously incorrect behavior, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

`decreaseBurnOrRedistributableShares`

-- `getBurnOrRedistributableShares(operatorSet, slashId) returns
(Strategy[] Strats, uint256[] shares)

returns (shares)
-- `getBurnOrRedistributableCount(operaotrSet, slashed) returns (count)`

**Result:**

Correct code with unit tests
rationale: The commit adds a check to prevent overwriting an existing entry in an EnumerableMap and rewrites the loop that removes entries to iterate backwards, fixing a bug where forward iteration could skip entries due to swap‑and‑pop. subject: fix(audit): out-of-gas issue (#1459)
body:
**Motivation:**

Previously, we stored `startBlock` and computed the `completeBlock` at
runtime by iterating through the list of added strategies for a given
`slashId`. This approach required recalculating the `completeBlock` each
time.

**Modifications:**

We now store `completeBlock` directly instead of `startBlock`. During
each call to `initiateSlashEscrow`, we compare the delay of the newly
added strategy to the current `completeBlock` for the `slashId`. If the
new delay is larger, we update `completeBlock` accordingly. This ensures
that the maximum delay is always preserved.

**Result:**

The `completeBlock` for each `slashId` is now computed and maintained
incrementally, eliminating the need for runtime iteration over all
strategies.
rationale: The commit replaces runtime iteration over all strategies to compute the escrow completion block with an incremental stored value, fixing an out‑of‑gas issue that could be triggered by many strategies and cause denial‑of‑service of slash escrow processing.

Release functions did not have a `nonReentrant` check, and while code is
well isolated it would be nice to prevent the concern entirely.

**Modifications:**

* Applied the `nonReentrant` modifier to both `releaseSlashEscrow` and
`releaseSlashEscrowByStrategy` functions within the `SlashEscrowFactory`
to prevent potential reentrancy vulnerabilities.

* Relocated the `nonReentrant` modifier from
`clearBurnOrRedistributableShares` to
`clearBurnOrRedistributableSharesByStrategy` in the `StrategyManager` to
ensure both methods are protected.

**Result:**

Less reentrancy-based security risk.
rationale: The diff adds the OpenZeppelin nonReentrant guard to releaseSlashEscrow functions and restores it to clearBurnOrRedistributableSharesByStrategy, fixing a missing reentrancy protection that could have allowed an attacker to repeatedly withdraw escrowed funds.

subject: feat: multichain deploy scripts (#1487)
body:
**Motivation:**

We need deploy scripts for multichain 

**Modifications:**

Adds a `crossChainDeployLib` from:
https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/pull/1474. This
library uses `createX` for deterministic deployments. In order to keep
the same address on all `destinationChains`, we deploy contracts from
the same multisig on each chain.

Add `testnet-base-sepolia` to CI for deploy scripts. 

Adds a `deploy_globalRootConfirmerSet` script. This script initiates a
global root confirmer set (ie. generator) and updates the `network.toml`
file used in the deploy scripts. It is only intended to be used on
`preprod` and `testnet`.

To distinguish between a source and destination chain we add a
`SOURCE_CHAIN: bool` and `DESTINATION_CHAIN: bool` to the Zeus Config.
We skip parts of the deploy if a chain is not a source or destination.

Deploys the contracts in 5 steps

1. `deploySourceChain.s.sol`: Deploys `KeyRegistrar`, `ReleaseManager`,
`CrossChainRegistry`.
2. `deployDestinationChainProxies.s.sol`: Deploys _empty_ proxy
contracts for `OperatorTableUpdater`, `BN254CertificateVerifier`,
`ECDSACertificateVerifier`. _Note: in order to have deterministic
proxies, we need to ensure the `initCode` is the same. Thus, the
implementation is the same `emptyContract` and the proxyAdmin is
initially the `multichainDeployerMultisig`_.
3. `deployDestinationChainImpls`: Deploys implementations using EOA
4. `instantiateDestinationChainProxies`: Upgrades the proxies to the
actual implementations. Transfer proxy admin to the actual `proxyAdmin`
5. `configureCrossChainRegistry`: Updates the `crossChainRegistry` on
the `SOURCE_CHAIN` to whitelist proper chainIds

**Result:**

Deploy scripts

---------

Co-authored-by: clandestine.eth <96172957+0xClandestine@users.noreply.github.com>
rationale: The commit introduces new multichain deployment scripts, CI configuration changes, and minor binding renames. It adds functionality rather than correcting previously incorrect behavior, and the diff shows no security-related bug remediation.
