  mvr slug, path to each package's index.yaml, one-line summary).
- schemas/llms-package-index-v1.json: extended to a oneOf over two forms —
  root catalog (packages[]) and per-package index (modules[]) — distinguished
  by disjoint required keys (repo+packages vs package+install+modules). One
  schema, no new file; dispatch stays by the shared `index.yaml` name.
- llms.txt: points at the root catalog as the structured discovery entry.
- CI: scope=DIFF grep widened to `(^|/)llms/` so the root llms/index.yaml
  (whose path has no leading slash) is picked up on change.

Deliberately minimal: no dedicated catalog schema or filename — an earlier
iteration that added both was reverted as overkill. The root catalog reuses
the index.yaml name + index schema; glob `**/llms/index.yaml` remains a
fallback for consumers with repo access.

(23/23 schema, 19/19 semantics).

subject: ci(llms): add completeness check (source ↔ metadata)
body:
Third validation layer above schema + semantics: asserts the metadata set
stays in sync with the Move source tree, catching the "added a module,
forgot its YAML" class (and the reverse).

scripts/validate-llms-completeness.py — per package:
- every non-internal `<pkg>/sources/**/*.move`, by its DECLARED module name
  (not the file basename — `conversions.move` declares `sd29x9_convert`),
  must have an `index.yaml` modules[] entry AND a per-module YAML whose
  module.name matches the fully-qualified declaration;
- orphan check: every per-module YAML must map to a real non-internal source
  module;
- every index modules[].path must resolve on disk.
Root catalog (`llms/index.yaml`): every listed package index must exist, and
every on-disk package index must be catalogued.

Workflow: completeness runs whole-tree and ALWAYS (even when the YAML diff is
empty) — a sources-only change can add a public module with no YAML, which
produces zero YAML diff but is exactly the gap to catch. Path filter gains
`**/sources/**/*.move`. Negative-tested: orphan YAML and missing index path
both flagged; current tree passes (3 packages complete).
rationale: The commit adds a new CI validation script and updates the workflow to enforce that every public Move module has corresponding metadata YAML and index entries, fixing a previous omission where such inconsistencies were not caught. This corrects a defect in the repository's validation process but does not address a security vulnerability.

subject: docs: [N-02]: warn against preserving bucket anchor across a rate change (#350)
body:
* docs: warn against preserving bucket anchor across a rate change

Accrual applies the current rate over the entire span since the anchor,
so carrying an old last_refill_ms anchor while changing refill_amount or
refill_interval_ms re-prices elapsed time at the new rate and mints
tokens instantly. Document this constraint in the new_bucket parameter
doc and the module-level Reconfiguration section.

deposit() joined the funds unconditionally and always emitted a
VaultDeposit event, so a zero-value deposit (e.g. cancel_emergency /
cancel_after_close routing empty proceeds through do_cancel) produced a
spurious VaultDeposit { amount: 0 }. Join still runs (consuming the
balance, a no-op for zero), but the event is now gated on amount != 0,
matching vesting_wallet::deposit.

subject: Removing more asserts in favor of require (#834)
body:
* Removed asserts and replaced them in favor of require

* Adapted tests to work with requires
rationale: The commit replaces `assert` on external calls (token.transfer, token.transferFrom, token.approve, and owner.send) with `require` or `transfer`. Using `assert` on external call return values can cause an invalid opcode revert that consumes all gas, enabling a denial‑of‑service attack if a token returns false. Switching to `require`/`transfer` correctly reverts without exhausting gas, fixing the bug and mitigating the DoS risk.

subject: Signature Malleability: (#1622)
body:
* Transaction Malleability:
If you allow for both values 0/1 and 27/28, you allow two different
signatures both resulting in a same valid recovery. (r,s,0/1) and
(r,s,27/28) would both be valid, recover the same public key and sign
the same data. Furthermore, given (r,s,0/1), (r,s,27/28) can be
constructed by anyone.

* Transaction Malleability:
EIP-2 still allows signature malleabality for ecrecover(), remove this
possibility and force the signature to be unique.

* Added a reference to appendix F to the yellow paper and improved
comment.

* better test description for testing the version 0, which returns
a zero address

* Check that the conversion from 0/1 to 27/28 only happens if its 0/1

* improved formatting

* Refactor ECDSA code a bit.

* Refactor ECDSA tests a bit.

* Add changelog entry.

* Add high-s check test.
rationale: The commit changes ECDSA.recover to reject non‑canonical signatures (v values 0/1 and high‑s values) that previously were accepted, fixing signature malleability. Allowing multiple valid signatures for the same message is a security flaw (signature spoofing/replay), thus the change is both a bug fix and a security fix.

subject: Update ReentrancyGuard for Istanbul Hard Fork (#1992)
body:
* Update ReentrancyGuard for Istanbul Hard Fork

Changes:
Added L37, `_guardCounter = 1;`

Rationale:
The planned _Istanbul Hard Fork_ will implement [EIP 2200](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/e4d4ea348e06c54d0075c400dc7b72430d427ff1/EIPS/eip-2200.md), which implements "net gas metering" for `sstore` operations. If the final value of `_guardCounter` is unchanged relative to the original value of it, a gas refund will be applied and charges for changing the value of `_guardCounter` will effectively not exist. This ends up being cheaper than the current implementation ONLY AFTER Istanbul. Before Istanbul, the added line actually ends up costing more gas.

Note that if `_guardCounter` is `0` initially, the initial cost and subsequent refund will both be larger than if `_guardCounter` is `1` initially. Although in both cases, the net gas cost (`gasCost - gasRefund`) are equal, it's better in terms of cost to have both the gas cost and refund smaller, as there is some limit to the percentage of a gas refund that can actually be realized.

* Update CHANGELOG.md

Added note for change to ReentrancyGuard.sol

* Update ReentrancyGuard.sol

* Update CHANGELOG.md
rationale: The commit only adds a line resetting _guardCounter to 1 after the reentrancy check to obtain a gas refund after the Istanbul hard fork. It does not change the functional behavior of the reentrancy guard, so it is a gas‑optimization change, not a bug fix or security fix.

body:
* Fix unnamed return variable warning

This commit fixes warnings thrown by the solc 0.7.4 compiler:
"Warning: Unnamed return variable can remain unassigned. Add an explicit
return with value to all non-reverting code paths or name the variable."

* Fix function state mutability warning

"Warning: Function state mutability can be restricted to pure"

This commit fixes warnings thrown by the solc 0.7.4 compiler:
"Warning: This declaration shadows an existing declaration."

1. Arguments by default are not underscored.
2. If the name isn't available due to shadowing, use prefix underscore.
3. If prefix underscore isn't available due to shadowing, use suffix underscore.
rationale: The changes only rename parameters, add explicit returns, and adjust function mutability to silence compiler warnings. No functional behavior is altered, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: Replace immutable with constant for _PERMIT_TYPEHASH (#3196)
body:
* replace `immutable` with `constant` for _PERMIT_TYPEHASH

This commit is related to the following issue discussion: https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/contracts-wizard/issues/89#issuecomment-1042391318

Since Solidity version `0.6.12` the `keccak256` of string literals is treated specially and the hash is evaluated at compile time. Since the OpenZeppelin Wizard also uses `constant` for OpenZeppelin's AccessControl's roles declarations, it's good practice to make this consistent.

subject: feat(entropy): Add callback failure states to the contract (#2546)
body:
Currently, the Entropy keeper cannot invoke a callback if the underlying callback fails. This creates confusion for users, who can't distinguish between "the keeper is offline" and "my callback code reverts".

This change creates a failure flow for callbacks that allows the keeper's transaction to succeed while explicitly reporting a failure of the underlying callback. Requests with failing callbacks remain on the blockchain and can be re-invoked by users. This feature allows users to gracefully recover in cases where the callback fails for transient reasons. (In the future, it will also allow recovery in the case where the callback uses too much gas.)

Note that this PR doesn't cover the case where the callback uses too much gas. I will send a follow-up PR for that.
rationale: The change replaces the direct callback call with a safe call and adds callback status tracking, preventing the keeper transaction from reverting when a user callback reverts. This fixes the previous bug where callback failures caused transaction failure and mitigates a denial‑of‑service vector where a malicious callback could block the keeper.

subject: fix(entropy): Only mark callbacks as failed if enough gas was provided, regardless of revert code (#3106)
body:
Summary
This PR removes the check that allows us to mark callbacks as failed (even if enough gas wasn't provided) if they revert with a non-empty return code.

Rationale
When we wrote this initally, we thought that all out-of-gas reverts from calling contracts would bubble up and be caught by the ret.length == 0 condition. However, we have found that some contracts catch out-of-gas reverts and then revert with a different error code. This means we can end up calling these callbacks without enough gas.

Simple fix here is to require enough gas to be provided regardless of the revert code.
rationale: The change removes the ret.length > 0 check, ensuring callbacks are only marked as failed when sufficient gas was provided. Previously, callbacks could be incorrectly marked as failed (or not retried) when they reverted with data but ran out of gas, allowing an attacker to cause a denial‑of‑service by crafting such reverts. The diff directly addresses this logic, indicating a security‑relevant fix.

subject: feat(sui-sdk): support multiple accumulator messages in single transaction
body:
This change removes the error that was thrown when multiple accumulator
messages were passed to updatePriceFeeds, updatePriceFeedsWithCoins, and
createPriceFeed methods.

The fix processes each accumulator message independently within the same
transaction by:
- Extracting the VAA from each accumulator message and verifying it
- Creating a hot potato for each accumulator message
- Parsing each accumulator message to extract the price feed IDs it contains
- Mapping each requested feed ID to its corresponding hot potato
- Updating each price feed using the correct hot potato
- Destroying all hot potatoes at the end of the transaction

This allows users to update price feeds that span different VAAs in a
single transaction, which was previously not supported.

Co-Authored-By: Ali <ali@dourolabs.xyz>
rationale: The change removes an SDK error that prevented multiple accumulator messages in a single transaction and adds logic to handle them, fixing incorrect behavior. No security-related checks are added or vulnerabilities addressed.

subject: ci: build SBF programs per-manifest, fix workspace feature unification
body:
Building the three SBF program crates from the workspace root with
`cargo build-sbf -- -p pyth-solana-receiver -p pyth-push-oracle -p
wormhole-core-bridge-solana` unifies features across the workspace.
The `workspace.dependencies` declaration sets `features = ["no-entrypoint"]`
on both `pyth-solana-receiver` and `wormhole-core-bridge-solana`, and
since `pyth-solana-receiver`'s regular (non-dev) dep on
`wormhole-core-bridge-solana = { workspace = true }` is in the selected
build graph, the feature gets activated on the wormhole cdylib build,
suppressing its entrypoint. The result is a 896-byte stub instead of
the real 553k-byte program, which then makes test_post_updates_with_wormhole
fail with `UnsupportedProgramId` when the test loads the .so.

Build each program standalone via `--manifest-path` instead — that roots
the build graph at the single crate and skips feature unification from
other workspace members. Run the integration tests directly with `cargo
test -p ...` and `SBF_OUT_DIR` set, since the SBF artifacts are already
built and we don't want `cargo-test-sbf` to rebuild them through the same
workspace path.

Also flip `cli`'s `pyth-solana-receiver` dep to `features = ["no-entrypoint"]`
so the cli is self-buildable (was previously relying on feature unification
from `common_test_utils`), and drop the now-stale `borsh0_10 is deprecated`
comment plus `#[allow(deprecated)]` in `price_update::check_size` since
`solana_borsh::v1::get_packed_len` isn't deprecation-flagged.
rationale: The commit fixes a build configuration bug where workspace feature unification caused the Solana program to be built without its entrypoint, resulting in a stub binary and failing tests. This is a functional bug fix, not a security vulnerability.

subject: fix(sui): disable set_governance_data_source as stopgap for replay bug (#3809)
body:
* fix(sui): disable set_governance_data_source as stopgap for replay bug

Replace the body of `pyth::set_governance_data_source::execute` with an
unconditional abort so that Pyth governance data source rotation cannot
fire on Sui. This kills the in-PTB replay attack against Sui Pyth
governance (bug bounty report #79076 / i-bouhkykq) without requiring a V2
contract migration.

The replay works because `WormholeVAAVerificationReceipt` carries only
`payload`, `digest`, and `sequence` — it does not bind to the data
source the VAA was verified against. An attacker who has a stale,
previously-signed governance VAA (e.g. `SetDataSources`, `SetUpdateFee`,
`SetStalePriceThreshold`, `SetFeeRecipient`, `ContractUpgrade`) can, in
one PTB, verify both the stale VAA and a fresh `SetGovernanceDataSource`
VAA against the current source, then execute the rotation receipt first.
Rotating the source also overwrites `last_executed_governance_sequence`
with the payload-controlled `initial_sequence`, so the stale receipt
slips past the post-rotation monotonicity check and replays against the
new source.

A proper fix has to bind the data source to the receipt and re-check it
at execute time, which under Sui's `compatible` upgrade policy can only
land as an additive V2 receipt + V2 function variants (changing existing
struct layout or function signatures is rejected by the package upgrade
verifier). Until that V2 upgrade ships, this stopgap closes the
rotation vector and makes the Sui Pyth governance emitter effectively
immutable. The governance source on Sui has been stable since
deployment, so disabling rotation temporarily is an acceptable cost.

Notes:
- Function signature is preserved (parameters underscored to silence
  unused-parameter warnings); this is a body-only change so the package
  upgrade verifier still accepts it under `compatible`.
- The dispatcher in `governance.move` is unchanged and still routes the
  `SetGovernanceDataSource` action to `execute`; the abort happens in
  the callee.
- Removed now-unused imports and the `GovernanceDataSource` /
  `from_byte_vec` helpers (private removals are allowed under
  `compatible`).
- Added an inline regression test that verifies a `SetGovernanceDataSource`
  governance VAA and asserts `execute_governance_instruction` aborts
  with `E_GOVERNANCE_DATA_SOURCE_ROTATION_DISABLED`. The test VAA is
  signed by the well-known Wormhole devnet guardian; the corresponding
  guardian address is wired into `setup_test`.

Local `sui move build` / `sui move test` could not be run in this
sandbox — the project pins Sui rev `041c5f2b` (compiler 1.27.2), which
requires libclang to build from source; the matching pre-built binary
is not published. CI will exercise the gate.

subject: fix(near): gate wormhole upgrade entry point to wasm32 so ABI builds
body:
The reproducible build failed because the raw `#[no_mangle] update_contract`
entry point was not gated to wasm32. On the host-target ABI dylib that
`cargo near` builds, the ungated entry point kept its deploy_contract/migrate
cross-contract promise calls alive past dead-code elimination, leaving
undefined NEAR host symbols (e.g. promise_batch_action_function_call_weight)
that fail ABI extraction at dlopen. near-sdk gates its own generated entry
points the same way, which is why the receiver builds ABI cleanly.

Gating it lets ABI generation succeed, so the wormhole container_build_command
now matches the receiver's exactly (drops the --no-abi workaround). The wasm32
output is unchanged (the gate is true when targeting wasm).

always reverts), and routing it through a linked library would make a
mis-linked deployment unrecoverable.

subject: test(solana): rehearse the guardian set migration against the mainnet bridge
body:
Adds an end-to-end test that starts from the Core Bridge binary currently
deployed on Solana mainnet, reproduces mainnet's guardian set history by
replaying the seven real Wormhole `GuardianSetUpgrade` VAAs, then performs the
migration — upgrade the program, close every guardian set, re-run `initialize` —
and relays a production Pyth Pro router VAA through the result.

The pre-migration binary is checked in as a fixture because the migration's
riskiest properties only hold across the program upgrade: that the legacy
guardian sets are all closable, that closing them frees the index-0 PDA that
`initialize` needs, and that the discriminants of the legacy instructions still
line up after the removals. None of that is observable from a test that only
ever runs the post-migration code.

The mainnet initial guardian and upgrade VAAs move from the CLI into
`wormhole-solana` so the test and the CLI share one copy, and the accumulator
update data moves into `common_test_utils` for the same reason.

`ProgramSimulator` now starts with a `ProgramTestContext` so it can expose
`advance_slot`, which the test needs because an upgraded program is not
executable until the slot after the upgrade lands.

subject: fix(entropy): re-resolve request after callback in revealWithCallback
body:
`revealWithCallback` cached a storage pointer to the request slot, called the
requester's `_entropyCallback`, and then kept reading and writing through that
pointer. A callback that reenters Entropy and creates a request colliding on the
same short key evicts the in-flight request into `requestsOverflow` and takes
over the array slot, so the cached pointer ends up aliasing a different request.

Re-resolve the request by identity after the call so the status reset and the
reveal events describe the request actually being revealed.
rationale: The change re‑looks up the request after invoking the callback, fixing a reentrancy bug where the cached storage pointer could be overwritten by a colliding request, leading to state corruption and potential loss of funds or denial of service.

subject: Mask Immutables in Local Verify Task (#691)
body:
Fixes #689

The local verification task does not work correctly for contracts with
`immutable`s. This is because, `immutable` values get written when the
contract's init code executes on-chain, but uses `0` place holders in
the `deployedBytecode` compiler output.

This causes the code that is fetched from the deployed contract to
differ slightly from the compiler's byte code output (fetched code has
non-0 `immutable` values, while the compiler output has 0 `immutable`
values).

The fix is to mask the `immutable`s from the fetched code with 0's
before comparing.

With this fix, `local-verify` script now works for the
`SimulateTxAccessor` contract:

```
$ npx hardhat local-verify --network localhost
Verification status for CompatibilityFallbackHandler: SUCCESS
Verification status for CreateCall: SUCCESS
Verification status for MultiSend: SUCCESS
Verification status for MultiSendCallOnly: SUCCESS
Verification status for Safe: SUCCESS
Verification status for SafeL2: SUCCESS
Verification status for SafeProxyFactory: SUCCESS
Verification status for SignMessageLib: SUCCESS
Verification status for SimulateTxAccessor: SUCCESS
```

subject: Add Safe to L2 Setup Contract (#759)
body:
This PR introduces a setup contract that can be called from the `Safe`
setup function in order to automatically promote a Safe at setup time if
the code is executing on an L2. Namely, this allows the Safe Proxy
factory to use a single singleton and initializer for all chains, but
end up with different `singleton`s depending on the chain ID.

The expected use of this contract is to use the standard proxy factory:

```solidity
Safe l1Singleton;
SafeL2 l2Singleton;
SafeToL2Setup l2Setup;

proxyFactory.createProxyWithNonce(
    address(l1Singleton),
    abi.encodeCall(
        l1Singleton.setup,
        (
            owners,
            threshold,
            address(l2Setup),
            abi.encodeCall(l2Setup.setupToL2, address(l2Singleton)),
            fallbackHandler,
            paymentToken,
            payment,
            paymentReceiver
        )
    ),
    saltNonce
)
```

On L1 (i.e. Ethereum Mainnet where `chainId == 1`), you would end up
with a Safe where `safe.singleton == l1Singleton` and on any other
chains, you would end up with `safe.singleton == l2Singleton`. This
would happen _before_ the first transaction.

body:
Fixes: #787 

## Summary

This PR adds a general migration contract that takes address of the
Safe, SafeL2 and fallback handler contracts during deployment. The
contract allows Safe to update the Singleton at `address(0)`.

- Uses error strings rather than error types because Solidity version
0.7.6 doesn't support it.

As of now tests cover below migration paths: 
- 1.3.0 to 1.5.0
- 1.3.0 to 1.4.1
- 14.1 to 1.5.0

See `SafeMigration.spec.ts` to see how tests are organised. Do share if
you any thoughts to better run same tests on different migration paths.

The migration contract stores address of the Safe singletons and
fallback handler rather than using code hash and requiring the user to
provide singleton address as described in the issue. The reason being as
follows:
 
Checking codehash of the target singleton means user has to provide the
address of the target singleton. Also, checking code hash has higher gas
costs.

The only argument for using code hash for upgrades is that it also
allows unofficial singletons to be used for migration using official
migration contract. But, users/projects can also deploy their own
version of migration contract by providing singleton addresses in the
constructor and have similar security guarantees as the official
migration contract.

## Changes in PR
- Create a general migration contract which is not tightly bound to any
specific Safe version
- Update tests
- Remove other migration contract as this PR supersedes it
 
Unlike `Safe150Migration.sol`, this new contract does not check if
slot(0) of the contract stores an address having some non-empty code. I
think this check is not need because this contract is not intended to be
used in general by other proxy contracts and checking slot(0) value is
only a partially correct way. Would like to know thought of others.

subject: optimize `getTransactionHash` by implementing it in assembly (#847)
body:
This pull request includes significant changes to the `Safe` contract
and its associated test suite. The changes focus on optimizing the
encoding of transaction data and enhancing the test coverage for
transaction hash calculations.

### Optimizations in `Safe` contract:

*
[`contracts/Safe.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-587b494ea631bb6b7adf4fc3e1a2e6a277a385ff16e1163b26e39de24e9483deL414-R467):
Rewrote the transaction data encoding logic in assembly to avoid
multiple memory allocations, improving gas efficiency.

### Enhancements in test suite:

*
[`test/core/Safe.Signatures.spec.ts`](diffhunk://#diff-d7bc3771858069f85022d38344b6cb5302146da4bafde1ac18910e3d7bfac43bL49-R56):
Enhanced the test case for calculating EIP-712 hash by introducing a
loop to generate and test multiple random transactions.
[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d7bc3771858069f85022d38344b6cb5302146da4bafde1ac18910e3d7bfac43bL49-R56)
[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d7bc3771858069f85022d38344b6cb5302146da4bafde1ac18910e3d7bfac43bR72).
The previous test case was inefficient as it contained empty safe
transaction data. The test would still pass if you forgot to include it
in hashing.
* I also added a FV rule to verify hash computation correctness.

### Benchmarks

#### Before
```
  ERC20 - transfer
           Used 51800n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with an EOA (137ms)
           Used 82980n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with a single owner Safe
           Used 88874n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with a single owner and guard Safe
           Used 90024n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with a 2 out of 2 Safe
           Used 97094n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with a 3 out of 3 Safe
           Used 97094n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with a 3 out of 5 Safe
```    

#### After

```
ERC20 - transfer
           Used 51800n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with an EOA (71ms)
           Used 82494n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with a single owner Safe
           Used 88375n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with a single owner and guard Safe
           Used 89547n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with a 2 out of 2 Safe
           Used 96577n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with a 3 out of 3 Safe
           Used 96589n gas for >transfer<
    ✔ with a 3 out of 5 Safe
```

On average, it saves ~485 gas, not much, but considering this is the
hottest path, it should result in significant accumulated savings.
(After 44 Safe transactions, a user would save 21k gas - enough for
broadcasting a native token transfer)

### Codesize

It saves 273 bytes in code size.

#### Before
SafeL2 22582 bytes (limit is 24576)

#### After

SafeL2 22309 bytes (limit is 24576)
rationale: The commit primarily refactors and optimizes the getTransactionHash implementation, changing its visibility to internal and commenting it out of the interface. No bug behavior is corrected, and no security-relevant issue is addressed.

subject: Assembly Memory Safety (#859)
body:
This PR does a once-over on memory Safety for the 1.5.0 contracts. In
particular, there were a couple of missing `memory-safe` tags for some
assembly blocks which were preventing the IR assembler from working
correctly.

Additionally, since the `MultiSend*` contracts changed anyway in 1.5.0,
I took this opportunity to change the assembly to be memory-safe so that
we can tag it. Note that it only adds more code in the revert case, so
it should not have a negative impact for most use-cases.

Furthermore, I added a comment explaining why we did not make the
`SafeProxy` contract memory-safe (that is one intentional).

Lastly, I noticed that there were some `eq(..., 0)` assembly calls which
can be written as `iszero(...)` to save some gas and code. Again, it was
an opportunistic change as the affected contracts have changed anyway
and will be re-audited.

---------

Co-authored-by: Shebin John <admin@remedcu.com>
rationale: The commit fixes missing `memory-safe` tags and adjusts assembly variable names to allow the IR assembler to compile; these changes correct a build‑time issue but do not alter runtime logic or introduce/mitigate a security vulnerability.


However, the tests seem to be quite flaky (ran on my machine once, but
the `anvil` node seems to crash quite often).

subject: Disable Pre-approved IsValidSignature (#866)
body:
This commit disables support for pre-approved signatures from
`msg.sender` for `isValidSignature` calls.

Note that we remove the new 1.5.0-only `checkSignatures` interface in
favour of one with `executor` explicitly provided to avoid issues for
contracts that make use of this function.
rationale: The commit removes the ability for a caller (msg.sender) to be treated as a pre‑approved signer in isValidSignature by making the executor explicit, fixing an authentication flaw where an attacker could supply their own address as executor and bypass signature checks, which could lead to unauthorized transaction execution and fund loss.

and a comment explaining why we only mask for handling the

This pull request includes a small but important change to the
`removeOwner` function in the `OwnerManager` contract. The change
optimizes the decrement operation for the `ownerCount` variable.

The previous code reads from storage twice with the `ownerCount`
variable. By doing pre-decrement (which is cheaper than post-decrement),
we can save on 1 SLOAD.

Optimization:

*
[`contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-795fb06764b4c2d991707584a31509badf0b036c9401bfbcb82d6bc9fdebab82L74-L80):
Modified the `removeOwner` function to use pre-decrement for
`ownerCount` to improve efficiency and ensure the threshold check is
performed correctly.
rationale: The commit only changes the order of decrement to save an SLOAD, preserving the same logical behavior; it does not fix incorrect behavior nor address a security issue.

subject: [Certora Audit] G-09. Cache array length outside of loop (#896)
body:
This pull request includes several optimizations to the `OwnerManager`
and `ERC165Handler` contracts by reducing the number of times array
lengths are accessed within loops. These changes aim to improve the
efficiency of the code by storing the array lengths in variables before
the loops.

If not cached, the solidity compiler will always read the length of the
array during each iteration. That is, if it is a storage array, this is
an extra sload operation (100 additional extra gas for each iteration
except for the first) and if it is a memory array, this is an extra
mload operation (3 additional gas for each iteration except for the
first).

Optimizations in `OwnerManager` contract:

*
[`contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-795fb06764b4c2d991707584a31509badf0b036c9401bfbcb82d6bc9fdebab82L38-R39):
Stored `_owners.length` in a variable `ownersLength` before the loop to
avoid repeatedly accessing the array length.
*
[`contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-795fb06764b4c2d991707584a31509badf0b036c9401bfbcb82d6bc9fdebab82L49-R50):
Updated `ownerCount` to use the `ownersLength` variable instead of
accessing `_owners.length` again.

Optimizations in `ERC165Handler` contract:

*
[`contracts/handler/extensible/ERC165Handler.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-aa0838f20fd3f37b00dc661645b4641500e68762b9b624addb99465fcc65a3e0L56-R57):
Stored `handlerWithSelectors.length` in a variable `len` before the loop
in `addSupportedInterfaceBatch` to avoid repeatedly accessing the array
length.
*
[`contracts/handler/extensible/ERC165Handler.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-aa0838f20fd3f37b00dc661645b4641500e68762b9b624addb99465fcc65a3e0L78-R80):
Stored `selectors.length` in a variable `len` before the loop in
`removeSupportedInterfaceBatch` to avoid repeatedly accessing the array
length.
rationale: The change only caches array lengths in local variables to save gas; it does not alter contract logic or fix incorrect behavior, so it is a performance optimization rather than a bug or security fix.

subject: [Certora Audit] G-10. ++i costs less gas compared to i++ or i+=1 (#897)
body:
This pull request includes several changes to increment and decrement
operations in various Solidity contract files. The primary goal is to
decrease gas usage.

Pre-increments and pre-decrements are cheaper.
For a uint256 i variable, the following is true with the Optimizer
enabled at 10k:
Increment:
- i += 1 is the most expensive form
- i++ costs 6 gas less than i += 1
- ++i costs 5 gas less than i++ (11 gas less than i += 1)

Decrement:
- i -= 1 is the most expensive form
- i-- costs 11 gas less than i -= 1
- --i costs 5 gas less than i-- (16 gas less than i -= 1)

Changes to increment and decrement operations:

*
[`contracts/Safe.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-587b494ea631bb6b7adf4fc3e1a2e6a277a385ff16e1163b26e39de24e9483deL296-R296):
Updated the for loop to use the prefix increment operator in the `Safe`
contract.
*
[`contracts/base/ModuleManager.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-82762908b9416ddadffb149ee4d25f328078fc27f938d454d8a207aad1ec3839L215-R215):
Changed the increment operation to use the prefix increment operator in
the `ModuleManager` contract.
*
[`contracts/base/OwnerManager.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-795fb06764b4c2d991707584a31509badf0b036c9401bfbcb82d6bc9fdebab82L38-R38):
Multiple updates to use prefix increment and decrement operators in the
`OwnerManager` contract.
[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-795fb06764b4c2d991707584a31509badf0b036c9401bfbcb82d6bc9fdebab82L38-R38)
[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-795fb06764b4c2d991707584a31509badf0b036c9401bfbcb82d6bc9fdebab82L63-R63)
[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-795fb06764b4c2d991707584a31509badf0b036c9401bfbcb82d6bc9fdebab82L80-R80)
[[4]](diffhunk://#diff-795fb06764b4c2d991707584a31509badf0b036c9401bfbcb82d6bc9fdebab82L142-R142)
*
[`contracts/common/StorageAccessible.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-a7dd65d90b0567bb9ba14ecd4ff414529a934cd3752ccf309800fad93fba354eL19-R19):
Modified the for loop to use the prefix increment operator in the
`StorageAccessible` contract.
*
[`contracts/handler/extensible/ERC165Handler.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-aa0838f20fd3f37b00dc661645b4641500e68762b9b624addb99465fcc65a3e0L56-R56):

[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-aa0838f20fd3f37b00dc661645b4641500e68762b9b624addb99465fcc65a3e0L56-R56)
[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-aa0838f20fd3f37b00dc661645b4641500e68762b9b624addb99465fcc65a3e0L78-R78)

[`contracts/libraries/SafeToL2Migration.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-925588b812f729cc164d14a48e571ce813e2f0ae6f5c5420fc0382c767287fd0L188-R188):
Changed the increment operation to use the prefix increment operator in
the `SafeToL2Migration` contract.
rationale: The changes only replace post‑increment/decrement with pre‑increment/decrement to reduce gas costs. This does not alter program logic or fix any incorrect behavior, so it is a non‑functional refactor rather than a bug or security fix.

subject: [Certora Audit] G-08. Use shift right/left instead of division/multiplication if possible (#895)
body:

`Safe.sol` and `StorageAccessible.sol` contracts by replacing
multiplication operations with bitwise shift operations. While the `DIV
/ MUL` opcode uses 5 gas, the `SHR / SHL` opcode only uses 3 gas.

Gas optimization changes:

*
[`contracts/Safe.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-587b494ea631bb6b7adf4fc3e1a2e6a277a385ff16e1163b26e39de24e9483deL168-R169):
Replaced the multiplication operation `* 64` with the bitwise shift
operation `<< 6` to reduce gas costs in the `gasleft` check.
*
[`contracts/common/StorageAccessible.sol`](diffhunk://#diff-a7dd65d90b0567bb9ba14ecd4ff414529a934cd3752ccf309800fad93fba354eL18-R18):
Replaced the multiplication operation `* 32` with the bitwise shift
operation `<< 5` to reduce gas costs when creating a new bytes array.
rationale: The commit only replaces multiplication by powers of two with equivalent left‑shift operations for gas savings. This change does not alter contract logic or fix any incorrect behavior, so it is a pure refactor, not a bug or security fix.

subject: Ensure Inner Simulation Reverts (#947)
body:
This PR makes a small modification the `simulate` function such that it
ensures its inner `simulateAndRevert` reverts as expected. This is to
prevent calls to the `CompatibilityFallbackHandler` from making
unexpected state changes when not called by a Safe.

While using the `CompatibilityFallbackHandler` for something other than
a Safe fallback handler is explictely not supported, it makes sense to
ensure the inner call inverts and prevent unintended behaviours.
rationale: The commit changes the `simulate` function to ensure the inner `simulateAndRevert` call always reverts, preventing unauthorized state changes when the handler is called outside of a Safe context. Previously, callers could trigger state changes, representing an authorization flaw that could be exploited to alter contract state.

subject: Ackee[M1]: Deprecate `createProxyWithCallback` Function (#955)
body:
It is possible to front-run a `createProxyWithCallback` deployment using
`createProxyWithNonce` with a crafted `saltNonce`. This would make it so
the proxy would be deployed, but the callback not executed. Since this
method is not in use, we are deciding to deprecate it.

Alternatively, it would be possible to bring it back by using a
different `CREATE2` salt computation method in case this method is
needed in the future. Integrations that require a specific call at
deployment call can use the `setup` parameters with a `to` and `data`,
which would guarantee a callback at deployment time.
rationale: [MEV] The commit removes the `createProxyWithCallback` functions that were vulnerable to front‑running: an attacker could craft a saltNonce to deploy the proxy without the callback executing, breaking expected initialization/security checks. Deprecating the function eliminates this ordering‑dependent race condition, fixing a security defect.

subject: Ackee[L3]: Mask `masterCopy` Selector (#960)
body:
This PR changes the proxy implementation slightly to mask the
`masterCopy` selector instead of assuming that the trailing bytes are 0.
This makes the `masterCopy()` handling Solidity ABI conformant. Without
this change, the `masterCopy` function would not be able to be used
behind an ERC-2771 trusted forwarder for example.
rationale: The commit changes the proxy's selector check to correctly mask the selector, fixing incorrect behavior when extra calldata bytes are present. This is a functional bug fix for ABI compliance, not a security vulnerability.

subject: Ackee[W1]: Less Confusing Event Emission (#973)
body:
We simplified the `ExtensibleFallbackHandler` to use a single event,
instead of selecting an event depending on the parameters. This makes
the events more consistent with the other Safe contract events, namely:

- We roughly emit one event per method (so, `setFallbackHandler` or
`setGuard` also do not distinguish between enabling and disabling, while
`addOwner` and `removeOwner` do)
- We consistently emit an event regardless of whether or not the storage
actually changed.
rationale: The commit only changes event emission logic and storage handling for removals, consolidating events into a single Changed event. This is a refactor for clarity, not a correction of incorrect behavior, and does not address any security issue.

subject: Ackee[W2]: Safe to L2 Migration Adjustments (#961)
body:
This PR changes the `SafeToL2Migration` contract to use `msg.data`
internally instead of re-computing the calldata. We also document that
the accuracy of the `SafeMultiSigTransaction` event data is best-effort
only, highlighting some possible senarios where it may be inaccurate.
rationale: The change replaces manually constructed calldata with msg.data for the SafeMultiSigTransaction event, fixing inaccurate event logging. This corrects a bug in event data but does not alter contract logic or introduce/mitigate a security vulnerability.

subject: Ackee[W3]: Clear High `masterCopy` Bits (#962)
body:
This PR changes the `SafeProxy` to write to the Solidity zero slot
instead of the scratch space. This ensures that the leading bits to the
encoded `masterCopy` value is guaranteed to be zero. While they
currently are 0 for all versions of Solidity that the code supports
(0.7.6 -> 0.8.30), this makes the code future-proof to potential
Compiler changes that may make the scratch space start dirty before
entering the `fallback` method.
rationale: The diff changes the memory location used to return the masterCopy address, ensuring high bits are zeroed. Previously the proxy wrote to a scratch slot that could contain non‑zero bits, potentially resulting in a malformed address and delegatecall to an attacker‑controlled contract, a serious security risk. The fix corrects this behavior, making it a security‑critical bug fix.

subject: Ackee[W4]: `SafeSetup` Outdated Event Parameters (#963)

We document that the `SafeSetup` may emit an event with outdated
parameters if the initializer `DELEGATECALL` modifies any of them on the
Safe.
rationale: The change moves the SafeSetup event emission earlier to ensure the emitted parameters reflect the actual state after delegatecall, fixing a bug where the event could contain stale data. This corrects logging behavior but does not introduce or mitigate a direct security vulnerability.

`TokenCallbacks` to make a best-effort check on whether the tokens were
sent to a Safe that configures a token callback handler contract as a
fallback handler, or if it sent to the fallback handler contract itself
directly.

Thanks @remedcu and @rmeissner for the suggestions on how to implement
it! Basically, it works calling the `msg.sender` and expecting it to be
a Safe configured with the fallback handler. This would either:

- Fail if the token doesn't implement `StorageAccessible`
- Fail if the token doesn't have the specific `FALLBACK_HANDLER_SLOT`
set to the actual fallback handler

Note, however, that it is possible to trick the fallback handler into
receiving tokens. Because of this, we document that the checks are
best-effort only! We add a test to document how the fallback handler can
be tricked.
rationale: The commit adds a best‑effort check in TokenCallbackHandler to ensure tokens are only sent to a Safe that has the fallback handler configured, preventing tokens from being unintentionally locked in the fallback handler contract. This corrects a previous defect that could cause loss of funds, qualifying it as a security fix.

subject: Deprecate `SafeToL2Migration` (#1008)
body:
The `SafeToL2Migration` contract was previously included in the Safe
v1.5.0 release, but it had not been modified to work with the Safe
v1.5.0 contracts. In particular, the version string "1.5.0" had not been
allow-listed by the contract for migrations.

The `SafeToL2Migration` contract is written in such a way that it
requires that the version of the L1 singleton matches the L2 singleton
for the migration to succeed. As such, adding support for the 1.5.0
singletons would have arguably very limited benefit, as all recent Safes
are created with the `SafeToL2Setup` contract in order to ensure
consistent addresses across Ethereum Mainnet and L2s (which use a
different singleton). As such, there should be no new Safes created by
the Safe{Wallet} interface that would require migration, and therefore,
there would be no v1.5.0 Safes created by the interface that would
require migration, making the contract no longer useful for future
versions. **Therefore, we have chosen to deprecate the
`SafeToL2Migration` contract for the 1.5.0 release**.

There is the possibility of adding migration contract from Safes with
singleton version `X.Y.Z+L1` to `1.5.0+L2`, but without clear
requirements, it does not have to be added now or affect the release of
the 1.5.0 contracts.
rationale: The commit only deprecates the SafeToL2Migration contract by removing it from CI, changelog, and certora configs. No code behavior is changed or bug corrected, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: Allow Safe to Own Itself (#998)
body:
This change was originally proposed by @akshay-ap 

This PR reverts an old change (See #229 and #259) and allows the Safe to
once again own itself. This is a step towards 7702 support (#997),
whereby we want the EOA that delegates to a Safe to be able to sign
transactions for itself.

The restriction was originally put in place because `execTransaction`
would call `isValidSignature` on itself (which used to be implemented on
the Safe itself and not as part of the compatibility fallback handler),
where the `msg.sender` would be the Safe itself, and allow for trivial
"approved hash" signatures (through

[this](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-smart-account/blob/36db12a140331c522e773849ebc87d39f5abae1e/contracts/GnosisSafe.sol#L244-L245)
mechanism).

This is no longer possible since v1.3.0, as the `isValidSignature` call
would be handled by the fallback handler, meaning that the `msg.sender`
that can trivially sign "approve hash" signatures is no longer the Safe
itself but the configured fallback handler. Since #866 and starting in
v1.5.0 the `CompatibilityFallbackHandler` is implemented to disallow
"approve hash" signatures regardless of the caller, further eliminating
the requirement for the restriction.

### Increasing Threshold Concerns

One concern with this change, and removing the restriction on having the
Safe own itself, is that the Safe cannot sign for itself, so you can
potentially block access to the account completely, by requiring the
Safe "self-owner" to be included as part of the signing threshold. For
example, if you have a n/n Safe (so `threshold == ownerCount`) and one
of the owners is the Safe itself, then the Safe will not be able to ever
produce a valid signature.
rationale: The change removes the prohibition on a Safe being its own owner, which is a functional/feature change to enable new use‑cases (7702 support). The diff does not fix an exploitable defect; it merely relaxes a previous security‑oriented restriction that is no longer needed.

body:
Description

buildSafeTransaction to avoid overwriting intentional falsy values
(e.g., 0).
- Why: || treats 0/"" as falsy and replaces them with defaults, which
can mask valid inputs and cause subtle bugs.

subject: Prevent Self-Ownership for Non-EIP-7702 Safes (#1062)
body:
Fixed #1055 

This PR changes the Safe smart account logic to disallow `owner == this`
in **unless** `this` is an EIP-7702 delegated account. This enables us
to use Safe as a delegation target, but without leaving in the footgun
where users can accidentally add a non-EIP-7702 Safe as its own owner
and effectively reducing the owner count (since a contract-based Safe
cannot sign for itself) and allowing situations where it is not possible
for generate a threshold of sigantures.

Additionally, I moved some Solidity files around to better reflect the
project layout:
- `Enum.sol` goes to the `interfaces/` directory, since it is arguably
an interface type
- `ErrorMessage.sol` goes into `common/` as it is not a library in the
Safe core contracts meaning of the word.

Added tests around the new logic, and with the refactoring I did in the
`OwnerManager.sol`, the code size actually decreased with this PR, even
with the added feature :)

As a side note, the EIP-7702 tests are unfortunately disabled for
coverage, as they fail with:

```
ProviderError: Cannot send both gasPrice and authorizationList
```

---------

Co-authored-by: Shebin John <admin@remedcu.com>
rationale: The commit adds logic (via EIP7702 inheritance) to reject adding the Safe contract itself as an owner unless it is an EIP-7702 delegated account. Previously, self-ownership could reduce the effective owner count and make the required threshold unreachable, allowing an attacker to lock the Safe's funds. This fixes a security-relevant bug causing potential denial of service.

subject: Add EIP-7951 Signer Support (#1061)
body:
Fixes #1054

This PR adds support for EIP-7951 (and thus RIP-7212) signers to the
Safe contracts, allowing P-256 signers to also sign Safe transactions.
In particular, this is interesting as it allows things like secure
enclave signatures (as the Nist P-256 curve is supported there while the
secp256k1 curve it not).

The new signer works by adding a new signature type (arbitrarily chosen
to be 2), which checks that the `p256verify` precompile returns that a
signature is valid, and checks `address(keccak256(qx, qy))` is a Safe
owner (same address derivation scheme as EOAs, but for the secp256r1
curve).
rationale: The change introduces support for a new EIP-7951 (P-256) signature type (v == 2) and updates related harnesses and specs. It adds functionality rather than correcting previously incorrect behavior, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: docs(FallbackManager): document CALL semantics, msg.sender rewrite, and security implications (#1106)
body:
Closes #532.

## What changed

### `contracts/interfaces/IFallbackManager.sol`
Expanded the `fallback()` NatSpec to document:
1. **Why `CALL` and not `DELEGATECALL`** — the handler executes in its
own storage context so it cannot read or write Safe state;
`DELEGATECALL` would give the handler unrestricted write access to all
Safe storage (contrast: modules already support `DELEGATECALL` when
owners explicitly enable it).
2. **`msg.sender` rewrite** — inside the handler's call frame
`msg.sender` is the Safe's own address, not the original external
caller.
3. **Security warning** — if the fallback handler exposes state-changing
functions that gate access on `msg.sender` alone (e.g. a token
contract), any external account can trigger those operations on the
Safe's behalf. Operators should only install purpose-built, audited
handlers.
4. **Caller recovery** — the original caller address is appended as the
last 20 bytes of calldata; handlers that inherit `HandlerContext` can
recover it via `_msgSender()`.

### `docs/overview.md`
Expanded the one-line "Fallback contract" entry with three sub-sections
that address both the original issue and the follow-up discussion in
#532:
- *How call forwarding works*
- *Why `CALL` instead of `DELEGATECALL`*
- *Security implications of `msg.sender` rewriting* (with a ⚠️ warning
block)

subject: Do Not Propagate Reverts on Signatures (#1115)
body:
This PR changes the behaviour of `checkNSignatures` to not propagate
reverts of `isValidSignature` calls. This is done because `signatures`
bytes are not trusted input, and allows an attacker to cause the Safe to
revert with attacker-controlled data. This ensures consistent use of
error codes across the signature validation logic in the core Safe
account.

New tests were added to check the implementation. A changelog entry was
also added, as this change introduces breaking behaviour around the
signature format (specifically dirty lower bytes and extra data appended
to the `isValidSignature` return data).

subject: Fix Revert Data Length in `CompatibilityFallbackHandler.simulate` (#1123)
body:
When the simulated call fails, `simulate` re-throws the error from
`response`, a `bytes` value laid out as `[length][data]`. The revert
started at the data (`add(response, 0x20)`) but used
`responseEncodedSize` (`length + 0x20`) as its size. So every re-thrown
error had 32 bytes of whatever memory followed `response` added to the
end.

This PR changes the revert size to `mload(response)`, so exactly
`length` bytes of revert data are returned.

The existing "should propagate revert message" test didn't catch this
because decoding `Error(string)` ignores trailing bytes. The new "should
propagate exact revert data" test compares the raw revert data byte for
byte.

This issue was submitted over the [bug bounty
program](https://docs.safefoundation.org/security/bug-bounty) but found
not to be in scope. Shout-out to the anonymous submitter who brought
this to our attention!

Agreement](https://docs.safefoundation.org/cla).
rationale: The change corrects the revert size to use the actual data length instead of length+0x20, fixing a bug where extra memory bytes were appended to revert data. The fix does not address a security vulnerability, as the extra bytes were harmless and the issue was deemed out of scope by the bug bounty program.

subject: Bind Approved Hash Signatures to dataHash When s Is Non-Zero (#1126)
body:
Fixed #187 

Approved hash signatures (`v = 1`) from the executor are not bound to
the hash being signed. If an owner submits the same `execTransaction`
call twice (for example, two identical transactions broadcast at the
same time), both calls succeed and execute for consecutive nonces,
because nothing ties the signature to a particular transaction hash.

This PR lets the `s` value of an approved hash signature optionally bind
it to a specific hash: when `s` is non-zero, `checkNSignatures` reverts
with `GS025` unless `s == dataHash`. Signatures with `s = 0` keep their
current behaviour, so existing signers are unaffected. The check applies
to all approved hash signatures, including hashes pre-approved via
`approveHash`, where it is redundant but harmless.

subject: Fix zero fee calculation (#813)
body:
If a swap has a trading fee and a zero owner fee, when calculating the owner
fee to pool token conversion, the simulated trading fee will be non-zero
because we floor the trading fee to 1 token.  If the input to trading
fee calculation is 0, then we will try to do `0 - 1` on an unsigned int,
which causes an underflow error.  The fix is to simply return a 0 fee
for a 0 input.
rationale: The change adds a guard for token_amount == 0 in calculate_fee, preventing an unsigned integer underflow (0 - 1) that caused a panic. The prior behavior could be triggered by a user input and would abort the transaction, constituting a DoS vulnerability.

subject: swap: Add rounding correction for deposit / withdraw (#1061)
body:
* Add rounding specification for deposit / withdraw

The fuzzing test was improved to make sure that the value of pool tokens
(minus fees) never changed, which revealed a calc bug with deposits and
withdrawals.  If someone withdraws, they can take additional small
value out of the pool in the form of truncated value.

Before, deposit and withdrawal used the same calculation, rounding up the token
A and B amounts.  Remember that deposit / withdrawal specify the pool
token amount, and calculate the amount of A / B required to get to that
many pool tokens.  On withdrawal, we were giving back a little bit too
much.  The concept is that everything would even out since a deposit is
required for a withdrawal, which makes everything a wash.

Fuzzing found this issue very quickly! The change is to introduce a
rounding parameter to avoid ever giving away too much value, either
during deposit or withdrawal.

subject: stake-pool: Add depositor key on init, required on deposit (#1616)
body:
* stake-pool: Add depositor key on init, required on deposit

Some stake pools need to be private, and not allow outside depositors.

Enhance the existing deposit authority in the stake pool be configurable
on initialization, and then require its signature on deposit.

The existing deposit authority is a program address, making deposits
permissionless. This allows a pool creator to set their own deposit_authority on
initialization. In a great turn of events, almost everything else works
the same way!

Here's the current workflow for deposit, where the user calls
stake_program::authorize and stake_pool::deposit in the same
transaction:

* stake_program::authorize assigns staker and withdraw authority to the
  stake pool deposit authority
* stake_pool::deposit
    - uses the deposit authority to assign authority on the deposited
  stake account to the stake pool withdraw authority
    - uses the withdraw authority to merge the deposited stake into the validator stake

The deposit authority must "sign" the transaction in order to reassign
authority to the withdraw authority. Currently, as a program address, it
can just do that. With this change, if the deposit authority is set
during initialization, then that deposit authority must sign the
instruction.

There's also a little update for ease-of-use to always do the
stake_program::authorize in the same transaction as stake_pool::deposit.
This way, in case someone tries to deposit into a forbidden stake pool, the
whole transaction will bail and their stake will stay as theirs.

* Address review feedback

* Fix rebase issues
rationale: The change introduces a new configurable deposit authority and requires its signature on deposits, which is a feature addition to support private stake pools rather than correcting incorrect behavior. No bug is being fixed, and thus no security defect is being remediated.

subject: fix ConcurrentMerkleTreeHeader (de)serialization (#3572)
body:
The `account_type` member of `ConcurrentMerkleTreeHeader` is currently
an `#[repr(u32)]` enum, but borsh only uses one byte to serialize or
deserialize an enum tag, which leads to issues with `try_from_slice`
calls that get passed slices computed based on applying `size_of` to
`ConcurrentMerkleTreeHeader`. This commit replaces the underlying
type of `account_type` with an integer type.

Signed-off-by: Alexandru Agache <alexandruag@gmail.com>

Signed-off-by: Alexandru Agache <alexandruag@gmail.com>
rationale: The change fixes a mismatch between Borsh serialization (1-byte enum tag) and the enum's assumed 4-byte size, which could allow crafted account data to bypass the account_type check, leading to type confusion and potential unauthorized actions. This is a security-relevant bug fix.

subject: transfer hook: add new offchain helper
body:
This PR adds a new offchain helper for adding the necessary account metas for an 
`ExecuteInstruction` to the SPL Transfer Hook interface, deprecating the old 
one.

As described in #6064, the offchain helper in Token2022 was using the original 
offchain helper from the SPL Transfer Hook interface incorrectly when resolving 
extra account metas for a transfer.

In order to provide a safer, more robust helper, this new function takes the 
instruction, fetch account data function, as well as the individual arguments 
for `instruction::execute(..)`. This will help to ensure Token2022 as well as 
anyone else using the helpers from the SPL Transfer Hook interface are properly 
resolving the necessary additional accounts.

Note: Although deprecated, the original helper in the SPL Transfer Hook 
interface is not broken. It's just less safe to use than this new helper, since 
it can easily be misused.
rationale: The change replaces the old offchain helper with a new one that validates required accounts are present and correctly adds extra account metas for ExecuteInstruction, fixing a prior misuse that could allow bypassing transfer‑hook checks and lead to unauthorized token transfers.

subject: token 2022: add new offchain helper
body:
This PR adds a new offchain helper for creating a `TransferChecked` instruction 
with the necessary accounts metas for a transfer hook `ExecuteInstruction` to 
Token2022, deprecating the old one.

As described in #6064, the original offchain helper in Token2022 was being used 
incorrectly to resolve extra account metas. Rather than providing the SPL 
Transfer Hook interface helper with a valid `ExecuteInstruction`, the original 
Token2022 helper was actually providing it with a transfer instruction, causing 
erroneous account resolution.

Taking advantage of the more secure SPL Transfer Hook interface offchain helper 
provided in #6099, this new offchain helper creates a `TransferChecked` 
instruction and calls `add_extra_account_metas_for_execute(..)`, providing the 
keys used to build the transfer instruction.

Note: unlike the deprecated helper in #6099, the deprecated offchain helper in 
Token2022 *is* in fact inaccurately resolving account metas for certain use 
cases, thus it should be vigilantly avoided.
rationale: The commit replaces an offchain helper that incorrectly built a Transfer instruction instead of a proper ExecuteInstruction for transfer hooks, leading to erroneous account resolution. This could allow bypassing transfer hook checks, a security-relevant access control flaw, and the new helper fixes it.

subject: token client: refactor transfer to use new offchain helper
body:
This PR continues the necessary repairs for addressing #6064 by refactoring the
Token Client's `transfer(..)` function to use the new offchain transfer hook
helpers.

If transfer hook accounts are provided, in either case they're appended to the

If no transfer hook accounts are provided:
- If decimals are provided, Token2022's offchain helper
  `create_transfer_checked_instruction_with_extra_metas(..)` is used.
- If decimals are not provided, SPL Transfer Hook interface's
  `add_extra_account_metas_for_execute(..)` is used.

In either case where no transfer hook accounts are provided, the new,
non-deprecated helpers are used.
rationale: The change refactors the transfer implementation to use newer offchain helper functions without altering observable behavior; it appears to be a code cleanup rather than fixing incorrect behavior or a security issue.

As another step for solving #6064, the onchain helpers now need to be
replaced. This PR makes that change in the SPL Transfer Hook interface.

Specifically, this commit adds a new `add_extra_accounts_for_execute_cpi(..)`

subject: token js: create new offchain helper

This is the final PR to round off the changes required to fix #6064.

Previously, the offchain helpers for adding extra metas to instructions have
been replaced with new ones in the SPL Transfer Hook interface and Token2022.

This PR follows suit and adds a new helper to SPL Token JS.

The new helper, `addExtraAccountMetasForExecute(..)`, mirrors the Rust helper in
SPL Transfer Hook interface, requiring the parameters for an
`ExecuteInstruction` to be passed into the function directly.

This change also adds a public function for creating an `ExecuteInstruction`, in
case developers wish to create such an instruction for directly sending
instructions to their transfer hook program.

- `createTransferCheckedWithTransferHookInstruction(..)`
- `createTransferCheckedWithFeeAndTransferHookInstruction(..)`

subject: token-2022: [I-03] Clarify `calculate_inverse_fee` math (#6874)
body:
#### Problem

According to the Certora audit report:

> Description: The function calculate_inverse_fee is not exactly an
inverse operation of calculate_fee. That is, it is not the case that
calculate_inverse_fee(x + calculate_fee(x)) == calculate_fee(x).
> Recommendation: Document that calculate_inverse_fee is not an exact
inverse and instead that only the relationship calculate_fee(x) <=
calculate_inverse_fee(x + calculate_fee(x)) holds in order to avoid
confusion with the potential users of calculate_inverse_fee.

#### Solution

Do the recommended thing. I don't think the math in the comment is
correct, so I've added a test to make sure the relationship is correct.
rationale: The commit only adds a proptest and documentation to clarify the relationship of calculate_inverse_fee; no functional code changes were made, so it does not fix a bug nor address a security issue.

subject: program-error: Add option to specify solana_program crate (#7112)
body:
* program-error: Add option to specify solana_program crate

Problem

There are going to be a lot of issues with people seeing errors on
spl_program_error derivation. When a build pulls in two version of
solana_program, the macro uses `::solana_program`, which now becomes
ambiguous.

Summary of changes

I'm not sure if this is a good idea, but this PR gives the ability
to specify which version of `solana_program` to use when deriving the
various traits on your error type.

Borsh has this same functionality, and it's saved us when pulling in
multiple versions of borsh in the SDK.

Note: this PR defaults to `solana_program` instead of
`::solana_program`, which might cause downstream issues.

* Address feedback

* Rename solana_program_crate -> solana_program

* Oops, change the name everywhere
rationale: The change fixes a compile‑time ambiguity when multiple versions of the `solana_program` crate are present by allowing the macro to specify which crate to use. This corrects incorrect behavior (failed builds) but does not introduce or mitigate a security vulnerability.

body:
* token-2022: Add Pausable extension

#### Problem

Users want a more Ethereum-style token experience by being able to
"pause" their token, similar to the "Pausable" interface. When a mint is
paused, tokens cannot be minted, burned, or transferred.

#### Summary of changes

Add the extension and some tests. It covers the following interactions:

* mint / mint-checked
* burn / burn-checked
* transfer / transfer-checked / transfer-with-fee
* confidential transfer / confidential transfer with fee
* confidential mint / confidential burn

Unfortunately, the confidential mint / burn extension doesn't have
testing, so I couldn't get a full end-to-end test for it.

Also note that it's still possible to:

The ROlesAuthority uses a BITNOT function to perform the NOT bit operation.

rationale: The change replaces high‑level calls with low‑level assembly for gas savings and adds a helper to interpret return data. No incorrect behavior is corrected; the commit is labeled as an optimization and does not alter security‑relevant logic.

subject: 🚧 More SafeERC20 optimizations
rationale: The commit replaces the previous getLastTransferResult logic with inline assembly that correctly checks the ERC20 return data (reverting on a false boolean return). The prior implementation could treat a false return as success, potentially causing silent token transfer failures, which is a security-relevant bug.

subject: ⚡️ Inline
rationale: The diff updates SafeERC20 assembly calls to correctly check the low‑level call status and handle return data (including non‑standard ERC20 contracts). Previously the library did not verify the call result properly, which could let a token contract silently fail and cause loss of funds. The added checks constitute a security‑relevant bug fix.

subject: ⚡️ Optimize safeApprove
rationale: The assembly rewrite preserves the acceptance semantics of the old code (revert on call failure, on a false bool, or on non-0/32-byte returndata; accept empty returndata or a true bool), and the .gas-snapshot changes show the same tests simply consuming less gas — this is a pure gas optimization with no corrected behaviour. The only differences (bubbled revert data instead of 'APPROVE_FAILED', any nonzero 32-byte word treated as true, explicit address masking that mirrors the ABI encoder's cleaning) do not fix a defect.

subject: ♻️ Abstractions
rationale: The change replaces manual assembly that used `mload(0x40)` without allocating memory for the calldata, which could cause out‑of‑bounds memory writes/reads and malformed calls to ERC20 tokens. Switching to `callOptionalReturn` with a properly constructed `bytes` calldata fixes this unsafe behavior, addressing a potential security issue.

subject: ♻️ Cleanup
rationale: The diff consists entirely of added comments/blank lines in SafeERC20.sol; no executable code changed, so behavior is identical before and after. This is a documentation cleanup, not a bug or security fix.

This is a refactor/optimization, so it is neither a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: Revert "⚡️ Optimize ReentrancyGuard"
body: This reverts commit 16953d752abdd1803b622fc58fb815934abe2fd2.
rationale: The commit reverts an assembly‑based ReentrancyGuard optimization back to a standard Solidity implementation, indicating the prior change broke the reentrancy protection. A broken guard can enable reentrancy attacks (fund loss) or lock functions (DoS), thus fixing a security‑relevant defect.

subject: ⚡️ Optimize ReentrancyGuard
rationale: This is a pure gas optimization: `require(status != ENTERED)` and `require(status == 1)` are semantically equivalent because the private status slot is initialized to 1 and only ever written to 2/1 inside the modifier, so no reachable behaviour differs. The gas snapshot confirms normal operation with only small gas deltas (~3-6), indicating no defect was corrected and no exploitable behaviour existed before.

subject: 💥 Don't check user == address(this) in Auth
rationale: The diff removes the `user == address(this) || ...` clause that auto-authorized any self-call through requiresAuth, so a contract previously could be induced to re-enter/call itself (e.g. via a call target resolving to itself) and pass authorization without being owner or authority-approved; the new code only grants access via authority canCall or ownership. Exploitation requires an application-level self-call path in a consuming contract, so this is a privilege-escalation hardening fix rather than a directly exploitable bug in solmate itself, hence Medium severity.

subject: ⚡️ Remove else branch
rationale: Replacing `else { return user == owner; }` with a fall-through `return user == owner;` after an if-block that returns on the true branch is semantically identical, so authorization behavior is unchanged; the only observable effect is the small gas reductions in .gas-snapshot. This is a gas-optimization refactor, not a defect correction.

subject: ♻️ Better var name
rationale: Every changed line is a consistent rename of the assembly local 'callData' to 'freeMemoryPointer'; mload(0x40), all mstore offsets, and the call arguments are byte-identical before and after, so behaviour is unchanged. This is a pure readability refactor with no defect corrected.

rationale: The change merely splits `authority != 0 && canCall(...)` into nested ifs with early return; since Solidity's && short-circuits identically, all three execution paths (authority unset, canCall true, canCall false) behave the same before and after. Only gas costs changed (as .gas-snapshot confirms), so no incorrect behavior was corrected.

subject: ♻️ Readability
rationale: The diff only replaces 32-byte selector literals (0x23b872dd/0xa9059cbb/0x095ea7b3 padded with 56 hex zeros) with bit-identical shl(224, selector) expressions, so call-data encoding behaviour is unchanged — a pure readability refactor per the commit message. The ±6 gas deltas in the gas snapshot merely reflect the slightly different bytecode, confirming no correctness or security change.

subject: 🔒 Safer SafeTransferLib
rationale: The commit fixes unsafe memory handling in SafeTransferLib by correctly advancing the free memory pointer after building call data, preventing overlapping writes that could corrupt call data and lead to incorrect token transfers or loss of funds.

subject: 🔒 Rollback optimizations for now
rationale: The commit replaces low‑level assembly calls that only checked call success with .call that also validates the optional boolean return value of ERC20 transfer/transferFrom, fixing a bug where tokens returning false would be treated as successful, which could be exploited to lose funds.

subject: ✅ Check owner if canCall reverts
rationale: Pre-fix, a revert from cachedAuthority.canCall (e.g., a malfunctioning, gas-grieved, or code-less authority) propagated out of isAuthorized, making every Auth-gated function revert and leaving even the owner's fallback check and setAuthority recovery path unreachable — a revert-inducible permanent DoS. The try/catch restores the owner fallback; no privilege escalation is introduced since the fallback grants only the owner, but exploitability depends on a misbehaving authority contract, so severity is Low.

subject: ✨ SafeCastLib
rationale: The commit is purely additive: it introduces a new SafeCastLib utility, its tests, and README/gas-snapshot entries, without modifying any existing code or changing prior behaviour. Since no pre-existing defect is corrected, this is a new feature rather than a bug fix or security fix.

subject: ⚡️ Unchecked
rationale: The diff merely wraps the existing computation in an `unchecked` block to skip Solidity 0.8 overflow checks; since `role` is a uint8 (max 255), `2**role` can never exceed uint256 and the bitwise AND cannot overflow, so behavior is unchanged and the only effect is gas savings (confirmed by the .gas-snapshot decrease). This is a gas optimization refactor with no behavior change, not a bug fix or security fix.

subject: ⚡️ Prioritize roles over root
rationale: The canCall rewrite is logically equivalent: the old code returned (public || isUserRoot) ? true : (roles-mask non-empty), and the new code returns public ? true : (roles-mask non-empty || isUserRoot) — both reduce to public || root || roles. It merely reorders pure mapping-read checks (roles before root) for gas, as confirmed by the .gas-snapshot deltas and the ⚡️ commit style, so no incorrect prior behaviour was corrected.

No branch, return value, or authorization decision changes — only gas costs drop (visible in .gas-snapshot), making this a pure gas-optimization refactor, not a bug fix.

Neither bumping nor leaving the free pointer dirty is attacker-inducible or fund-threatening, so this is an optimization, not a bug or security fix.

subject: ✨ fmulUp
rationale: The diff is purely additive: it introduces a new utility function fmulUp (multiplication with round-up) alongside existing fmulDown/fdiv, without modifying any pre-existing code path. Since no prior behavior was wrong or changed, this is a feature addition, not a bug fix, and thus cannot be a security fix.

subject: ♻️ Cleanup 4626
rationale: The diff moves a concrete ERC4626Vault into a new abstract ERC4626 mixin (file move/rename plus added hooks like beforeWithdraw/afterDeposit and balanceOfUnderlying), with the visible deposit/withdraw/redeem and share/underlying math behaving equivalently to a standard vault implementation — no corrected check, bound, or arithmetic is shown. Since most of the deleted file is truncated I cannot fully verify no behavior changed, so confidence is lowered, but nothing visible indicates a defect being corrected, let alone an attacker-exploitable one.

subject: ✨ WithdrawFrom and RedeemFrom
rationale: The diff purely adds new functions withdrawFrom/redeemFrom (a feature, matching the ✨ subject) and changes baseUnit from public to internal visibility; nothing incorrect in the pre-existing withdraw/redeem/allowance logic is corrected. Notably the added withdrawFrom deducts allowance before shareAmount is assigned (subtracting 0), which is a defect introduced here, not fixed — but it does not make this commit a bug fix.

subject: ♻️ Fix visibility
rationale: The diff only changes external → public on withdraw, redeem, and balanceOfUnderlying, which leaves the external ABI, state transitions, and allowance logic untouched; it merely lets inheriting contracts call these functions internally, correcting a visibility oversight (inconsistent with deposit/mint). Since no externally reachable behavior changes and no attacker can influence the pre/post difference, it is a usability bug fix, not a security fix.

subject: 🐛 Ordering bug
rationale: The change moves share calculation before the allowance reduction, fixing an ordering bug where allowance was never decreased, allowing unlimited use of allowance and potential fund loss.

subject: spec fixes
rationale: The diff corrects ERC4626 accounting functions (withdraw, mint, redeem) and share/underlying calculations that previously returned constant values or used wrong formulas, which could allow incorrect token balances and potential fund loss. The changes fix these logic errors, indicating a bug fix with security impact.

subject: ✅ Fix ERC1155 fail tests
rationale: The diff fixes erroneous test-helper validation in ERC1155.t.sol: the old condition only reverted when all three input arrays were empty, allowing mismatched-length fuzz inputs to be silently truncated to minLength, whereas the new check reverts whenever min3(...) == 0. This corrects wrong test behaviour but touches only test code, leaving the production ERC1155 contract unchanged, so it has no attacker-reachable or financial security impact.

subject: fix bug
rationale: The commit fixes incorrect accounting: it moves the calculation of `underlyingAmount` out of the `emit` statement and adds a proper `totalUnderlying()` implementation, preventing use of an uninitialized/incorrect value in `beforeWithdraw` and exchange rate calculations, which could have allowed attackers to withdraw incorrect amounts.

subject: ✅ Simplify fmul fuzz test
rationale: The diff touches only the fmul fuzz-test harness in FixedPointMathLib.t.sol, replacing the operand-halving loop with an early return that skips overflow cases; the fmul library code itself is unchanged, so no product behaviour is corrected. Both versions assert valid properties (the old loop tested scaled-down inputs, the new one skips overflowing inputs), making this a test-only simplification, not a bug or security fix.

subject: add mint fix
rationale: The pre-fix code evaluated calculateUnderlying(shareAmount) after _mint had already inflated totalSupply, so mint charged the minter the post-mint (diluted) exchange rate — less underlying than the shares were worth. An attacker could repeatedly mint/withdraw, or mint a huge flash-loaned shareAmount, to extract value from existing depositors and drain the vault; the fix moves the conversion before _mint, restoring the invariant that the exchange rate is unchanged by a mint.

subject: 🚧 WIP 4626 Updates
rationale: The changes rename parameters and events and switch to preview functions, but they also introduce incorrect allowance handling and misuse of previewMint in withdraw, indicating a refactor rather than a bug fix; no security impact is evident.

subject: 🚧 Better FPM and update 4626
rationale: The commit corrects ERC4626 function signatures and replaces FixedPointMathLib fmul/fdiv arithmetic with mulDiv/mulDivUp, fixing rounding/precision bugs that could be exploited to gain or lose assets.

subject: ♻️ Cleanup 4626
rationale: The change only adds named return variables to view functions without altering any logic or state; this is a refactor/cleanup, not a bug fix, and introduces no security-relevant behavior change.

subject: 🔒 Rounding safety checks
rationale: The diff replaces previewMint with previewWithdraw in withdraw(), fixing shares burned being computed by the wrong conversion (assets-from-shares instead of shares-from-assets), which mis-accounts every withdrawal whenever the exchange rate deviates from 1:1 — a deviation an attacker can induce via donation/first-depositor manipulation to make withdrawers over-burn shares or siphon assets. It also adds ZERO_SHARES requires on deposit/redeem, blocking the rounding-to-zero path where users transfer assets and receive nothing (or burn shares for nothing), a known ERC4626 inflation-attack theft vector.

subject: ♻️ Fix error message
rationale: The diff only renames the revert reason in redeem() from "ZERO_SHARES" to "ZERO_ASSETS"; the require condition, state updates, and burn/transfer logic are identical before and after, so no exploitable behavior changes — it merely corrects a misleading error string, which is cosmetic, not a security fix.

rationale: The diff is a uniform identifier rename (underlying → asset) across the immutable state variable, constructor parameter, and all four safeTransfer/SafeTransferFrom call sites; the same token is used and no logic, accounting, or access control changes. This is an EIP-4626 naming refactor with no behavioral correction, so it is neither a bug fix nor a security fix.

rationale: The diff replaces the use of a constant SCALAR for zero‑supply conversions with the actual input amounts, fixing incorrect share/asset calculations that could be exploited to mint or withdraw disproportionate amounts when the vault is empty.

subject: ⚡️ Optimize using Overlay trick
rationale: The old mulDivUp computed z + denominator - 1 and reverted when that intermediate addition overflowed, causing spurious reverts for large products even though ceil((x*y)/d) is always representable; the new ((z-1)/d)+1 form eliminates that false revert while preserving exact rounding, so it corrects prior behaviour (and saves gas).
