body:
This PR introduces a new Move type called Versioned. It represents a
wrapper of a versioned inner type. This provides flexibility in what
type to load from the inner (dynamic field) object.
We then define ValidatorWrapper which is a thin wrapper of Versioned to
provide all interfaces that hide the inner type of Validator.

impossible to migrate all `inactive_validators` to use new types when we
upgrade the Validator type, and hence we must support this form of
polymorphism.
In a follow up PR I will also use this type for validator_candidates.

subject: [hardening] dynamic check for child object authentication
body: If there is a bug `ChildObjectResolver::read_child_object` that allows an attacker to look up a child object that does not belong to the parent (e.g., I believe the bug fixed by https://github.com/MystenLabs/sui/pull/7937 falls into this category), we will detect it and fail at runtime with an `InvariantViolation`.
rationale: The change adds a runtime check that validates the owner of a child object matches the expected parent ID, returning a storage error otherwise. Previously the resolver could return a child object belonging to a different owner, allowing an attacker to read unauthorized objects, which is an access control flaw.

subject: [upgrades] adapter sets link context and table (#9932)
body:
## Description

### Create MovePackage before verification

Preparation for package upgrades, where to verify `CompiledModules`,
we need linkage and type origin tables, which are created as part of a
`MovePackage`, but currently, the `MovePackage` is created after
verification.

This change allows us to deserialize bytes to create
`CompiledModule`s, then build a `MovePackage` from those by reference,
and use that to publish and verify the deserialized modules.

### Removes version parameter from MovePackage::new_initial

Get rid of `publish_and_verify_new_modules`,
`publish_and_verify_upgraded_modules` and `generate_package_id` in
favour of inlining them into their respective call-sites.  This is to
prepare for generating a `MovePackage` before calling
`publish_and_verify_modules` which requires having access to the list
of `CompiledModule`s after deserialization and address substitution.

In preparation for verification requiring a context that needs to be
derived from a `MovePackage`.

### LinkageView

Remove implementation of LinkageResolver for `StorageView`, and
introduce `LinkageView` as a wrapping type that holds linkage
information and delegates all other resolution queries to
`StorageView`.

Relies on move-language/move#1009 which adds support to `Session` for
resolvers that are richer than just a reference.

### Set linkage table for ExecutionContext

Add an API to set the linkage table based on a `MovePackage`, and
read from it when responding to `relocate` and `link_context` queries.

Setting the appropriate linkage context for calls into the VM and type
loading.  After setting the package's link context for a move call, we
also update its package ID to its runtime ID.

Sui Move bump, bringing in the following changes:

- Expose more of the loader to the adapter layer.
- More flexible compatibility checks
- ...and other fixes

### Backwards Compatibility

- Make sure the order of errors produced by publish remain consistent
when upgrades are not enabled as a feature, and don't perform any relinking.

### Hardening

Make it an error to try and overwrite an existing link context.  This
also uncovered a bug where we set the link context as part of taking
user events at the end of a move call, which could cause issues in the
case of:

- a publish
- ...with multiple modules
- ...multiple of which have initializers
- ...which emit events
- ...which come from a different package

## Test Plan

Existing tests and newly enabled upgrade tests:

```
$ cargo simtest
$ env SUI_SKIP_SIMTESTS=1 cargo nextest run
```

Fixes to the interleaved package upgrade test, resolving two issues:

1. The helper function for building the package, computing the digest,
   and the like was returning the wrong IDs (it was returning original
   package IDs and not the new dependency IDs).
2. We were trying to use the new object ID for the dependency as both
   the `published-at` and address value for the package.

New enabled tests:

- Calling into an upgraded package.
- Referencing types introduced during upgrades.

subject: [debug] Disable printing on nodes (#10561)
body:
## Description

Despite trying to disable printing using feature flags in #8795, it came
back because of the additive nature of `feature`s. This time, disable
debug printing on validators and full nodes for good, by controlling
their inclusion using a flag passed in during native function creation,
that controls whether to link against a silent version of the debug
print functions or not.

Unit tests, and other CLI usages of the VM typically link against the
unsilenced native functions, and the version used by validators is
silenced.

## Test Plan

Run all existing tests:

```
$ cargo simtest
$ env SUI_SKIP_SIMTESTS=1 cargo nextest run
```

Create a test move package with the following content:

```
module test::test {
    struct ImALittleTeapot has copy, drop, store {}
    public entry fun print() {
        std::debug::print(&ImALittleTeapot {});
    }

    #[test]
    fun test_printing() {
        print();
    }
}
```

And confirm that the following does print debug output

```
sui$ cargo build --bin sui --release
sui$ cargo build --bin sui-node --release
sui$ ./target/release/sui move test -p $PKG
```

While publishing to a local network and repeatedly calling `print` does
not pollute the validator or fullnode logs.
rationale: The change disables the Move debug::print native on validators/full nodes, preventing potentially sensitive internal state from being logged. This mitigates information leakage via log files, a security concern (CWE-532). The commit alters behavior that was previously unintended, thus fixing a bug.

## Description

If the validator binary includes a system package that doesn't exist
on-chain, then during the protocol/framework upgrade that introduces it,
we shoud run its module initializer. This aligns with the behaviour

subject: Replay tool (#11009)
body:
## Description 

Tool to replay TX execution locally. Verified on testnet. Will augment
for Devnet etc as needed.

Note: only protocol version 4 and up will be officially supported as old
full nodes dont have a critical RPC endpoint required.
This tool requires that full nodes expose a new rpc endpoint, which is
still being rolled out.
For now internal use, a modified full node which supports older protocol
versions can will be provided to you on demand.

# **Commands:**

## **1. Replay Transaction**
Replays a transaction given the transaction digest
`sui-tool replay --rpc {url} tx -t  {tx-digest}`

```
$> sui-tool replay --rpc $RPC_URL  tx -t  DPfpQbMXZauxJu9iWoJ8ofRxhNMF6HcvSvfzfHFZhzdK

2023-04-17T21:40:41.694279Z  INFO sui_tool::replay: Executing tx: DPfpQbMXZauxJu9iWoJ8ofRxhNMF6HcvSvfzfHFZhzdK
2023-04-17T21:40:44.227333Z  INFO sui_tool::replay: Execution finished
```
The execution reports are terse, but its expected that folks will ad-hoc
print whatever info they need.
I'll also add more reporting capabilities for verbose & tracing needs.

Although this should never happen under normal behavior, it is possible
for the replay tool to fail by forking, meaning the effects computed
locally differ from those on chain, an error is generated with the diff
of the effects:

```
On-chain vs local diff
  
   SuiTransactionBlockEffectsV1 {
       status: Success,
       executed_epoch: 761,
       gas_used: GasCostSummary {
---        computation_cost: 1000000,
+++        computation_cost: 100000000,
           storage_cost: 691250400,
```
If an _unintended_ fork happens, please contact @oxade to check if
there's a bug in the tool.
Thanks @tzakian for recommending the diff tool.

## **2. Replay Range Of Checkpoints**
Replays all the transactions in a range of checkpoints

`sui-tool replay --rpc {url} checkpoints -s {start} -e {end}`


subject: [upgrade-compatibility] Disallow adding `key` ability to types during package upgrades (#11167)
body:
Adds a new protocol version (7) and adds a check to make sure that a
`key` ability cannot be added to a type during an upgrade.

This also updates the ability checker so that we can pass it an
`AbilitySet` of abilities that we don't want to allow to be added to
pre-existing types.
rationale: The commit adds a compatibility check that rejects package upgrades which add the `key` ability to existing types, fixing a bug where such upgrades were previously allowed. Allowing `key` ability could grant additional privileges (e.g., use as table keys) and break invariants, representing a potential security issue.

subject: [sui-framework/package] `Publisher` checks recognise upgrades (#12026)
body:
## Description

Change the behaviour of functions like:

```
sui::package::from_package<T>(self: &Publisher): bool
sui::package::from_module<T>(self: &Publisher): bool
```

to return `true` when `T` is from an upgraded version of the package
associated with `Publisher`. Previously it was impossible to check the
package ownership of a type introduced in an upgraded package (the
upgraded type's type name didn't match the original package's
`Publisher` and it was impossible to create a `Publisher` for the
upgraded package, because it requires an OTW which we can't create for
upgraded packages).

This support was added by introducing a new stdlib function:
`std::typename::get_original`, as of protocol version 11, which produces
a runtime representation of the type that uses original (aka runtime)
package IDs instead of defining package IDs (the default behaviour for
`std::typename::get` and any other case where a runtime representation
of the type is converted into an on-chain or storage representation of a
type).

## Test Plan

New transactional test cases for `std::type_name::get_original` and
`sui::package::from_package`:

```
$ cargo nextest run -- upgrade/type_names.move
$ cargo nextest run -- upgrade/publisher.move
```

- [x] breaking change for validators or node operators (must upgrade
binaries)

### Release notes

As of protocol version 11:

- `sui::package::from_package<T>(self: &Publisher)` and
`sui::package::from_module<T>(self: &Publisher)` return `true` when `T`
is a type introduced at any upgraded version of the package associated
with `self: &Publisher` (rather than just the types originally present
when that package was published).
- `std::type_name::get_original` is introduced as a new stdlib function
to return a representation of the type where package IDs have all been
normalized to "original" IDs (the ID of the first version of a package)
in contrast to the default behaviour of `std::type_name::get` which
distinguishes types introduced at different versions of a package by
assigning them the ID of the package that introduced them.

subject: Swarm config refactoring (#12117)
body:
This PR does a series of refactoring on how we construct node config and
swarm configs to make it cleaner:
1. Renames utils.rs in sui-config/ to local_ip_utils.rs, and moved all
the IP and port management port into it. Now it contains a manager to
generate new IPs and new ports for simtest; for non-simtest it always
use localhost and new available port.
2. Previously we start fullnode inside TestCluster, which runs on the
client node in simtest. This created a lot of tech debt. This PR moves
all fullnode creation into Swarm. Now we can start arbitrary number of
fullnodes in a Swarm. When starting TestCluster, it uses Swarm to launch
a fullnode, and keep a copy of the fullnode handle locally for rpc
access.
3. Also added the ability to start more fullnodes after a test cluster
started running, inside swarm. This means we could also run those
fullnodes in a container, managed by the swarm.
4. Heavy use of the builder pattern: added ValidatorGenesisConfigBuilder
to build a ValidatorGenesisConfig; added ValidatorConfigBuilder and
FullnodeConfigBuilder to build their node configs.
5. Removed a number of unused fields in ConfigBuilder and SwarmBuilder.

This this PR, we should be able to start removing all the code that
spawns individual nodes instead of inside a container.

subject: [deepbook] Introducing the implementation of self-matching prevention. #12464 ## Description
body:
The self-matching prevention mechanism ensures that the matching engine
takes measures to avoid unnecessary trades
when matching a user's buy/sell order with their own sell/buy order.

There are four Self-Trade Prevention Options.
1. Decrement & cancel: Cancel smaller order and decrement larger order by the smaller size.
                       If the same size, cancel both.
2. Cancel oldest: Cancel older (resting) order in full.
                  Continue to execute the newer taking order.
3. Cancel newest: Cancel newer (taking) order in full.
                  Let the old resting order remain on the order book.
4. Cancel both: Cancel both orders immediately.

For now, we have only implemented the behavior of canceling the oldest order.
However, we have reserved the self_matching_prevention option as a parameter
in case we need to implement other behaviors in the future.
This approach allows us to maintain backward compatibility
and provides us with the capability to extend functionality.

subject: [protocol-upgrades] Add ability to add abilities
body:
Relax the restriction on adding new abilities to types introduced
during system package upgrades -- only the `key` ability remains
restricted.

This change is not guarded by a protocol config, because it is in the
codepath that decides whether an system package upgrade is compatible
in the first place -- i.e. if a quorum of validators do not have this
change, the proposal to upgrade to a package where an existing type
has additional abilities will not succeed.  This codepath is also not
run on fullnodes (who assume that if a system package upgrade proposal
was executed successfully, validators confirmed that the upgrade was
compatible), so again, there is not a need for a feature gate in the
protocol config to coordinate the launch of this change -- it is
self-coordinating.

Test Plan:

Updated existing E2E tests and added a new one for the new restriction
on `key`:

```
sui-e2e-tests$ cargo simtest
```
rationale: The commit relaxes a restriction on adding abilities during system package upgrades, which is a protocol behavior change rather than a correction of erroneous behavior. It does not address a vulnerability or fix a security issue; it merely expands allowed upgrades.

subject: Complete tracking and expiry of valid JWKs via the AuthenticatorState object (#13576)
body:
I apologize for the large PR (although a lot of the + lines are docs and
tests) - this turned out to be much more complicated than I could ever
have guessed.

The main challenge here was managing the creation of the new system
object at `0x7` that is used to track the authenticator state. It can't
be created until one epoch after the protocol upgrade that brings in the
new framework, and we have to be careful not to create it twice. I tried
many different approaches before arriving at this one.

The system works as follows:
- `ChangeEpoch` is replaced with `EndOfEpochTransaction`, which contains
a list of transactions to perform at the end of the epoch. For now the
possible end-of-epoch actions are ChangeEpoch, AuthenticatorStateCreate,
and AuthenticatorStateExpire.
- If the protocol feature flag is off, do nothing.
- If the feature flag is on, check if the authenticator state object
already exists (and cache its existence for the duration of the epoch).
- If it does not exist, then at the end of the epoch, add an
`AuthenticatorStateCreate` tx just before the `ChangeEpoch` (inside
EndOfEpochTransaction).
- This was necessary because doing the creation from within
`ChangeEpoch` posed the following difficulties:
- ~~The start version of the authenticator state object would be
variable instead of being fixed at 1.~~ Using EndOfEpochTransactions
re-introduces this issue, which required adding the correct
intial_shared_version to the transaction data.
- I could not find an easy way to ensure that the creation could only
happen once in this scenario.
- This had the added benefit of giving a simple way to probe for
existence of the `create` function. If the `AuthenticatorStateCreate` tx
fails due to `FunctionNotFound` when attempting to augment the
checkpoint, we simply omit the tx.
- If it does exist, then we add an `AuthenticatorStateExpire` tx just
before the `ChangeEpoch` tx.
- I had similarly hoped to do the expiry from within the `ChangeEpoch`
tx, but that would have required the set of shared_input_objects to the
`ChangeEpoch` tx to change at a certain point. And because that point is
delayed until the epoch after the protocol version bump (due to
framework upgrade) it would have been extremely ugly to do this.
- There would be no easy way to pass in a `min_epoch` argument to
ChangeEpoch tx without add a ChangeEpochV2 transaction type with an
additional argument. (as well as a new entry point to the
`advance_epoch` function).
- CheckpointExecutor has been modified to treat both of these "end of
epoch" txns the way we previously treat `ChangeEpoch` - i.e. only
execute it via CheckpointExecutor after all other transactions have been
executed.
- I tried to avoid this by having `handle_consensus_output` insert the
`AuthenticatorStateExpire` tx, but this proved to be very awkward. It's
not possible to tell whether the tx should be added until the
`EndOfEpoch` messages have been processed, and by that point it is too
late to add new system transactions.

The state machine for voting on JWKs, approving them, and created
`AuthenticatorStateUpdate` transactions remains basically the same as in
the previous version of this PR.

TODO: I am still working on a few tests, in particular one that provides
multiple different JWKs from multiple providers to the TestCluster.

---------

Co-authored-by: Mark Logan <mark@marklgn.com>
rationale: The change adds proper creation, tracking, and expiry of the AuthenticatorState object (JWKs) and guards against duplicate creation and stale keys. Previously the system could retain or create invalid JWKs, potentially allowing unauthorized authentication. The added checks, expiry logic, and metrics constitute a fix to an access control/authentication flaw.

## Description 

Add interfaces for fetching randomness: `RandomGenerator` is a PRG with
a seed that is derived from the global randomness (which is the same
between randomness rounds) and a fresh UID (which is guaranteed to be
unique by the framework). In other words, the seed is unpredictable
without knowing the global randomness, and different for each created
generator (thus not predictable even by different functions invoked for
the same tx).

`RandomGenerator` manages an internal state with a buffer of random
bytes derived using the PRG, and provides high level functions for
deriving integers from those random bytes.

subject: Add quantity_min_tick to DeepBook. Quantity must be divisible by this amount, rather than lot_size. (#17335)
body:
## Description 

We have some pools with a large lot_size. All trade quantities must be a
multiple of lot_size, so they must be truncated to meet this
requirement. Assets being bridged from another chain utilize all decimal
points, and truncating these decimals results in users losing non
negligible amount of assets. For example: USDC has 6 decimal points, and
a user may bridge 10.129218 USDC. If we attempt to swap that amount into
SUI, the user's USDC is truncated to 10.00000.

QUANTITY_MIN_TICK is a constant that's set to 1000, this will make it so
only the last 3 decimal points are truncated. In the above example, the
user will be able to swap 10.129000 USDC, and their loss amount is
negligible.

Essentially, lot_size now becomes min_size, and quantity_min_tick is now
lot_size. We can't rename lot_size because that would change the API.
This is not as bad as it sounds.

Unit tests were affected heavily because input / output amounts were now
validated by 1000. Unit tests were originally written with a lot_size of
1, which in my opinion is not reflective of a real world scenario. I had
to 10x a lot of the values.

## Test plan 

Unit tests. Code changes are not invasive.

subject: move: support automated address management (#17995)
body:
## Description 

This PR adds automated address management support for `sui client
publish` and `sui client upgrade`. The `chain_id` is resolved early in
sui commands and propagated down where published ID resolution is
needed.

High-level:

- If a package contains a `Move.lock` that contains info to support a
package upgrade, then that is used, and a user does not have to (nor
should they) maintain a `published-at` address in their `Move.toml`.

- If a package does _not_ have any `Move.lock` information to support a
package upgrade, we will still fallback to `Move.toml` as we do today.
Nothing changes.

- If a package has both a `Move.lock` and `Move.toml`, then the
`Move.lock` will be used (the user is free to delete `published-at` in
their `Move.toml`). Caveat: If a published address is in both of these
files, they must be the same (we will raise a `Conflict` error message
otherwise).
 
- Note: docs to follow and merge at the same time as this PR,
particularly [this section on
upgrades](https://docs.sui.io/concepts/sui-move-concepts/packages/upgrade#example)

- Note after this PR it is still required to set `[addresses]` to `0x0`
in `Move.toml`. This requirement will be removed subsequently (which
also requires setting to `0x0` still). I didn't want to meddle with that
logic all at once.

## Test plan 

How did you test the new or updated feature?

We cover three cases:

- Upgrade with `Move.toml` only (existing package upgrade test)
- Upgrade with `Move.lock` only (extension of existing package
management test)
- Upgrade with `Move.lock` and `Move.toml` with conflicting addresses
error condition (new test)

- Existing e2e tests pass (and SDK tests now resolve chain ID for
publish commands)

---

subject: sui-framework: use test instead of build script
body:
One area that contributes very negatively to our compilation times is
sui-framework crate's build script that builds the system packages. The
build script results in duplicate compilations of a number of crates,
both first and third-party, as well as the actual build time for system
packages. This patch removes the build script in favor of doing the
compilation step in a test function.

Instead of always building the system packages they'll be checked-in to
the repo resulting in no additional build step. Instead a test function
will do the compilation and do a comparison against the checked-in
compiled packages (and docs) vs the newly generated ones, failing if
they differ. The checked-in packages and docs can trivially be updated
by running the test with the `UPDATE` envvar set, e.g.
`UPDATE=1 cargo test -p sui-framework --test build-system-packages`

Here are some simple timing measurements for running `cargo check` at
the root of the repo on my laptop with and with-out this patch:

  with-patch:
    clean build: 3m 15s
    changing sui-types: 17.33s
  without-patch:
    clean build:  4m 00s
    changing sui-types:  1m 42s
rationale: The change removes a build script and replaces it with a test that validates compiled packages, aiming to reduce compilation time. It does not alter runtime logic or fix incorrect behavior, so it is a refactor/performance improvement rather than a bug or security fix.

subject: [CLI] store framework versions in sui binary (dvx-195) (#21018)
body:
## Description 

This PR adds a module `sui::framework_version` containing functions to
obtain metadata about historical framework versions (git commit hashes,
system package names and paths). This information will be needed to
support implicit framework dependencies.

This information is gathered at build time from the manifest in the
`sui-framework-snapshot` crate. This required adding additional data to
that manifest, since the package names and source paths were not
previously stored. The code in `sui-framework-snapshot` that maintains
that manifest was updated.

## Test plan 

There are unit tests for `sui::framework_versions` that check the
correctness of the metadata that is returned. There are also updated
integration tests in `sui_framework_snapshot` that check that the
updated manifest matches the `Move.toml` files in
`sui-framework/packages`.

subject: Check conservation of settlement transactions correctly. (#22967)
body:
First, we need to make SUI contained in accumulator objects visible
so that it can be accounted for in the conservation check that happens
at reconfiguration, when all objects are scanned.

Once we do that, it then appears that settlement transactions are
minting SUI. Settlement transactions gather SUI deposited or
withdrawn from the effects of other transactions, and write it to
accumulator objects. But execution cannot see where this SUI came
from, so it appears that the transaction is minting SUI, and the
conservation checks fail.

To address this, we pass the total input and output SUI to the
settlement prologue entry point.  These numbers are then recorded
in the object runtime and eventually propagated to the TemporaryStore
so that they can be accounted for in conservation checks.
rationale: The commit fixes a bug where settlement transactions were incorrectly seen as minting SUI because accumulator SUI was not accounted for, causing conservation checks to fail. This could be exploited to cause denial‑of‑service by making legitimate settlement transactions reject, impacting availability. The fix adds proper accounting of total input/output SUI to the prologue, restoring the invariant.

## Description 

Enable the Poseidon hash function on mainnet.

There is a small change made to the function as well: It now only
accepts between 1 and 16 inputs. Previously, larger inputs were hashed
using an 16-ary Merkle tree which is compatible with zkLogin but not
other Poseiodon implementations which typically uses a 2- or 4-ary
Merkle tree.

This new version follows what seems to be the consensus on how to
implement Poseidon over BN254, and the limit of 16 inputs in the new
version is compatible with
https://github.com/iden3/go-iden3-crypto/tree/master/poseidon,
https://github.com/iden3/circomlib/blob/master/circuits/poseidon_constants.circom
and https://github.com/arnaucube/poseidon-rs. We leave it to the user to
decide how to handle larger inputs but provide an example (in form of a
unit test) of how to it for an 16-ary Merkle tree as used in zkLogin.

See also the SIP,
https://forums.sui.io/t/sip-12-poseidon-in-sui-move/45136.

subject: Add pending balance change APIs for reading accumulator state in-transaction
body:
Add new Move functions to read pending balance changes within a transaction:
- `sui::balance::pending_funds_deposits<T>(address): u64` - returns total
  pending deposits for the address from `send_funds` calls in current tx
- `sui::balance::pending_funds_withdrawals<T>(address): u64` - returns total
  pending withdrawals for the address in current tx
- `sui::balance::pending_funds_net_positive<T>(root, address): Option<u64>` -
  computes `settled + deposits - withdrawals`, returning Some(value) if
  non-negative or None if underflow

Implementation:
- Add native functions that read from ObjectRuntimeState's
  accumulator_merge_totals (deposits) and accumulator_split_totals (withdrawals)
- Add dedicated gas cost params (accumulator_emit_cost_base and
  accumulator_pending_balance_cost_base) instead of borrowing from event costs
- Add comprehensive tests for all new functions including edge cases

subject: [move-stlib] Checked and lossless helpers for << and >> (#25003)
body:
## Description 

- Adds helpers for shift left and shift right
- The << and >> abort if the rhs is too big for the bitsize, e.g. 63 is
fine for u64, but 64 aborts.
- As such, `checked_shl` and `checked_shr` return `option::none` iff the
rhs is too large.
- There are no `checked_*` variants for `u256` since the rhs is always
valid
- `lossless_shl` and `lossless_shr` return `option::some` iff the
operation is reversible (and in that sense lossless). That is, if `(x <<
y) >> y == x` (and similarly for `>>`.
  - Note this means they also return `none` if the rhs is too large 

- We will use the `lossless_` prefix for integer division that does not
round (when the remainder is 0)

subject: move-stdlib: add enumerate_map, chunks_map and append_ref to vector
body:
Adds a few convenience helpers to `std::vector`:

- `enumerate_map` / `enumerate_map_ref`: like `map` / `map_ref` but the
  closure also receives each element's index.
- `chunks_map`: splits a vector into sub-vectors of length `n`, applies a
  closure to each chunk, and collects the results (last chunk may be shorter;
  aborts if `n` is zero).
- `append_ref`: appends copies of a borrowed vector's elements onto `lhs`,
  leaving the source intact (requires `copy`).

Regenerates the framework docs and compiled-package snapshots. The macros are
inlined and do not affect the published API; `append_ref` is the only new
public function.

subject: Check object-funds withdraw sufficiency inside the Move VM
body:
Adds a check_sufficient_object_funds native, called from withdraw_from_object, that consults the
temporary store's in-execution funds check. On insufficient funds it aborts (a committed failure);
when the accumulator root has not caught up it aborts after the store has recorded a retry, so the
authority discards the effects and re-enqueues. Gated by the check_object_funds_withdraw_in_execution
feature flag (protocol version 128, devnet and testnet); when off, the prior post-execution checker
path runs unchanged. When on, successful withdrawals are recorded as unsettled for later
transactions in the same consensus commit.

Note: the in-execution unsettled-withdrawal read is not yet replay-deterministic (see FIXME in
temporary_store.rs); the flag stays off on mainnet pending that fix.
rationale: The commit adds an in-VM check for sufficient object funds, fixing a bug where insufficient‑funds withdrawals were only detected after execution, potentially allowing over‑withdrawals. This validation prevents unauthorized fund loss, a security issue, and the change alters runtime behavior, confirming it is a bug fix and a security fix.

subject: Check object funds withdraw sufficiency inside the Move VM
body:
A check_sufficient_object_funds native, called from withdraw_from_object, consults the temporary
store: availability of the accumulator root at the transaction's required version, then the
owner's settled balance net of unsettled in-commit and earlier in-transaction withdrawals.
Insufficient funds abort with a Move-level error (a committed, deterministic failure).

When the accumulator root has not caught up locally, the temporary store records the retry
request and returns the unwind error in one atomic act, minting the dedicated
SYSTEM_OBJECT_NOT_AVAILABLE_LOCALLY status code (new, execution range). The error rides the
outer PartialVMResult channel through resolver, object runtime and native untouched — it is
deliberately not a NativeResult abort, which would be a deterministic Move-level outcome.
convert_vm_error maps the code explicitly, and enforce_retry_invariant checks at the end of
execution that the unwind error and the retry request only ever appear together, in either
direction (debug_fatal on mismatch: panics in tests, alerts in release; authority behavior
stays keyed off the retry request alone).

Gated by check_object_funds_withdraw_in_execution (protocol v130, devnet and testnet); when
off, the prior post-execution checker path runs unchanged. Dry-run / simulate support is added
in the next PR.
rationale: The commit adds a proper insufficient‑funds check inside the Move VM and changes error handling to prevent withdrawals when the accumulator root is not up‑to‑date, fixing a bug that could allow overdrawing object funds, a clear security issue affecting user funds.

subject: Simplify GCP attestation API to Nitro-like verify_gcp_attestation(token, clock)
body:
Follow-up PR 1 on top of c327ff72ef ("fix: harden GCP attestation
integration"). Removes the separate `kid` Move argument: the trusted
key id is now extracted from the JWT header itself, matching the Nitro
attestation entry point shape.

sui-types/gcp_attestation.rs:
- Introduce `ParsedGcpJwt`, a single-parse representation of the JWT
  structure/header that retains the exact signed bytes and the
  base64 payload/signature segments. `ParsedGcpJwt::parse` extracts a
  required, non-empty `kid` (max 4096 UTF-8 bytes) and validates `alg`
  up front, so the native path never re-parses the header.
  `ParsedGcpJwt::verify` takes the looked-up JWK modulus/exponent and
  performs signature + claim verification. `verify_gcp_attestation`
  remains as a convenience wrapper composing parse + verify.
- Centralize `GCP_ISSUER`, `RS256_ALG`, `MAX_KID_SIZE`,
  `MIN_RSA_MODULUS_SIZE`/`MAX_RSA_MODULUS_SIZE`, and
  `validate_rsa_public_key` as public constants/helpers, reused by
  sui-node ingestion and the native verifier instead of being
  duplicated.

sui-move-natives/lib.rs + crypto/gcp_attestation.rs:
- `JwkMap` is now GCP-only and keyed by `kid`: `from_active_jwks`
  filters to `GCP_ISSUER` and fails closed on conflicting duplicate
  `kid` values (ambiguous entries are dropped rather than picking one
  key). `AuthenticatorState` is not reintroduced as a Move argument.
- Native `verify_gcp_attestation_internal` arity drops to
  (token, current_timestamp_ms). It parses once via `ParsedGcpJwt`,
  looks up the kid in `JwkMap`, and maps errors: missing/empty/
  oversized `kid` or malformed token -> PARSE; unknown `kid` ->
  KID_NOT_FOUND; signature/claim failure (including tampering with a
  registered key's header) -> VERIFY. Token bytes remain charged.

sui-framework/sources/crypto/gcp_attestation.move:
- `entry fun verify_gcp_attestation(token, clock)` — no `kid` param.

sui-node/src/lib.rs:
- JWKS ingestion reuses the centralized `GCP_ISSUER`, `RS256_ALG`, and
  `validate_rsa_public_key` instead of locally duplicated constants.

Tests updated/added (all passing, see verification below):
- sui-types unit tests: new fixtures with `kid` in the header, plus
  coverage for missing/empty/oversized `kid`, alg validation, header
  tampering against a registered key (VERIFY), and RSA bound checks.
- sui-move-natives: new `JwkMap` unit tests (issuer filter, kid lookup,
  conflicting-duplicate fail-closed behavior).
- Move framework test: kid read from token header;
  `test_gcp_attestation_missing_kid_is_parse_error` added.
- shared_object_version_manager synthetic tx now passes 2 args.
- sui-e2e-tests PTB builder updated to 2 args.
- Framework docs/compiled package regenerated via
  `UPDATE=1 cargo test -p sui-framework --test build-system-packages`
  (frozen sui-framework-snapshot files untouched; published_api.txt
  unchanged since it only lists names, not signatures).

Verification (all green):
- cargo test -p sui-types --lib gcp_attestation (25 passed)
- cargo test -p sui-move-natives-latest --lib jwk_map_tests (6 passed)
- cargo test -p sui-node --lib gcp_jwks (4 passed)
- cargo test -p sui-core --lib shared_object_version_manager
  --test-threads=1 (10 passed)
- cargo test -p sui-e2e-tests --test gcp_attestation_tests (2 passed;
  msim-gated happy path requires a simulator build and was not run)
- FILTER=gcp_attestation cargo test -p sui-framework-tests (2 passed)
  and full framework Move suite (86 passed)
- cargo test -p sui-framework --test build-system-packages (regen + rerun)
- cargo fmt --check (clean) and cargo clippy -D warnings for sui-types,
  sui-move-natives-latest, sui-node, sui-core, sui-e2e-tests (clean)
rationale: The commit removes the external `kid` argument and enforces extraction and validation of the `kid` from the JWT header, adds size checks and duplicate‑key handling, reducing the attack surface where a caller could supply a mismatched or malicious key identifier. This corrects prior behavior and addresses improper input validation, a security concern.

subject: [forwarding-address] Add ForwardingAddressRegistry system object (step 1) (#26891)
body:
## Description

First step of the **forwarding-address** feature (Sui-native deposit
aliases that forward funds to a registered master at resolution time —
the design analog of Tempo TIP-1022, deliberately named "forwarding
address" rather than "virtual address" since these are pure forwarding
aliases that can't sign or own state).

This PR adds **only** the minimal foundation: an empty registry object
and the machinery to create it. No registration or resolution APIs yet.

- **Move:** new `0x2::forwarding_address` module with
`ForwardingAddressRegistry { id: UID }` and a system-only `create()`.
Static object ID `0xfa` added in `object.move` and `sui-types`.
- **Protocol flag** `create_forwarding_address_registry`, enabled in
**v132** for non-mainnet/testnet chains only. v130 is cut in
`sui-v1.76.0` (with its framework bytecode snapshot frozen), and v131
was claimed by other features on `main`, so the flag lives in v132's
existing devnet-only block.
- **Epoch-change / genesis creation:** new
`EndOfEpochTransactionKind::ForwardingAddressRegistryCreate`, wired
through the authority's end-of-epoch tx assembly, the epoch-start
configuration (registered in `SYSTEM_SHARED_OBJECT_IDS`, so no new
configuration version is needed), the existence check, and the genesis
builder. The real executor impl lives only in `latest`
(execution_version 4); v0–v3 are frozen pre-exec-4 versions that reject
the variant.
- **Allowlisting the hardcoded UID for sharing:** the move-compiler
ID-leak "fresh UID" list + symbol pool, and the runtime
`object_runtime::is_framework_obj` set, so `share_object` accepts `0xfa`
at genesis / epoch change.
- Regenerated framework artifacts, protocol-config / BCS-format /
GraphQL / OpenRPC snapshots.

The `sui-types` conversions to the externally-pinned `sui-sdk-types` /
`sui-rpc` types are real arms: MystenLabs/sui-rust-sdk#288 added the
`ForwardingAddressRegistryCreate` variant upstream, and this PR bumps
the pinned `rev` in `Cargo.toml` to it.

(Also includes a small, separate commit tidying `.typos.toml`: relax the
Base58 ignore threshold 44→43 and exclude compiled Move bytecode.)

## Test plan

- Registry creation at genesis is exercised by every test network
started with default (devnet) protocol config, and is pinned in the
populated-genesis snapshot.
- The framework build test verifies the new `forwarding_address` module
compiles and that the ID-leak allowlist accepts sharing the hardcoded
`0xfa` UID.
- Tests that pin execution version 3 (`move_package_upgrade_tests`,
`address_balance_tests`, `coin_registry_tests`) disable the flag,
covering the constraint that the registry object cannot be created
pre-exec-v4.
- Protocol-config, BCS format, GraphQL schema, and OpenRPC snapshots pin
the new flag, transaction kind, and API surface.
- New `test_create_forwarding_address_registry_object_at_upgrade` e2e
simtest covers the epoch-change creation path (the one existing chains
like devnet will actually take, since only fresh networks get the
registry at genesis): it starts a cluster at protocol 130 with the
frozen v130 framework snapshot (which predates the `forwarding_address`
module), upgrades to 132, and verifies every node creates the shared
registry object at the end of the epoch.

## Description 

This adds a new function `original_package_id` on an `UpgradeCap` that
returns the original package ID for the package that the upgrade cap
controls.

In order to do this, we need to be able to load a package from the
object runtime as the upgrade cap doesn't hold this data. However, to be
extra careful to make sure that there is no possibility of running into
issues with unsequenced reads the API for reading a package from the
object runtime is very narrow -- you can only read a package by
providing a specific `(version, version_id)` pair. This will return

subject: Check object funds withdraw sufficiency during execution (#27524)
body:
## Description

Second half of the stacked object-funds change, on top of #27523:
object-funds withdrawal sufficiency is checked inside the Move VM at
withdrawal time instead of by the post-execution `ObjectFundsChecker`
wait/re-execute path. Protocol v137 enables
`check_object_funds_withdraw_in_execution` on devnet only.

The native reads the settled object balance through the temporary store
at the transaction accumulator version, relying on #27523 to block the
implicit system-object read when that version is not yet local, and
discounts unsettled withdrawals from earlier transactions in the same
consensus commit. Insufficiency is a deterministic framework abort
surfaced as `MoveAbort(funds_accumulator, E_OBJECT_FUNDS_INSUFFICIENT)`.

The first settled-balance read for each `(owner, type)` pair is charged
a fixed 184 internal gas units. This matches the fixed work of the
equivalent dynamic-field lookup: 52 for hashing, 52 for borrowing, and
80 for loading the fixed-size accumulator field contents. The existing
transaction-local `ObjectFundsAvailable` state records when that balance
has been queried, so later withdrawals for the same pair reuse the
running balance and are not charged for another cold read. Withdrawals
fully covered by deposits earlier in the same transaction also avoid the
store read and its charge.

Known caveat carried over from the old PR: isolated replay does not
reconstruct in-commit unsettled withdrawals (`unsettled = 0`; see the
TODO in `crates/sui-replay-2/src/execution.rs`), which can diverge from
the original execution. Mainnet enablement is blocked on resolving that.

## Test plan

- Successful and insufficient-funds gRPC simulations return the
accumulator root object at exactly the version referenced by
`ReadOnlyRoot` in their effects. Both cases fail without implicit-read
tracking and pass with the fix.

- Cold-read metering follows the actual storage-access decision for each
`(owner, type)` pair. A zero withdrawal or a withdrawal covered by
transaction-local funds needs no settled-balance read. The first
withdrawal that exceeds those funds takes the cold path and is charged
184; after that balance is marked queried, later withdrawals reuse the
running balance and do not take or pay for another cold read, including
when the cached balance is insufficient. Protocol snapshots verify that
the cost is absent through v136 and set to 184 in v137.
- A vault funded with 1,000 units accepts withdrawals within its
available balance, including zero and the exact remaining balance. A
5,000-unit withdrawal and the second of two 600-unit withdrawals fail
specifically with `E_OBJECT_FUNDS_INSUFFICIENT`. The same boundary is
verified for both simulation and committed execution.
- Deposits earlier in the same transaction are immediately available to
later withdrawals: depositing 500 before withdrawing 1,400 from a
1,000-unit vault succeeds, while withdrawing 1,600 fails. Depositing 700
into an empty vault and then withdrawing 600 succeeds and leaves a net
balance of 100. This verifies command ordering and netting within one
execution.
- When two withdrawals use the same accumulator-root version in one
consensus commit, unsettled withdrawals are deducted from the balance
visible to later execution. From a settled balance of 1,000, two
600-unit withdrawals produce exactly one success and one insufficiency
abort; two 400-unit withdrawals both succeed; withdrawing the exact
remaining 200 then succeeds. A newly started fullnode catches up all
resulting effects, exercising exact-version reads during replay and
catch-up.
- With the feature enabled, a successful withdrawal records the
accumulator root as a `ReadOnlyRoot` dependency. With it disabled, the
same withdrawal succeeds without that dependency and continues through
the legacy object-funds checker path, preserving pre-upgrade effects
behavior.
- Regression cases attempt unbacked `u64::MAX` SUI and custom-coin
withdrawals combined with gas smashing, gas refunds, accumulator merges,
and gas-coin merges. Each transaction aborts at the object-funds check
before poison accumulator writes are emitted; no value is credited, and
the network can still reconfigure afterward. Each regression also runs
with the new check explicitly disabled, preserving the
`CoinBalanceOverflow` and custom-coin merge-cap assertions for the
legacy path still used by mainnet and testnet.
- Concurrent stress covers owned, party-owned, and shared vaults while
seven workers perform randomized transfers and expected overdraw
attempts. All workers complete and the network reconfigures afterward,
exercising the execution-time check under contention across ownership
modes.

## Release notes

Check each box that your change affects. If none of the boxes relate to
your changes, release notes are not required.

- [x] Protocol: Protocol v137 enables
`check_object_funds_withdraw_in_execution` on devnet only. Object-funds
withdrawal sufficiency is checked inside the Move VM at the point of
withdrawal, insufficient withdrawals abort with a
`sui::funds_accumulator` Move abort, and the first settled-balance read
for each `(owner, type)` pair costs 184 internal gas units.
- [ ] Nodes (Validators and Full nodes):
- [ ] gRPC:
- [ ] JSON-RPC:
- [ ] GraphQL:
- [ ] CLI:
- [ ] Rust SDK:

This prevents potential over‑withdrawal of funds, a security issue, thus constituting a security fix with high impact.

subject: Support object and address funds withdraw in Move test_scenario (#28048)
body:
## Description

Move unit tests couldn't meaningfully exercise funds withdrawals. The
unit-test runner's funds resolver reported an unlimited balance for
every object. `test_scenario` dropped accumulator events at the end of
each transaction. And there was no way to create a withdrawal from an
address or to read a balance. So `withdraw_funds_from_object` always
succeeded, whatever had been deposited, and address funds were
write-only.

`InMemoryTestStore` now keeps a settled balance per `(owner, type)`,
where the owner is an address or an object. Each `test_scenario`
transaction boundary settles that transaction's accumulator events into
it, netting each key's deposits and withdrawals first, as real
settlement does. Deposits are the same mechanism for both kinds of
owner, so they share this table, but the two withdrawal paths are
checked separately, under their own rules:

- Object withdrawals keep going through
`funds_accumulator::withdraw_from_object` and the object runtime's
reservation, with the store serving as its `ObjectFundsResolver`. As in
production, funds deposited earlier in the same transaction are
available.
- Address withdrawals get
`test_scenario::withdraw_balance_from_address<T>(owner, value)`, which
stands in for a transaction's funds withdrawal input: the reservations
taken from an owner within a transaction are summed and checked against
its settled balance only, so funds sent to the owner during the
transaction are not available. Insufficient funds abort with
`test_scenario::EInsufficientFunds`. As with a transaction input, whose
reservation must be non-zero, a zero withdrawal aborts with
`test_scenario::EZeroWithdrawal`, whereas a zero object withdrawal
succeeds, as it does in production.

`test_scenario::settled_balance<T>(owner)` reads an address's or
object's balance as of the end of the previous transaction. Both follow
the framework's own layering: the natives are generic over the
accumulated type, and the `Balance<T>` wrapping and `u64` clamping
happen in Move, as `balance::withdraw_funds_from_object` and
`balance::settled_funds_value` do.

Limitations:
- The settled balance is clamped at zero, because withdrawals created
without a reservation (`allowance::new_withdrawal_for_testing`) redeem
from balances that were never funded, and the existing allowance tests
depend on that.
- Reservations from gas paid out of an address balance are not modeled.
- Accumulator-root fields are not simulated, so
`balance::settled_funds_value(&AccumulatorRoot, _)` is unchanged.

## Test plan

New tests in `sui-framework/tests/funds_accumulator_tests.move`, all
driven through `test_scenario`:
- Object: deposit 1000, then withdraw 400 and, in a later transaction,
the remaining 600. `settled_funds_value` reads 0 before the first
transaction boundary, then 1000, 600 and 0.
- Object: withdrawing 1001 from 1000 aborts with
`E_OBJECT_FUNDS_INSUFFICIENT`. So does withdrawing 601 after an earlier
400 has settled.
- Object: a 500 deposit made during the transaction is available, so
1500 can be withdrawn from a settled 1000.
- Address: the same deposit, withdraw and read sequence, including two
successful withdrawals (300 + 100) in one transaction. Reservations are
keyed per owner and type: another owner's and another coin type's full
balances are still withdrawable in that same transaction.
- Address: two withdrawals of 600 and 401 from 1000 in one transaction.
The second aborts, so reservations add up within a transaction. The same
holds when the 600 is reserved and never redeemed, so it is the reserved
limit that counts.
- Address: depositing 500 during the transaction does not make a 1001
withdrawal from a 1000 balance succeed, unlike the object case above.
- Zero and never-funded owners: from an address that never received
funds, withdrawing 0 aborts with `EZeroWithdrawal` (this test fails
without the check) and withdrawing 1 aborts with `EInsufficientFunds`;
withdrawing 0 from an object that never received funds succeeds.
- `settled_balance` aborts with `EBalanceOverflow` once more than
`u64::MAX` has been settled to one owner across transactions.
- An unreserved 100 withdrawal from an unfunded address, sent back to
the same address in the same transaction, settles to 0. Clamping per
event would leave 100; this test failed with that version.

Before this change, the object over-withdrawal tests failed (the
withdrawals succeeded). The existing framework and example Move tests
all still pass, including the allowance tests that redeem from unfunded
addresses.

---

withdrawal succeeded in unit tests). Two new test-only functions:

subject: Reserve allowance test withdrawals and reject unbacked withdrawals in test_scenario (#28096)
body:
## Description

Follow-up to #28048. `test_scenario` there had to clamp a negative
settled balance to zero, because `allowance::new_withdrawal_for_testing`
built its withdrawal with `funds_accumulator::create_withdrawal`:
nothing was reserved, and the allowance tests spent from a funder that
never received any funds. The clamp also hid unbacked withdrawals in any
other test.

- `allowance::new_withdrawal_for_testing` and
`new_sponsor_withdrawal_for_testing` now take the inner `Withdrawal<T>`
instead of a funder and amount. Tests pass one from
`test_scenario::withdraw_balance_from_address`, which reserves against
the funder's settled balance like the real allowance-backed PTB input.
`allowance` itself doesn't depend on `test_scenario`.
- The allowance test harness sends `FUNDER` a balance up front, and
`test_wrong_funder_rejected` funds its wrong funder, so that test still
reaches the allowance's funder check instead of failing the reservation.
- Settlement in `test_scenario` now aborts with `EUnbackedWithdrawal`
when a transaction withdrew more from an owner than it had, instead of
clamping.

## Test plan

- New `test_withdrawal_kept_across_transactions_is_unbacked`: a
withdrawal of an owner's whole balance, kept from an earlier transaction
and redeemed alongside a fresh reservation of the same balance, aborts
with `EUnbackedWithdrawal` at settlement. With the old clamping, the
test fails (the settlement goes through).
- Every allowance test now spends from a funded `FUNDER` through
reserved withdrawals and still passes. That covers caps, rate limits,
app permits, a dropped withdrawal (its reservation still counts in its
transaction), the sponsor rejection, and wrong-funder and wrong-app
rejections.
- The existing `test_unreserved_withdrawal_nets_with_deposits` still
passes: withdrawing and sending back the same amount in one transaction
nets to zero, so nothing is unbacked.

subject: Read forwarding master records from the store and charge a registration fee
body:
Resolution now reads the registry's master record the way object funds
withdrawals read accumulator balances: `ObjectFundsResolver::forwarding_master`
loads the registry at the version consensus assigned and reads the record from
the backing store under that bound. This drops the child-object-store path
(`load_child_object_bytes`, `track_system_root_version`) and the manual layout
handling in the native, and takes system-object loading back off the funds
resolver trait. A record written earlier in the same transaction is no longer
visible, so registering and depositing in one PTB aborts as unregistered.

The resolve native now charges a fixed lookup cost before the read instead of
per-byte charges after it, so an unregistered id pays for the lookup too.

`register` calls a new `charge_registration_fee` native that charges
`forwarding_address_register_cost_base` (900K gas units at 139), which lands a
registration in the 1M-unit computation bucket.

The upgrade test now rolls out in order: validators reach 138 and create the
registry, then upgrade to 139, and a register plus deposit in the first
forwarding-enabled epoch must resolve.

rationale: The commit changes how forwarding address registry records are read, fixing a bug where a record written in the same transaction was incorrectly visible, and adds a registration fee that charges gas even for unregistered lookups, preventing free enumeration/DoS. These changes correct incorrect behavior and mitigate a potential resource‑exhaustion attack.

Move bytecode can only express bulk vector operations one element at a
time, making common operations disproportionately expensive in gas and
validator CPU.
Add the following "primitives": `replace_range`, `keep_range`,
`copy_range`, and `remove_range`.
`append`, and `truncate` (like others too) remain Move wrappers over the
general primitives, and affected functions in `std::vector`,
`std::ascii`, `std::string`, and `sui::bcs` reuse them.

## Test plan

- Move tests cover the new APIs, invalid ranges, ability constraints,
and affected wrappers.
- VM tests cover primitive and container representations, deep-copy/drop
behavior, exact gas formulas, and out-of-gas-before-mutation behavior.

## Release notes

`keep_range`, `copy_range`, `remove_range`, and `truncate`

subject: Add pause and two-step master rotation to the forwarding address registry
body:
A leaked master key must not keep every published forwarding address paying
the attacker. The record now carries a lifecycle, chosen by the registrant at
`register(registry, rotation_delay_epochs, ctx)`:

- Pause is immediate and either key can do it: `pause` with the `MasterCap`,
  `pause_by_master` as the current master. Deposits to a paused id fail at the
  end of execution like deposits to an unregistered id. Only the cap can
  `unpause`, so a stolen master key cannot undo the owner's pause.
- Rotation is two-step. The cap proposes a new master (which must not carry
  the magic, since chaining is not resolved yet), the proposal becomes
  effective `rotation_delay_epochs` later, and anyone may finalize it once
  due. Deposits keep crediting the old master while pending. Either the cap
  or the current master can cancel, which is what stops a rotation proposed
  with a stolen cap.
- `rotation_delay_epochs` is 1..=30 and can only be increased afterwards.

`MasterRecord { master, paused, pending, rotation_delay_epochs }` keeps a
deposit at one record read. The resolver fails on a paused record; the
`ImplicitSystemObjectResolver` hands it a `ForwardingMaster { master, paused }`
so the store schema stays in `sui-types`. `test_scenario` follows the
`Paused`, `Unpaused` and `RotationFinalized` events to keep its view of the
registry in step. Every transition emits an event so an indexer never has to
diff the record.
rationale: The change introduces pause and delayed two‑step master key rotation to the forwarding address registry, fixing a prior flaw where a leaked master key could continue to authorize deposits and drain funds. This addresses an improper access control/privilege management issue.

subject: [poc] Account policies: opt-in, key-bounded account rules enforced in execution
body:
Adds `sui::account_policy`, an opt-in per-address policy that bounds what a
transaction signed by the account key alone may do. Policies live as dynamic
fields of a new `AccountPolicyRegistry` system object (0xab, created at
genesis), which every transaction implicitly reads at the version consensus
assigned to it, so execution can look up the sender's policy deterministically
without the transaction declaring it.

While a policy is active, execution rejects the transaction with a new
`AccountPolicyViolation` status if it exceeds the gas budget cap, publishes or
upgrades a package, calls any package other than 0x3, moves more SUI (coins
plus stake principal plus address-balance withdrawals) out of the sender than
the per-transaction limit, or lets any non-SUI-coin object the sender owned
leave the sender's ownership. The guardian exempts individual transactions by
approving their digests. A policy only takes effect one epoch after it is
enabled, and the owner can cancel it before then with the key alone, which
closes the lockout grief where a thief enables a policy on a stolen key.

The registry read is recorded in effects only when the sender has a policy,
so transactions of senders without one are unchanged on replay.

Gated by the devnet-only `enable_account_policy` flag in protocol version 140.
rationale: The commit introduces a new account policy feature and related system object handling; it does not correct previously incorrect behavior, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

peel_address and peel_vec_u8 now use it, so peel_address no longer pops
its 32 bytes one at a time.
rationale: The change fixes incorrect deserialization of fixed‑length byte arrays (address and vec<u8>) which previously popped bytes one at a time, leading to reversed byte order. Mis‑interpreted addresses could cause funds to be sent to unintended recipients, a potential spoofing/unauthorized‑transfer security issue.

body:
Replaces the approved-digest list with a second signature. A transaction may
carry one signature beyond its required signers when account policies are
enabled; validators verify it like any other, and execution derives the
co-signer addresses from the envelope. The policy check exempts a transaction
co-signed by the guardian, and `update`/`disable` require the same through
the new `tx_context::co_signers` native. Replay and backtest pass no
co-signers yet.
rationale: The commit introduces a new feature (guardian co‑signatures for account policies) by adding fields, config flags, and verification logic. It does not correct previously incorrect behavior, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: Account policies: per-type coin limits, recipients, package permissions and custody attribution
body:
The policy now carries a per-coin-type outflow limit (types without an entry
cannot flow out), a recipient list that coins and objects may be sent to
without limit, and a package allowlist keyed by original package ID where each
entry may grant custody of the owner's objects, optionally limited to listed
types. The system package is always callable with custody.

Objects the sender possessed (owned inputs, received objects and dynamic
fields of owned objects) must stay with the sender, go to a listed recipient,
or be taken by a package with custody. To attribute an object's departure to a
command, the object runtime tags every transfer and deletion with the index of
the executing command, and the PTB context records input objects taken by
value so silent wraps are attributed too; the temporary store receives the map
through a new `Storage::record_object_consumers` hook.

Every active-policy change needs the guardian's co-signature; pending policies
are configured with the key alone.
rationale: The commit adds new account policy capabilities (per-coin limits, recipient allowlist, package custody rules) and associated tests, but does not modify existing behavior to correct a defect; it is a feature addition rather than a bug fix, so no security fix is implied.

subject: Account policies: per-epoch coin and custody budgets tracked in accumulator counters
body:
Coin limits and custody permissions now bound an epoch, not a transaction.
Spend is merged into accumulator counters (`account_policy::Spent<T>`) at an
address derived from the owner and epoch, so the owner's transactions need no
sequencing against each other and the budget resets by moving to a fresh
address. The check reads the counter settled at the assigned accumulator root
version plus the unsettled merges of earlier transactions in the same commit,
and a transaction's own spend is merged after gas is charged: coin outflow and
custody only when it succeeds, gas always, so failing transactions still burn
budget.

Custody permissions take an optional per-epoch object cap; exceeding it is a
new `CustodyLimitExceeded` violation.
rationale: The change adds a new accumulator type for account policy counters and records unsettled counter merges, fixing the previous per-transaction budget enforcement. This prevents attackers from exceeding per-epoch coin/custody limits across multiple transactions, a flaw that could lead to unauthorized fund loss.

subject: Borrow the Clock in Move without a Clock input (#28241)
body:
## Description

Follows #28244, which renamed the resolver this change extends.

Move code can only read the time by taking `&Clock` as a parameter, so a
function deep in a call stack that newly needs the time forces every
caller up to the entry function to thread the Clock through. The Clock
is already written by every consensus commit's prologue, so its value is
known for every transaction in the commit without being declared.

This adds `sui::clock::borrow(): &Clock`, a native that returns a
reference to the Clock without it being a transaction input, and makes
the Clock an implicitly read system object (like the accumulator root
and the forwarding address registry). The read is version-assigned per
transaction, recorded in effects as a read-only root, and reproduced
from effects on fullnodes and in replay, so there is no on-wire change.
The Clock is pinned for every transaction on every protocol version;
that is node-local scheduling state and only reaches effects when the
function is called, which the protocol 141 framework upgrade gates on
its own. The only protocol-config change is the native's cost parameter.

The native returns a reference into a value the object runtime owns for
the whole transaction, the same mechanism dynamic fields use. No native
today returns a reference without taking one, so this is a new pattern
for the Move team to confirm.

## Test plan

- `test_clock_version_follows_consensus_commit_prologue` (sui-core): a
transaction sequenced before a commit prologue pins the pre-prologue
Clock version, and one sequenced after it pins the version the prologue
writes.
- `implicit_clock_tests` (e2e, own Move package so older-framework tests
can still publish `move_test_code`): one transaction passes `&Clock`
explicitly and asserts in Move that `borrow().timestamp_ms()` equals
`clock.timestamp_ms()`. Another passes no Clock, calls a function
written against `&Clock` through `borrow()`, checks the Clock appears in
effects as a read-only root, and compares the emitted timestamp against
the Clock object at that version as read from the fullnode, which
exercises the from-effects version reconstruction. A third reads the
Clock and aborts, checking the read is still recorded and the fullnode
settles the failed transaction. A fourth simulates the transaction on
the fullnode and checks the simulated effects pin the Clock version
whose timestamp was emitted.
- Move unit test in `clock_tests.move`: `borrow().timestamp_ms()` is 0
in unit tests and follows the `Clock` a test creates or mutates through
the existing `create_for_testing`, `set_for_testing` and
`increment_for_testing` helpers.
- `test_implicit_clock_read_uses_pinned_version` (sui-core): with two
Clock versions in the store, a transaction pinned to the older one reads
that timestamp, not the latest, and records the pinned version in
effects.
- Transactional test `clock/borrow.move`
(sui-adapter-transactional-tests): a published module reads the time
through a `&Clock` helper fed by `borrow()` with no Clock input; the
recorded timestamp follows `advance-clock`, the implicit read shows up
as `unchanged_shared: 0x6` in effects, a borrowed Clock agrees with an
explicitly passed one, and an aborting read reports the Move abort.
- Existing `shared_object_version_manager` tests cover the Clock entry
in the per-transaction system object versions.

framework. It returns the Clock without it being a transaction input, at

Available from protocol version 141 with the framework upgrade.

subject: Require the new master to finalize a rotation; add the emergency brake and event size limits
body:
An ordinary address becomes a master only by signing for it: `finalize_rotation`
must now be sent by the proposed master (`ENotNewMaster`), otherwise anyone
could point an id at a well-known merchant and hand out addresses that appear
to be its while keeping the cap. A forwarding address cannot sign, so once
chaining lands a rotation to one is finalized by anyone.

`freeze_forwarding_addresses` is the emergency brake: a protocol flag, off
everywhere, under which resolution fails for every forwarding address while
registration and the lifecycle functions keep working. It is separate from
`enable_forwarding_addresses` because that flag off means "ordinary address"
and would strand funds.

Adapter-emitted events now count against `max_event_emit_size` and, together
with the size `event::emit` metered for the Move events, against
`max_event_emit_size_total`, not only against `max_num_event_emit`. The object
runtime hands that total out through `RuntimeResults`.

Also adds an e2e test that a gasless payment of an allowlisted token to a
forwarding address stays gasless, and brings the design doc in line with the
SIP (coin melting, chain creation, chained ids, gasless).
rationale: The change enforces that only the proposed new master can call `finalize_rotation`, fixing a missing authorization check that previously allowed any party to hijack a forwarding address and potentially steal funds.

subject: Melt coins sent to forwarding addresses, follow forwarding chains, and let ids point at them
body:
A `Coin<T>` owned by a forwarding address at the end of execution is melted:
the object is deleted (or never created) and its value becomes a funds credit
to that address, which resolves like any `send_funds` deposit, so the master
sees one address-balance credit and one `ForwardingDeposit<T>` however the
payer sent the funds, and the deny-list check sees the master. Any other
object owned by a forwarding address fails the transaction, as do the gas
coin and a party object that grants a forwarding address permissions.

A master that is itself a forwarding address resolves again, up to
`forwarding_address_max_hops` (3 at protocol version 141), with the lookup
charged before every registry read. Each hop emits its own `ForwardingDeposit`
with the sum that passed through that address, recorded in the stream of that
hop's master, so every party along a chain sees deposits into its own address.
The post-gas invariant now only forbids funds credited to a forwarding address,
since a hop's stream can be keyed by one.

Chains are built with `register_with_forwarding_master` and by
`propose_rotation` onto a forwarding address, both requiring the magic, a
variant the resolver supports (read through a new `variant_is_supported`
native) and another master id. A forwarding address cannot sign, so it needs no
consent and anyone finalizes a rotation to one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit changes handling of forwarding addresses so that coins sent to them are melted and credited to the master, fixing a previous bug where funds could be locked or bypass deny‑list checks. This corrects an access‑control flaw that could be exploited to move funds improperly, indicating a security fix of high severity.

subject: [fix] Reject an overflowing x-coordinate in secp256r1_ecrecover behind a protocol flag (#28460)
body:
## Description

`secp256r1_ecrecover` could return a key that does not verify the
signature: when the recovery id marks x(R) as reduced and r + n
overflows 256 bits, the sum wrapped instead of failing (Wycheproof tc
482). Fixed in fastcrypto by
https://github.com/MystenLabs/fastcrypto/pull/1106 and pulled in by
#28502, which left every execution version on recover_with_hash_legacy.
This gates the strict check behind
`secp256r1_ecrecover_checks_x_below_p`, enabled in protocol version 141
on all chains, and switches latest to it. The frozen execution versions
keep the wrapped result so earlier transactions replay unchanged.

## Test plan

- Move test: the wrapped signature aborts with `EFailToRecoverPubKey` at
the current protocol version.
- e2e test `ecdsa_r1_ecrecover_tests`: the same call aborts with the
flag on and succeeds with it off.

## Release notes

- [x] Protocol: `secp256r1_ecrecover` now aborts with
`EFailToRecoverPubKey` on a signature whose recovered x-coordinate r + n
overflows, instead of returning a key that does not verify it. Honest
signers never produce such a signature.

subject: fix: replace denylist with allowlist in _checkV4PositionManagerCall (BBP #719)
body:
The denylist in _checkV4PositionManagerCall missed MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS
(0x05), allowing fee theft from V4 positions whose owners approved the
Universal Router. Switching to an allowlist ensures only MINT_POSITION and
settlement actions (>= SETTLE) pass the guard, closing both the 0x05 gap
and any future action additions.

Adds regression tests for INCREASE_LIQUIDITY_FROM_DELTAS and
MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS via V4_POSITION_MANAGER_CALL.

Vulnerability class: CWE-184 (Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs)

Co-Authored-By: Clarion <noreply@clarion.sh>
rationale: The commit replaces a denylist with an allowlist in _checkV4PositionManagerCall, closing a gap that allowed MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS (and related actions) to bypass the guard and enable fee theft from V4 positions. This corrects a security‑critical defect.

subject: fix: require MINT_POSITION in V4 migration guard and replace denylist with allowlist
body:
The _checkV4PositionManagerCall guard used a denylist that only blocked
four specific actions, allowing SWEEP, TAKE, TAKE_PAIR, and other
settlement actions to pass unchecked. A SWEEP-only V4 PositionManager
payload could drain migrated V3 principal to an attacker without minting
any V4 position. This also addresses the previously-reported bypass via
INCREASE_LIQUIDITY_FROM_DELTAS (0x04) and MINT_POSITION_FROM_DELTAS (0x05).

The fix:
1. Replaces the denylist with an allowlist (only MINT_POSITION and actions
   >= SETTLE are permitted).
2. Requires at least one MINT_POSITION in the plan, preventing settlement-
   only payloads from extracting balances.

Cantina BBP Finding: #721, #719

Co-Authored-By: Clarion <noreply@clarion.sh>
rationale: The change replaces a denylist with an allowlist and enforces at least one MINT_POSITION, closing a vulnerability where sweep-only or settlement-only V4 payloads could drain migrated V3 funds. This corrects improper access control that could be exploited to steal user funds.

subject: fix(dispatcher): reject command inputs shorter than the fields they read
body:
Commands that decode fixed fields with `calldataload` read at fixed offsets
from `inputs.offset` without consulting `inputs.length`. Solidity's ABI
decoder accepts non-canonical calldata in which a `bytes[]` element declares
a short (or zero) length while attacker-chosen words remain physically
present immediately after the length word, so those reads can run past the
declared end of the input.

This matters for `executeSigned`: `RouteSigner._setSignatureContext` hashes
each input as `keccak256(inputs[i])`, which covers exactly `inputs[i].length`
bytes. Anything read beyond that length was never covered by the EIP-712
signature, so the router could authenticate one byte range and execute a
different one — breaking the guarantee documented at IUniversalRouter.sol:52
that all commands are covered by the signature.

Add a minimum-length guard to the 13 commands that read fixed fields. Nine
have no bounds-checked decoder behind them and are directly affected; the
four V2/V3 swap paths are already saved incidentally by `toBytes` /
`toAddressArray` / `toUint256Array`, and are guarded here so reachability
does not have to be re-derived per command later.

Reported as Cantina #703 (duplicate #809).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds explicit length checks before reading fixed-size fields from calldata, preventing out‑of‑bounds reads that could let an attacker craft inputs where the signed hash covers fewer bytes than the router actually executes, breaking signature authentication and enabling unauthorized actions.

* fix: decode SWEEP amountMinimum at full uint256 width

The SWEEP branch decoded its third calldata word into a uint160 local, so

silently reduced modulo 2**160 -- an encoded 2**160 became 0, disabling the
aggregate output check entirely while the calldata, and for executeSigned

the least significant bits, so 2**160 + 1 enforced a minimum of 1.

branch with the same shape kept uint256. Payments.sweep and the planner ABI
already declare uint256, so this restores the pre-refactor semantics with no
ABI change and no behavior change for any value that fits in 160 bits.
Dropping the mask also reduces runtime size by 3 bytes.

type(uint160).max.
