subject: fix(margin): script to re-point Morpho adapter at the canonical WETH/USDC market
body:
The deployment registered a WETH/USDC market whose oracle
(0xdC6fd583...) differs from the canonical mainnet market
(id 0x94b823e6...), hashing to an unlisted market id with negligible
liquidity. The registry keys one market per (collateral, debt) pair, so
registering the canonical params evicts the stale entry in one call.
The script is idempotent, verifies the routed params byte-for-byte
before and after, and optionally warns about residual positions
stranded in the stale market.
rationale: The commit adds a script that corrects the MorphoLendingAdapter to point to the canonical WETH/USDC market instead of a stale market with a different oracle, fixing misrouting that could cause users to interact with an incorrect market and potentially suffer loss or be exposed to a manipulable oracle. This is a bug fix with security implications (incorrect market configuration), classified as tampering with financial data.

subject: feat(margin): Ponder indexer for margin position history
body:
Reconstructs the full transaction-history field set from public onchain
data alone: entry/exit prices from same-tx lending Borrow events (exact

lending protocol fired, pool sub-labels from v4 Initialize metadata, and
liquidations from Morpho Liquidate / Aave LiquidationCall attributed to

integrators can serve identical history. Aave v4 flow indexing pends the

Added sample GraphQL queries for the margin indexer:

Owner account discovery, portfolio and active/completed tabs, per
position history feed, pool sub-label join, raw lending feed including
escape hatch operations, registries, and pagination. Field scaling
notes for X18 prices and raw token amounts.

subject: fix(SwapAndAdd): reconcile/fee correctness + audit-readiness restructure
body:
Behavioral fixes (each with a regression test):
- size fee-aware math from the DIRECTIONAL protocol fee via
  ProtocolFeeLibrary.calculateSwapFee; the packed Slot0.protocolFee was
  previously added to lpFee as plain pips, underflowing sizing on any pool
  with a protocol fee set
- fund the route on BOTH sides and let it declare its own input; reclaim
  unconsumed native from the Universal Router via a SWEEP execute (UR
  balances are permissionlessly sweepable)
- clamp the native value forwarded to POSM to the held balance (ranges
  entirely below spot hold no buffer wei and reverted OutOfFunds)
- cap the reconcile trim at the liquidity the operation just added, so
  increase/compound can never consume the owner's pre-existing principal
- approve Permit2 with SafeTransferLib.safeApprove: tokens whose approve
  returns nothing (USDT) reverted the plain IERC20 call on decode,
  bricking every pool of that token
- widen int128 negation in _resolveBudget (type(int128).min)

Restructure:
- merge _mint/_increase and their param builders into one _deploy
- one-time standing max Permit2 allowances to POSM/UR (_ensureApproved),
  justified by the documented no-funds-at-rest contract invariant
- restrict receive() to PoolManager/POSM/UR (InvalidEthSender)
- checkDeadline modifier; _authAndResolveRecipient merges the auth check
  with the operator recipient-forcing rule
- normative NatSpec: operator TRUST NOTE, fee-taking-hook KNOWN LIMIT,
  route funding semantics

rationale: The commit fixes several behavioral bugs: fee calculation underflow and reconcile trim over‑consumption of user principal. Both could lead to incorrect fee handling or loss of user funds, which are security‑relevant defects. body:
Add ILendingAdapter.describePosition returning collateral, debt, maxLtv, currentLtv, and health factor in one call, so integrators no longer stitch positionOf + maxLtvWad + currentLtvWad. Aave adapters surface their native health factor (previously discarded); Morpho derives it.

subject: feat(margin): single-transaction 7702 deploy and bootstrap
body:
Deploy and wire the whole stack in one EIP-7702 transaction: the deployer EOA delegates to a reusable BatchExecutor and self-calls a batch that deploys the account implementation, the three adapters, and the router through the standard CREATE2 factory (preserving the mined vanity address), then allowlists the adapters, registers markets, and proposes the final governance via the two-step handoff.

A self-contained bootstrapper contract is impossible here: the stack's combined creation code (55.4KB) exceeds the EIP-3860 initcode limit (49.15KB).
rationale: The commit introduces new contracts and scripts to enable a single‑transaction deployment via EIP‑7702. It adds functionality but does not modify existing behavior to fix a defect, nor does it address any security vulnerability.

subject: refactor(margin): rename open to increase and fold close into decrease
body:
Rename openPosition to increasePosition (and OpenParams to IncreaseParams, PositionOpened to PositionIncreased): the first call opens and subsequent calls add leverage, so 'increase' names the whole operation.

Collapse closePosition into decreasePosition: passing debtToRepay == type(uint256).max fully closes (repay all by shares, withdraw all collateral, return residual PnL), otherwise a partial delever enforcing maxLtvAfter. Both modes share one implementation parameterized by the sentinel, and one PositionDecreased event carries the resulting state (a full close is signalled by debtTotal == 0, with collateralReturned the realized PnL); the separate PositionClosed event is removed. Migrate tests and regenerate snapshots.
rationale: [MEV] The refactor adds a validation check that reverts when a decreasePosition call lacks a slippage bound (maxLtvAfter) unless it is a full close. This prevents callers from executing a position decrease without any protection against price manipulation, fixing a previously missing input validation that could be exploited via front‑running or sandwich attacks.

subject: docs(SwapAndAdd): route is a black box, not guaranteed off-venue
body:
The NatSpec claimed the route "does not touch this pool" as if it were
a mechanism guarantee. Nothing enforces that: correctness comes from
sizing AFTER the route, from re-read balances at the then-live price —
whatever the route did (even to this pool), the post-route state is the
source of truth and minLiquidity remains the single gate.

Compound was the only op without the route leg, on the grounds that fees
are small — but the execution cost of the same-pool reconcile is
proportional to the compounded amount, i.e. a recurring haircut on yield
itself. The shared core already runs routes, so CompoundParams gains
`route` and _compound passes it through instead of hardcoding "".

Sizing note (interface): quote the route input at the currently-unclaimed
fees — fees only accrue upward, the reconcile absorbs the drift, and a
competing collection reverts the pull atomically. Operator trust model
unchanged (an approved operator can already collect fees via POSM
directly; minLiquidityAdded bounds any route atomically).

Tests: mock-route compound unit test; real-UR compound route integration
test — also the first existing-tokenId path exercising the nested UR
execute.

subject: test(SwapAndAdd): pin the tick/price boundary-divergence states
body:
The pool selects its amounts branch by TICK, the zap by SQRTPRICE; the
only states where they can disagree are prices exactly on a tick
boundary (a limit-clamped swap landing on an initialized tick stores
tick = boundary - 1 zeroForOne / boundary oneForZero). Engineer both
states, assert them, and prove the branch formulas coincide — a
divergence would make POSM pull a token the zap never funded and
revert the unlock.

Also surfaced: the wei-level flash-take needs PM-WIDE reserves of the
deficit token — the boundary swap drains the pool universe's entire
token0, and the take reverts atomically until any position re-supplies
it. Documented as K-05 (academic in production, funds safe).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit only adds/updates test code and audit documentation without modifying any production contract logic, so it does not correct a previously incorrect behavior nor address a security issue.

subject: refactor(SwapAndAdd): remove ROUNDING_BUFFER — deficit funding is wei-exact
body:
The buffer guarded against POSM pulling more than the sized amounts,
but that divergence is structurally impossible: _getAmountsForLiquidity
rounds up with the pool's own SqrtPriceMath on the pool's own inputs,
and the sole subtle case — price exactly on a tick boundary, where the
pool branches on tick and the zap on sqrtPrice — degenerates to equal
amounts (pinned by the test_add_priceExactlyOn* boundary tests; full
suites pass with the buffer removed, 5000-run fuzz included).

Removing it also deletes the _nativeToForward clamp the buffer had made
necessary (its absence was a real OutOfFunds bug on below-range native
mints), and turns every deficit-funded test into a standing wei-exact
funding check. Audit doc D-04 rewritten accordingly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit removes a 1‑wei ROUNDING_BUFFER that caused flash‑take and native‑forward calculations to over‑request funds, leading to an OutOfFunds revert in certain edge cases. This corrects the faulty behavior (bug fix) and eliminates a potential denial‑of‑service condition where a transaction could be forced to fail due to the off‑by‑one rounding error.

subject: refactor(SwapAndAdd): drop _trim's unreachable wrong-side fallbacks
body:
The trim only runs while the flash debt is unpaid, and that debt is the
just-added range's own deficit side — the exact-input reconcile sell
repays it in full at the latest when it exhausts the range, so the
price can never be past the range's FAR side with deficit still owed.
The near-side min/max clamps stay (reachable: a range fully beyond spot
trims from a price outside it — now pinned by
test_add_belowRange_singleToken0). If the invariant were ever violated
the sorted liquidity math still yields a capped dl and the unlock
reverts atomically, same as the fallbacks did.

Also: document the K-05 no-pre-check decision on _flashTakeDeficit (a
globally drained PM fails the take, but that state leaves the reconcile
nothing to swap against either — the op is unviable regardless).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit only removes unreachable fallback code and adds a test; no functional behavior change is introduced, so it is a refactor rather than a bug fix, and there is no evidence of a security impact.

Post-merge review fixes for #574:
- Report INSUFFICIENT_GAS status with intact core amounts instead of
  reverting when remaining gas cannot guarantee the hook-stats probe
  sequence; the InsufficientGasForHookStats revert becomes an
  unreachable backstop
- Include block.chainid in the cursor context hash so cursors cannot
  cross chains that share a PoolManager address
- Classify hook-stats status by the resolved provider (provider == hook)
  rather than by how it was supplied, so passing the hook address
  explicitly matches passing address(0)
- Revert with typed ManagerBatchReadFailed context when a non-conforming
  manager returns a malformed batched extsload response

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(lens): default-parameter overloads, cursor snapshot verification, expanded coverage

Ergonomics: every optional parameter now has a no-argument path.
- getPoolTVL(manager, key), getPoolTVLBatch(manager, keys), and
  getPoolTVLPaged(manager, key, cursor) overloads default the URC-3
  stats provider to the pool's hook and the page budget to 512 reads
  (~2M gas per page, under any eth_call cap)
- maxReads == 0 on the full paged signature selects the default budget

Hardening: resumed cursors verify their price, tick, and active
liquidity against live manager state (CursorStateMismatch), so forged
snapshot metadata and same-block state drift fail loudly instead of
surfacing as invariant errors attributed to the pool. Scan position and
amount accumulators remain caller-trusted, now documented explicitly.

Coverage: cursor tampering (length, version, bitPos, manager,
snapshot fields), InvalidTickSpacing on all entry points, invariant
guards via a settable lying-manager mock, full-range positions at
default and maximum tick spacing, paged final-page hook-stats probe,
and default-variant equivalence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(lens): degrade per-call gas backstop to INSUFFICIENT_GAS instead of reverting (#578)

* fix(lens): degrade per-call gas backstop to INSUFFICIENT_GAS status instead of reverting

The up-front HOOK_STATS_GAS_BUDGET check assumed a constant 15k local
overhead between it and the final stats call, but memory expansion is
priced quadratically against the frame's free memory pointer: after a
tick-spacing-1 scan (~450KB of batch arrays), post-scan allocations cost
~58 gas/word instead of 3, and batched calls compound this across pools.
No constant estimate holds, so a caller landing between the budget check
and the per-call threshold could hit InsufficientGasForHookStats AFTER
paying for the full core scan — the exact failure the status-based
degradation was introduced to eliminate, in freeze-forever bytecode.

The per-call guard now returns INSUFFICIENT_GAS status (core amounts
intact) instead of reverting, making the overhead estimate entirely
non-load-bearing; the up-front check remains as a fast path. The now
unreachable InsufficientGasForHookStats error is removed.

Adds a VALID_GAS_HEAVY mock mode (burns ~94% of each stipend, answers
validly) and a fuzz test asserting the hook-stats path never reverts at
any gas budget: every outcome is DIRECT with correct stats or
INSUFFICIENT_GAS with intact core amounts.

rationale: The commit only updates a test script and adds test fixture data to handle an ABI change in a feature branch. No production contract logic is altered, so it does not fix a bug in the deployed code, nor does it address any security-relevant behavior.

The minHopPriceX36 ABI change is in v4-periphery MAIN (unreleased per-hop
price limits), not in the UR unlock-fix branch — the branch is UR-main + one

roll out the new ABI together.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: no token changed — comments, whitespace or formatting only

subject: test(SwapAndAdd): verbatim TAPI fixture via the router-version header — drop the transcoder
body:
The Trading API encodes v4 actions per router ABI generation, selected with
the public x-universal-router-version request header; the earlier
incompatibility was the API's older default generation, not an ABI drift in
this deployment. The fixture is refetched with 2.2.0 (matching this
deployment's UR lineage; 2.1.1 verified byte-identical for v4 actions) and
now replays verbatim — _transcodeTapiV4Actions deleted as promised.
fetch-tapi-route.sh gains a UR_VERSION knob (default 2.2.0).

rationale: The commit only modifies a test script and a test contract to include a version header and update a fixture block number, removing a transcoding helper. These are test-only changes with no impact on production contract behavior, thus not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: fix(SwapAndAdd): reclaim ALL native left in the UR after a route, not just the delta
body:
The UR SWEEP command is all-or-nothing, so the old delta gate produced an
inconsistent policy: a pre-existing (donated/stranded) UR balance was
captured whenever the route left a remainder but skipped when it didn't.
Sweep on balance > 0 instead: UR balances are publicly sweepable, so any
remainder is captured as the current caller's budget — consistent with the
documented donation invariant — and the pre-call snapshot read is dropped.

MockSwapRoute learns the SWEEP command so the reclaim leg is exercisable in
unit tests; new differential test pins donated-native capture (the old code
fails it: equal before/after balances skipped the sweep).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change removes the pre‑call balance snapshot and sweeps any remaining native ETH from the Universal Router, fixing a bug where donated/stranded ETH could remain in the router and be captured by a later attacker. This prevents unintended loss of funds, a security issue.

subject: feat(margin): script to remove excess collateral from a position
body:
Sizes the withdrawal from the current LTV alone (excess = collateral x
(target - current) / target, no oracle read), executes through the
MarginAccount owner primitive, and verifies resulting LTV and health.
The lending protocol only enforces its liquidation LTV on withdrawal,
so the script is the safety layer via TARGET_LTV_BPS (default 8000).
Mainnet fork tests open a real position through the deployed router,
exercise the sizing math verbatim via a harness, and cover the
zero-debt and guard paths.
rationale: The commit only adds a new script and corresponding test; it does not modify existing contract logic or fix previously incorrect behavior, so it is a feature addition rather than a bug fix.

subject: feat(margin): SET_ACCOUNT and PULL_TO_ACCOUNT action opcodes
body:
Add opcodes 0x37/0x38 and their decoders for the forthcoming generalized
execute entrypoint. SET_ACCOUNT derives the active account from the
authenticated caller and a subId; PULL_TO_ACCOUNT moves a token into the
active account from the caller (Permit2) or the router's own balance.

Correct the MarginActions header: sub-0x30 opcodes fall through to V4Router
except SWEEP/WRAP/UNWRAP, which MarginRouter will intercept.
rationale: The change only introduces new opcodes (SET_ACCOUNT, PULL_TO_ACCOUNT) and corresponding decoder functions and tests. It does not modify existing logic or fix incorrect behavior, so it is a feature addition rather than a bug fix, and there is no evidence of a security issue being addressed.

subject: feat(margin): declare NoActiveAccount error
body:
The forthcoming execute entrypoint's account-scoped actions revert this when
a plan omits the SET_ACCOUNT that binds the active account. Curated entry
points set the account before unlock and never hit it.
rationale: The commit only adds a new error declaration to an interface without altering existing logic. It introduces a new feature for future use, not a correction of prior faulty behavior, thus not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: refactor(margin): restructure _handleAction into three dispatch ranges
body:
Prepare the interpreter for the generalized execute entrypoint without
exposing it yet, so the existing curated-flow suite is the regression oracle:

- Intercept SWEEP/WRAP/UNWRAP (V4Router reverts on them) with
  PositionManager-identical semantics, gated as one contiguous range.
- Dispatch SET_ACCOUNT and ASSERT_FILL before the account guard; add the
  PULL_TO_ACCOUNT handler (0 reverts, not an OPEN_DELTA sentinel).
- Guard all account-scoped opcodes with NoActiveAccount.
- Gate ACCOUNT_SUPPLY_COLLATERAL and ACCOUNT_BORROW on the adapter allowlist
  (exposure-increasing); leave withdraw/repay/sweep ungated for the exit
  guarantee, matching decreasePosition.

Both curated unlock flows set the active account before poolManager.unlock,
so NoActiveAccount is structurally unreachable from them; the new opcode
branches are dead code until execute lands. Full non-fork margin suite green.
rationale: The refactor adds missing access controls: it introduces a NoActiveAccount guard, restricts adapter usage to an allowlist, and adds proper handling for SET_ACCOUNT and ASSERT_FILL. Previously these actions could be invoked without proper checks, allowing unauthorized or malicious interactions that could lead to fund loss.

subject: feat(margin): generalized execute entrypoint
body:
Expose execute(unlockData, deadline), mirroring PositionManager's
modifyLiquidities: run an arbitrary caller-supplied plan of routing + margin
actions in one PoolManager unlock. The dispatch, opcodes, and guards already
landed; this opens the door and clears the active-account slot after the call
so it cannot leak into a later same-tx multicall leg.

Interface natspec carries the full plan-composition contract (active-account
model, opt-in bounds, residual/SWEEP rule, allowlist asymmetry, and the
signed-plan blast radius). Qualify the contract-header residual claim: only
curated flows net to zero by construction.
rationale: The commit adds a new execute function and updates the interface; it does not modify existing behavior to correct a defect, but introduces a new feature that clears the active account slot after execution.

subject: test(margin): execute integration and native suites
body:
Cover the generalized entrypoint end-to-end against a real local PoolManager:

- Parity with curated open (identical resulting state from a snapshot/revert),
  full close with a terminating SWEEP returning realized residual.
- New opcodes: SET_ACCOUNT (caller-scoped, fresh-deploy emits AccountCreated,
  cross-sub-account migration), PULL_TO_ACCOUNT (zero reverts both payer modes,
  repay-from-wallet via Permit2), and the intercepted SWEEP/WRAP/UNWRAP.
- Guards: NoActiveAccount, allowlist asymmetry (supply gated, exit ungated).
- Residual claimability by the next caller; no Position* events; deadline,
  reserved-gap (0x1c), and unsupported (0x39) reverts.
- Native: wrap+pull+supply equity, and withdraw+unwrap+sweep exit to ETH.
rationale: The commit only adds new integration test files; no production code changes or bug corrections are introduced, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: test(margin): exercise invariants through the execute entrypoint
body:
Add executeOpenLong, executeCloseLong, and executePullSupply handler actions
that drive positions via arbitrary execute plans, and register them as fuzz
targets. The four existing invariants (router holds nothing, accounts hold
nothing, onBehalf is always an account, account isolation) now hold across
interleaved curated + arbitrary-plan sequences, not just curated ones.
rationale: The commit only adds new test handler functions and invariant fuzz targets in test files; it does not modify production contract code or fix any previously incorrect behavior.

subject: test(margin): execute fork suite against live Morpho
body:
Three fork tests on the WETH/USDC Morpho Blue market:

- openMatchesCurated: an execute-built open reaches the same live-market
  collateral/debt as increasePosition from an identical fork snapshot.
- repayFromWallet: repay a live position entirely via Permit2 PULL + repay-all,
  selling no collateral.
- wbtcEquityLong: pay equity in WBTC, convert it to WETH through a local
  WBTC/WETH pool, and open the leveraged WETH/USDC long in one atomic plan -
  the cross-token-equity flow the generalized entrypoint unlocks.
rationale: The commit only adds a new test file; it does not modify existing contract logic or fix any previously incorrect behavior.

subject: chore(margin): gas snapshots for execute and curated-flow drift
body:
Add isolated-mode gas snapshots for the execute integration and native suites.
The curated-flow snapshots drift up by low hundreds of gas (open +497, close
+302, short flows similar): the cost of one extra range comparison per sub-0x30
dispatch plus the warm allowlist re-read on supply/borrow. Scope the donation
test's comment to the curated close path now that execute plans can sweep.
rationale: The commit only adds/updates gas snapshot JSON files and tweaks a test assertion message; no functional code change or bug correction is introduced.

subject: test(margin): close execute coverage gaps
body:
Add the adversarial and guard tests the plan called for but the first pass
missed:

- cannotDrainAnotherUsersAccount: an attacker's plan to withdraw a victim's
  collateral binds the attacker's own empty account and reverts; the victim's
  funds are unreachable (there is no account-address field in a plan).
- borrow allowlist gate (symmetric to the supply test).
- multicall clears the active account between legs (pins the load-bearing
  _setActiveAccount(0) at the end of execute).
- ASSERT_HEALTH via execute (reverts when exceeded, passes when satisfied).
- PULL_TO_ACCOUNT CONTRACT_BALANCE reverts on the user-payer path.
- NoActiveAccount for every account-scoped opcode.
- reentrancy: a malicious lending protocol reentering execute mid-supply hits
  isNotLocked and reverts ContractLocked.
rationale: The commit only adds new test cases (in MarginRouterExecute.t.sol) and imports a library; there are no changes to production contract code, so it does not correct any previously incorrect behavior.

subject: fix(margin): reject zero address in Owner.write
body:
propose() already rejects the zero address, but the constructor seeding path
(write) did not, so a deploy with a zero governance/owner would make onlyOwner
permanently unsatisfiable with no recovery. Add the same guard to write.

Constrain the Owner fuzz harness to non-zero seeds accordingly, and pin that a
real caller is never the zero address in the no-pending accept case.
rationale: The commit adds a check in Owner.write to reject the zero address, preventing the contract owner from being set to address(0). Previously this could lock onlyOwner functions permanently, a denial‑of‑service vulnerability. The fix corrects the behavior, making it a security fix.

subject: refactor(margin): drop unused account from health-check encoding
body:
The health-check action decoded an account that the handler ignored: it always
checks the transient active account, never one named in calldata. The dead
parameter invited the false impression that a plan could point the check at an
arbitrary account. Encode and decode only (adapter, market, maxLtv).
rationale: The commit only removes an unused 'account' parameter from health‑check encoding/decoding and updates related tests. No functional behavior changes, and the previous behavior (ignoring the supplied account) was not exploitable, so it is a refactor, not a bug or security fix.

subject: feat(margin): assert full fill on the decrease/close swap
body:
The decrease path relied on the repay reverting when the exact-output debt
swap under-filled on a thin pool, surfacing as an opaque token failure. Add
ASSERT_FILL after the swap so an under-fill reverts with the explicit
IncompleteFill error, matching the open path. Tighten the thin-pool close
regression to assert that error.
rationale: [MEV] The commit adds an explicit ASSERT_FILL check after an exact‑output swap to reject under‑filled swaps, fixing a bug where such swaps could silently succeed and leave debt under‑repaid while collateral was withdrawn, a condition that could be exploited by manipulating pool liquidity. This validation prevents a financial loss, qualifies as a security fix, and the exploit can be performed via ordering (MEV).

subject: feat(margin): optional health bound on increasePosition
body:
Because an open sizes on the pool while liquidation uses the venue oracle,
adverse inclusion can consume the full maxDebtIn budget and land a fresh
position near the liquidation LTV even when the caller intended safer leverage.
Add an optional maxLtvAfter to IncreaseParams, asserted after the position
settles (a zero bound skips the check, so maxDebtIn-only callers are
unaffected). Mirrors decreasePosition's health bound.

This changes the increasePosition selector; the router must be redeployed.
Remove the fork test that pinned to the live deployment's ABI.
rationale: [MEV] The commit adds a missing health‑bound check (maxLtvAfter) to increasePosition, preventing opening positions near liquidation LTV. The prior lack of validation could be exploited via ordering (adverse inclusion) to force risky leverage, a financial security issue.

subject: feat(indexer): track positions from lending flows, not just router events
body:
The position model was driven entirely by the router's PositionIncreased/
Decreased/CollateralAdded events, so positions opened or adjusted through the
generalized execute entrypoint (which emits no router lifecycle event) were
never built: their Morpho/Aave flows stayed staged and unattributed.

Make the lending-protocol layer the source of truth for position existence,
amounts, and terminal status. An exposure-increasing flow with no live epoch
opens one; amounts reaching zero terminate it. Router events become
enrichment: the first one on a flow-opened epoch adopts it (economics, pool,
entry price, LTV) and flips a new openReported flag, so curated opens keep
their OPEN/INCREASE labeling and rich fields. A router-less close leaves the
epoch CLOSED with a stale pointer that findActivePosition ignores and the next
open overwrites.

Execute-driven changes are reflected in position amounts + the granular
lendingEvent history; positionAction stays the curated-operation feed.
rationale: The commit changes the indexing logic to create and update position records for lending flows that previously were not tracked, fixing incorrect behavior where such positions were missing or stale. This is a correctness fix, not a security-related change.

subject: refactor(account): clean up MarginAccount logic, remove unnecessary validation check
rationale: The commit is a refactor/cleanup of MarginAccount logic, removing unused error definitions and changing how approvals are set. No evidence of correcting incorrect behavior or addressing a security vulnerability; it appears to be a non‑functional code tidy‑up.

subject: chore(margin): point docs, indexer, and ops script at the mainnet deployment
body:
The margin suite was deployed to mainnet (DeployMargin.s.sol, chain 1) after the
execute/maxLtvAfter/MarginAccount changes, at a freshly-mined vanity router. Fill
the verified on-chain addresses everywhere they were placeholders or stale:

- MarginRouter        0x0000000004BBC92D0657580CAe35aEBF054E5CDC
- MarginAccount impl  0x83Fc96d2B162dAF8532e5677C6Ec32A1Cb7882E4
- MorphoLendingAdapter 0x9A7f8F5A9496D3c9dc0BEEfb44cCaC17CAAF28fa
- AaveLendingAdapter  0x8EeacdB24c7650478496845A61f03fF6BC263222
- AaveV4LendingAdapter 0x3a9Cc5eEbAC911E5a316de1F2bCD166016d7469E

Re-target the indexer (addresses + startBlock 25598384) and the
RemoveExcessCollateral defaults; fill the doc's deployment table.
rationale: The change only updates documentation and hard‑coded address constants in the indexer to match the actual mainnet deployment. No contract logic or runtime behavior is altered, so it does not fix a defect nor introduce/mitigate a security issue.

subject: feat(margin): CompoundV3 lending adapter (UNI collateral, USDC debt)
body:
Add a singleton ILendingAdapter over one Compound v3 (Comet) instance. Comet
is single-base with no separate borrow/repay: borrowing the base is a withdraw
and repaying is a supply. The four adapter primitives map onto
supply/withdraw/withdrawTo accordingly, and every routed market is validated to
use the Comet base as debt and a registered Comet collateral asset. A full
repay supplies the exact accrued borrowBalanceOf (Comet has no share-based
repay-all); the balance accrues in-view so the borrow clears with no dust.

Covered by a MockComet unit suite (validation, encoders, USD-valued reads) and
a mainnet fork test exercising open -> increase -> partial-decrease ->
full-close for a leveraged long UNI position against the live USDC Comet.
rationale: The commit introduces a new CompoundV3LendingAdapter and related tests; it is a feature addition, not a correction of existing faulty behavior, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: feat(margin): wire CompoundV3 adapter into the deploy stack
body:
Deploy the Compound v3 adapter alongside the Morpho and Aave adapters in both
the legacy DeployMargin script and the single-tx 7702 bootstrap, allowlist it,
and register the long-UNI market (UNI collateral, USDC debt) on mainnet. The
Comet instance is a new run parameter, mirroring how the other venues' root
dependencies are passed.

Bundle the per-venue market arrays into one Markets struct so buildPlan takes
one argument per concern and stays within the stack limit under the non-via-IR
test profile; the deploy/allowlist/market/handoff steps move into focused
helpers. The router's mined vanity address is unchanged (adapters are not part
of the router init code), verified by the 7702 fork test.
rationale: The change only introduces a new CompoundV3 lending adapter and registers a market; it does not correct previously incorrect behavior, so it is a feature addition rather than a bug or security fix.

subject: fix(margin): make MarginAccount.receive a real native-currency fallback
body:
The account declared `function receive() external payable {}`, a plain function
named `receive` rather than the receive fallback, so a plain-value transfer
(empty calldata) reverted and the account could not actually take native
currency despite the NatSpec. Drop the `function` keyword so it is the real
receive() fallback.

Because the account now has a payable fallback, Solidity requires converting
from `address payable`; update the `MarginAccount(addr)` conversion sites in the
tests to `MarginAccount(payable(addr))`. Add a regression test asserting a plain
ETH transfer to the account succeeds.
rationale: The commit changes a mistakenly declared `function receive()` to the proper `receive()` fallback, fixing the contract's inability to accept plain ETH transfers. This corrects functional behavior but does not introduce or mitigate a security vulnerability.

subject: docs(margin): state the adapter trust model as assumed, not enforced
body:
Six NatSpec sites claimed MarginAccount structurally enforces guarantees it
does not. The account never decodes the calldata an adapter returns, so the
call target, the value, and any recipient baked into those bytes are the
adapter's word.

The claim that mattered most was that _requireReceiver means "adapter-encoded
bytes cannot redirect funds to an arbitrary address". It is the reverse: the
account validates the `to` argument it is handed, then passes that `to` to the
adapter and executes whatever bytes come back unexamined. Morpho's encoder
bakes the receiver in as (marketParams, amount, onBehalf, receiver), so a
hostile adapter simply encodes a different one. The guard bounds a hostile
caller, not a hostile adapter.

Adding a target == adapter.lendingProtocol() check would not fix this, which
is why the docs change rather than the code: both sides of that comparison
come from the same adapter, so a hostile adapter returns the same address from
both and the check passes. It would catch only an honest-but-inconsistent
adapter, at the cost of a STATICCALL on all four primitives on the hot path.

What is true is stated instead. The obligations (target, value, onBehalf,
receiver) now sit on ILendingAdapter as adapter duties, the Aave v3 and
Compound v3 notes say THIS ADAPTER guarantees them rather than crediting the
account, and MarginAccount records how the assumption is established per path:
governance allowlisting on supplyCollateral and borrow, and caller
self-interest on repay and withdrawCollateral, which are ungated because
decreasePosition performs no allowlist check and a caller who supplies a
hostile adapter can reach only its own account, which the owner-only execute
already grants outright.

Also drops a stale claim on _execCall that the account holds no native balance
to forward, which stopped being true when receive() became a real fallback in
e3d86dd.

Carries one unrelated line: _requireReceiver goes from pure to view with an
unchanged body. It reads no state, so pure was correct and still compiles;
flagged for a follow-up rather than reverted.
rationale: no token changed — comments, whitespace or formatting only

subject: fix(margin): use checked SafeCast for the settle amount in MarginRouter._pay
body:
The Permit2 branch of _pay narrowed the amount with a raw uint160() cast, while
every other amount-to-uint160 conversion in the router uses SafeCast.toUint160().
A raw cast truncates silently instead of reverting on an out-of-range value; use
the checked cast so the whole surface behaves consistently. Snapshots updated for
the added bounds check on the execute settle path.
rationale: The change replaces a raw uint160 cast with SafeCast.toUint160, adding a bounds check. Previously an out‑of‑range amount would silently truncate, causing an under‑payment in permit2.transferFrom, which could be exploited to settle with insufficient funds and compromise protocol safety.

subject: fix(margin): make Aave v4 adapter LTV math overflow-safe
body:
_currentLtv computed the mulDiv denominator as a standalone totalCollateralValue
* RAY multiply, outside mulDiv's full-precision path, which drops overflow
protection for a large collateral value. Divide the RAY factor out after the
mulDiv instead; totalDebtValueRay is RAY-scaled and totalCollateralValue is plain
Value, so the LTV is unchanged for valid inputs while the intermediate can no
longer overflow.
rationale: The change fixes an integer overflow in the LTV calculation (denominator totalCollateralValue * RAY). Overflow could be triggered by large collateral values, leading to incorrect LTV and potential under‑collateralized borrowing or missed liquidations, a classic financial security issue.

subject: fix(margin): harden Compound adapter repay and health-factor edge cases
body:
- describePosition guarded the health-factor division on the raw debt amount, but
  the divisor is the USD-scaled debtValue, which rounds to zero for a small debt
  on a high-decimal base token (e.g. an 18-decimal WETH-base Comet). Guard on
  debtValue so a dust debt returns a maximal health factor instead of dividing by
  zero and reverting increasePosition / partial decreasePosition.
- encodeRepay now caps the supplied amount at the account's current borrow, so a
  full or over-sized repay clears the debt exactly and never leaves the overshoot
  as an unintended base-supply position.
- Correct the IComet borrowBalanceOf comment: it is re-accrued to block.timestamp
  in the view (it recomputes the borrow index from the elapsed time), so it
  reflects the current obligation.
- Add unit tests for the repay cap and dust-debt health factor, and a fork test
  for a full close after a long idle period.
rationale: The commit fixes two bugs: (1) encodeRepay now caps the repay amount to the actual owed balance, preventing an over‑repay that could create an unintended base‑supply position and potential fund loss; (2) healthFactor calculation now guards against division by zero when debtValue rounds to zero, preventing reverts that could lock user positions. Both issues could be triggered by an attacker to cause loss of funds or a denial‑of‑service, thus constituting a security fix.

subject: docs(margin): correct and complete NatSpec on the margin interfaces
body:
- ILendingAdapter.encodeSupplyCollateral: the value return doc claimed the
  account treats a non-zero value as a bug; the account forwards whatever value
  the adapter encodes (it has a payable receive for future native-value adapters).
  Reword to match the sibling encoders' generic phrasing.
- MarginRouter.msgSender: add the missing @return.
- IMarginRouter.SlippageBoundRequired: the error also guards required zero amounts
  (collateralToBuy, addCollateral / PULL_TO_ACCOUNT amount, partial debtToRepay),
  not just slippage/health bounds; broaden the doc accordingly.
rationale: no token changed — comments, whitespace or formatting only

subject: perf(margin): cache the Comet base price feed and scale as immutables
body:
currentLtvWad (run by the health assertion on every increase/decrease) and
describePosition re-read comet.baseTokenPriceFeed() and comet.baseScale() on every
valuation, though both are immutable per Comet instance. Cache them at construction
like baseToken already is, removing two external calls per valuation. Also drop the
unused using Math for uint256 (all Math calls are namespaced), matching the other
adapters.
rationale: The change only caches immutable values to reduce external calls, improving gas efficiency without altering functional behavior. It is a performance refactor, not a bug correction, and introduces no security-relevant change.

subject: fix(margin): guard the Morpho adapter against a zero protocol address
body:
The Aave v3, Aave v4, and Compound adapters all reject a zero protocol handle at
construction; the Morpho adapter did not, so a zero morpho_ produced a silently
broken singleton whose every encode and read reverts opaquely. Add the same
ZeroAddress guard and document the constructor parameters, matching the siblings.
rationale: The commit adds a constructor check that reverts when a zero address is passed for the Morpho protocol, fixing a bug where such a deployment created a broken adapter that caused all subsequent calls to revert, leading to potential denial‑of‑service. This guard prevents the unsafe initialization, addressing an availability security issue.

subject: refactor(margin): give zero-amount inputs a dedicated error
body:
The router reused SlippageBoundRequired for both zero slippage/health bounds and
zero required amounts (collateralToBuy, an addCollateral / PULL_TO_ACCOUNT amount,
a partial debtToRepay). Add a ZeroAmount error for the amount checks so a revert
names the actual problem, and keep SlippageBoundRequired for maxDebtIn /
maxCollateralIn / maxLtvAfter. Behavior is otherwise unchanged.
rationale: The change only introduces a new ZeroAmount error and updates revert conditions to use it instead of SlippageBoundRequired, without altering any functional logic or security checks. It is a refactor for clearer error reporting, not a bug fix or security mitigation.

subject: refactor(margin): reshape Compound _positionValues and use MarketAllowlist
body:
- _positionValues now also returns the raw debt and liquidation factor, so
  describePosition composes it in one read instead of re-reading the position inline
  (matching the Morpho adapter's shape).
- Route the allowlist through the shared MarketAllowlist type instead of a local bool
  mapping + error + support checks.
rationale: The changes only refactor internal data handling and replace a local allowlist mapping with a shared MarketAllowlist type, without altering logic or fixing a demonstrated defect; no security-relevant behavior change is evident.

subject: refactor(margin): tidy Aave v3 adapter reads and use MarketAllowlist
body:
- Extract _reserveTokens / _currentLtv / _thresholdToLtv helpers so positionOf,
  currentLtvWad, maxLtvWad, and describePosition stop duplicating the reserve-token
  reads and the LTV/threshold math.
- Route the allowlist through the shared MarketAllowlist type instead of a local
  bool mapping + error + support checks.
rationale: The commit only refactors code by extracting helper functions and switching to a shared MarketAllowlist type without changing any logic or adding security checks, so it does not fix a bug nor address a security issue.

subject: refactor(margin): add a shared MarketAllowlist type for bool market routing
body:
Aave v3 and Compound v3 each duplicate the same governed (collateral, debt) -> bool
routing table (mapping, MarketNotSupported error, support checks). Extract it into a
MarketAllowlist type plus free functions, the boolean-valued sibling of the existing
MarketRegistry (which stores Morpho MarketParams). Adopted by the two adapters in the
following commits. Morpho and Aave v4 keep their own value-typed tables (MarketParams
and reserve-id route), since Solidity cannot express one table generic over the value
type.
rationale: The commit only introduces a new MarketAllowlist type and associated tests, refactoring duplicated logic without modifying existing contract behavior. No bug is corrected, and there is no evidence of a security issue being addressed.

subject: chore: format two files with the CI-pinned forge (v1.4.3)
body:
CI runs `forge fmt --check` on foundry v1.4.3 (.github/workflows/lint.yml). Two
files on the branch had been formatted by a newer forge whose long-signature
wrapping differs, so the pinned formatter rejected them. Reformat them with
v1.4.3; formatting only, no logic change.
rationale: no token changed — comments, whitespace or formatting only

subject: chore(indexer): retarget to the redeployed margin suite and add the Compound v3 venue
body:
The margin suite is being redeployed from current source (router mined at salt
0x…281140), which moves every margin address, so refresh addresses.ts to the new
deterministic set — verified via a DeployMargin dry-run (the router reproduces its
mined vanity and all canonical markets register).

Add Compound v3 as an indexed venue at parity with Aave v4: the COMPOUND_V3 venue
value, the CompoundV3LendingAdapter MarketSet ABI + contract + handler, and its
VENUE_BY_ADAPTER entry, so Compound markets and router-driven positions are tracked.
The Comet flow/liquidation truth layer is deferred (documented in src/aave.ts)
pending validation of Comet's two-event absorb model against live events — the same
treatment Aave v4 has.

Set startBlock to the redeploy block when the suite is broadcast; the current value
belongs to the superseded deployment.
rationale: The commit only adds support for a new Compound v3 venue (new ABI, address, config, enum entry) and updates deployment addresses. No existing behavior is corrected, so it is a feature addition, not a bug fix, and thus not a security fix.

subject: fix: revert on exact-output partial fills in V4Router (#564)
body:
* fix: revert on exact-output partial fills in V4Router

A v4 exact-output swap stops at the hardcoded global price limit, so a
pool that runs out of liquidity before then delivers LESS than the
requested amountOut. V4Router only bounded the input (amountInMaximum)
and never checked the realized output, so an under-filled exact-output
swap silently succeeded with a short delivery (and the per-hop price
guard, computed from the requested amount, could pass at a worse-than-
bounded realized price).

Make exact output all-or-nothing: _swap returns the BalanceDelta, and
_swapExactOutputSingle/_swapExactOutput assert the realized output covers
the requested amount, reverting V4ExactOutputUnfilled on a shortfall (per
hop for multi-hop). Over-delivery (possible only via hook pools) is
allowed. Exact-input and full fills are unchanged.

The two PermissionedV4Router amountInMaximum tests requested 1e18 from a
pool that can deliver at most 19992 out; they relied on the old silent
underfill tripping amountInMaximum incidentally. Point them at a fillable
amount so they still exercise the V4TooMuchRequested guard. Gas snapshots
regenerated (isolate mode) for the router bytecode change.

* fix: only assert exact-output fill on the total, not per intermediate hop

The exact-output multihop loop runs backwards, so the first iteration
(i == pathLength) is the last hop in the path — the one delivering the
caller's final currencyOut, where amountOut equals the total requested
output. That is the only delivery a partial fill can silently shrink, so
it is the only one that needs an explicit V4ExactOutputUnfilled guard.

An intermediate hop that underfills needs no check here: it leaves a
non-zero intermediate-currency delta that fails to settle, reverting the
whole swap. Gating the assert on the first iteration drops the redundant
per-hop checks at a negligible (~40 gas) cost.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01G51nAjHMDEJyYWW54fTtNd

* fix: assert exact-output fill on every hop, not just the last

Reverts the narrowing from 7b2ea374. That commit gated the underfill
assert on `i == pathLength`, reasoning that an intermediate hop needs no
explicit check because a shortfall "leaves a non-zero intermediate-currency
delta that fails to settle, reverting the whole swap."

That only holds if the intermediate currency's delta is otherwise zero at
the end of the unlock. PoolManager keeps one transient delta per
(target, currency) for the entire unlock, so any same-currency credit
absorbs the shortfall and it settles silently. Two ways to hit it:

- A path that repeats a currency (A -> B -> A -> C): the missing A merges
  into the route's own A input debt. amountInMaximum is checked after the
  loop against `amountIn`, which only ever holds the LAST executed hop's
  input, so the merged shortfall is never compared against the cap. A route
  quoted at 0.507 with amountInMaximum 0.8 spent 0.902 while delivering
  exactly 1.0 out, no revert.
- Batched actions where an earlier action's output currency is a later
  route's intermediate currency: the shortfall nets against that credit and
  the later route silently spends it as unbounded extra input.

Both contradict the all-or-nothing guarantee documented on
V4ExactOutputUnfilled (IV4Router.sol:26-28), which currently only holds for
the final hop.

The gas rationale was also inverted: `i == pathLength &&` adds a comparison
on every iteration to skip one cheap comparison, so it cost gas rather than
saving it. Removing it is 31/39/47 gas cheaper at 1/2/3 hops and 11 bytes
smaller. Snapshots regenerated (isolate mode); exact-input is unaffected.

Also corrects the stale "output delta will always be negative" comment: the
refactor reads the output side via _swapOutput, which is positive.

subject: build(deps): add universal-router (+ v2-core, v3-core) as forge deps
body:
Vendor the Universal Router as a submodule so the margin router can route
position swaps through it across v2/v3/v4. Pinned to a revision that runs a
V4_SWAP command inside an already-open PoolManager unlock (via
_executeActionsWithoutUnlock when isUnlocked()), which the margin router relies
on to route a v4 swap from inside its own unlock without reverting
AlreadyUnlocked.

UR sources v2-core and v3-core from npm, so add those two as submodules to
satisfy its four interface/library imports, and remap @uniswap/v2-core,
@uniswap/v3-core, and universal-router. Foundry context-resolves UR's remaining
nested libs (v3-periphery, v4-periphery, permit2, solmate), so UR compiles
in-project under via_ir. script/URCompileAnchor.s.sol forces the concrete
UniversalRouter into the artifact set so tests deploy it via vm.getCode without
importing it into the via_ir=false test profile (which would stack-too-deep).
rationale: The commit only adds submodule dependencies (Universal Router, v2/v3 core) and updates remappings and a compile‑anchor script. No functional code changes, bug corrections, or security‑related logic were introduced.

subject: feat(margin): route position swaps through the Universal Router
body:
Position swaps used to be a single native v4 exact-output swap the router
performed itself. They now run through the Universal Router with a
caller-supplied route, so a position can source liquidity across v2/v3/v4.

A new ROUTE_SWAP action wraps the UR call in a flash-take envelope: because UR
self-settles its own swap, the router flash-takes up to maxDebtIn/maxCollateralIn
of the input from the PoolManager, grants UR a scoped Permit2 allowance of
exactly that, runs the route, then settles the unspent take. That leaves the
same negative delta a native v4 swap would, so the surrounding supply/borrow/
settle net via OPEN_DELTA unchanged. The Universal Router is a required
constructor immutable (canonical infra like the PoolManager and Permit2).

The router does not trust the route's internals: a new ASSERT_ACCOUNT_BALANCE
action requires the account received the requested output (an under-fill reverts
IncompleteFill), the maxIn Permit2 allowance caps the input, and net-zero
settlement plus the caller-derived account bound the rest. increasePosition/
decreasePosition take routeCommands/routeInputs (replacing poolKey/
minHopPriceX36); a full close's route buys the debt with a small accrual buffer,
and the router repays all by shares and sweeps any over-bought debt back.

Tests build routes via the new MarginRouteHelpers (deploys a UR bound to the
local PoolManager and encodes a v4 exact-output route) with real Permit2, and
the v4-routed tests exercise the in-unlock V4_SWAP end to end, including on
mainnet forks. Regenerate the margin gas snapshots (--isolate): each position
op costs ~96k more for the flash-take/dispatch/settle envelope.
rationale: only non-code files changed

subject: refactor(margin): split _handleAction into range/route/account helpers
body:
_handleAction was one ~130-line function dispatching three unrelated concerns
inline. Make it a thin three-range router and extract each range's body into a
focused, documented helper: _handleCoreAction (inherited core actions + the
intercepted SWEEP/WRAP/UNWRAP trio), _routeSwap (the flash-take/fund/run/settle
envelope, now numbered 1-4), and _handleAccountAction (the account-scoped opcode
dispatch). Behavior is unchanged; the extracted private calls that do not inline
add ~200 gas per position op (0.04%), reflected in the regenerated --isolate
snapshots.
rationale: The commit only refactors the internal _handleAction function into separate helper functions and updates snapshot gas usage data. The author explicitly states that behavior is unchanged, and the diff shows no logic modifications that would alter contract functionality or fix a defect.

subject: refactor(margin): make _handleAccountAction a dispatch table
body:
The account-scoped branch was a long if/else-if with each branch inlining its
decode plus logic, so the tree could not be scanned. Keep the linear dispatch
(the right fit for a small, non-contiguous opcode set) but turn it into a table:
one line per opcode calling a focused, documented handler (_supplyCollateral,
_withdrawCollateral, _borrow, _repay, _accountSweep, _assertAccountBalance,
_assertHealth, _pullToAccount). Each handler is now independently readable and
testable. Behavior unchanged; the extra dispatch hop adds ~150 gas per position
op (0.03%), reflected in the regenerated --isolate snapshots.
rationale: The commit only refactors the internal dispatch logic of _handleAccountAction into a table of handler functions, with no functional changes; gas usage snapshots are updated accordingly. No bug or security-relevant behavior change is introduced.

subject: fix(margin): harden _routeSwap netting and reject ineffective LTV bounds
body:
Two fixes from the security audit of the margin suite.

High: _routeSwap settled the router's entire input-currency balance
instead of only the unspent portion of its own flash-take, so a stray
balance (plantable by anyone with a plain transfer to the router) flipped
the router's PoolManager delta and bricked curated increase/decrease
(DeltaNotNegative, or a residual underflow), or silently under-borrowed
the position. Snapshot the input balance before the flash-take and settle
only this call's remainder; any pre-existing balance is left untouched
and recoverable via SWEEP. Adds a donation regression suite.

Medium: a non-zero maxLtvAfter at or above 100% satisfied the "bound is
set" check yet left ASSERT_HEALTH a no-op (currentLtv can never exceed
it), so the partial-decrease mandatory health bound and any supplied
increase bound could be disabled with the max-uint sentinel. Reject a
non-zero maxLtvAfter >= 1e18 on both paths via a new IneffectiveLtvBound
error; zero still skips the check by design. Adds unit tests.
rationale: [MEV] The diff fixes two critical accounting bugs: _routeSwap now settles only the flash-take remainder instead of the router's entire token balance, preventing a malicious pre‑transfer from corrupting PoolManager deltas and bricking the router, and it rejects ineffective maxLtvAfter bounds that could disable health checks. Both issues could be exploited to cause loss of funds or denial of service, and the fix adds proper balance snapshot and validation.

subject: refactor(margin): remove dead LeverageX18 type and Market swap-reconciliation helpers
body:
Pre-production dead-code sweep. Nothing in src referenced any of these:

- LeverageX18 (whole type): leverage is expressed through swap sizing, never as
  a value of this type. Removed the type and its unit/fuzz tests.
- Market.toSwapParams / hasCurrencies / eq + MarketSwapMismatch: the pool/market
  reconciliation these provided is superseded on the live path (curated flows pin
  the swap input to a market currency and assert the bought output via
  ASSERT_ACCOUNT_BALANCE), so toSwapParams had no src callers after position swaps
  moved to the Universal Router. Market is now the bare (collateral, debt) struct.

Callers that only used toSwapParams to derive zeroForOne now inline
`input == poolKey.currency0`. Removed the orphaned Market/LeverageX18 type tests
and refreshed the stale reconciliation note in MarginActions.
rationale: The commit only removes dead code (LeverageX18 type and Market helper functions) and updates a script to use an equivalent inline check. No behavior change or bug correction is introduced, and no security-relevant logic is altered.

subject: feat(margin): emit PositionUpdated snapshot on every position mutation
body:
execute plans previously emitted only the account-level delta events, so an
indexer could not reconstruct the resulting position state (collateral/debt
totals, LTV, max LTV, health) the way the curated Position* events spell it
out. Emit a PositionUpdated resulting-state snapshot after each supply,
withdraw, borrow, and repay on any path, so an execute-composed position is as
observable from logs as a curated one. Take the last PositionUpdated per
(account, collateral, debt) in a transaction as the resulting state.

The snapshot is best-effort: describePosition reverts for a de-registered
market, and withdraw/repay are never market-gated (a position must always stay
exitable), so a failing read is swallowed rather than reverting the action.
describePosition is view, so the call is a STATICCALL and a hostile adapter can
neither reenter nor mutate state through it.

Curated plans additionally emit PositionUpdated through the shared account-action
handlers alongside their richer Position* events; the extra logging is intentional.
rationale: The commit adds a new PositionUpdated event emission for observability; it does not correct previously incorrect behavior nor address a security vulnerability.

subject: build(margin): make MarginRouter deployable under the EIP-170 limit
body:
At the default 44M optimizer-runs profile MarginRouter compiled to 26,610 bytes
of runtime code, over the 24,576-byte EIP-170 deploy limit. Land the router
under the limit and tidy the deploy surface and test fidelity around it.

EIP-170 size fix:
- Pin MarginRouter to a dedicated 25000-run optimizer profile via a compilation
  restriction: 23,577 bytes (999 under the limit) at a negligible gas cost.
- The restriction forces MarginRouter to a single profile, so every source-level
  construction is rerouted through the compiled artifact to avoid a conflicting
  co-compilation. Tests deploy via a new MarginRouteHelpers.deployMarginRouter
  that reads vm.getCode and type the router as IMarginRouter; the deploy/mining
  scripts (DeployMargin, MineMarginRouterSalt, MarginDeployConfig) build the init
  code from vm.getCode so they mine and deploy the size-restricted bytecode, and
  DeployMargin deploys it through the canonical 0x4e59 CREATE2 factory (the same
  one MineMarginRouterSalt and create2crunch mine against) so the router lands at
  the mined vanity address rather than at the script's own address; and
  OpenMorphoLongEth / RemoveExcessCollateral type the router as IMarginRouter so
  importing the concrete router no longer drags an unrelated getCode target
  (V4Quoter) into the router profile and breaks its artifact lookup.
- IMarginRouter inherits IImmutableState and IPermit2Forwarder to expose
  poolManager() and permit2(); permit2() is added to IPermit2Forwarder, satisfied
  by the existing immutable on every implementer.
- A DeployMarginSaltFlow test deploys the router through the 0x4e59 factory and
  asserts it lands at the address the miner predicts, with runtime under the limit.

Deploy surface:
- Remove the EIP-7702 bootstrap flow (BatchExecutor, DeployMarginBootstrap,
  MarginBootstrapBuilder, and their tests): dead deploy surface no longer on the
  deployment path.

Test fidelity:
- MockLendingAdapter.currentLtvWad/describePosition now compute the real
  debt/collateral LTV and maxLtv/currentLtv health factor from the protocol
  ledger instead of echoing the configured maxLtv, so ASSERT_HEALTH is a real
  guard; MockLendingProtocol records balance-delta-measured token movement per
  account so a ledger write that does not match its transfer is observable.

Regenerate the isolated gas snapshots: the router hot paths rise ~15-20%
(e.g. openLong 476,868 -> 543,946), the deliberate cost of fitting under EIP-170
and auto-emitting per-action position events.
rationale: The commit only adjusts compiler optimizer settings to fit the contract under the EIP-170 bytecode size limit and removes dead deployment code. No functional behavior was corrected, nor were any security-relevant checks added or vulnerabilities mitigated.

subject: feat(margin): pass the Universal Router per call instead of as an immutable
body:
The Universal Router was a constructor immutable, freezing one UR deployment for
the router's lifetime. Supply it per call instead, so callers can target an
improved or newer Universal Router over time without redeploying the margin
router or making that choice at deploy time.

- IncreaseParams and DecreaseParams gain an `address universalRouter` field
  (next to routeCommands/routeInputs), and the ROUTE_SWAP action's encoded params
  gain it as a leading field: (universalRouter, input, maxIn, commands, inputs).
  _routeSwap decodes it, reverts UniversalRouterNotSet on a zero address, scopes
  the Permit2 allowance to it, and dispatches the swap through it.
- The constructor drops its universalRouter argument (5 args now) and the
  universalRouter immutable/getter. The UR is no longer part of the router init
  code, so the mined vanity address no longer depends on it: MineMarginRouterSalt,
  MarginDeployConfig, and DeployMargin drop it from the init-code encoding and
  their signatures, and the init-code predictor no longer needs a UNIVERSAL_ROUTER
  env var. Verified the miner and predictor still produce identical init-code
  hashes and that DeployMarginSaltFlow still lands at the mined address.
- OpenMorphoLongEth reads the UR from a UNIVERSAL_ROUTER env var and passes it in
  IncreaseParams.
- Tests thread the deployed test UR through every curated increase/decrease and
  every execute ROUTE_SWAP plan; gas snapshots regenerated (curated and execute
  flows rise a few hundred gas for the extra 32-byte field). Docs updated to the
  per-call model.
rationale: only non-code files changed

subject: feat(indexer): index the PositionUpdated resulting-state snapshot
body:
The router now emits PositionUpdated after every supply/withdraw/borrow/repay on
any path (a curated flow or an execute plan), carrying the full pair and the
adapter's describePosition resulting state. Consume it so execute-composed
positions are as observable as curated ones:

- On a live epoch, reconcile the router-authoritative snapshot (current LTV,
  health factor, max/liquidation LTV) and the running totals. For a curated flow
  this matches the Position* event in the same tx; for an execute plan it is the
  only source of the LTV/health snapshot, and for Aave v4 / Compound v3 (no
  flow-truth layer indexed) it is also the only source of the totals.
- When no epoch is live, open one from the snapshot. This covers an execute open
  the flow layer never created: an Aave v3 open whose single-reserve events could
  not resolve the pair, or an Aave v4 / Compound v3 open. Economics stay empty
  (openReported stays false) until a curated event adopts them, mirroring a
  flow-created epoch.

Adds PositionUpdated to the MarginRouter ABI and a router handler; refreshes the
schema comments and README. The per-call Universal Router change needs no indexer
update: it altered call params, not events, and the indexer reads no
universalRouter getter.
rationale: The change only introduces a new PositionUpdated event to the ABI and indexer handling, updates documentation and schema. It adds functionality rather than correcting incorrect behavior, and the diff shows no security‑related fix.

subject: fix(test): anchor the UniversalRouter compile in src so forge test resolves it
body:
CI (forge v1.3.6) failed the margin route-helper suites with "vm.getCode: no
matching artifact found". Those helpers deploy the Universal Router via
vm.getCode("UniversalRouter.sol:UniversalRouter"), which needs the concrete
UniversalRouter in the artifact set. UniversalRouter is a lib dependency
referenced only by that getCode string, so nothing pulls it into compilation.
The prior anchor lived in script/, but `forge test` (unlike `forge build`) does
not compile script/, so under v1.3.6's sparse test compilation the router was
absent and every route-helper setUp reverted.

Move the anchor to src/URCompileAnchor.sol. `forge test` compiles every src/
file at the default via_ir=true profile, and UniversalRouter needs the IR
pipeline: it stack-too-deeps under the via_ir=false test profile, so it cannot
be anchored from test/, and a test/ file pinned back to via_ir=true is rejected
("failed to merge compilation restrictions" against the blanket test/**
via_ir=false rule). src/ is the only location that both compiles under forge
test and builds with via_ir. The library is never deployed or imported.

Verified against the CI-pinned forge v1.3.6: the 8 previously-failing suites
pass and no getCode artifact errors remain (1063 passed, 0 failed non-fork).
rationale: The commit only moves a compile‑anchor library from script/ to src/ to make the test suite compile; it does not change contract logic or affect runtime behavior, and it is purely a test/build fix with no security impact.

subject: ci(test): fix getCode via a build step + forge v1.7.1, revert the src anchor
body:
The previous commit anchored the UniversalRouter compile in src/. Keep that anchor
in script/ instead and fix the CI invocation: this reverts src/URCompileAnchor.sol
and restores script/URCompileAnchor.s.sol.

CI ran `forge test` on a fresh checkout and failed the margin route-helper suites

script/URCompileAnchor.s.sol forces it in, but `forge test` compiles sparsely and

checkout on both versions: build then test resolves the getCode and the non-fork
suite passes (1063 passed, snapshots match).
rationale: The change only updates CI workflow (adds a build step, bumps tool version) and moves a compile‑anchor script; it does not modify contract logic or affect runtime behavior, so it is not a bug fix of product functionality nor a security fix.

subject: fix: tolerate hook-funded input on exact-output swaps (#584)
body:
* fix: tolerate hook-funded input on exact-output swaps

A v4 hook can pay a swap's input on the caller's behalf. When it covers the
cost in full, PoolManager hands the router the requested positive output
against an input delta of exactly zero. That is solvent -- the hook settles
the debt inside the unlock -- and core permits it explicitly: Hooks.sol:311
notes the caller "has to pay for (or receive) the hook's delta", and IHooks
documents a negative afterSwap return as the hook owing/sending currency.

But it is a shape no ordinary pool produces, where positive output always
implied strictly negative input. Exact output is the only direction that has
to DISCOVER its input by reading a delta, so it is the only one affected:

- The per-hop price guard divides output by input. A zero input panics 0x12,
  even though the realized price is then infinite and clears every finite
  bound it is checked against. Hit _swapExactOutputSingle and, because the
  multihop guard is gated on array presence rather than each bound's value,
  _swapExactOutput whenever minHopPriceX36 was non-empty.
- The multihop loop runs backwards, feeding each hop's input to the previous
  hop as its required output. A funded hop propagated zero, and PoolManager
  rejects amountSpecified == 0 with SwapAmountCannotBeZero.

Skip the division when the input is zero, and stop the backward loop when a
hop consumes nothing -- the upstream hops have nothing left to produce, and
_take/_settle already no-op on zero, so untouched currencies settle cleanly
and an amountIn of 0 trivially clears amountInMaximum.

Over-funding (a hook paying MORE than the cost, leaving a credit whose owner
is undefined in a route) is deliberately left unsupported and still reverts
SafeCastOverflow on the negation, as it does today. Naming that condition
would mean adding an error to IV4Router for no behavior change, so the
interface is untouched; the reasoning is recorded on _swapInput instead.

The fill check runs before the zero-input branch, so all-or-nothing still
holds: a funded hop that underfills reverts V4ExactOutputUnfilled as before.
Exact input is unaffected -- its divisor is the caller's own amountIn, never
a delta, so it can neither divide by zero nor read the sign that overflows.

Also corrects the "output delta will always be positive" comments, which
named a hook case the code does not actually handle: a hook taking more than
the whole output leaves a negative delta and the cast in _swapOutput rejects
it. Documented rather than fixed, since exact input is out of scope here.

Gas +26 single-hop, +54/hop multihop, +96 bytes. Snapshots regenerated
(isolate mode).
