subject: fix(margin): make DeployMargin idempotent for reruns and partial deploys
body:
Deploy every contract through the canonical CREATE2 deployer via a shared
_deployDeterministic helper that skips addresses that already have code,
and guard setAdapterAllowed/setMarket behind isAdapterAllowed/
isSupportedMarket. A rerun after a partial deploy (or after only the
router init code changed) now broadcasts just what is missing instead of
reverting on a CREATE2 collision. Inherit MarginDeployConfig to drop the
duplicated CREATE2_DEPLOYER/ACCOUNT_SALT/WETH constants.
rationale: The change makes the DeployMargin script idempotent by skipping already-deployed contracts and adding guards, fixing a deployment revert issue. This corrects behavior but does not address a security vulnerability.

subject: fix(lens): SafeCast the swap delta conversions in V4Quoter
body:
V4Quoter read the unspecified side of a swap's BalanceDelta with a bare
truncating uint128(...). Only the specified side is guaranteed to have the
expected sign. The unspecified side is whatever remains after Hooks.afterSwap
applies the hook's returned delta, and a hook holding AFTER_SWAP_FLAG plus
AFTER_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA_FLAG can drive it past zero.

The only existing guard, BaseV4Quoter._swap's NotEnoughLiquidity check, compares
the specified side against the requested amount, so it cannot see this. The cast
wrapped and the quoter returned roughly 2^128 as a successful quote with no
revert, for a pool that in reality pays out nothing. A consumer that ranks
candidate pools by raw quoter output picks that pool over every honest one.

V4Router already handles the same two quantities correctly, so the quoter now
uses those exact forms. The output sides at _quoteExactInput and
_quoteExactInputSingle take the int128 overload of toUint128, matching
_swapOutput. The input sides at _quoteExactOutput and _quoteExactOutputSingle
widen before negating, uint256(-int256(x)).toUint128(), matching _swapInput.

The widening matters on its own. Negating an int128 first would panic on
type(int128).min before SafeCast ever ran, and that input is a legitimate
magnitude, not a corrupted one. The widened form yields 2^127.

Keeping the router's forms also preserves the hook-funded input case added in
bbd43468: an input delta of exactly zero still quotes as an amountIn of 0
rather than reverting, so a route the router can execute stays quotable.

Two related sites are fixed alongside. _quoteExactInput and
_quoteExactInputSingle built the swap amount as -int256(int128(amountIn)) from a
uint128. Above type(int128).max that reinterprets as negative, and the outer
negation flips the sign, so an exact-input quote silently simulated an
exact-output swap. Both now widen through uint256 as the router does.

A hook that corrupts the delta makes its own pool unquotable rather than
returning a clamped zero. Clamping would be wrong: a negative output delta means
the caller owes the output currency, not that the pool pays nothing, and the
router rejects that state too. Reverting keeps the quote and the swap in
agreement about which pools are usable.

Behavior on rejection is the existing shape. SafeCastOverflow bubbles out of the
simulation and parseQuoteAmount wraps it in UnexpectedRevertBytes, the same
outer error NotEnoughLiquidity already produces. No interface change.

One divergence from the router is left in place. In multi-hop exact output, a
fully hook-funded hop makes the router break out of its loop, while the quoter
propagates the zero into the next swap and hits SwapAmountCannotBeZero. That is
a revert rather than a wrong number. A test records the current behavior so a
future change to it is visible.

Reverting src/lens/V4Quoter.sol fails 8 of the 10 new tests. Four fail with "did
not revert as expected", which is the wrapped value being returned as a valid
quote, and the type(int128).min case fails with an arithmetic overflow panic.

Snapshots regenerated with Foundry v1.3.6 to match the version CI pins.
rationale: The commit fixes unsafe signed‑to‑unsigned casts of BalanceDelta values that could wrap to 2^128 when a hook returns a negative delta. Previously the quoter could return a huge quote, allowing a malicious hook/pool to manipulate routing decisions and cause financial loss. The fix adds SafeCast and proper widening, preventing the overflow.

subject: fix(margin): emit PositionUpdated from the unlock-free paths
body:
addCollateral and the zero-debt swap-free close mutate positions without
entering the unlock interpreter, so no action handler fired the
resulting-state snapshot. That broke PositionUpdated's documented
contract (reconstruct position state from router logs on any path):
snapshot-only consumers saw collateral grow silently on top-ups and
never saw a zero-debt close terminate, and CollateralAdded carries
neither the debt currency nor maxLtv, forcing indexers into
pair-resolution heuristics that fail on ambiguous or bootstrap adds.

addCollateral now emits the snapshot inline, reusing the
describePosition read it already makes (+3.9k gas); the zero-debt close
emits the terminal snapshot via _emitPosition before PositionDecreased.
NatSpec and the margin guide now state the actual invariant, including
the escape-hatch exclusion.
rationale: The change adds missing PositionUpdated events for addCollateral and zero-debt close paths, correcting behavior that previously violated the documented contract. This is a functional bug fix affecting off‑chain indexing, not a security vulnerability.

subject: feat(indexer): resolve CollateralAdded pairs via the same-tx snapshot
body:
Post-snapshot routers emit PositionUpdated (full pair, lower logIndex)
from addCollateral, so by CollateralAdded time the epoch exists and was
just reconciled: prefer the candidate updated at this block before
falling back to the single-open-position heuristic. Fixes the ambiguous
add (two open positions sharing a collateral token) and the
collateral-first bootstrap equity undercount on venues without a flow
layer, while keeping the fallbacks for the live pre-upgrade deployment.
Also corrects the escape-hatch comment: account-direct mutations emit no
router events at all.
rationale: [MEV] The change fixes ambiguous handling of multiple open positions sharing a collateral token by selecting the one just updated in the same block, preventing undercount of collateral/equity which could be exploited to misrepresent health factors and cause improper liquidations or borrowing. This corrects a logic bug that has security implications.

subject: feat(margin): adapters implement IAmountResolver for route amount resolution
body:
Ships the resolver side of the proposed Universal Router RESOLVE
callback instruction ahead of the instruction itself: every lending
adapter now doubles as an IAmountResolver, so a route can resolve
position-dependent amounts onchain at execution time. Context ABI is
abi.encode(PositionAmount kind, address account, Market market); DEBT
resolves the live interest-accrued debt a full close must buy (no
offchain accrual buffer, no over-buy), COLLATERAL the live balance of a
full withdrawal. Reads route through positionOf, so unrouted markets
revert MarketNotSupported exactly as the read surface does.

positionOf becomes public (memory market) so the shared
PositionAmountResolver mixin reads it with an internal call instead of
an external self-call; the touched internal helpers relax calldata to
memory, shifting the Aave short-inverse gas snapshots by tens of gas.
rationale: The change introduces a new feature (adapters now implement IAmountResolver and expose positionOf) and adjusts calldata handling; the commit message and diff show no correction of previously incorrect behavior, thus it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: docs(margin): point all address registries at the 2026-08-12 redeploy
body:
The deployment table, indexer registry (startBlock 25740584, resolving
its PENDING REDEPLOY note), indexer README, and the
RemoveExcessCollateral script defaults all move to the live suite:
router 0x000000000075e82F7B7DdC5DD1B4984b560eF5D4 and the four
IAmountResolver adapters. Verified onchain: code, governance, adapter
allowlist, every canonical market, and a resolveAmount probe (the
broadcast's commit field is stale; the bytecode includes f591e92 and
7fc38d2).
rationale: The commit only updates documentation and address registry entries to point to newly redeployed contracts; there is no code change that alters behavior, so it is not fixing a defect nor addressing a security issue.

subject: fix(margin): resolve the Aave data provider on each use (audit M-01)
body:
The AaveLendingAdapter cached the protocol data provider as an immutable
resolved once at construction. Aave's PoolAddressesProvider.setPoolDataProvider
overwrites the DATA_PROVIDER entry with a new, non-proxied address (unlike
the Pool, which is a stable proxy), and the adapter has no setter and is
not upgradeable, so a redeployment would strand it on a deregistered
provider whose reads could later revert or return wrong reserve tokens.

Cache only the PoolAddressesProvider and resolve the data provider from
it on each use via a public dataProvider() view (preserving the external
getter). The Pool stays immutable. Correct the NatSpec that claimed both
were stable proxies. Adds a repoint regression test (mock provider gains
setDataProvider); the extra getPoolDataProvider staticcall on the Aave
read path shifts the short-inverse gas snapshots.
rationale: The change stops caching the Aave data provider address, which could become stale after a setPoolDataProvider call, leading to reverted reads or wrong reserve token addresses. This could be exploited to cause fund loss or denial of service, so the commit fixes a security-relevant defect.

subject: fix(margin): explicitly enable supplied collateral via a post-supply hook (audit M-02)
body:
The Aave v3 supply relied on Aave auto-enabling the reserve as
collateral, which only fires on an account's FIRST supply of that
reserve. A prior aToken balance (e.g. an unsolicited dust transfer to
the deterministic account address) makes a later supply a non-first
supply, so the reserve is never flagged and the borrow leg reverts: a
cheap, pre-emptible DoS on opening a v3 position.

Add encodeEnableCollateral to ILendingAdapter, run by
MarginAccount.supplyCollateral immediately after every supply (the
single chokepoint all supply paths funnel through). Aave v3 encodes
setUserUseReserveAsCollateral; Aave v4 moves its setUsingAsCollateral
out of the old Spoke.multicall into this hook (plain supply + enable,
same net effect, consistent with v3); Morpho and Compound return empty
callData (collateral is implicit) and the account skips. Idempotent, so
safe on every supply including top-ups.

Adds encode-shape tests for both Aave adapters, an end-to-end
ShortInverse regression that pre-seeds dust and asserts the open still
flags collateral, and a MockAavePool setUserUseReserveAsCollateral
recorder. The extra post-supply call shifts supply-path gas snapshots
(the empty-return staticcall on Morpho/Compound, the real enable on
Aave).
rationale: [MEV] The commit adds an explicit post‑supply call to enable collateral, fixing a bug where Aave only auto‑enables collateral on the first supply. Prior aToken dust could prevent this, causing borrow to revert and allowing a cheap DoS on opening positions. The fix addresses this security issue.

subject: fix(margin): fill check enforces the swap delta, not absolute balance (audit M-03)
body:
ASSERT_ACCOUNT_BALANCE compares the account's absolute balance against
the threshold, so a pre-existing balance (the blessed zero-equity +
direct-transfer funding pattern, execute-staged funds, a cross-market
same-subId balance, or an unsolicited donation to the public account
address) relaxed the check and could mask a routed-swap under-fill,
defeating the documented all-or-nothing guarantee.

Keep ASSERT_ACCOUNT_BALANCE an absolute check (its contract, relied on
by execute plans) and fix the two curated flows to set the threshold to
the account's pre-unlock balance PLUS the amount the route must deliver.
The absolute check then enforces the swap DELTA: increasePosition
requires balanceBefore + collateralToBuy, decreasePosition requires
balanceBefore + (fullClose ? debt : debtToRepay). Mirrors the
balanceBeforeTake snapshot _routeSwap already uses for the router's own
balance. IncompleteFill/NatSpec reworded to the absolute-resulting-balance
framing.

Adds regressions: an increase and a partial decrease each revert on a
short-filling route despite a masking pre-existing balance, and an
increase with an idle donation still succeeds when the route delivers
fully. The extra balanceOf read shifts the open/close/decrease snapshots.
rationale: The commit changes the fill check to enforce the swap delta rather than an absolute balance, fixing a bug where pre‑existing balances could mask an under‑filled swap. This could be exploited by a malicious route to receive less than expected, leading to financial loss, thus a security‑relevant fix.

subject: fix(margin): clear the ROUTE_SWAP Permit2 allowance after the swap (audit L-08)
body:
ROUTE_SWAP granted the caller-supplied Universal Router a Permit2
allowance scoped to maxIn with a block-timestamp expiration but never
cleared it. Permit2 spends while block.timestamp <= expiration, so the
residual allowance stayed live for the rest of the block; a same-block
re-entry through attacker-controlled UR code could pull against it.
Zero the allowance (amount 0) after settling the flash-take, so no
spendable allowance to the unvalidated address lingers past the call.

Adds a regression asserting the router->UR allowance amount is zero
after an open. The extra approve shifts ROUTE_SWAP-path gas snapshots.
rationale: [MEV] The commit adds a call to permit2.approve(..., 0, 0) to clear the Permit2 allowance after a ROUTE_SWAP. Previously the allowance persisted for the rest of the block, allowing an attacker controlling the Universal Router to re‑enter in the same block and spend the leftover allowance, leading to unauthorized token transfers. This corrects the faulty behavior (bug fix) and mitigates a fund‑stealing vulnerability (security fix) with high severity, classified as improper access control (CWE-284) and elevation of privilege, exploitable via same‑block ordering (MEV).

subject: fix(margin): read the Comet base price feed on each use (audit L-14)
body:
CompoundV3LendingAdapter cached the Comet base-token price feed as an
immutable resolved at construction. The base feed is governance-mutable
behind the same Comet proxy, and debtValue (the LTV/health denominator
feeding ASSERT_HEALTH) is priced with it, so a feed migration would
value debt with a superseded feed on an adapter that cannot be
repointed. Resolve it fresh from the Comet on each valuation via a
public baseTokenPriceFeed() view (preserving the external getter);
baseToken and baseScale stay immutable (genuinely fixed per Comet).
Same shape as the M-01 Aave data-provider fix. Adds a feed-repoint
regression.
rationale: The adapter previously cached the Comet base token price feed, which could be changed via governance, causing stale price usage for debt valuation and incorrect health factor calculations. The fix reads the feed on each valuation, preventing oracle manipulation and potential liquidation attacks.

subject: fix(margin): make curated event-only reads best-effort (audit L-05)
body:
increasePosition, decreasePosition (partial), and addCollateral read
describePosition after the mutation only to populate their rich Position*
/ CollateralAdded events. describePosition consults the venue oracle,
which can revert (e.g. downtime, or a Morpho debt-free position that
still triggers an oracle read), and that revert rolled back an
already-complete mutation - including a risk-reducing addCollateral
top-up, which is exactly when you would want it to go through.

Wrap the three post-mutation reads in try/catch: emit the rich event on
success, skip it on failure, never revert the completed mutation. The
resulting-state PositionUpdated snapshots (emitted inside the unlock, or
inline for addCollateral) are already best-effort, so state observability
degrades gracefully. Corrects the addCollateral comment that wrongly
claimed the read could not revert.

Adds a mock describePosition-revert toggle and regressions: a top-up and
an increase both complete with the read reverting. try/catch overhead
shifts curated-flow gas snapshots.
rationale: The commit wraps post‑mutation oracle reads in try/catch, preventing a revert from describePosition (e.g., oracle downtime) from rolling back the mutation. Previously, an attacker could force the oracle to revert and cause a user’s addCollateral/top‑up to fail, leading to loss of funds or liquidation risk, a classic availability/security issue.

subject: fix(margin): clamp the Morpho repay encoder at the reported debt (audit L-01)
body:
The Morpho repay encoder rejected two boundary amounts. Repaying the exact
debt positionOf/describePosition report (expectedBorrowAssets, rounded up)
took the asset path, which converts back to more shares than the account holds
and underflows inside Morpho. And a debt-free full repay read zero borrow
shares and encoded a (0, 0) repay Morpho rejects, so a generic repay-then-
withdraw exit plan could not run against a position with no debt.

encodeRepay now reads the borrow-share balance once: zero shares encode an
empty no-op the account skips, and a request at or above the reported debt
(max sentinel or >= expectedBorrowAssets) burns the exact shares via the
dust-free share path. MarginAccount.repay skips the call and reports zero when
the adapter encodes an empty no-op. This harmonizes Morpho with the Aave and
Compound adapters, which already clamp.

MockMorpho now serves market()/extSloads so expectedBorrowAssets resolves in
unit tests; adds unit + fuzz boundary coverage, a MarginAccount no-op guard
test, and fork regressions for both boundaries against real Morpho.
rationale: The commit fixes a bug where Morpho repay encoding could underflow or reject boundary amounts, causing transactions to revert and preventing users from repaying and withdrawing positions, which could lock funds and lead to liquidation. The added clamping and no‑op guard correct the behavior, addressing a potential denial‑of‑service/security issue.

subject: feat(indexer): port the flow-derivation layer onto the post-audit branch
body:
Replays felipe/margin-trading-poc-v2's indexer work onto margin-trading, which
since the fork gained the post-audit redeploy registry and three indexer fixes
of its own. The original port was a merge commit; this is its resolved diff,
re-resolved against the newer base. Resolutions that were not mechanical:

- Swap sourcing: margin-trading replaced the sender-filtered PoolManagerSwaps
  source with recordTxSwaps, which parses the margin tx's own receipt (the swap
  caller is whatever Universal Router the route named, so a sender filter cannot
  be written). That supersedes our allowlist approach, so PoolManagerSwaps stays
  deleted and pools.ts keeps only Initialize.
  recordTxSwaps moved to src/swaps.ts and is now ALSO called by the flow layer:
  the router only records from its own handlers, which fire after each venue
  event within an execute plan and never at all for an owner escape-hatch
  operation, so a flow-derived price would otherwise read an empty swap table.

- Liquidation terminal state: both branches independently replaced the
  stored-principal arithmetic with a venue read. Merged to the stronger form —
  margin-trading's semantics (the read refreshes debtPrincipal, with the
  arithmetic as fallback) over our read layer (canonical Pool getters, cached,
  block-pinned, plus the Aave v4 leg), and Morpho's borrowShares now convert via
  toAssetsUp because the value feeds debtPrincipal rather than a zero test. The
  read soft-fails to null instead of throwing, so an unreadable venue degrades
  to the arithmetic rather than halting a liquidation-storm backfill.
  Consequently aaveV3DataProvider / aaveDataProviderAbi are dropped: the Pool's
  own getReserveVariableDebtToken serves that lookup and needs no second
  registry address (both getters verified against live mainnet).

- addresses.ts takes the post-audit suite wholesale (router, four adapters,
  startBlock 25842465) plus our aaveV4Spoke and aaveOracle entries.

- drainFlows keeps both sides: margin-trading's measured repaidAssets (used for
  the decrease's priceX18 and debtDelta) and our DEFICIT skip.

Tests: swaps are staged into a stubbed receipt (harness.onReceiptLogs +
scenario.stageSwap encoding a real log) rather than dispatched, since there is
no Swap handler to dispatch to. stubChainDebt now also stubs Morpho's market
read — without it the Morpho cases silently fell through to the arithmetic
fallback and passed for the wrong reason. Divergence cases (c)/(d) updated to
the merged semantics, and three cases added: shares->assets conversion, its
round-up floor, and the unreadable-venue fallback. 50 pass, typecheck clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit is a feature/porting effort adding new ABI definitions, updating swap sourcing and liquidation logic, and merging indexer work. It does not correct previously incorrect behavior, nor does the diff show a security-relevant fix.

subject: feat(indexer): resolve escape-hatch Aave pairs from the account clone's own events
body:
Restore the MarginAccount clone observation layer carved out of the previous
commit: a tx-scoped map keyed on the router's AccountCreated factory, with
CollateralSupplied=collateral and Borrowed=debt registered-pairs-only, whose
staged rows replay through applyStagedFlows. Its remaining producer is the owner
escape hatch (MarginAccount.execute emits only Executed, no snapshot). Restores
the 5 aavePairResolution cases and the harness's side-effect registration.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change restores a missing observation layer for MarginAccount events, fixing incorrect behavior where Aave pair resolution was not applied. It corrects functionality but does not introduce or mitigate a security vulnerability.

subject: fix(indexer): guard drainFlows' null-pair claim by named reserve and replay in numeric log-index order
body:
drainFlows claimed every staged (null-pair) lendingEvent row unconditionally, so
one tx touching two markets that share a reserve would drain both markets' flows
into whichever pair resolved first. Claim a null-pair row only when the single
reserve it named belongs to THIS pair in the role its kind implies (the belongs
predicate applyStagedFlows already uses); refuse reserve-less rows (fail-closed).

consumeSwaps and txLendingEvents ordered by the row id, which is
`${txHash}-${logIndex}` — a lexical sort puts logIndex 12 before 8. Order by the
parsed numeric log index (new logIndexOf helper) so same-tx flows and swaps
replay in emission order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The change adds a reserve check to null‑pair rows and orders events by numeric log index, fixing a bug where drainFlows would claim any staged row regardless of market, allowing a transaction that touches two markets sharing a reserve to drain the wrong market's flows. This could be exploited by manipulating transaction ordering, leading to unauthorized fund movement, thus a security issue (improper access control) with MEV relevance.

subject: fix(indexer): don't fold a curated open into a snapshot-terminated epoch
body:
PositionIncreased and CollateralAdded read the activePosition pointer raw, so a
curated open (or add) on a pair whose pointed epoch was already terminated by an
execute-composed close snapshot would fold into the dead epoch. Route both
through findActivePosition, which treats a non-OPEN pointed epoch as absent: the
open starts a fresh epoch and overwrites the pointer, the add fails closed.
PositionDecreased keeps the raw read (a same-tx curated close may still enrich a
snapshot-closed epoch). The terminal PositionUpdated snapshot now also records
closeTxHash/closedAt (economics stay null) and leaves the pointer in place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The change fixes a logic error where raw reads of the activePosition pointer could cause a curated open or add to be applied to a terminated epoch, leading to incorrect state that could be exploited via transaction ordering to manipulate position state and potentially cause fund loss. The fix adds proper active position lookup, preventing the TOCTOU-like bug.

subject: fix(SwapAndAdd): require caller auth and collect fees first on increase
body:
POSM's INCREASE_LIQUIDITY credits the position's entire accrued fee
balance against the settle, which broke increase() two ways:

- DoS: whenever accrued fees exceeded the required amount on a side
  (unconditionally for out-of-range positions with fees on the empty
  side), the fee credit flipped the delta positive and SETTLE_PAIR
  reverted DeltaNotNegative.
- Fee redirect: with fees below the required amounts the credit reduced
  the pull instead, and since the liquidity was already sized from the
  caller's budget the fee value fell through to the sweep — increase had
  no caller auth, so anyone could harvest an approved position's fees to
  a chosen recipient at dust cost.

Both halves ship together (either alone makes things worse): increase
now runs _authAndResolveRecipient like compound/rebalance (operator
output forced to the owner), and the OP_INCREASE callback collects the
accrued fees FIRST (DECREASE by 0) so they join the pulled budget and
are reinvested. This also unifies the paths: OP_COMPOUND is gone,
compound is an increase with a zero pulled budget, both built by the
shared _growPayload.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change adds caller authentication and fee collection before increase, fixing a missing access control that let anyone harvest a position's accrued fees and cause a DoS. This corrects improper access control (CWE-284) and prevents unauthorized fund extraction.

subject: fix(SwapAndAdd): gate the UR native reclaim to operations that pushed value
body:
Narrows 10e2e99: the SWEEP reclaim after a route now runs only when the
operation forwarded native value to the UR. The push is a whole-balance
over-push, so a remainder is expected there and must not stay in the
permissionlessly sweepable router — and the all-or-nothing SWEEP still
folds any pre-existing donation into the caller's budget. Value-less
operations leave the UR's balance alone (a route stranding its own
output there is a broken route; minLiquidity gates it like any other).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change adds a guard so that native ETH is only reclaimed from the Universal Router when the caller actually forwarded value. Previously, any caller could trigger a sweep of the router's balance even when no value was sent, allowing unauthorized draining of ETH. This is a fix of incorrect behavior and prevents a fund-stealing vulnerability.

subject: refactor(SwapAndAdd): rename RebalanceParams additionalA/B to additional0/1
body:
Pure rename for consistency: every other pool-token pair in the surface
uses 0/1 naming (amount0In/amount1In, budget0/budget1, withdrawn0/1 in
the docs) — the rebalance deltas were the lone A/B holdout. Field names
do not affect the ABI encoding.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit only renames struct fields and corresponding variables for naming consistency; no logic, state changes, or ABI alterations are introduced, indicating a pure refactor without fixing a defect.

subject: test(SwapAndAdd): treat an empty FORK_URL env var as unset in the mainnet fork suite
body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change only adjusts test code to treat an empty FORK_URL env var as unset, fixing test suite behavior. It does not modify production logic and has no security impact.

subject: test(SwapAndAdd): out-of-range increase regression suite
body:
Promoted from the internal-review scratch: pins that increase works on
out-of-range positions with accrued fees (the pre-fix DeltaNotNegative
DoS), that collected single-sided fees are sized sanely at spot, and the
no-funds-at-rest / operator-cannot-redirect / stranger-rejected
properties of the grow-in-place path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit only adds a new test file and does not modify any production contract code. Adding tests does not constitute fixing a bug in the software's behavior, nor does it address a security vulnerability.

subject: fix(SwapAndAdd): round the trim's token->liquidity inverse up
body:
_trim compensated the DECREASE's rounded-down return with "+1 liquidity
unit" — but the shortfall it must absorb is measured in token wei, a
different quantity. getLiquidityForAmount0 floors an intermediate value
whose truncation is scaled by the amount, so the under-trim error is
unbounded in the amount: single-sided token1 budgets reverted
CurrencyNotSettled at real sizes (from ~6.4 tokens on a price-1e-9
pool). Price 1 is the one level where the intermediate does not
truncate, which is why the price-1 unit suite never saw it.

The inverse now rounds UP on every division, over amountOut + 1, so an
uncapped trim provably frees the debt (the pool's floored return is
still >= amountOut). The lopt cap is then reachable only when the
budget sits within the pool's ~1-wei mint/burn rounding toll — the trim
removes all of lopt, the added liquidity is 0, and any minLiquidity >= 1
floor surfaces it as InsufficientLiquidity before the unlock's delta
check; a zero floor (the explicit opt-out) still sees CurrencyNotSettled.
Documented as a KNOWN LIMIT in ISwapAndAdd.

Regression: SwapAndAddTrim.t.sol (low-price sweep incl. the 6.4-token
threshold, 4.4e30 scale pin, both dust-regime surfaces, happy-path
sweep, never-unsettled fuzz on mid- and low-price pools) and
SwapAndAddTrimMath.t.sol (pure-math pins of the old formula's failure
and the shipped inverse across widths, amounts and price levels).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The commit changes rounding in the _trim function to round up, fixing an unbounded under‑trim error that caused CurrencyNotSettled reverts. The previous behavior could be triggered by price conditions, allowing an attacker to force transaction failures (availability impact) and waste gas, which is a security‑relevant defect.

subject: feat(SwapAndAdd): routeFunding — zap in from arbitrary tokens
body:
Adds an optional TokenAmount[] routeFunding to add/increase/rebalance
(not compound): non-pool tokens pulled from the caller solely to fund
the route, so a position can be entered from any token the route can
convert (e.g. supply USDC, receive a WETH/UNI position).

The core is untouched — sizing, reconcile and trim still only ever see
the post-route pool-token balances. The feature is a pre/post wrapper
in the entrypoints:

- _pullFunding (pre-unlock): Permit2-pulls each entry and wires its
  approvals. Guards: funding requires a non-empty route (it is route
  input by definition); pool currencies are rejected — they are budget
  (amount0In/amount1In), keeping one canonical encoding. Native ETH may
  be an entry only on non-native pools (on a native pool address(0) IS
  currency0 and is rejected), so msg.value always has exactly one
  meaning: the native budget or the native funding, never both.
- _runRoute now forwards the contract's whole native balance — under
  no-funds-at-rest that is exactly the operation's own native budget or
  funding, zero otherwise; the existing UR SWEEP reclaim covers native
  route leftovers unchanged.
- _sweepFunding (post-unlock): sweeps every listed token to the
  RESOLVED recipient (operator leftovers forced to the owner — a route
  can also produce a funding token from position value, so leftovers
  are output like any other). Zero-amount entries pull nothing but are
  still swept: donated balances become claimable, consistent with the
  donation doctrine.
- the OP_INCREASE nothing-to-deploy gate now tolerates a route: an
  increase funded purely by routed tokens has zero pool-token budget
  and zero fees at collect time but is perfectly viable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit introduces a new feature (routeFunding) and related wrapper logic, without fixing previously incorrect behavior. The diff adds functions and guards but does not address a bug, and there is no indication of a security vulnerability being patched.

subject: refactor(SwapAndAdd): drop the reconcile's dust re-denomination swap
body:
_reconcile step 4 sold any excess deficit-token balance back so leftovers
arrived in "the surplus (= input) token". That property was only ever
real for the single-sided no-route case: with two-sided inputs the
surplus is merely the over-weighted side, with a route it depends on the
fill, and with routeFunding the caller never held a pool token at all.
Meanwhile the conversion paid the pool fee and impact on the converted
amount and presented one extra swap callback to hooks — a fee on
cosmetics.

Leftovers are now swept in whatever pool tokens they are. Sizes are
unchanged: the dominant dust (the trim's surplus-side release, ~k*s^2/L)
was never re-denominated to begin with, and the deficit side returns at
most a few wei of trim round-up overshoot (test_add_lowDust's 5-wei
token0 tolerance passes unchanged). _takeCredit stays on both sides —
that is settlement, not cosmetics.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The diff removes the extra dust‑re‑denomination swap that was previously executed during reconciliation, changing contract behavior (a bug fix) but the removed step only incurred fees and an extra callback, with no evident security impact such as fund loss, re‑entrancy, or ordering exploit.

subject: test(SwapAndAdd): property fuzz over pool configuration; guard zero-sized mints
body:
The trim under-estimate survived the entire suite because every pool sat
at price 1 and the one full-domain fuzz only supplied token0-side
budgets — the vulnerable configuration (low price x single-sided token1)
was never generated. Fixed amounts and pool configs are what create
false confidence, so the new SwapAndAddFuzz suite fixes NOTHING: initial
price (±300k ticks), fee (0..10%), tick spacing, seeded depth, range and
both budget sides are all fuzzed, across add, routed add, increase-after-
drift and rebalance-to-any-range.

The property: an operation either succeeds leaving no funds at rest, or
reverts with an error the design explicitly allows (InsufficientLiquidity,
NoFeesToCompound, SafeCastOverflow, the pool's TickLiquidityOverflow /
PriceLimitAlreadyExceeded). CurrencyNotSettled, panics and wrapped
low-level failures always fail the property. Budgets are VALUE-capped
per fuzzed price so the flash-take stays below the reserve pool and the
documented K-05 limit cannot masquerade as a violation.

First victim: wei-scale budgets (or a rebalance whose floor-rounded
withdrawal is zero tokens) size to zero liquidity, and a zero-sized MINT
hit v4's opaque CannotUpdateEmptyPosition before the floor check could
run. _addCore now surfaces the contract's own InsufficientLiquidity for
zero-sized mints (grow-in-place ops keep their add-zero semantics);
pinned deterministically in the unit suite.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds an explicit revert for zero-sized liquidity mints that previously hit an opaque internal error (CannotUpdateEmptyPosition) causing a crash. This corrects faulty behavior and prevents a denial‑of‑service scenario where an attacker could trigger the crash, so it is both a bug fix and a security fix.

subject: fix(SwapAndAdd): address production-readiness review findings
body:
Three independent fresh-eyes reviews (routeFunding surface, reconcile/
trim settlement, auth/recipients) confirmed the core properties hold;
these are the actionable findings.

[Medium] increase/compound with a route leg through the TARGET pool
re-accrued LP fees on the position AFTER the callback's collect
prologue; POSM credits the whole accrued balance on INCREASE_LIQUIDITY,
so a credit exceeding a side's principal flipped the delta positive and
SETTLE_PAIR reverted DeltaNotNegative — bricking a route shape the
contract advertises as supported (a router may pick the target pool).
_addCore now re-collects after the route on the grow path, folding
route-accrued fees into the budget (reinvested, never leaked).
Regression: test/SwapAndAddSamePoolRoute.t.sol.

[Low] recipient == address(0) was not rejected: on increase/compound it
silently BURNED swept leftovers — with routeFunding, up to the entire
unconsumed funding input (not just dust). _validateRecipient now rejects
the zero address on all four entrypoints (this supersedes the earlier
"zero recipient = explicit burn" framing, whose premise was false — the
NFT ops revert on it late anyway). Tests: test_revertsWhenRecipientIsZero.

[Low] the UR native-reclaim gate `value > 0` predated routeFunding;
an ERC20-in/native-out route on a non-native pool pushes zero value yet
can strand native in the permissionlessly sweepable UR. Gate on the
router's balance alone. Test updated: test_add_route_reclaimsAnyUrNative.

[Info] restated the no-funds-at-rest INVARIANT to match what the code
enforces (well-formed operations; undeclared donations are claimable,
never third-party-reachable via allowances), documented the
route-construction requirement (no CONTRACT_BALANCE-style whole-balance
consumption, since the whole native balance is forwarded), and added
receive() sender-allowlist coverage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds validation rejecting address(0) as a recipient and fixes a native‑token reclaim gate that could strand native assets, both preventing loss or locking of user funds. These are security‑relevant bug fixes of low severity.

subject: fix(margin): emit owner-lifecycle events from OwnableAdapter and the router constructor (audit N-12)
body:
OwnableAdapter declared no events, so an adapter-owner proposal or completed
handoff was unobservable onchain even though the owner is the sole market
curator, and the router constructor seeded initial governance silently.

The adapter now emits Ownable2Step-shaped OwnershipTransferStarted on propose
and OwnershipTransferred at construction (from the zero address) and on each
completed acceptOwnership; the router constructor emits the existing
GovernanceTransferred from the zero address so initial governance is indexed
the same way a handoff is. No behavioral change; gas snapshots unaffected.
rationale: The commit adds missing OwnershipTransferStarted, OwnershipTransferred, and GovernanceTransferred events to make ownership changes observable. This corrects a defect (lack of events) but does not change contract logic or close a direct security vulnerability.

subject: docs(margin): correct NatSpec/guide inaccuracies and document acknowledged behaviors (audit N-15)
body:
Corrects every documentation inaccuracy OZ flagged in N-15 and records the
behaviors acknowledged without a code change:

- ILendingAdapter/PositionData: collateral is interest-accrued only where the
  venue accrues it (Aave; Morpho/Comet collateral earns none); the health
  factor is maxLtv/currentLtv only on Morpho/Compound (Aave reports its own),
  is zero for debt against zero collateral value, and account-level read
  caveats now cover Compound's base debt and currentLtvWad (the health-check
  input); encodeRepay's full-repay semantics are stated per venue instead of
  share-based.
- Adapter headers: replace the blanket "no protocol math is reimplemented"
  claims with what each adapter actually computes locally.
- IMarginRouter: PositionUnhealthy is the caller-supplied ASSERT_HEALTH bound
  (zero skips), not the adapter LLTV; execute NatSpec no longer denies the
  PositionUpdated snapshots plans emit; IncompleteFill also names ASSERT_FILL;
  createAccount is documented as permissionless with a salt-bound owner
  (MarginAccountFactory header likewise).
- IV4Router/V4Router: document the minHopPriceX36 fields (output-per-input,
  X36 scale) and fix the inverted per-hop price-limit error descriptions.
- Acknowledged behaviors (L-09/L-12/L-13/N-05/N-10/N-13/N-14): requested-vs-
  measured event fields and the OPEN_DELTA equity absorption, the Comet
  minimum viable partial decrease, CollateralWithdrawn's per-venue amount,
  the zero/OPEN_DELTA sentinel collisions, base-supply positions being out of
  router scope, and the live-Comet asset-set dependence of priced reads.
- Guide: Compound venue notes, corrected read-accrual wording, and an events
  reference covering the full event set (incl. the N-12 ownership events)
  with field caveats.
rationale: The commit only updates documentation and NatSpec comments without any code changes; therefore it does not correct any previously incorrect behavior and introduces no security-relevant changes.

subject: chore(margin): cosmetic maintenance pass (audit N-04, N-06, N-07, N-08)
body:
The four cosmetic cleanups deferred from the OZ margin-trading audit, with no
behavioral change:

- N-04: rename the router constructor param to accountImplementation_ so it no
  longer shadows the inherited MarginAccountFactory immutable (and matches its
  sibling params).
- N-06: drop the unused named returns from all eight MarginCalldataDecoder
  decoders, which returned an explicit abi.decode over them.
- N-07: remove the dead Position/Currency imports from MorphoLendingAdapter and
  the Ltv.raw/Ltv.lte helpers never called in src/; the remaining raw() callers
  in scripts and tests migrate to the canonical Ltv.unwrap, and the Ltv type
  tests now exercise gt (the one comparison the router uses) directly.
- N-08: storage-type mutators consistently return nothing; Owner.write,
  Owner.propose, and MarketRegistry.register returned a storage reference for
  chaining that every call site discarded.
rationale: The commit only performs cosmetic clean‑ups: renaming a constructor parameter, dropping unused returns, removing dead imports, and adjusting scripts/tests to use Ltv.unwrap instead of a removed helper. No functional behavior is altered, and no security‑relevant logic is changed.

subject: fix(margin): report undefined opcodes as UnsupportedAction (audit N-09)
body:
The active-account guard preceded the UnsupportedAction fallback, so an
undefined opcode in a plan with no bound account misreported as
NoActiveAccount. The margin opcode space is contiguous
[ACCOUNT_SUPPLY_COLLATERAL, ASSERT_ACCOUNT_BALANCE], so anything above it is
rejected as UnsupportedAction before the guard; defined opcodes still require
a preceding SET_ACCOUNT. Regressions cover the undefined opcode with and
without a bound account, and a constants test pins the contiguous range the
bound check assumes. Costs one comparison per account-scoped action
(snapshots +22 to +88 gas per flow, regenerated isolated).
rationale: The commit adds a check to reject undefined margin opcodes as UnsupportedAction, fixing a bug where such opcodes were misreported as NoActiveAccount. The change corrects error handling but does not introduce or fix a vulnerability that could be exploited for fund loss or other security impact.

subject: fix(margin): reject a partial decrease against a debt-free position
body:
The Morpho boundary-repay fix turned this path from a loud underflow into a
silent success: with no debt, the swap bought debtToRepay of debt tokens that
no repay consumed (only a full close sweeps the surplus back), stranding them
in the account while PositionDecreased reported a repay that never happened,
costing the caller swap fees and slippage. Flagged by OZ in the L-01 review
thread with a fork reproduction on both revisions.

decreasePosition now reverts NoDebtToRepay when a partial decrease reads zero
debt, restoring the pre-fix loud failure with a precise error. This also keeps
a stale partial decrease against a re-pointed pair (whose reads see zero debt)
a revert rather than a silent value leak. A debt-free position exits via the
full close, which is unaffected.
rationale: The commit adds a validation that reverts when a partial decrease is attempted on a debt‑free position, fixing a silent success that stranded tokens and caused the caller to lose swap fees and slippage. This corrects a bug and prevents unintended fund loss, qualifying as a security‑relevant fix.

subject: fix(margin): repay encoders no-op uniformly on a debt-free account
body:
The interface documents that a debt-free repay encodes empty callData the
account skips, but only Morpho honored it: Aave v3 reverts NoDebtOfSelectedType
and the Aave v4 Spoke reverts InvalidAmount on a debt-free repay, and Compound
encoded a zero supply the Comet merely tolerates. Flagged by OZ in the L-01
review thread after probing all four venues.

Both Aave encoders now return the empty skip signal when the account holds no
debt in the market's reserve, and Compound returns it instead of a zero supply,
so the generic repay-then-withdraw exit plan documented on encodeRepay runs
against a debt-free position on every venue. Regressions assert the no-op shape
per venue; the existing repay-shape tests seed live debt.
rationale: The commit adds checks for zero debt in encodeRepay for Aave and Compound adapters, preventing calls that would revert on debt‑free accounts. Previously the revert could block a user’s exit transaction, constituting a denial‑of‑service vulnerability. The fix restores the intended no‑op behavior.

subject: docs(margin): ASSERT_ACCOUNT_BALANCE is an absolute floor, not a fill delta
body:
The M-03 fix corrected _assertAccountBalance and IncompleteFill, but the three
places a plan author actually reads still described the action as a delta
check, promising an all-or-nothing fill guard where the action is a balance
floor. Flagged by OZ in the M-03 review thread.

MarginActions, decodeFillCheck, and the guide's action table now state the
check is absolute (any pre-existing balance counts toward the minimum) and
that the delta guarantee comes from how the caller computes minAmount. The
guide additionally spells out that the curated technique is not replicable
inside a plan (static calldata, no mid-plan snapshot, no delta opcode) and
what to do instead: prefer ASSERT_FILL where output lands on the router (a
true per-unlock delta), and for account-delivered ROUTE_SWAP output either
run against an account holding none of the output currency or bake an
offchain-observed balance into minAmount and accept the race.
rationale: The commit only updates documentation and makes no code changes; it does not correct any previously incorrect behavior, thus it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: chore(margin): drop engagement-specific audit tags from src comments
body:
The audit-fix commits left seven '(audit X-NN)' suffixes in src comments.
The identifiers are engagement-specific: they mean nothing to a future reader
and drift as issues are renumbered or the report is superseded. The
explanatory text stays; only the tags go. Regression tests keep their finding
references as provenance for why each test exists.
rationale: no token changed — comments, whitespace or formatting only

subject: fix(margin): saturate the event deltas so the guarded reads cannot panic
body:
The best-effort event wrapping guards the describePosition call, but the
success block computed two deltas from reads taken at different times:
the increase event's position.debtAmount - debtBefore and the partial
decrease event's collateralBefore - position.collateralAmount. Venues accept
permissionless onBehalf repays and supplies, so one landing inside the
transaction (from code in the route path, e.g. a hook on a route pool) can
move the position against the operation's direction; the subtraction then
panics inside the success block, which the catch does not cover, rolling back
the completed mutation. Flagged by OZ in the L-05 review thread.

Both deltas now saturate to zero, so the success block cannot revert; the
resulting-state fields in the same event and the in-unlock PositionUpdated
snapshots still carry the true position. Regressions stage the wrong-direction
read on both flows and reproduced the panic before the fix.
rationale: [MEV] The change saturates subtractions in event emission to avoid underflow reverts that could be triggered by permissionless onBehalf actions within the same transaction, which previously caused the whole transaction to revert. This is a bug fix and mitigates a denial‑of‑service vector where an attacker controlling ordering could cause the underflow, so it is a security fix.

subject: docs(margin): the Aave constructor param no longer claims the data provider is stored
body:
The M-01 fix corrected the header, dataProvider(), and the address registry,
but the constructor's @param provider NatSpec still said the Pool AND the data
provider proxy addresses are resolved and stored immutably, contradicting the
in-body comment four lines below and repeating the proxy misclassification
that caused M-01 in the first place; the integration guide's adapter section
carried the same sentence. Both now state the split correctly: the Pool (a
stable proxy) is stored immutably, the data provider is a plain repointable
address re-resolved on each use. A sweep for other survivals of the caching
claim found none.
rationale: The commit only updates documentation and a NatSpec comment to correctly describe that the protocol data provider address is re-resolved on each use, without changing any contract logic or storage. No behavior is altered, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: fix(margin): gate the partial decrease on the measured repay, not the pre-unlock read
body:
The NoDebtToRepay guard read the position before the unlock, but the repay leg
consults the encoder inside it: a permissionless onBehalf repay landing in
between (route-path code can execute one on every venue) cleared the debt, the
now-uniform zero-debt no-op skipped the repay, and the silent partial decrease
returned: bought debt tokens stranded in the account while the event reported a
repay that never happened, with ASSERT_HEALTH passing trivially at the cleared
LTV. Flagged by OZ in the L-01 review thread as a residual of the previous two
fixes composing.

The ACCOUNT_REPAY handler now records the account's measured repay in a
transient slot (initialized to zero before the unlock, fail-closed) and the
curated partial branch reverts NoDebtToRepay when it reads zero after the
unlock, restoring full parity with the original at-repay-time failure. The
full close is untouched (it tolerates the no-op and sweeps the over-bought
debt back) and execute plans never read the slot, so their zero-repay no-op
contract is unchanged. Regression stages the mid-unlock no-op with the health
read mocked to the cleared-debt state.
rationale: [MEV] The commit fixes a race‑condition where a permissionless onBehalf repay could be injected between the router's pre‑unlock debt check and the unlock, causing the router to skip the actual repay and leave debt tokens stranded while emitting a false event. This could be exploited to cause financial loss, so the fix is a security‑relevant bug fix. The added LAST_REPAID slot and post‑unlock check restore correct ordering, addressing a CWE‑362 race condition and a Tampering/MEV vector.

subject: docs(margin): close the residual doc-pass instances and document encodeEnableCollateral
body:
Closes the residuals OZ flagged on the N-15 and M-02 threads:

- PositionAmountResolver no longer claims collateral is interest-accrued
  (deferring to ILendingAdapter.positionOf's per-venue semantics), and the
  accrual attribution now distinguishes v3 aToken rebasing from the v4 Spoke's
  accrued supplied assets (interface and guide).
- The share-based full-repay framing is venue-neutral everywhere it survived:
  IMarginAccount.repay, the full-close plan comment, and the guide's full-close
  mechanics line; the remaining share-based mentions are the venue-correct
  Morpho and Comet statements.
- The execute events note includes CollateralWithdrawn among the account-level
  events a plan emits.
- IncompleteFill's requested/received params describe both throw sites
  (ASSERT_ACCOUNT_BALANCE and ASSERT_FILL).
- The minHopPriceX36 fields are documented as struct-level NatSpec @param tags
  on all four IV4Router param structs, so the X36 scale and output-per-input
  orientation reach generated docs.
- The guide's Aave v4 bullet no longer describes the removed Spoke.multicall
  batching: it documents the encodeEnableCollateral hook both adapters use,
  and the adapter-surface sections (3.3 and the reference) list all five
  encoders with the note that an out-of-tree adapter must implement the hook
  (empty callData is the skip signal).
rationale: The commit changes PositionAmountResolver to stop incorrectly treating collateral as interest‑accrued and defers to per‑venue semantics, fixing a miscalculation that could cause under‑collateralized positions and potential loss of funds. This correction addresses a security‑relevant accounting bug.

subject: feat(router): expose virtual amount hooks for execution-time swap resolution
body:
Add _mapSwapAmount (default identity) to V4Router, applied to the amount
read from swap params before the OPEN_DELTA sentinel is interpreted, so an
inheriting router can resolve a route-level sentinel (a callback register
populated by a prior command) into a concrete uint128 at execution time
without reimplementing any private swap helper. Also make
DeltaResolver._mapTakeAmount virtual for symmetry with _mapSettleAmount,
so TAKE amounts are equally overridable.

Default behavior is unchanged (identity mapping). Cost is +15 bytes of
bytecode and +15 gas per swap (a single JUMP into the hook). Router and
margin swap tests pass; snapshots regenerated in isolate mode.

subject: fix(SwapAndAdd): close each deploy currency by sign instead of asserting a debt
body:
POSM applies `liquidityDelta + feesAccrued` to its own delta, so on a
grow op a fee credit larger than that side's principal makes the delta
POSITIVE — and SETTLE_PAIR (via _getFullDebt) asserts a debt, reverting
DeltaNotNegative. The callback already collects the position's fees
before the route, but a route leg that trades the TARGET pool re-accrues
them before the deploy, bricking a route shape the contract advertises
as supported.

_deploy now uses CLOSE_CURRENCY per currency, which settles a debt or
takes a credit. That removes the whole failure class rather than the one
known cause (a hook trading the pool mid-operation is another), and it
replaces the previously committed post-route re-collect, which cost an
extra modifyLiquidity plus an extra remove-liquidity hook callback on
EVERY routed grow op — even the common off-venue case that never needed
it. Measured ~59k gas cheaper on the same-pool path. DeltaNotNegative is
now structurally unreachable: the zap encodes neither SETTLE_PAIR nor
SETTLE, and its own helpers branch on the delta sign.

Semantics this settles, measured in the regression test: fees accrued
DURING an operation are credited after sizing, so they cannot grow the
position past its already-fixed optimistic size. The reconcile spends
what it needs on the flash debt (avoiding a trim) and the rest is
refunded to the recipient. Fees accrued BEFORE the operation are
unaffected — the prologue collect puts them in the budget ahead of
sizing, so compound still reinvests them in full.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change replaces SETTLE_PAIR (which asserts a debt and could revert when fees accrued during the operation make the delta positive) with CLOSE_CURRENCY, eliminating a condition that caused transactions to revert and thus a denial‑of‑service scenario. The fix corrects previously incorrect behavior, making it a bug fix with security impact.

subject: docs(SwapAndAdd): scope hook non-support by permission flag, not by intent
body:
The known limit said "fee-taking hooks", which reads far broader than the
actual boundary and gives integrators nothing to check. It is now stated
as the four v4 *_RETURNS_DELTA permissions, per flag:

- AFTER_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA / BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA skim the reconcile
  swap's output; AFTER_REMOVE_LIQUIDITY_RETURNS_DELTA skims what the
  trim, fee collect or rebalance burn frees. Both unsupported — the call
  reverts atomically (CurrencyNotSettled, or DeltaNotPositive when a
  removal's delta turns negative) and funds are always safe.
- AFTER_ADD_LIQUIDITY_RETURNS_DELTA charges the deploy instead, which the
  contract settles from the budget, so it should read as extra cost gated
  by minLiquidity. Reasoned, not test-verified, so documented as
  unsupported until it is.

Also states positively that hooks without those permissions ARE
supported, dynamic LP-fee hooks included (a beforeSwap override returns a
fee, not a delta).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: no token changed — comments, whitespace or formatting only

subject: test(SwapAndAdd): fix three harness gaps the property fuzz exposed under load
body:
None are contract findings — all three are limits of the harness itself,
found by running the properties far past the default 256 runs:

- increase_afterDrift value-capped budgets at the pool's INITIAL price,
  but it drifts the price before the increase, whose flash-take is sized
  at the post-drift price. A cached counterexample implied a 1.274e30
  take, i.e. the documented K-05 PoolManager-drained limit rather than
  the property under test. Now re-caps at live spot.
- at 3k runs the fuzzer picked fee 10000 + spacing 200 and collided with
  the harness's own reserve pool (PoolAlreadyInitialized). The reserve
  pool now uses a fee above the fuzzed range, so collision is impossible.
- the tick-ordering vm.assumes rejected ~75% of inputs (both ranges in

subject: feat(SwapAndAdd): permit-and-operate in one transaction via Multicall_v4
body:
Inherit POSM's Multicall_v4 so a caller with no standing Permit2
allowance toward the zap can batch [permitBatch, op] — approve by
signature and operate atomically; zero-value batches also let keepers
compose ops across positions. Batching adds no fund-mixing surface:
delegatecall preserves msg.sender and every op sweeps before returning
(no-funds-at-rest holds per op, not per transaction).

msg.value keeps one meaning per batch, now enforced clearly: the exact
equality checks already reject ERC20 ops in value-bearing batches, and
a new balance guard in _pullBudget/_pullAdditional makes a second
native claimant revert InvalidEthValue at its own pull instead of
opaquely inside the deploy (native spending is balance-funded, so a
double-claim could only ever revert — the guard just names it early).

Both properties are pinned by test/SwapAndAddMulticall.t.sol, alongside
the flagship permit+op flows for add/increase/rebalance, a keeper batch,
permit front-run tolerance and a batched-vs-direct equivalence fuzz.

Bytecode: 20,562 runtime (down from 22,351 — via_ir's global inlining
lands smaller for this shape; the CI size gate pins it either way).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds explicit balance checks to prevent a second native token claim from causing an opaque revert later, fixing a bug in the contract's handling of native ETH. The change improves error handling but does not address a vulnerability that could be exploited for loss of funds or other security impact.

subject: refactor(SwapAndAdd): one unlock payload and one result shape for all ops
body:
Every entrypoint now builds its CoreParams before the unlock and funnels
through a single _run helper encoding one UnlockData shape: the core
params plus two sentinel tokenIds (growTokenId for increase/compound,
burnTokenId for rebalance) and rebalance's signed deltas. The callback
shrinks to at most one budget-resolution prep — the two preps mutually
exclusive by construction and stated so with else-if — followed by the
shared core; the result is always (tokenId, liquidity, amount0, amount1),
grow ops echoing their own id.

Deletes the OP_* constants and dispatch, _prepareRebalance and the
per-op payload decoders. Behavior unchanged: 784 tests green under
--isolate with snapshot check; bytecode 20,562 -> 18,485.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit only refactors the SwapAndAdd contract by consolidating unlock payload handling and removing unused constants. The author explicitly states behavior is unchanged and tests still pass, indicating no bug was corrected, thus it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: test(SwapAndAdd): adversarial multicall suite — mixing calls grants nothing
body:
Adds the batch-equivalence theorem as a fuzz: any 3-call sequence of
add/increase/compound with fuzzed budgets must behave identically as
one batch and as three separate transactions — batch succeeds iff every
sequential call succeeds, per-call returndata is byte-identical, final
wallet balances, position liquidity, minted ids and the empty zap all
match. Reverting sequences are in-domain (the batch must reproduce the
failure). Held at 5000 runs.

Targeted pins around it: atomic rollback of earlier subcalls on a later
failure; a victim's mempool-public permit signature mixed into an
attacker's batch moves no victim funds (pulls always draw from
msg.sender); an operator batching over the owner's position cannot
redirect value to itself (recipient resolution holds mid-batch, its
balances only decrease); nested multicall behaves like flat; compound
(non-payable) is unbatchable with value; batch value no op consumes
strands as the documented donation and is swept to the next native op's
recipient.

rationale: The commit only adds/updates a test file (SwapAndAddMulticall.t.sol) and does not modify any production contract logic. It introduces no functional changes, so it does not fix a bug nor address a security issue.

subject: fix(indexer): attribute v4 swaps from the margin transaction's receipt
body:
The Swap stream filtered PoolManager events on sender == MarginRouter, but
since position swaps route through a caller-named Universal Router (any
address, per call), the UR is the swap caller and the filter dropped every
curated-route swap, leaving openPoolId and action poolId null. Flagged by
Codex review on the PR.

The sender-filtered stream is gone; the router handlers (curated events and
the PositionUpdated snapshot, so execute-plan swaps are kept too) fetch the
margin transaction's receipt via the cached client action and record the
PoolManager Swap logs it contains, which attributes exactly the swaps sharing
a transaction with a margin event on every execution path. Verified against
live mainnet data: previously-null openPoolId now resolves.
rationale: The change removes an incorrect event filter that dropped legitimate swap events and adds receipt parsing to correctly record them, fixing missing data in the indexer. This corrects a functional bug but does not affect on-chain security or expose any exploitable vulnerability.

subject: fix(indexer): decide full liquidation from the venue's live debt
body:
The stored debtPrincipal lags accrued interest, so a partial liquidation
repaying more than the stored value clamped the remainder to zero, marked the
position LIQUIDATED, and deleted its active pointer while accrued debt was
still outstanding. Flagged by Codex review on the PR.

recordLiquidation now reads the venue's remaining debt at the liquidation
block (Morpho borrow shares converted with the virtual-offset share math;
Aave v3 variable-debt token balance via the protocol data provider) and
derives both the refreshed principal and the terminal decision from it,
falling back to the stored-principal arithmetic only when the venue is not
readable.
rationale: [MEV] The change fixes a logic error where liquidation used a stale stored debtPrincipal, allowing a partial liquidation to clear the position while accrued debt remained, potentially letting an attacker claim liquidation rewards without fully repaying debt. The new code reads live debt from Morpho/Aave contracts to correctly decide full liquidation, addressing a business‑logic security flaw.

subject: fix(indexer): record the measured repay on partial decreases
body:
PositionDecreased.debtRepaid is the caller's requested amount, which the
venue clamps when it exceeds the live debt (per the events reference), so
recording it as the action's debt delta could overstate the reduction beyond
the position's entire prior debt and distort the computed execution price.
Flagged by Codex review on the PR.

drainFlows now aggregates the measured repay assets from the same-tx venue
flows, and the decrease handler prefers that for the action's debtDelta and
priceX18. Aave v4 and Compound stage no flow layer yet and fall back to the
requested amount; the position row itself already stored the event's measured
resulting totals.
rationale: The change fixes an accounting bug where the caller's requested repay amount (potentially larger than the actual repayment) was used to compute debtDelta and execution price, leading to overstated debt reduction and price distortion. This could be exploited by a malicious actor to manipulate pricing or liquidation outcomes, constituting a security-relevant flaw.

subject: test(SwapAndAdd): pin the POSM subscriber doctrine
body:
Subscribers are the one owner-chosen external-call surface inside the
unlock that is not a hook: notifyModifyLiquidity fires full-gas with
revert bubbling on the grow ops' fee collect, the INCREASE and any trim;
notifyBurn fires on the rebalance burn. Until now the suite had zero
subscribed-position coverage.

Pins: a well-behaved subscriber is transparent (increase/compound/
rebalance complete, notifications counted, the rebalanced position's
fresh NFT carries no subscription over); a reverting subscriber can only
DoS its own position's operations (atomic revert, funds and NFT
untouched); a subscriber that trades the pool mid-operation — between
the fee collect and the sizing read, settling its own deltas — is gated
by the minLiquidity floor exactly like a hook or the caller's route
(honest floor -> InsufficientLiquidity, accept-anything floor ->
completes at the moved price, tick assertion proves the trade happened).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit only introduces a new test file (SwapAndAddSubscriber.t.sol) and does not modify any production code. Adding tests does not constitute fixing a bug, nor does it address any security vulnerability.

subject: refactor(SwapAndAdd): burn the rebalanced position in its own POSM unlock
body:
Rebalance's burn moves out of the shared callback into rebalance()
itself, executed through POSM's self-unlocking modifyLiquidities — the
vanilla, battle-tested user burn path — with the budgets resolved from
the proceeds before the main unlock opens. The special case now lives
in the special function.

Consequences: the unlock payload IS the CoreParams for every op (the
burn triple and the _run overload disappear), and the callback shrinks
to the grow ops' fee-collect prep plus the shared core. The between-
unlocks window carries no PoolManager state: session 1 fully settles
into plain balances protected by the allowance invariant, the only
external call in the gap is the owner-chosen recipient's cash-out
transfer, whose powers (pool ops gated by minLiquidity, own-asset POSM
ops) it already had in-session under the old design.

Measured cost: +4.1k gas on ERC20 rebalances, +8.3k native (~0.4-0.6%,
rebalance only); the over-withdrawal revert got 87k cheaper. All other
ops unchanged. 803 tests green unmodified under --isolate with snapshot
check; bytecode 17,969 -> 17,950. Net -13 lines.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: [MEV] The commit moves the burn of a rebalanced position from a shared callback into its own POSM unlock, removing the previous unlock payload that included burn parameters and eliminating a window where pool manager state could be manipulated. This change fixes a bug in the rebalance flow and closes a potential reentrancy/order‑dependence attack surface, qualifying it as a security fix (ordering‑based tampering).

subject: refactor(SwapAndAdd): pass an inert max deadline to the rebalance burn
body:
Staleness is checked exactly once per operation, by the entrypoint's
checkDeadline modifier — the contract-wide rule (no other POSM call
takes a deadline; modifyLiquiditiesWithoutUnlock has none). Threading
params.deadline into the burn created a second, provably-inert check
site on one path and implied POSM's check had a role it cannot have
(same transaction, same timestamp, same comparison). type(uint256).max
states the truth and returns _withdraw to three arguments.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change only refactors the internal _withdraw function to use a constant max deadline instead of forwarding the caller‑provided deadline, removing a redundant parameter. No functional behavior or security property is altered, so it is not a bug fix nor a security fix.

subject: refactor(SwapAndAdd): merge _pullFunding and _pullBudget into one _pull
body:
expectedValue — the msg.value narrative — is now born, accumulated
(funding natives, then the native pool budget) and asserted in a single
scope, instead of being threaded between two functions. The external-
call sequence is unchanged (funding pulls always preceded budget pulls
at every call site), so behavior is identical: 803 tests green
unmodified. The hand-off itself was a latent mistake class — a future
call site passing a wrong fundingValue — that is now unrepresentable.

Wiring intentionally stays split and the doc block now says why in one
place: funding tokens wire here (the only place that sees the list),
pool tokens wire in _addCore (rebalance and compound pull nothing yet
their deploys still need the allowances).

funding[0]/funding[1] convention — it would not unify wiring (compound
has no funding input), cannot absorb rebalance's signed deltas, trades
named fields for positional protocol, and reopens the msg.value
exclusivity argument.

rationale: The refactor adds explicit input validation (rejecting funding tokens that are the pool's own tokens and requiring a route when native funding is used) and consolidates funding and budget pulls, fixing a latent bug where incorrect funding values could be passed and potentially exploited to misdirect token pulls.

subject: feat(SwapAndAdd): op-level events; rename _addCore to _swapAndAdd
body:
Four events for offchain attribution, declared in ISwapAndAdd and
emitted once per operation, before the NFT hand-off and sweeps: Added,
Rebalanced, Increased, Compounded. Indexed fields lead: recipient and
the tokenIds — the parties/keys that cannot be found any other way —
while the caller rides as data (callers can always enumerate their own
transactions). Rebalanced carries the old->new tokenId lineage that
nothing onchain otherwise links. On the grow ops the recipient is the
RESOLVED recipient (forced to the owner for operators), stated in the
NatSpec and pinned by an operator test. Event fields mirror the return
values, asserted against actual returns via recorded logs in
test/SwapAndAddEvents.t.sol.

Also renames the shared core _addCore -> _swapAndAdd: it is the
contract's namesake primitive, and every entrypoint now reads as its
definition (add = pull + _swapAndAdd, rebalance = burn + _swapAndAdd,
increase = pull + collect + _swapAndAdd, compound = collect +
_swapAndAdd). Plus doc touch-ups.

subject: test(SwapAndAdd): full-domain math fuzzes — trim inverse, fee-aware accuracy
body:
Three fuzzes for the math claims the existing suites do not discriminate:

- trim inverse (pure, both branches): across the full sqrt-price/width
  domain with the debt correlated to the geometry (bounded by what a
  max-liquidity position holds over [lo,su]), burning the shipped
  round-up dl must free >= amountOut under v4's round-down burn.
- fee-aware sizing accuracy: an add's dust must stay price-impact-small
  (<= 10bps) across fee tiers (0.5%..10%) and budget splits. This is
  the one test that fails if the fee discount is broken — every other
  suite tolerates the over-mint because the trim claws it back; only
  the dust betrays it. Verified discriminating: with the discount
  neutered in src it fails at 378x the bound on the first sample.
- extreme-tick token1 mirror of the existing token0 full-deployment
  fuzz: >= 99.9% of feasible liquidity at any tick, exercising the
  price<1 numeraire branch of _sizeLiquidityWeighted.

All held at 5000 runs. The uncorrelated-debt domain also surfaced a
reachable-in-principle overflow revert in the token0 inverse (price
within ~2^-64 of the upper boundary while the debt is still large ->
mulDiv result exceeds uint256, EvmError instead of the lopt cap);
atomic revert only, noted in the test comment, fix under discussion.

subject: fix(SwapAndAdd): skip the reconcile sell when step 1 already retired the debt
body:

advertised same-pool-route flow) retires the flash debt in reconcile
step 1, the sell-all bought nothing the operation needed: it paid the
pool fee converting the surplus into a refund and re-denominated it,
contradicting the sweep doctrine. The guard hoists step 3's deficit-
delta read and only swaps while a debt remains; the surplus now comes
back in its own token. Pinned red-first by
test_increase_creditRetiresDebt_skipsGratuitousSwap; the existing
same-pool-route test's expectations updated to the corrected semantics
(refund = credit minus flash debt, ~92% here, plus the token1 surplus).

Also adds test/SwapAndAddFarEdge.t.sol — the referee for the claimed
trim div-by-zero at the range's far edge: a deterministic tight-config
grid plus a 5000-run fuzz hunting the state across the user-reachable
space. Both hold: the sell's average execution is a geometric mean
below spot while the fee-aware surplus is spot-sized net of fees, so
full-range extraction is unaffordable and the price stays strictly
inside the far edge on supported pools. That argument is now written
at the trim INVARIANT, and the interface's unsupported-pools note
gains the low-level-revert shape that returns-delta hooks (the only
way to reach the edge) can produce.

rationale: The change adds a guard to skip an unnecessary swap when the flash debt is already retired, fixing incorrect behavior that caused extra pool fees and incorrect token handling. The fix does not address an exploitable security issue, only corrects functional semantics.

subject: fix(lens): stop V4Quoter reverse traversal when a hook funds the whole input
body:
V4Router._swapExactOutput breaks out of its reverse loop once a hop's input
delta reaches zero, since a hook that fully funds the input leaves the
upstream pools with nothing to produce. V4Quoter._quoteExactOutput never
gained the mirror guard, so it propagated the zero into the preceding pool
and called swap with an amountSpecified of zero, which PoolManager rejects.
The QuoteSwap payload was then replaced by SwapAmountCannotBeZero on the way
out, surfacing as UnexpectedRevertBytes instead of a zero-input quote.

Routes the router executes for free were therefore unquotable, so
quote-dependent integrations excluded valid subsidy paths.

test_quoteExactOutput_fullyFundedHop_revertsSwapAmountCannotBeZero asserted
the broken behavior, so it passed against the bug. It is replaced by
test_quoteExactOutput_fullyFundedHop_quotesZeroInput, which pins the quote to
zero and matches the router's
test_exactOutput_multiHop_hookFundsFinalHop_skipsUpstreamHops.

Costs 29 gas per exact-output hop.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit adds a guard that stops processing when a zero output amount is encountered, fixing a bug where the quoter would call a pool swap with amountSpecified=0, causing a revert. The pre‑fix behavior could be triggered by a malicious hook fully funding the input, leading to denial‑of‑service for quoting free routes, thus a security‑related availability issue.
