A minimality pass over the nine-commit indexer series before it lands as a
production stack. Net −664 lines; the delta against margin-trading goes from
+6757/−181 across 34 files to +6160/−248 across 30.

Dead code, all verified unreachable rather than merely unused:
- FlowEvent.txTo: six writers, no reader. It was the input to a tx.to close gate
  that was deliberately dropped; its own comment said "diagnostics only".
- swapEconomics().attributable: hard-coded true, so `attributable && bought > 0n`
  was `bought > 0n`, guarded by fifteen lines documenting a tripwire that cannot
  trip.
- reverseAndSupersedeAdjust's collateral/debt params: destructured, never read,
  passed by all four callers.
- The two Aave v3 token caches and their _clear*ForTests exports — test-only
  exports in shipped code, saving one eth_call on two rare paths.
- aaveV4SpokeAbi.SetUsingAsCollateral, deployments.chainId, deployments.compoundComet.
- The raw-candidates arm of CollateralAdded's pair resolution. addresses.ts already
  called it pre-startBlock-only, and MarginRouter emits PositionUpdated inside the
  same try as CollateralAdded, so justUpdated can never be empty. It was also a
  hazard: if reached it attributes the top-up to whatever single OPEN position
  shares the collateral token, which may be the wrong pair.

The deficit layer is removed entirely — recordDeficit, resolveDeficitPosition,
both handlers, the DEFICIT enum value, position.badDebt and the v4 hub ABI. It
existed to populate badDebt, which the backend selects and no business logic
reads, and the v4 leg cost two chain reads per event. Morpho keeps its own
bad-debt figure from Liquidate.badDebtAssets, which is free.

Duplication: reserveAssetForId re-ran resolvePairByReserveId's exact query, so
the latter now returns { pair, reserveAsset } from the candidates it already
fetched. The `belongs` predicate was copy-pasted into router.ts from
lendingFlows.ts — two copies of the rule deciding which position a flow lands
on — and is now one reserveBelongsTo in helpers. `event: any` is typed.

Comments: twenty-five corrections. The largest were factually wrong rather than
merely stale — a block in detectRouterlessClose that claimed to derive close
economics directly contradicted the next paragraph and the code; four comments
said Aave v4 has no flow-truth layer when aave.ts implements one; two blamed a
"pre-upgrade deployment" that startBlock excludes; marginAccounts blamed
execute() for a gap only owner-driven clone calls create; and a docstring for
synthesizeAdjust sat above hasLiquidationInTx. Also dropped plan-and-ticket
archaeology from the tests (IDX-3/4/8, "D0 gate", "plan cases a-f", a commit SHA)
and the letter prefixes on test titles.

Tests: 68 -> 61. mergePort.test.ts grouped by merge seam rather than behavior;
both its cases moved to adjust.test.ts and drainFlows.test.ts, the second
re-keyed off COMPOUND_V3, which no handler can stage. harness.test.ts tested the
harness; its real-receipt decode moved to liquidations.test.ts and its synthetic
liquidation was a strict subset of case (a). One of the two 18KB receipt fixtures
was redundant with the other.

Kept deliberately, each having survived a removal proposal: marginAccounts.ts and
the MarginAccounts factory (MarginAccount._authCaller admits owner as well as
manager, so owner-driven supplyCollateral/borrow emits clone events with no
router event at all, and USDC is the debt token of nine of the twelve launch
markets); applyStagedFlows' skip block, which is the type narrowing from the
schema enums to FlowEvent's unions; the equityBase null guard, required because
the column must stay nullable; readVenueBalances and readVenueDebt, which differ
in units and error semantics; and detectRouterlessClose.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: only non-code files changed

subject: fix(indexer): never halt indexing on an unavailable oracle mark
body:
Every position action stamps a venue-oracle mark, and the read fell through to a
blocking readMarkAtBlock that throws when the oracle is unavailable or reverts —
halting the whole indexer. That is an ops risk on the curated path and a serious
one in the flow layer: synthesizeAdjust and recordLiquidation read the oracle
too, and oracle staleness clusters during a liquidation storm, exactly when the
indexer must keep up.

readMarkAtBlockSoft wraps the read as warn + null, and every per-action path goes
through it. The mark columns are nullable and the other economics are computed
independently, so an unavailable oracle yields honest null PnL for that action
rather than a halt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit replaces a hard-failing oracle read (which threw and halted the indexer) with a soft wrapper that catches errors, logs a warning, and returns null, preventing the indexer from stopping when the oracle is unavailable. This fixes a bug and mitigates a denial‑of‑service risk where an attacker could cause oracle failures to halt indexing.

subject: fix(indexer): adapt to the post-audit event saturation and order the flow-layer swaps
body:
Two defects the rebase surfaced, neither of which either branch handled.

The audited router saturates PositionIncreased.debtDrawn to zero (0bc21971) so
its best-effort event block cannot revert: a permissionless onBehalf repay
landing inside the transaction can leave the debt below its pre-increase level.
It is never legitimately zero — _increase rejects collateralToBuy == 0 and
borrows OPEN_DELTA, exactly the swap cost — so zero means the borrow cost is
UNKNOWN, not free.

An unknown fill must contribute nothing to the cost basis, not merely carry a
null price on its action row. On INCREASE, totalCollateralBought grew by a real
fill while totalDebtDrawn stood still, halving avgEntryPriceX18 and keeping it
there, since the inflated denominator is permanent. On OPEN, the null price
looked like the fix working, but the epoch was seeded with a real
totalCollateralBought against a zero cost, so the next ordinary increase averaged
against a denominator nothing paid for. Both branches now skip the basis
entirely; the authoritative fields are untouched, since collateralAmount and
debtPrincipal come from the event's own totals rather than the running sums.

The decrease side already degraded safely: a saturated collateralWithdrawn zeroes
collateralSold, which the existing guard maps to null.

Separately, txSwaps ordered by swapEvent.id, which is `${txHash}-${logIndex}` and
sorts lexically, so log index 10 preceded 9. swapEconomics attributes the pool
from the first row, so the flow layer could name the wrong pool. This is the same
bug 259655a7 fixed in consumeSwaps and txLendingEvents; the flow layer's copy was
missed. The curated path was never affected — it reads consumeSwaps.

Each case is pinned by a test that fails without its fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change corrects off‑chain indexing logic (cost‑basis calculation for PositionIncreased events and swap ordering) that was previously incorrect, but it does not alter on‑chain behavior or introduce/mitigate a vulnerability that an attacker could exploit to steal funds or affect protocol security.

subject: refactor: Renaming and small restructure
rationale: The change replaces getAmountsForLiquidity with a rounding‑up variant and renames settlement functions, fixing a calculation bug where amounts could be rounded down, potentially leaving a deficit that could be exploited for profit. This is a functional fix with security implications (economic loss), thus a security fix of medium severity.

subject: feat(indexer): attribute a position's venue from the clone's adapter
body:
`drainFlows` can only name a venue that staged a lendingEvent row. Compound has
no flow-truth layer — Comet is not an indexed contract — so a Compound
transaction stages nothing and both epoch-opening sites wrote UNKNOWN, which the
backend cannot join to a market. Venue was written once at open and nothing could
correct it.

The MarginAccount clone already reports the adapter of every action it performs,
as an indexed topic on CollateralSupplied and Borrowed, and those events are
already indexed on a factory source covering every clone — the handler was
reading the currency and dropping the adapter. markets.ts already maps adapter to
venue. So this needs no new contract, no new ABI concept and no chain read.

Ordering makes it safe: MarginRouter calls the account and only then emits its
snapshot (_emitPosition), so the sighting is always in hand before the handler
that needs it runs. Ponder matches a factory child's logs in the same block as
its AccountCreated, so a first-ever open is covered.

Sightings are keyed by (txHash, account, currency, role) rather than by account.
One transaction can drive one clone through two adapters for two pairs, and an
account-wide key would hand one pair's venue to the other. Within a pair the
latest sighting wins, which is exact because each snapshot immediately follows
the account call that caused it. Two distinct adapter ADDRESSES for one pair
means the transaction touched two venues and neither is attributable — compared
by address rather than by mapped venue, so an adapter the registry does not know
still forces the ambiguous answer instead of leaving one venue standing.

CollateralWithdrawn and Repaid are indexed too, for their adapter only. Their
amounts are unusable — CollateralWithdrawn logs zero on every venue but Aave v4,
per its own NatSpec — and the venue events remain the single writer of balances.
Without them a transaction that only exits has no sighting for either currency.

The hint is always last in precedence: real flow evidence first, then the epoch's
own venue, then the adapter. `upgradeVenue` repairs a live epoch on a later
transaction but only ever turns UNKNOWN into a known venue, never rewrites one
venue as another, so a row cannot flap. It is skipped on terminal updates:
MarginRouter's debt-free full close can emit its snapshot with no adapter-bearing
clone event at all, so the only hint in scope there may belong to another leg.

Adds a test-only reset for the module-scoped sighting maps, since they are
transaction-scoped rather than test-scoped and outlive the harness's table wipe.

Five of the seven new cases fail without this change. The other two are guards
that assert UNKNOWN — the same answer HEAD gives — and exist to discriminate
against a venue-keyed latch and against adopting a foreign leg's hint on a
terminal snapshot.

Compound liquidation detection and per-flow history are still missing; they need
the Comet truth layer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The change adds missing events to the ABI and implements logic to correctly attribute a position's venue from the adapter, fixing previously incorrect venue mapping in the indexer. This corrects a functional bug but does not affect on-chain security or expose exploitable behavior.

subject: test: replace high-rejection vm.assume filters with bound
body:
Correcting the ignored `fuzz_runs` key to the valid `fuzz.runs` finally honors
the configured run counts (256 -> 10k default / 100k CI). The rejection budget
scales with runs, so 25 pre-existing fuzz tests whose `vm.assume` discards a
large fraction of inputs began tripping `max_test_rejects` (65536).

Remove the rejection instead of masking it:
- add createFuzzyTwoSidedLiquidityParams / addFuzzyTwoSidedLiquidity, which
  force a straddle-0 range structurally via bound (minSpacingsPerSide keeps the
  one wider-straddle test's exact domain)
- convert the tickLower<0<tickUpper, tick-ordering, and decreaseLiquidityDelta
  assumes across the position-manager suite
- bound the competition deadline timestamp assume (restores full fuzzing)
- cap runs on the two CREATE2 vanity-address tests, whose betterThan rarity
  cannot be expressed with bound

All 25 previously-failing tests pass at 100k runs with zero rejections.
rationale: The commit only modifies test files, replacing vm.assume with bound and adding helper functions for fuzzing. No production code or contract logic is changed, so it does not fix a bug in the deployed behavior and does not address any security issue.

subject: feat(margin): enumerate an adapter's supported markets onchain
body:
isSupportedMarket confirms a pair but can't list one, and the router only
enumerates adapters, so building a market picker meant pulling a venue's whole
catalogue (~1700 Morpho markets, ~1200 Aave pairs) and probing every entry. Log
scanning doesn't fix it: setMarket is re-callable, so reconstructing the live set
needs a full-history replay taking the latest per key, and the cold-build cost
grows with chain height.

Add supportedMarketsLength() and supportedMarkets(offset, limit) to
ILendingAdapter, backed by an enumerable key set maintained in setMarket:
- MarketRegistry (Morpho) and MarketAllowlist (Aave v3, Compound) gain a keys
  array + 1-based index; register/set keep it in sync (append on add, swap-pop on
  remove, dedupe a Morpho re-registration)
- AaveV4LendingAdapter tracks the same over its bespoke reserve-id routes
- add Market.paginate as the shared, overflow-safe bounded slice

Requires redeploying the adapters.
rationale: The commit adds new enumeration functions and internal bookkeeping to list supported markets; it does not correct previously incorrect behavior nor address a security vulnerability.

subject: refactor(margin): extract EnumerableMarketKeys, dedupe the market-key set
body:
The Market[] + 1-based index + swap-pop key tracking was hand-written in four
places (MarketAllowlist, MarketRegistry, AaveV4LendingAdapter, MockLendingAdapter),
each an independent chance to get the last-element / index edge case wrong.

Extract it into one tested EnumerableMarketKeys primitive (add/remove/has/count/
page) and embed it:
- MarketAllowlist becomes a thin wrapper: membership == enumeration via has(),
  dropping the parallel _allowed map
- MarketRegistry keeps its MarketParams value map but uses has() as the single
  membership source, so isSupported/resolve and count/page can't desync (retires
  the zero-pair sentinel gap structurally; the zero guard stays as its policy)
- AaveV4LendingAdapter's inline swap-pop collapses to add()/remove()
- MockLendingAdapter collapses onto it too
rationale: The commit replaces hand‑written add/remove logic for market keys with a tested EnumerableMarketKeys primitive, fixing potential edge‑case bugs (e.g., swap‑pop index errors) that could cause inconsistent market enumeration. This is a functional correction, not a new feature, but the change does not introduce explicit security mitigations or address an exploitable vulnerability.

subject: revert: restore hook-funded input tolerance on exact-output swaps (#604)
body:
Reverts a7af5b34 (#601), which reverted bbd43468 (#584). This restores
#584 in full for the 2.3.0 line.

#601 removed #584 only because it was caught up in rolling universal-router
back to what was actually deployed (Uniswap/universal-router#514). Nothing
was wrong with #584 itself, and the 2.3.0 work needs it back. It lands on
this dev branch rather than main so it stays out of an upstream release
until the 2.3.0 audit clears.

Restores the two guards #601's reviewer note called out:

- `params.minHopPriceX36 != 0 && amountIn != 0` in exactOutputSingle, and
  the same `amountIn != 0` term in the multi-hop per-hop bound. Without it,
  a hook funding the entire input divides by zero and panics.
- `if (amountIn == 0) break;` in the multi-hop loop, which stops the route
  from calling swap with amountSpecified == 0, which PoolManager rejects.

Both are reachable only when a hook funds the whole input of an
exact-output swap; MockFullySubsidizingHook and
V4RouterHookFundedExactOutput.t.sol come back with them.

The only difference between src/V4Router.sol here and at #584 is #585's
`_validatePoolKey` hook, which is untouched by this revert.

## Verification

- `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=ci forge test --isolate` — 952 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped
- `FORGE_SNAPSHOT_CHECK=true` — clean, no snapshot drift; #584's gas values
  restore exactly (V4Router_Bytecode 10,415 -> 10,511)
- The 10 restored hook-funded tests all pass
- `forge fmt --check` — the only diff is the pre-existing PositionManager.t.sol
  artifact from local forge 1.8.1 vs CI's pinned 1.4.3; untouched here

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit restores checks that prevent a division‑by‑zero panic and a call to swap with amountSpecified == 0 when a hook fully funds the input of an exact‑output swap. Previously the router could revert (crash) under these conditions, which is an availability issue exploitable by a malicious hook. The added guards fix the bug, making it a security‑relevant fix (CWE‑369, DoS).

subject: refactor(margin): drop the router's adapter allowlist and governance
body:
The caller already chooses the market on every call and vets it; the adapter
is no different. The router derives the account from the authenticated caller,
so a caller-chosen adapter can reach only the caller's own account, a power the
owner escape hatch already grants outright. Gating exposure-increasing actions
on a governance allowlist therefore protected nobody but the caller from
itself, and it was the router's only governed surface.

Remove `_allowedAdapters`, `_governance`, `setAdapterAllowed`,
`isAdapterAllowed`, `governance`, `pendingGovernance`, `transferGovernance`,
`acceptGovernance`, the `AdapterAllowed` and `GovernanceTransfer*` events, and
the `AdapterNotAllowed` error; the constructor loses its governance argument.
The `Owner` type has no remaining user and is deleted. Supply and borrow no
longer gate on the adapter, and the account's trust model NatSpec states the
caller-chosen argument for every path. The deploy script has no post-deploy
wiring left, the salt-mining scripts hash the four-argument constructor, and
the operational script no longer checks the allowlist.

Tests drop the governance and allowlist-asymmetry suites and the shared router
deployer's governance argument; the swap-free exit plan test stays under a
behavioral name. Router runtime is 22,360 bytes; snapshots regenerated with
--isolate (0.01% to 0.9% less gas per flow).
rationale: The commit removes the router's adapter allowlist and governance, which is a refactor of access control logic rather than a correction of incorrect behavior. No new security checks are added, and the change does not address a previously exploitable defect.

subject: fix(router): decode V4 swap params with abi.decode (#593)
body:
The four V4 swap parameter decoders assigned their struct pointer in
assembly, which suppresses solc's validation. Solc bounds the dynamic
members of such a struct against calldatasize() rather than against the
enclosing slice, so a member could begin inside `params` and extend past
`params.length`. A caller that authenticates `params` at its declared
length -- universal-router's RouteSigner hashes each command input at that
length -- could then execute on bytes it never covered, letting a declared
route and an executed route diverge.

Decoding with abi.decode works from a copy of exactly `params.length`
bytes, so the bound is enforced by the compiler and holds transitively:
the path array header, each element's offset, each PathKey's own hookData,
minHopPriceX36, and the single-hop hookData.

The decoders now return memory, so `_swap`, the four `_swap*` helpers and
PathKeyLibrary.getPoolAndSwapDirection take memory as well.

Two deliberate relaxations, both bounded by `params` and so unable to
reach unsigned bytes: a non-canonical but in-bounds offset is accepted,
and the effective minimum length is the struct head rather than a fixed
constant. Both are covered by tests.

Costs 274 bytes of V4Router runtime size here and ~410-730 gas per swap.

CalldataDecoderSwapEncoding.t.sol asserts the property rather than the
implementation, so it still fails if the decoders are rewritten in
assembly to reclaim size.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
rationale: The commit replaces unsafe assembly decoding that allowed dynamic struct members to read beyond the declared params length, a bug that could let a signed route be executed with extra unchecked data, potentially leading to fund loss. The fix adds proper abi.decode bounds checking, correcting the security flaw.

* feat(router): add _mapSwapAmount hook for execution-time swap amounts

Add `_mapSwapAmount(uint128)` to V4Router, an internal virtual identity
mapping applied to the amount read from each swap action's params before
the OPEN_DELTA sentinel is interpreted. An inheriting router can override
it to resolve a route-level sentinel (such as a register populated by a
prior command) into a concrete amount at execution time without
reimplementing the private swap helpers. The Universal Router's RESOLVE
command needs this to support exact-output v4 swaps whose amount is only
known onchain.

Default behavior is unchanged. Cost is +18 bytes of V4Router bytecode and
+22 gas per swap action; snapshots regenerated in isolate mode.

* docs(router): tighten _mapSwapAmount NatSpec

subject: fix: OZ 2.3.0 audit fixes on the router path (L-02, N-01, N-05, N-08) (#608)
body:
* fix(lens): SafeCast the swap delta conversions in V4Quoter

V4Quoter read the unspecified side of a swap's BalanceDelta with a bare
truncating uint128(...). Only the specified side is guaranteed to have the
expected sign. The unspecified side is whatever remains after Hooks.afterSwap
applies the hook's returned delta, and a hook holding AFTER_SWAP_FLAG plus
AFTER_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA_FLAG can drive it past zero.

The only existing guard, BaseV4Quoter._swap's NotEnoughLiquidity check, compares
the specified side against the requested amount, so it cannot see this. The cast
wrapped and the quoter returned roughly 2^128 as a successful quote with no
revert, for a pool that in reality pays out nothing. A consumer that ranks
candidate pools by raw quoter output picks that pool over every honest one.

V4Router already handles the same two quantities correctly, so the quoter now
uses those exact forms. The output sides at _quoteExactInput and
_quoteExactInputSingle take the int128 overload of toUint128, matching
_swapOutput. The input sides at _quoteExactOutput and _quoteExactOutputSingle
widen before negating, uint256(-int256(x)).toUint128(), matching _swapInput.

The widening matters on its own. Negating an int128 first would panic on
type(int128).min before SafeCast ever ran, and that input is a legitimate
magnitude, not a corrupted one. The widened form yields 2^127.

Keeping the router's forms also preserves the hook-funded input case added in
bbd43468: an input delta of exactly zero still quotes as an amountIn of 0
rather than reverting, so a route the router can execute stays quotable.

Two related sites are fixed alongside. _quoteExactInput and
_quoteExactInputSingle built the swap amount as -int256(int128(amountIn)) from a
uint128. Above type(int128).max that reinterprets as negative, and the outer
negation flips the sign, so an exact-input quote silently simulated an
exact-output swap. Both now widen through uint256 as the router does.

A hook that corrupts the delta makes its own pool unquotable rather than
returning a clamped zero. Clamping would be wrong: a negative output delta means
the caller owes the output currency, not that the pool pays nothing, and the
router rejects that state too. Reverting keeps the quote and the swap in
agreement about which pools are usable.

Behavior on rejection is the existing shape. SafeCastOverflow bubbles out of the
simulation and parseQuoteAmount wraps it in UnexpectedRevertBytes, the same
outer error NotEnoughLiquidity already produces. No interface change.

One divergence from the router is left in place. In multi-hop exact output, a
fully hook-funded hop makes the router break out of its loop, while the quoter
propagates the zero into the next swap and hits SwapAmountCannotBeZero. That is
a revert rather than a wrong number. A test records the current behavior so a
future change to it is visible.

Reverting src/lens/V4Quoter.sol fails 8 of the 10 new tests. Four fail with "did
not revert as expected", which is the wrapped value being returned as a valid
quote, and the type(int128).min case fails with an arithmetic overflow panic.

Snapshots regenerated with Foundry v1.3.6 to match the version CI pins.

(cherry picked from commit 8d163f14d578443ebc552444f89ac269dd65eace)

* fix(lens): stop V4Quoter reverse traversal when a hook funds the whole input

V4Router._swapExactOutput breaks out of its reverse loop once a hop's input
delta reaches zero, since a hook that fully funds the input leaves the
upstream pools with nothing to produce. V4Quoter._quoteExactOutput never
gained the mirror guard, so it propagated the zero into the preceding pool
and called swap with an amountSpecified of zero, which PoolManager rejects.
The QuoteSwap payload was then replaced by SwapAmountCannotBeZero on the way
out, surfacing as UnexpectedRevertBytes instead of a zero-input quote.

Routes the router executes for free were therefore unquotable, so
quote-dependent integrations excluded valid subsidy paths.

test_quoteExactOutput_fullyFundedHop_revertsSwapAmountCannotBeZero asserted
the broken behavior, so it passed against the bug. It is replaced by
test_quoteExactOutput_fullyFundedHop_quotesZeroInput, which pins the quote to
zero and matches the router's
test_exactOutput_multiHop_hookFundsFinalHop_skipsUpstreamHops.

Costs 29 gas per exact-output hop.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
(cherry picked from commit 7a1a256207c25fcf025ba7abd6dc005c282fd323)

* fix(router): revert on an empty path in the V4Router multi-hop swaps

An exact-input or exact-output swap with a zero-length path ran its loop
zero times and completed without swapping anything, so a route could
succeed while delivering no output. Both multi-hop helpers now revert with
EmptyPath before touching the register or the delta. OZ 2.3.0 audit L-02.

* docs(router): correct the exact-output over-delivery comment

The comment claimed a hook pool could deliver more output than requested.
It cannot: v4-core folds a hook's specified-side delta into the amount it
swaps and afterSwap can only adjust the unspecified side, so the caller's
output is at most the request. OZ 2.3.0 audit N-01.

* fix(decoder): bound the head word read by CalldataDecoder.toBytes

toBytes read the offset word for element `_arg` without checking that the
word lies inside the slice, so a params blob shorter than its declared
layout had its hookData offset read from whatever followed it in calldata.
Check the head word in whole words before reading it, which also covers a
`_arg` large enough to wrap the byte offset. The five PositionManager
decoders that rely on toBytes are the callers affected. OZ 2.3.0 audit N-08.

subject: refactor(margin): dispatch margin opcodes by explicit membership
body:

table: SET_ACCOUNT and ROUTE_SWAP by equality, the account-scoped opcodes

opcode means deciding there whether it needs an account), and everything
else through V4Router, which already reverts UnsupportedAction for an
opcode it does not define. _handleCoreAction likewise names SWEEP, WRAP,
and UNWRAP individually instead of relying on their contiguity, so the
test that pinned that contiguity is replaced by one that pins the
membership table. Behavior is unchanged, including the audit N-09
guarantee that an undefined opcode reports UnsupportedAction whether or
not an account is bound. The longer comparison chain costs about 1,000
gas per six-action plan.

subject: feat(margin): refuse native value on a router deployed without WETH9
body:
The router converts between native value and an ERC-20 only by wrapping
1:1 through the WETH9 it was deployed with. On a chain with no canonical
wrapper that constructor argument is the zero address, and until now the
native paths then failed only by accident: a wrap into an address with
no code, or a NativeCollateralMismatch that a zero-address collateral
would have slipped past.

Arc is the case that matters. Its native USDC is 18 decimals as
msg.value while the ERC-20 USDC interface is 6, both views of one
balance with nothing wrapping between them, so there is no wrapper to
deploy with and any accidental path from msg.value to a token amount is
a 1e12 scaling bug. Every native path (msg.value equity on
increasePosition and addCollateral, WRAP, UNWRAP) now reverts
NativeNotSupported when WETH9 is unset, and ERC-20 flows are untouched.
A new suite deploys a router without WETH9 and pins all four paths, the
zero-address-collateral case, the receive guard, and an ERC-20 plan.
rationale: The change adds a revert (NativeNotSupported) for native‑value paths when the router is deployed without a WETH9 wrapper. Previously these paths would wrap to address(0) or mis‑scale native USDC (18 decimals) to ERC‑20 USDC (6 decimals), causing loss of funds or under‑collateralized positions. Fixing this prevents the scaling bug and accidental ETH burn, which are exploitable security issues.

subject: build(script): verify weth9 is a 1:1 wrapper before broadcasting
body:
DeployMargin now checks the wrapper argument before startBroadcast. The
zero address is accepted and logged as the no-native deployment. Any
other address must have code and round-trip one wei through deposit and
withdraw 1:1, which rejects a bridged asset, a plain ERC-20, or a native
token interface in other decimals (Arc lists a bridged WETH that is not
a wrapper of its native USDC). The check runs in simulation only.
rationale: The commit adds validation of the WETH9 address to ensure it is a proper 1:1 wrapper, fixing a prior bug where any address could be used. Without this check, a malicious or incorrect wrapper could be deployed, leading to potential fund loss, making it a security fix (improper input validation).

over the adapter's describePosition, STATICCALL since it's view) and
_emitPosition (a pure emit helper taking an already-resolved

https://github.com/Uniswap/v4-periphery/pull/563#discussion_r4339971100

subject: remove requirement for half_q on pub key x

rationale: The commit removes an unnecessary check that public‑key x < HALF_Q in both the Go library and Solidity contracts. subject: solana/agent: always submit signature verify transactions
body:
The first transaction acquires a pseudo-lock by setting
initial_creation = true, which will fail if a signature account
already exists. However, this is unsafe since the operation
consists of multiple operations and is not atomic - if the first
validator fails to submit a full set of signature transactions,
other guardians will not retry submitting signature verification txs.

We disable this mechanism to never set initial_creation, which
causes guardians to spend more fees in exchange for fault tolerance.

Instead of failing with an AlreadyExists error, duplicate transactions
will now succeed as a no-op and all nodes will attempt to submit
the full series of signature transactions.

Co-authored-by: Hendrik Hofstadt <hendrik@nexantic.com>
Change-Id: I0c418497f19cc97c9ae7a11b206035d6e70c1b66
rationale: The change removes a non-atomic pseudo-lock (initial_creation flag) that could cause duplicate signature verification transactions to fail, leading to incomplete verification and a potential denial‑of‑service for VAA processing. Fixing this race condition restores availability, qualifying it as a security fix.

subject: Deserialize only the discriminant in the entrypoint.
body:
It would seem that Borsh, when deserializing an enum will consume a
large amount of stack space proportional to the number of discriminants.
This causes the entrypoint to trigger stack frame access violations
during the initial deserialization.

This change uses an enum represented by a u8 instead, and removes the
association between the discriminant and the data. Deserializing the
associated data is now pushed down to within the entrypoint match arms
instead.

Change-Id: I2dcb466bf7820b3344e175ad92988bb89f30cb15
rationale: The commit changes instruction serialization to avoid Borsh deserializing the full enum, which previously caused stack frame access violations (stack overflow) in the entrypoint. This crash could be triggered by a crafted transaction, leading to denial‑of‑service. The change fixes that bug, making it a security‑relevant fix.

rationale: The change makes the old guardian set account mutable (both in the struct and the instruction's AccountMeta), allowing the program to mark the previous guardian set as expired. Previously it was read‑only, so the old set could remain active, potentially letting former guardians sign messages after an upgrade, leading to unauthorized actions. This is a bug fix that addresses a security flaw (improper access control) with high impact.

* p2w-attest: mention attestation size in batch

This commit ensures that no matter the attestation format, a batch
will never contain attestations of different sizes. This guarantee
enables forward compatibility by adding new constant-size fields at
the end of a batch at all times. An older implementation will simply
not consume the remaining newer values while respecting the stated
batch member alignment.

subject: solitaire: Infer entry point argument type in solitaire! macro (#927)
body:
The type of the `ix_data` binding withing the solitaire! macro expansion
is explicitly annotated with its type, which comes from the macro's
pattern binding `$kind`. However, this type annotation is entirely
optional, since `ix_data` is passed in as an argument to `$fn`, whose
type forecs `ix_data` anyway, and rust will happily infer that from the
application. So we remove the explicit annotation which makes the entry
point macro easier to use.

commit-id:d428306c
rationale: The commit only refactors the `solitaire!` macro to drop explicit type annotations, simplifying usage. No functional behavior change, bug correction, or security impact is introduced.

subject: solitaire: remove recursive FromAccounts and 'c lifetime.
body:
Solitaire parses accounts using two traits, FromAccounts and Peel. The
FromAccounts derive macro generates a function, `FromAccounts::from()`,
which calls `Peel::peel` to construct each field in the struct:

```
let example = Example {
    foo: Peel::peel(next_account_iter(accs)?),
    bar: Peel::peel(next_account_iter(accs)?),
    baz: Peel::peel(next_account_iter(accs)?),
    ...,
}
```

The FromAccounts derivation also attempts to implement Peel for the
structure itself however, which means `Example` itself is embeddable as
a field in another accounts struct. This is only used in ClaimableVAA
which is a large source of confusion and the complexity is not worth
maintaining.

This commit removes the recursion by:

1) Removing the `impl Peel` derived by FromAccounts.
2) Removes the AccountInfo iterator from Context as it is no longer needed.
3) Adds the current parsed account to Context instead, safe thanks to (2)
4) Move message out of ClaimableVAA and pass in to verify everywhere instead.
5) Removes Peel/FromAccounts from ClaimableVAA.
rationale: The commit primarily refactors account parsing by removing recursive FromAccounts and restructuring how ClaimableVAA and PayloadMessage are handled. No functional bug is fixed; the changes appear to be a code cleanup without altering security checks.

subject: ethereum: deploy test token nonce race condition fix

[tests] Error: Returned error: VM Exception while processing transaction: the tx

It's not safe to submit txs in parallel, because the nonce can get out of sync.

subject: sui: reduce duplication of latest & previous version
body:
The latest & previous versions are needed in a few places within the
version control logic, but spelling them out individually everywhere
leaves room for error. Since Move doesn't have type type aliases, we
can't define a LATEST_VERSION alias. The only way to reduce duplication,
thus, is by instead of explicit type instantiation, we pass witnesses of
the versions and rely on type inference to fill in the types. We can
then just define `latest_version()` and `previous_version()` once, and
ensure they are all used consisntently. It also allows adding a test to
check these two versions are always different.
rationale: The commit only refactors version handling by introducing helper functions and passing version witnesses instead of explicit type parameters. No functional behavior change or bug correction is evident, and there is no indication of a security vulnerability being fixed.

subject: Revert "ethereum: fix view error with newer version of forge"
body:
This reverts commit 05cec3d7293d056baffa6bde5ad84da893155fe3 (#3059)

The commit was erroneously included in anticipation of a forge version
update, but it actually only generates an error with an outdated
forge-stdlib version.

The old version's `vm.addr` function
(see
https://github.com/foundry-rs/forge-std/blob/ddb69063e4c9cc4aa863b224fc8a166be5d330ce/src/Vm.sol#L15)
has no `pure` modifier, thus any function using it can not be `pure` (or `view`).
The new version (see
https://github.com/foundry-rs/forge-std/blob/66bf4e2c92cf507531599845e8d5a08cc2e3b5bb/src/Vm.sol#L55)
on the other hand does. In fact, with the new version, removing the
modifier produces a warning.
rationale: The commit reverts a previous change that added a `view` modifier, restoring the function to non‑view so it compiles with older versions of forge‑stdlib where `vm.addr` is not pure. This fixes a build‑time bug but does not alter runtime behavior or introduce/mitigate a security issue.

subject: node: Add Transfer Verifier mechanism (#4169)
body:
Adds a new package and command-line tool for Transfer Verification. This is a process of validating message publications from the core contracts. When a message is emitted, Transfer Verification will examine the corresponding receipt or other logs to ensure that funds were sent into the token bridge whenever this kind of message is emitted from the core bridge. 
This is a defense-in-depth mechanism to guard against a scenario where an attacker finds a way to spoof message publications.
rationale: The commit introduces new Dockerfiles, k8s resources, and a monitoring package for Transfer Verification, but does not modify existing logic to correct a defect. It is a feature addition, not a bug fix, and therefore not a security fix.

subject: solana: reclaim rent for old accounts (#4746)
body:
* solana/solitaire: add support for anchor-style event cpi

This is implemented as an opt-in feature.

* solana/bridge: store VAA submission time

* solana: close old posted_message, signature_set, and posted_vaa accounts

* solana/bridge: emit entire account in close_posted_message

* solana/bridge: make retention period 1 day on solana testnet

The main challenge in doing this is figuring out when we're on testnet,
since the solana contract only indirectly encodes this by taking the
contract address as an env variable.

The approach we take is minimally invasive in that it doesn't require
introducing a new flag. Instead, we just check that the contract address
is the testnet address.

* solana/solitaire: extract emit_event_cpi helper

Pulls Anchor-style self-CPI event emission (PDA derivation + invoke_signed)
out of the bridge into a reusable solitaire helper. The bridge close path
now only validates self_program against ctx.program_id (returning
InvalidProgramOwner instead of the misnamed InvalidEventAuthority) and
delegates the rest to the helper. Drops the now-unused
Error::InvalidEventAuthority variant.

Also fixes the dispatch guard to surface the offending key in
SolitaireError::InvalidSigner when the first account is non-signer instead
of always returning Pubkey::default().

* solana/bridge: use checked_add for reclaimed lamports

The += accumulators when transferring reclaimed rent to the fee_collector
could in principle wrap around. Match the rest of the bridge (e.g.
post_message.rs:202) by going through checked_add and returning
MathOverflow on saturation.

* solana/bridge: enforce full-closure semantics on reclaim

Match the bridge's "live account" definition (lamports > 0, data > 0,
program-owned) when reclaiming rent.

* Truncate the data buffer to length 0 with realloc(0, false) instead of
  zero-filling the existing buffer. Other bridge code probes data_len()
  to detect initialized accounts (and the close path itself does so for
  the PostedVAA), so a zero-filled but full-length buffer would still
  read as "initialized" elsewhere.
* Add lamports > 0 to the PostedVAA "is initialized" check, mirroring
  data_len > 0 / owner check. After this commit, all three become zero
  in lockstep at close time.

* solana/bridge: shape-check accounts before reclaiming rent

Defense-in-depth against type-cosplay: even though the prefix and PDA
derivation checks are believed sufficient, add invariant checks on field
values that post_message / post_vaa always uphold. An account that fails
any of these is either corrupt or impersonating a different account type
under a matching prefix; refuse to close it (and reclaim rent).

PostedMessage (msg/msu): submission_time != 0, vaa_time == 0,
emitter_chain == OUR_CHAIN_ID. vaa_time is decisive — post_vaa writes
that field on the separate "vaa"-prefixed account, never the message.

PostedVAA (vaa): vaa_version != 0, vaa_time != 0, and
vaa_signature_account == signature_set.key. The last constraint pins the
close to the specific signature set that verified this VAA, not merely
any signature set whose hash collides on the same VAA payload.

Also documents the SignatureSet constraints inline on the close
struct, since SignatureSet has no magic prefix and the security argument
relies on the parse + hash-derivation chain holding together.

* solana/bridge: tighten close-path test helpers

The set_submission_time helper indexes data[41..45] without checking
that the account exists or has any of the expected layouts; a
mismatched account would silently corrupt unrelated bytes and produce
a hard-to-diagnose Custom(0) downstream. Add an explicit length check
and a "msg"/"msu"/"vaa" prefix assert so a layout change surfaces as a
panic at the patch site.

Also corrects the four "Set submission_time to 0 (epoch)" comments in
integration.rs — the helper actually backdates to ~31 days ago.

* solana/bridge: extend close-path test coverage

Adds three pieces of coverage from PR review:

* test_close_signature_set_rejects_wrong_data_length: a regression
  test confirming that the SignatureSet close path rejects an account
  whose data length doesn't match SignatureSetData. The test pads a
  legitimate signature_set with one trailing byte and expects the
  close to fail, exercising the try_from_slice "no leftover bytes"
  guarantee that protects against arbitrary-account-close attacks
  given the absence of a magic prefix on SignatureSet.

* test_close_posted_message_unreliable: the unreliable ("msu") path
  was only checking that the account was zeroed; align it with the
  reliable test by also asserting that fee_collector received the
  reclaimed lamports and bridge.last_lamports was bumped to match.

* test_close_signature_set_and_posted_vaa_happy_path: assert
  bridge.last_lamports tracks fee_collector after closing both the
  sig set and the posted VAA — previously only the totals on
  fee_collector were verified.
rationale: The commit adds checked_add to prevent lamport overflow, enforces full-closure semantics and proper data truncation to avoid account revival, and adds retention checks. These changes fix bugs that could be exploited to steal or misuse funds, constituting a security fix.
